#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.4.3.2 — A node's cursor does not survive its inbox being pruned

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0456`. Opened by DOC-0152 (the attached clause).
- 🔴 As found (DOC-0152's census; reproduced RED first by this leaf, the control written BEFORE the repair as the clause demands): every cursor writer was `COALESCE(MAX(cursor), 0) + 1` over the rows that happened to remain (`node_channel.rs` `enqueue` and `enqueue_in_tx`; `node_admin.rs` the quarantine replay) and nothing recorded a high-water mark, while the three refusals (handshake, poll, ack) compared the node's reported cursor with that same maximum. The retention prune deletes delivered rows, the top of the ledger included, so a node that acknowledged up to N and had those rows pruned was refused `cursor_ahead` on every crossing, and every row written afterwards took a cursor ≤ N that its `cursor > N` replay never offered — hidden work, held against the backlog cap.
- Owns: a durable per-node cursor floor every writer allocates above; RED first — the prune-everything-then-reconnect control; book.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — the high-water mark was DERIVED from the ledger's rows instead of RECORDED, and the ledger is pruned: `MAX(cursor)` answers *the highest row still here*, not *the highest cursor ever handed out*, and the two diverge exactly when the prune removes the top. The existing retention control (`prune_deletes_only_delivered_rows_older_than_the_window`) keeps `cmd_prune_3..5`, a partial prefix holding the maximum, so it never asked the second question — the attached clause's finding, confirmed by the RED.
- [x] **ADDRESSED** — `migrations/0103_node_inbox_cursors.sql`: one row per node, `high_water`, seeded from today's maxima (`INSERT … SELECT node_id, MAX(cursor) … GROUP BY node_id`, so no live node moves). `node_channel::next_cursor_in_tx` is THE allocator: an upsert that sets `high_water = GREATEST(mark, MAX(cursor)) + 1` and returns it — the mark never goes down, a row written past it (a fixture, a ledger older than the mark) is never numbered under, and the row is the natural per-node lock. Every writer goes through it: `enqueue` (now one transaction, so the allocation and the row commit together), `enqueue_in_tx`, and the quarantine replay (`cursor = $6`). `current_cursor` / `current_cursor_in_tx` read `GREATEST(mark, MAX(cursor))` (`CURRENT_CURSOR_SQL`), so the three refusals measure against the mark. ⚠️ NOT recoverable by data: a node whose WHOLE ledger was pruned before this migration has no maximum to seed from and keeps the cursor it lost — the migration says so. ⚠️ The allocator's row lock very likely also removes `.4.3.4`'s collision; that leaf proves it with its own control and is NOT closed here. Cleanup plans: `node_inbox_cursors` added to all 30 plans naming `node_inbox` (a counter left behind would start the next fixture's cursors above 1). ⚖️ `SHARED-REGISTRY-WRITES` adjudicated: the table is node-keyed with no tenant dimension by construction — a node's mark is one number whichever tenants' work it carries (the origin binding) — so it is the class of `node_leases`, `node_keys` and `node_events`; the eight baseline rows whose reach it joins (the five node-channel routes and `enroll-tokens` by `node_channel`'s module reach; the three thread routes by the dispatch's real write) are refreshed in `.doctrine/shared_registry_baseline.tsv` with their admissions unchanged, and the published pair does not move (`25 site-global writers (9 on identity alone) across 10 tables, residue 0` — the ten enrolment-only tables are untouched). Book: `node-channel.md` (the ledger the node is measured against; retention never moves the cursor), `qualification-review.md` (both `.4.3` rows annotated — `.4.3.1`'s was owed by REPAIR-0455 and is caught up here).
- [x] **VERIFIED** — RED FIRST on the REPAIR-0455 code (`9f12993` + the control): `RB_DEMO=0 bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh node_inbox` → `test result: FAILED. 11 passed; 1 failed` — `a_nodes_cursor_survives_its_inbox_being_pruned` at arm (1), *a node whose delivered rows were pruned is not `cursor_ahead`*: `409 {"code":"version_conflict","message":"reported cursor 3 is ahead of this server's ledger (2): the node's journal saw commands this server cannot reproduce"}`. GREEN: the same → `test result: ok. 12 passed; 0 failed`. The control: three rows, the middle quarantined before delivery; the node takes 1 and 3 and acks 3; the delivered rows are aged and pruned (`deleted 2, after 1`); (1) the reconnect at 3 is 200 with `current_cursor 3` and an empty replay; (2) the quarantined row replayed is numbered 4; (3) a fresh enqueue is numbered 5, and the reconnect at 3 is offered exactly `[cmd_floor_2, cmd_floor_4]` with `current_cursor 5`.
- [x] **FALSIFIED** — M1 (the pre-repair writers and readers) IS the RED. M2 (the allocator lets the ledger's maximum overwrite the mark — `GREATEST` dropped) → `test result: FAILED. 11 passed; 1 failed` at arm (2), *a replayed row is numbered above what the node acknowledged* — `left: 3, right: 4`. M3 (the reader consults the ledger's maximum only — the mark dropped from `CURRENT_CURSOR_SQL`) → `test result: FAILED. 11 passed; 1 failed` at arm (1) — the reconnect at 3 refused `409 version_conflict … ahead of this server's ledger (2)`, the RED's own failure. Each restored, `shasum -a 256 -c` OK.
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — every other `node_inbox` control passes unedited, the partial-prefix retention control included (its survivors and counts unchanged). `RB_DEMO=0 bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh node_channel node_work node_result_ordering node_replacement quarantine invitations` rc=0 (49, 12, 6, 2, 1, 7) and `… profiles migration_upgrade mcp command_api` rc=0 (89, 8, 6, 42) — ten suites, 223 tests, 0 failures, every control unedited; `migration_upgrade` covers the seed of the mark from a ledger that predates it, and the MCP suite's raw inbox row (cursor 1, no mark) reads back through the same `GREATEST`. #### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.4.3.3 — A result's idempotency and the `consumed` rung are not bound to the node

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0457`. Opened by DOC-0152.
- 🔴 As found (DOC-0152's census; reproduced RED first by this leaf at both surfaces): `apply_node_result_in_tx` claimed idempotency on `(tenant_id, command_id)` — the claim, the applied `Command`'s key and its three stored rejections — so two nodes holding one command id in a tenant folded at most once between them: the second node's result met the first node's claim with a different request hash (its own principal), was stored as an `idempotency_mismatch` rejection and lost. `node_inbox_state`'s `consumed` rung joined `node_events` on `e.operation_id = i.command_id` with no node predicate (`0078:74`), so another node's result read this node's row consumed. Command ids are unique per node only (`UNIQUE (node_id, command_id)`).
- ⚖️ **Measured before deciding, as the leaf was told to:** dispatch names every work item `work_{trigger_event_id}` and BOTH dispatch sites hand one trigger event to exactly one node (`accept_invitation` → the accepting role's node; `challenge` → the author's node), and the replacement ritual re-enrols the SAME node id — so the collision is LATENT today (server-assigned ids, one dispatch per event) and reachable by the next dispatch shape that fans one event out, not by any node deliberately. Of the two remedies, *the idempotency key names the node* is chosen over *command ids unique per tenant*: the first makes the fold's key structurally the work item's own identity (`(node_id, command_id)`, the inbox's key), while the second is a naming convention at the dispatch site that the next dispatch would have to remember. Consequence measured: one stored-row rewrite (below), one test reader re-keyed, no wire change.
- Owns: both keyed to the node; RED first with two nodes and one command id.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — the fold treated the command id as the work item's identity when the inbox itself keys work items by `(node_id, command_id)`; the rung was written for the same one-node world as the reconciliation lookup `.4.3.1` bound (its join had no node because nothing else in the view needed one).
- [x] **ADDRESSED** — `api::node_result_fold_key(node_id, command_id)` = `"{node_id}:{command_id}"`; `apply_node_result_in_tx` claims on it, applies the `Command` under it and stores all three rejections under it (`unauthorized` runs-here, authorization denied, prepare refused). `migrations/0104_node_result_fold_key.sql`: (1) `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW node_inbox_state` with `e.node_id = i.node_id` on the `consumed` rung — same columns, so `node_presence` (0079) is untouched; (2) stored fold rows re-keyed where the work item is unambiguous — the key equals the command id of a thread-work row (`payload->>'kind' IN ('contribute','revise')`) held by exactly ONE node in the tenant. ⚠️ Stated residuals: a key whose id two nodes hold (nothing says whose fold it was) or that no row holds any more (pruned) is left bare, and a later re-emission of THAT result under a NEW event id would fold again; a caller-chosen CLI key equal to a work command id would be re-keyed too — a shape no caller here produces. `node_work.rs`'s reader of the stored rejection keys by `{role}:{command_id}` (the dev rule: the node id is the role's). Book: `node-channel.md` (the ladder's `consumed` row — a receipt **from this node**; *Ordering a node result* — the fold's key is the work item's identity), `qualification-review.md` (the `.4.3.1` row's third place, the `consumed` rung, now closed here).
- [x] **VERIFIED** — RED FIRST on the REPAIR-0456 code (`298c90a` + the two controls): `RB_DEMO=0 bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh node_result_ordering` → `test result: FAILED. 6 passed; 1 failed` — `two_nodes_holding_one_command_id_each_fold_their_own_result` at *each node's result is its own work item's fold* — `left: 1, right: 2`; `… node_channel` → `test result: FAILED. 49 passed; 1 failed` — `a_foreign_nodes_result_does_not_read_this_nodes_row_consumed` at *another node's result does not consume this node's row* — `left: "consumed", right: "transport_received"`. GREEN: `RB_DEMO=0 bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh node_result_ordering node_channel node_work` → `ok. 7 passed`, `ok. 50 passed`, `ok. 12 passed` (the last with its re-keyed reader). The fold control: two roles accepted on one thread, each with its dispatched work item; B's row is given A's command id; A's result and B's result both `accepted` and the thread gains TWO contributions; B re-emitting its result under a new event id is a new receipt and no third contribution. #### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.4.3.4 — Enqueue is not serialized per node

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0458`. Opened by DOC-0152; the last of `.4.3`'s four.
- 🔴 As found (DOC-0152's census at `e6e19f3`): two concurrent `COALESCE(MAX(cursor), 0) + 1` allocations computed one cursor; the loser's insert raised the `(node_id, cursor)` key and its dispatching command rolled back rather than retrying — the docblock called the profile *single-writer*. The origin binding made two tenants' dispatches to one node real, and no tenant guard ordered them. No control exercised concurrent enqueue.
- ⭐ **Already removed by `.4.3.2`, and this leaf is the PROOF rather than a second repair:** since `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0456` every writer allocates through `node_channel::next_cursor_in_tx` — an upsert on the node's mark row (`node_inbox_cursors`) that takes the row's lock, so a second concurrent allocation waits on the first and reads the bumped value. DOC-0152 had named the mark row as *the natural lock row* for exactly this. ⛔ A control that has never been seen to refuse is not known to work, so the leaf's evidence is the control written GREEN and then FALSIFIED against the pre-0456 allocation.
- Owns: allocation serialized per node; the control; the falsification.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — the allocation READ the ledger (`MAX(cursor)`) and WROTE it in one statement with nothing between two writers: the read is not locked, so two transactions could both read N and both insert N+1. `.4.3.2` replaced the read-then-write with an upsert on a row that exists to be locked — the mark — which is what serializes the allocations.
- [x] **ADDRESSED** — no product change; `next_cursor_in_tx`'s docblock now cites the control instead of deferring the claim to this leaf. The proof: `concurrent_enqueues_to_one_node_serialize_on_its_mark` (`node_channel`) — a transaction holds the node's mark row `FOR UPDATE` the way an allocation in flight holds it; an enqueue spawned meanwhile is reported by `pg_stat_activity` as BLOCKED on a statement naming `node_inbox_cursors`, has written no row, and — once the holder commits — lands with cursor 2; then eight enqueues spawned at once all land with cursors exactly `3..=10`. Observed waits, never elapsed-sleep guesses (`blocked_on`, the suite's own helper).
- [x] **VERIFIED** — `RB_DEMO=0 bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh node_channel` → `test result: ok. 51 passed; 0 failed` with the control, on its first run (the property already held) and again after the holder was made to seed the row.
- [x] **FALSIFIED** — M1 (the pre-0456 `enqueue`: `MAX + 1` inside the insert, a pooled connection, no mark row). ⚠️ **The first run refused at the control's own precondition, not at the property**: `FAILED. 50 passed; 1 failed` at *the mark row is held: RowNotFound* — the old writer never creates the mark row, so the holder's `FOR UPDATE` found nothing. A refusal at a precondition proves the fixture, not the claim, so the holder now seeds the row idempotently (`INSERT … ON CONFLICT (node_id) DO NOTHING`, a no-op on the repaired code) and the control is about whether an enqueue WAITS on the row, never about which writer created it. Second run → `test result: FAILED. 50 passed; 1 failed` at *nothing ever blocked on node_inbox_cursors* — the spawned enqueue under the old allocation never touches the mark row, so the observed-wait assertion refuses within its 5 s bound. Restored, `shasum -a 256 -c` OK. ⚠️ This is the ONLY falsification the property admits: the two-writers race cannot be made RED deterministically against the old code (whether two `MAX + 1` reads interleave is timing), which is why the control observes the LOCK rather than the collision — under the mutant nothing ever blocks on the mark row, and that is deterministic.
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — every other `node_channel` control passes unedited; `RB_DEMO=0 bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh node_inbox node_work profiles` rc=0 — 12, 12, 89 (the three suites that drive the enqueue writers and the origin fixture's two-tenant dispatches to one node), every control unedited. Strict clippy on `reasonbraid-server` (`--all-targets --locked -D warnings`) rc=0; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0; `make book`; the doctrine gate at commit.

### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.4.4 — Node recovery and unknown outcomes

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.4.4.1 — An ambiguous attempt is reconciled by any receipt under its operation, and an operator's verdict is flattened

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0459`. Opened by DOC-0153; the worst of the census.
- 🔴 As found (DOC-0153 at `ff18c72`; reproduced RED first at both surfaces): the handshake's directive loop answered `Adjudicated reconciled` for ANY `node_events` row under the attempt's operation (`event_id_for_operation`, which `.4.3.1` had bound to the node but which filters on nothing else) — the node's own `work_dead_lettered` report, emitted by `report_dead_letter` after it refused an unauthorized retry of that very attempt, or a later attempt's `work_result` — so the ambiguity closed with no evidence for it, and `record_ambiguous_reports` closed the operator's row `adjudicated`. On the node, every `Adjudicated` directive was applied as `journal.reconcile(attempt_id)`, dropping `terminal` and `evidence`: an operator's `completed` and `failed_known` both became `reconciled`, the admission never reached the journal, and `retry_decision` refused `reconciled` as terminal.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.4.4.4 — A crash between the terminal record and the outgoing event loses a paid result for good

- Status: `done` — closed by `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0464` (`.4.4.4.2.2`). Opened by DOC-0153; SPLIT on 2026-09-23 into ✅ `.4.4.4.1` REPAIR-0462 (the loss: one transaction, delivery deferred rather than refused) → `.4.4.4.2` (no dispatch while unschedulable). The split is measured, not guessed: seven worker controls (`worker_cached_decision.rs` :263, :399, :455, :538, :657; `worker_retry_policy.rs` :170, :305) drive a NEVER-reconciled node and accept `Err(WorkerError::Node(_))` after a completed dispatch. Each one encodes the loss as passing behaviour, and none can reach `Schedulable` without a server. The dispatch refusal therefore needs a harness of its own, which one safe slice cannot also carry.
- 🔴 `record_completed` (`crates/reasonbraid-node/src/supervisor.rs:278`) and the outgoing `work_result` event (`emit_event` → `record_outgoing_event`) are separate transactions in separate modules, with the content only in memory between them. After a death in that window the attempt is `completed` with no event: the handshake reports nothing (`pending_operations` excludes completed attempts), the retry gate refuses the item as terminal, it is dead-lettered and quarantined, and a replay cannot revive it. The same loss needs no crash — `emit_event` refuses `NotSchedulable` after completion, and the worker never checks schedulability before dispatching.
- Owns: the completed transition and the outgoing event (content included) commit in ONE journal transaction, so a death after it leaves a pending event the reconcile re-emits with its original id; the worker checks schedulability before it dispatches; RED first — a kill point between the two writes (`journal_kill_points`) and the offline-dispatch arm; book (`node-channel.md` *Duplicate safety* / the recovery chapter).

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.4.4.4.1 — The completed record and its result event are one transaction, and an undeliverable result waits instead of vanishing

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0462`. Split from `.4.4.4`.
- Owns: the journal writes an attempt's `completed` transition (by the runtime answer OR a status-lookup proof) and its outgoing `work_result` event (content included, the operation taken from the attempt row) in ONE transaction; `execute_attempt` gains a result-event form the worker uses; the worker delivers the already-journaled event, and while the node is not schedulable it DEFERS: the event stays pending and the reconcile re-emits it with its original id, never an error that strands it. RED first: the seven controls that accept the loss are rewritten to assert the pending event; an atomicity control makes the event write fail and proves the transition rolled back. Book: `node-channel.md` *Duplicate safety*.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — the completion and the result were two writes owned by two modules: the supervisor journaled `completed` and returned; the worker built the payload from the in-memory report and wrote the event through `Node::emit_event`. The attempt's durable state and its result were therefore never one fact. `emit_event`'s schedulability refusal came BEFORE its journal write, so an unschedulable node discarded a completed attempt's result without writing it, even with no crash.
- [x] **ADDRESSED** — `Journal::record_completed_with_event(attempt, evidence, &ResultEvent, at)` over a private `apply_transition_emitting` (the transition, its ledger row and a plain `INSERT … SELECT operation_id FROM attempts` in ONE transaction; plain rather than `OR IGNORE`, because a minted id colliding is a defect that must undo the transition). `execute_attempt_emitting(…, &ResultEventBuilder)` builds the event from the finished report and lands it through `land_completed` on BOTH completion paths (the runtime answer and the status-lookup proof); `ExecutionReport.result_event` hands it back. `execute_attempt` keeps its form for its eighteen direct call sites in the node crate's tests (`grep -rn "execute_attempt(" crates/reasonbraid-node/tests | wc -l` → 18). `Node::deliver_journaled_event` → `EventDelivery::{Delivered, Deferred}`: an unschedulable node leaves the event pending for the reconcile instead of erroring; `emit_event` and it share `send_journaled`. Book: `node-channel.md` *A completed result and its event are written together* (death table, a journal example, the `.4.4.4.2` limit) and the *Schedulability gate* paragraph.

The miss, `Node::send_journaled → Ok(())`, is invisible to the node crate, which has no server to reach `Schedulable`. #### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.4.4.5 — A transport failure or an unknown outcome exits the node process, and the channel has no timeouts

- Status: `active` — opened by DOC-0153; SPLIT on 2026-09-23 into ✅ `.4.4.5.1` REPAIR-0465 (channel timeouts) → ✅ `.4.4.5.2` REPAIR-0466 (classification: a send failure reconciles, an unknown outcome continues the tick, an item-local error spares the other items) → `.4.4.5.3` (the reconcile retry backs off, bounded). Three mechanisms in three places (the channel client, the worker and loop, the loop's retry), each with its own RED. ⚖️ Narrowed by `.4.4.4.2.2` (REPAIR-0464): *the worker then dispatches into `NotSchedulable`* is closed. The worker refuses before the provider, and `rb-node` reconciles on that refusal via `WorkerError::calls_for_reconcile()`, which is where this leaf's send-failure and unknown-outcome classifications belong.
- 🔴 `reqwest::Client::new()` (`crates/reasonbraid-node/src/channel.rs:470,485`): no connect or request timeout, so a server that accepts and never answers hangs the worker for ever. In `rb-node`'s loop only `WorkerError::Channel` reconciles; a failed `send_event` (`NodeError::Channel` → `WorkerError::Node`) and `SupervisorError::OutcomeUnknown` (`WorkerError::Supervision`) both `exit(1)`; a failed reconcile sleeps one fixed second and returns to `run()`; a reconcile that fails after its handshake leaves the node Offline with a fresh lease, and the worker then dispatches into `NotSchedulable`; one item's error aborts the tick.
- Owns: bounded timeouts on the channel client; a send failure is a channel loss (reconcile, never exit); an unknown outcome is a FACT about the attempt already journaled — the tick continues; the reconcile loop backs off, bounded; one item's failure does not abort the others; RED first with a fake transport (a refused connection, a stalled response) driving `Worker` and the loop's classification; book (`node-channel.md` *Reconnect and cursor resume*).

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.4.4.8 — A completed, delivered work item is dead-lettered on the next tick

- Status: `pending` — opened 2026-09-23 by `.4.4.5.2`'s control, which measured it by accident; owned rather than routed.

Mechanism: `Journal::work_items` lists every contribute/revise command, finished or not (`crates/reasonbraid-node/src/journal.rs`, `work_items`); `retry_decision` answers `Some(_) => Refuse { "the attempt is terminal" }` for `completed` (`crates/reasonbraid-core/src/retry.rs`); `Worker::process` reports EVERY retry-gate refusal as a dead letter. Server side, `api.rs` (`kind == "work_dead_lettered"`) sets `quarantined_at` / `quarantine_reason` on the inbox row with no condition on whether that row's work finished, so a successfully completed item reads *dead-lettered: the attempt is terminal* one poll interval after it succeeded.
- Owns: a finished item (`completed`, and each other terminal, decided per state: `failed_known` IS a dead letter, and `reconciled` is an operator's verdict) is skipped silently, or reported once as what it is, and never as a dead letter; decide whether the server should also refuse to quarantine a row whose result it folded; RED first, the node side in-crate and the server side live (the inbox row's `quarantined_at` after a completed dispatch and one more tick); book.

### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.4.6 — The observability slice says it is the dev profile, and nothing owns the sink it defers to

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.4.7.2.1.4.2`, whose tranche-2 adjudication returned `fired and open` for the Phase-1 deferral *OpenTelemetry, operator dashboards, SLO baselines, game days*.
- ⚠️ **WHAT IS SHIPPED, FIRST, because the gap is smaller than the row's four nouns suggest.** `crates/reasonbraid-server/src/telemetry.rs` is a real observability slice: structured JSON-line operational logs on stderr and an in-process metrics registry over the §18.3 minimums that apply to the dev profile, under ADR-023's four-record doctrine — these counters are operational signals, never audit facts.
- 🔴 **AND THE MODULE'S OWN HEADER IS THE DEFERRAL, RESTATED WHERE NOTHING EVALUATES IT**: *the OpenTelemetry sink stays the ADR-023 trigger*. `grep -riE "opentelemetry|prometheus|metrics" crates/*/Cargo.toml` returns **nothing**, so no sink exists; every `SLO`, `dashboard` and `game day` occurrence in the tree is documentation.
- ⛔ **This is the exact shape `.11.4.7.2.1` measured at 27 of 27**: a revisit condition written in prose, inside a source comment this time rather than a decision record, with nothing that notices it firing. The remedy there was an adjudication pass, and this leaf is the adjudication for one condition.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.4.6.1.5.2 — A backup or restore test leaves no record the server can report

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0410`.
- Owns: the receipt each script writes after its step succeeds (`backup.sh`: bytes, SHA-256, taken-at, database name; `restore.sh`: verify the SHA-256 first, restore, check that the migrations are present, then write the restore receipt); `rb-server --backup-dir`; the report (each backup, the time since the newest one and since the newest restore-tested one, and §17.5's `recovery_control` verdict), with a size re-check of every receipted dump.
- Acceptance: produced by RUNNING the two scripts against a real database, never by writing receipts by hand; a truncated dump is reported as such; a backup never restored is listed but does not make the verdict `accepted`; RED first; book, the restore runbook and `SURFACE-JUDGEMENT`.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — `scripts/backup.sh` wrote only the dump and `scripts/restore.sh` only restored it; `tests/backup_restore.rs` dropped its target and recorded nothing. #### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.1.1 — The match surface classifies every tenant's candidate by the reader's own class

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0438`. Opened by DOC-0144's census, recorded on the parent.
- 🔴 As found: `directory_match` (`crates/reasonbraid-server/src/api.rs`) computed ONE `reader_class` for the caller — the owner `Full`, a member `Tenant` — clamped the expression's scope against it, judged every candidate's eligibility at the expression's scope, and filtered every returned profile with that one class, across ALL tenants. So a member of A read B's tenant-view fields, and B's tenant-only claim satisfied A's requirement. `directory_presence` classified per tenant all along, and the book's site-authority chapter described the one-class shape as the design.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — the surface was written when the directory had one tenant's worth of readers in mind: the reader's class was a property of the READER, computed once, while the visibility model makes it a property of the reader's RELATION to each candidate's tenant — own, federated, or foreign — which `classify_reader` and `directory_presence` both compute and the match never did.
- [x] **ADDRESSED** — `directory_match`: the clamp is against the reader's class toward its OWN tenant (`own_class`); each candidate's tenant is read from `node_presence`; the class toward that tenant is memoised per tenant — own → `own_class`, federated (`has_effective_directory_agreement`) → `Tenant`, else `Network`; each candidate is judged at the LOWER of the expression's scope and that class (a scoped clone of the expression), ranked in per-scope groups merged by the ranker's own key (per-candidate scoring; the cross-candidate dependence facts are the close's), and rendered with `filter_profile` at its own class. Book: `docs/book/src/site-authority.md` (the paragraph corrected, with what it used to say).
- [x] **VERIFIED** — `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh profiles` → **82 passed, 0 failed** (81 + `the_match_surface_classifies_each_candidate_by_its_own_tenant`): a member of A matching at tenant scope for owner-attested `code_review` — B's attested claim visible only to B's tenant → B is NOT a candidate; B publishes the claim to the network → B is a candidate rendered at the network view (its tenant-visible `scopes` absent) while the member's own tenant-mate keeps its tenant view; the effective directory agreement both ways → B at the tenant view (`scopes` present).
- [x] **FALSIFIED** — RED FIRST against the one-class surface (`git stash push -- crates/reasonbraid-server/src/api.rs`; the control kept): `a foreign tenant-only claim does not satisfy the requirement: [… "1 of the 1 required capabilities are declared (and visible at this scope)" …]` — B listed as a candidate on a claim the member could not see — `FAILED. 79 passed; 3 failed`; popped, `shasum -a 256 -c` OK, `82 passed`. 🔎 Two of the three RED failures were MINE: a fixture edit meant for the match control landed in the directory-reads control (the same `role_b_id` PUT shape), and an assertion I added to the match control misread its `role B` as foreign when it is the owner's second role. Both reverted; neither survived into GREEN, and the leaf says so rather than counting them.
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — the existing match control passes with its two own-tenant candidates unchanged (both rendered full for the owner), the directory-reads control unchanged, the scope clamp unchanged in effect (a member demanding `full` is still refused); strict clippy clean on core and server (`-D warnings`); `cargo fmt`; `make book`; `make gate`.
- ⚠️ **Honest limits, owned:** the effective-agreement predicate is now read once per foreign tenant per match, on the pool (a read racing a revocation sees one snapshot; a read cannot widen); the presence listing's per-tenant classification was not unified with this one — two sites, one shape, named in each other's comments.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.1.3 — An absent dependence fact is read as variation

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0444`. Opened by DOC-0149.
- 🔴 As found (`crates/reasonbraid-server/src/matching.rs`, `dependence.rs`): a candidate with no facts scores diversity `1.0`, and one missing an attribute is never penalized on it, so declaring less ranks higher; an attribute no member declared is explained as *varies across the panel*; the sharer test compares a value against all five of another member's attributes instead of the same one.
- Owns: diversity over KNOWN facts only, attribute by attribute; a candidate with no known fact scores `0` (unknown contributes nothing) and its explanation says so; an indicator distinguishes *varies* from *not declared* and counts the undeclared; RED first per shape; book (`recruitment.md`).
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — one cause, three shapes: the diversity score and the indicators were written over *values present*, so absence had no representation and fell through as the most favourable reading. `rank_with_dependence` started each candidate at `heaviest = 0` and returned `1 − heaviest`, so a candidate with nothing to compare kept `1.0`; the maximum form ignored an undeclared attribute entirely (hiding a shared one paid); the sharer test OR-ed a value against all five of another member's attributes; `dependence_indicators` built groups only from declarers, so *no groups* covered both *all different* and *nobody declared*.
- [x] **ADDRESSED** — `matching::diversity` (pure; called by `rank_with_dependence`): the MEAN over the five attributes of `1 − sharers/declarers`, an attribute counting only when the candidate AND at least one other declare that SAME attribute, every other attribute 0, the denominator always five — so an undeclared fact scores what a fact shared with everyone scores and declaring less never ranks higher; the explanation names each compared attribute (`its provider is shared by 1 of the 2 (50%)`) and how many contributed nothing, or says *unknown contributes nothing*. `dependence::ATTRIBUTES` is the one attribute list both modules read. `DependenceIndicator.undeclared` counts the silent members; the explanation says *no panel member declares a …*, *only 1 of N … declares*, *varies across the K that declare one*, and appends *M of N do not declare one*. Decision record: `docs/decisions/2026-09-23_diversity-is-a-mean-over-five-attributes-and-unknown-scores-zero.md` (why a mean, not the heaviest overlap). Book: `recruitment.md` *What the panel is known to share* (the facts, the rule, a worked table, the indicator wording, the §10.4 caveat, the as-found).
- [x] **VERIFIED** — RED per shape, the four controls spliced onto `HEAD`'s `matching.rs`/`dependence.rs` (fixed files restored, `shasum -a 256 -c` OK): `FAILED. 21 passed; 4 failed` — (a1) `a_candidate_with_no_known_fact_scores_zero_diversity`: `rol_c` (no entry) and `rol_d` (all `None`) scored `1.0`; (a2) `declaring_an_unshared_fact_ranks_above_leaving_it_undeclared`: all three tied at `1.0`; (c) `the_sharer_test_compares_the_same_attribute_only`: provider `x` vs harness `x` scored `0.0`, *shares … with 100%*; (b) `an_undeclared_attribute_is_unknown_not_variation`: the silent harness read *varies across the panel*. GREEN: `cargo test -p reasonbraid-server --lib -- matching dependence` → **25 passed**; `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh profiles` → **86 passed** (the snapshot control now also asserts the stored `lineage` indicator: `undeclared = 2`, no *varies*).
- [x] **FALSIFIED** — M1 (the mean over the DECLARED attributes, i.e. silence pays again) → `FAILED. 24 passed; 1 failed` at (a2); M2 (a value matched against any of the other's attributes) → `FAILED. 24 passed; 1 failed` at (c). Each restored, `shasum -a 256 -c` OK.
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — the existing `matching`/`dependence` units pass unedited (`the_diversity_feature_rewards_the_attribute_variation` still sees C above A and *50%*); the 85 other `profiles` controls unedited; strict clippy on `reasonbraid-server`; `cargo fmt --check`; `make book`; the doctrine gate at commit.
- ⚠️ **Honest limits:** the snapshot control's new `lineage` arm was not itself run RED (it reads a field the old code did not emit, so it is RED by construction; the unit control (b) is the observed RED for that shape). `lineage` is declared by nothing and `owner` is uniform at a single-tenant close, so today only provider, model family and harness can separate joiners. Census for *declared by nothing*: `git grep -n "MemberFacts {" -- crates` → one production constructor, `crates/reasonbraid-server/src/api.rs:6649` (the close), which writes `lineage: None` at `:6654`; the other six hits are test fixtures in `matching.rs`/`dependence.rs`.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.1.4 — The initiator's ranking weights are unbounded

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0443`. Opened by DOC-0149.
- 🔴 As found: `RankingPreferences`' six weights are unvalidated `f64` (`POST /v1/directory/match`), so a negative diversity weight ranks the most correlated candidates first and weights near `f64::MAX` overflow the total to `inf`, which the sort's `unwrap_or(Equal)` treats as a tie.
- Owns: each weight finite and in `[0, 1]` (ordinal ranking — every ratio stays expressible), refused `400` naming the weight; RED first; book (the match section documents the preferences it never has).
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — `RankingPreferences` was a plain serde struct of six `f64`s with no invariant, deserialized straight into the ranker; nothing between the wire and `rank` stated what a weight may be, and both sorts compared totals with `partial_cmp(..).unwrap_or(Equal)`, so an infinite or NaN total silently became a tie.
- [x] **ADDRESSED** — `RankingPreferences::validate` refuses the first weight (declaration order) outside `[0, 1]` — NaN and the infinities included — as `the ranking weight `X` must be a finite number from 0 to 1`; `directory_match` calls it after the principal resolves and before the directory is read, answering `400 invalid_command`. `matching::by_rank` (`total_cmp`, ties by role id) replaces the two duplicated `partial_cmp` sorts (the ranker's and the match surface's merge), so the order is total whatever the totals are. Book: `profiles.md` *Matching the directory* (the route, the request, the two stages, the six weights and their features, defaults, the `diversity`-scores-0-here caveat) and *The weights are bounded*; *A claim's expiry* now links it.
- [x] **VERIFIED** — RED: `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh profiles` with the control and without the repair → `FAILED. 85 passed; 1 failed` — `diversity = -1.0` answered `200 {"candidates":[],"scope":"full"}`. GREEN: unit `cargo test -p reasonbraid-server --lib matching` → **16 passed** (+ `a_weight_outside_the_unit_interval_is_refused_by_name`: both ends admitted; −1, −`MIN_POSITIVE`, 1+`EPSILON`, `MAX`, NaN, ∞ refused by name; the first stray named when two stray); `profiles` → **86 passed, 0 failed** (+ `the_ranking_weights_are_bounded_and_a_stray_one_is_named`: three shapes on three weights `400` naming each, all-0 and all-1 `200`).
- [x] **FALSIFIED** — two mutants of the bound, each restored and `shasum -a 256 -c` OK: M1 (lower bound dropped) and M2 (upper bound and NaN dropped) → `FAILED. 15 passed; 1 failed` each. The pre-repair behaviour (no check) is the RED above.
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — the 85 existing `profiles` controls and 15 existing `matching` units pass unedited; strict clippy on `reasonbraid-server` (`--all-targets -D warnings`); `cargo fmt --check`; `make book`; the doctrine gate at commit.
- ⚠️ **Honest limits:** JSON cannot carry NaN or ∞ and `serde_json` refuses an out-of-range literal, so the finiteness arm is reachable only from Rust callers and is exercised by the unit control, not over HTTP. The close's `rank_with_dependence` uses the defaults and never saw a caller's weights, so it had no exposure.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0443`.

Every item of the goal line is met or discharged.
- ⛔ **SEQUENCING LOCK** (`docs/decisions/2026-09-22_three-storm-controls-were-deferred-behind-triggers-that-have-fired.md`): the once-per-tenant key below was the ONLY bound on auto-initiation. ✅ **The lock's first half is met** — `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.7.2.1.5.3.1` (REPAIR-0415) bounds DECLARED chains by depth and cycle. ⚠️ Undeclared chains are bounded by nothing but this key until the rate gate (`.11.4.7.2.1.5.3.2`) lands, so the repeat-initiation repair should land WITH that gate. ✅ **Both halves met** — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0417` landed the `initiator` quota (`.11.4.7.2.1.5.3.2.1`) and the per-initiation key (clause 1 below) in ONE commit.
- Sources / owned surfaces: `calls, offers, panels, auto-thread endpoints`.
- Goal and acceptance: Bind call/thread/tenant/actor and grants, make panel/close/offer transitions atomic, enforce post-filter minimums and concurrent caps, and make repeated legitimate auto initiation possible with full budget/topics/classification semantics.
- 🔴 **MATCHED FINDINGS annotated here by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.9.1.3.2`** (2026-09-15, while reading `R-76-77-3`'s handler; not introduced by it). Both are inside `create_thread_auto`, and the first is what makes the record's coverage clause a live defect rather than a test gap.
  1. ✅ **REPAIRED by `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0417`** (with `.11.4.7.2.1.5.3.2.1`): `AutoCreateRequest.idempotency_key`, required and non-empty, and the row key is `auto_{role}_{key}`; the control makes two initiations under two keys, replays the first key, and observed RED under the old key. As found: **A role can auto-initiate exactly ONCE per tenant, for ever.** The key is `let key = format!("auto_{}_{}", role, tenant_id)` — a function of the role and the tenant ALONE, with no subject, objective, nonce or instant in it — while `migrations/0001_atomic_transaction.sql:39` makes `idempotency` `PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, idempotency_key)`. So the second auto-initiation REPLAYS the first thread when the body matches and answers `idempotency_mismatch` when it does not. This leaf's goal line already says "make repeated legitimate auto initiation possible"; the cause is recorded here so the repair does not have to rediscover it, and `R-76-77-3` clause 1 carries the measurement that the existing test cannot reach the case (one success, then only policy refusals).
  2. ✅ **REPAIRED by `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0421`** (`.11.4.7.2.1.5.3.2.3.2`): the handler reads spend, topics and depth from the grant the admitting authorization record names; the control seeds an expired `500` beside a live `50` and a budget of 60 is refused. As found: ⛔ **The spend gate is a SIXTH spelling of the grant-liveness question `.9.3.1` unified, and it is the permissive one.** Before authorization runs, the handler asks `SELECT max((spend_limits->>'amount')::float) FROM authority_grants WHERE subject_id = $1 AND status = 'active' AND actions @> '["thread_create_auto"]'::jsonb` — no validity window and no boundary join, where `authority::grant_is_live` requires `status = 'active' AND valid_from <= now() AND expires_at > now()` and `.3.5.2` repaired the metrics surface for exactly the missing boundary. So an EXPIRED or not-yet-started auto grant, or one under a revoked boundary, still raises today's ceiling — and `max()` takes the most generous of them, while `run_thread_command` then authorizes on a different, live grant whose own spend limit is never compared with the request. ⚠️ `grant_exceeds_boundary` compares the grant's limits to the BOUNDARY's, not the request's budget to the grant's, so nothing downstream re-checks it. ⛔ Reproduce before repairing, as `.3.5.2` did: this is a source reading with the omission read directly, not a runtime reproduction.
- ⭐ **ATTACHED CLAUSE — a routed-record finding this leaf's goal line does NOT make visible** (`R-76-77-2` clause 3, tranche 2c; `docs/tasks/artifacts/signoff_review/RECONCILIATION.md`). ✅ **DISCHARGED by `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0422`** (`.11.4.7.2.1.5.3.2.3.3`): `open_recruitment_call` loads the thread's projection tenant-bound and answers `404 scope_hidden` for an absent or foreign id; three fixtures (the two below and the panel snapshot) now seed real threads and keep every assertion. As found: **Two fixtures ENCODE the missing bind, so the cheap way to make them pass is to weaken them.** `profiles.rs::the_open_call_storm_controls_hold_at_the_dev_scale` posts `/v1/calls` with the literal `thr_00000000-0000-7000-8000-000000000001` and asserts 200 four times; `the_open_call_advertises_to_the_subscribers` does the same with `…0002`. Both go green today only because `open_recruitment_call` checks neither the thread's existence nor its tenancy and `migrations/0020_recruitment_calls.sql:13` declares `thread_id TEXT NOT NULL` with no foreign key. ⛔ When this leaf adds the bind, both turn red, and the repair is to SEED REAL THREADS — never to relax the assertion or drop the test. `.5.1`'s goal line carries a fixture clause ("use equally qualified foreign fixtures"); this leaf's reaches the handler only, which is why the obligation is written here rather than assumed.
- Verification: in the children — `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.2.5` (the minimum on the selected panel, RED first with a lapsed attestation) and `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.2.4` (four race controls RED first, one lock mutation), each with its own boxes; the bind items were verified by the repairs that met them (REPAIR-0185, 0417, 0421, 0422).

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.2.4 — No recruitment-call transition is one transaction

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0429`. Opened by DOC-0142; the mechanism and the late-join answer are `docs/decisions/2026-09-23_each-call-transition-is-one-transaction-and-a-late-join-is-refused.md`.
- 🔴 As found — Open: two fan-out counts, then the call's INSERT, then one INSERT per offered subscriber — all on the pool; the cap is read-then-write and a crash mid-way leaves a call with partial offers. Respond: a stale `call()` read, then the upsert. Close: reads, then `snapshot_panel`'s panel INSERT and status UPDATE as two statements — two concurrent closes both read `open` and the second raises `recruitment_panels`' primary key (`500`, the shape `docs/knowledge/a-raised-constraint-cannot-be-a-recorded-refusal.md` forbids), and a join can land between the close's reads and its UPDATE.
- Owns: each transition in one transaction — open with the caps decided under a per-tenant serialization (the mechanism chosen with its reason) and the offers written with the call; close with the call row locked `FOR UPDATE`, the status re-checked inside, the panel and status written together, a second close answering `409`; respond with the call row locked `FOR SHARE` beside the upsert. RED first with `enrollment_transaction.rs`'s race harness (`hold_issuance` / `waiter`); the late-join answer decided after it is reproduced; book (`recruitment.md`).
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — every transition was several statements on the pool (`crates/reasonbraid-server/src/api.rs`, `crates/reasonbraid-server/src/recruitment.rs`): the open counted the two caps, inserted the call, then one offer per subscriber — the caps read-then-write over a SET no row stands for; the respond read `call()` and upserted against that stale row; the close read, then `snapshot_panel` wrote the panel INSERT and the status UPDATE as two statements. Measured RED on the unrepaired code by four controls (FALSIFIED below): two opens at the cap both `200` (5 open under a cap of 4); a join during a close `200`, on the record and off the panel; two closes → one `200`, one `500` (`duplicate key value violates unique constraint "recruitment_panels_pkey"`); a faulted offer write → `500` with the call row left behind (`count = 1`).
- [x] **ADDRESSED** — open: `recruitment::serialize_opens` (a transaction-scoped advisory lock, `pg_advisory_xact_lock(class, hashtext(tenant_id))` — the caps are counts over a set, so no row lock can guard them; the `tenants` row and the authority guard rejected in the record), both caps counted under it, `open_call` and `offer_to_subscribers` (one `INSERT … SELECT`) on the same transaction, a refusal rolled back before `refuse_storm` records it on its own commit; respond: `call_locked(…, CallLock::Shared)` from the read to `record_response`, one transaction; close: `call_locked(…, CallLock::Exclusive)` from the read through `snapshot_panel`, one transaction — a second close reads `closed` and answers `409`. `serialize_opens`, `open_calls_by`, `open_call`, `offer_to_subscribers`, `record_response`, `call_locked` and `snapshot_panel` take `&mut PgConnection`, so a transition cannot run them on the pool by accident; `call` and `responses` stay executor-generic for the inspection. ⚖️ A join that lost the race to a close is REFUSED (`409`, *the call is closed*), not recorded as late — the record says why. Book: `docs/book/src/recruitment.md` (*Each transition is one transaction*, and notes under the open, answer and close sections).
- [x] **VERIFIED** — `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh profiles` → **78 passed, 0 failed** (74 + `two_concurrent_closes_yield_one_panel_and_one_refusal`, `a_join_that_races_a_close_waits_and_is_refused`, `two_concurrent_opens_at_the_cap_admit_exactly_one`, `a_failed_offer_write_leaves_no_call_behind`). Each race is held deterministically with the trigger-and-advisory-lock shape `crates/reasonbraid-server/tests/enrollment_transaction.rs` introduced (`hold_inserts` / `wait_for_waiters`, reading `pg_stat_activity` for backends in `Lock` wait): every INSERT into the table under test waits behind a holder, so both requests are past their reads before either can write, and the control asserts that both are blocked before it releases. `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh mcp_write mcp invitations` → mcp_write 7, mcp 6 + 1 (the seam that rides `respond_to_call_core`), invitations 7 — **0 failed** (`regress rc=0`).
- [x] **FALSIFIED** — twice. RED FIRST, against the unrepaired transitions (`git stash push -- crates/reasonbraid-server/src/api.rs crates/reasonbraid-server/src/recruitment.rs`; the controls kept): `FAILED. 74 passed; 4 failed`, each on its own defect — `left: 200 right: 429` (both opens landed), `left: 200 right: 409` (the late join recorded), `[(200, …panel…), (500, dependency_unavailable)]` (the raised primary key), `left: 1 right: 0` (the call row left behind); `git stash pop` → `78 passed`. MUTATION M1 — the close's lock weakened to `CallLock::Shared`: the two closes deadlock (`deadlock detected`, a `500`) and the late join lands `200` — `FAILED. 76 passed; 2 failed`; reversed and `shasum -a 256 -c` OK on both files. The exclusive lock is load-bearing, not ceremony.
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — the existing call fixtures (the artifact, the storm controls, the advertisement, the panel snapshot, the minimum) pass unedited; the MCP `join_call` seam is unchanged (`respond_to_call_core` keeps its signature and owns its transaction); the wire shapes of open, respond and close are unchanged except that a second concurrent close is `409` where it was `500`; strict clippy clean on core and server (`-D warnings`); `cargo fmt`; `make book`; `make gate` — which caught three things, each done rather than worked around: the live-status ledger rotated to its derived target (`scripts/rotate_changelog.py --ledger live-status --apply`, 26 records retired, 30,389 bytes of headroom); the knowledge map regenerated; and `SHARED-REGISTRY-WRITES`' baseline refreshed with its adjudication — the offers INSERT moved from `api.rs` into `recruitment.rs`, so the module-reach over-approximation stopped attributing `recruitment_offers` (a table with no tenant column) to every route that reaches the handler module: module-reach rows 30 → 15, eleven rows narrowed and fifteen routes left the over-approximated population, while the PUBLISHED figures are unchanged — walk rows 25 → 25, identity-only 9 → 9 (`25 site-global writers (9 on identity alone)`), `--self-test` 45/45. A false attribution removed, not a reach lost.
- ⚠️ **Honest limits, owned:** the advisory lock serializes a tenant's opens — at the dev caps (8 per tenant, 4 per initiator) that is the intended shape, and a busier profile revisits it with the caps. The respond's tenant read (`reader_tenant`) and the close's administrator check run on the pool: neither touches the call's tables, so neither is inside the race. The deadlock under M1 is what PostgreSQL does with two shared holders that both upgrade; it is reported as observed, not claimed as the only failure shape.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0429`.

- Goal and acceptance: Complete remote recruitment under explicit local grants, bind receipts to actual digest references, transact identity/profile/quota/receipt import together, isolate replay and provenance, and prove revocation races cannot widen visibility or effects.
- ⭐ **ATTACHED CLAUSES — routed-record findings this leaf's goal line does NOT make visible** (`R-43-4` clauses 3 and 4, tranche 4b; `docs/tasks/artifacts/signoff_review/RECONCILIATION.md`). ⚠️ The goal line reaches "revocation races"; neither clause below is about a revocation, and an agreement has no lifecycle of its own for either to hang from.
  1. **A terms change is not re-consented by the counterparty.** Re-proposing a direction with DIFFERENT terms resets the caller's own row to `proposed` and clears its acceptance, while the other side's `accepted` row stands unchanged and participates in the new terms at the next pairing. ⚠️ Bounded by clause 2 below: `has_effective_directory_agreement` and `has_effective_recruitment_agreement` both require BOTH rows `accepted` AND both booleans true, so each side's row remains its own declaration and a re-proposal cannot mint a capability the counterparty never declared. What is missing is any record that the counterparty's declaration was given against THESE terms.
  2. **An agreement carries no version, no expiry and no signature.** `migrations/0048_federation_agreements.sql` declares `agreement_id`, the two tenant ids, `directory_visibility`, `recruitment`, `status`, `proposed_at` and `accepted_at` — and nothing else. #### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.3.2 — A card replay is decided by its label, and the imported role's origin is stored nowhere

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0431`. Opened by DOC-0143 (goal item 4).

The origin role id was stored nowhere: `grep -rn origin_role_id crates/reasonbraid-server/src migrations` → the card struct and the response only.
- Owns: a provenance record written in the import's transaction — importing tenant, local role, origin tenant, origin role, card digest, the admission — unique per origin role per importing tenant, refused as a VALUE (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING`), never a raised constraint; a repeat of the same origin role answers a replay naming the original local role (the enrolment route's shape, `replayed: true`) and the digest on file when the card differs; the label collision stays a label collision; a read of the provenance on the profile's full class; book (`profiles.md`'s *Importing a card* and *What is not here yet*). RED: the same origin role under two labels lands two local roles today.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — nothing recorded an import's origin, so the only collision the transaction could meet was the label's (`agent_roles (tenant_id, name)`), and the only answer to a repeat was the label refusal it happened to hit. Identity by label is wrong in both directions: two different origins can share a label, and one origin can change its label between two cards.
- [x] **ADDRESSED** — `migrations/0095_card_imports.sql`: `card_imports (role_id PK → agent_roles, tenant_id, origin_tenant_id, origin_role_id, card_digest, record_id, imported_at)`, `UNIQUE (tenant_id, origin_tenant_id, origin_role_id)`. In `import_after_admission`, after the allowlist rung (a revoked agreement refuses the replay too) and before the boundary and the grant: the record is READ under the importing tenant's exclusive guard, which serializes that tenant's imports, and a row on file answers `CardImportResult::Replayed { role_id, digest_on_file }` writing nothing — the effect record `no_op`, the wire `200 {role_id, origin_*, replayed: true, digest_on_file}` (the enrolment shape). After the enrollment row the record is written `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING`; a miss there is a storage failure that rolls the import back, because the guard makes it impossible and a second refusal vocabulary would claim otherwise. `LabelTaken` is now only ever a DIFFERENT origin's card. `GET /v1/profiles/{role_id}` carries `imported_from` on the full class. #### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.3.4 — A direction never lapses

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0433`. Opened by DOC-0143 (attached clause 2's expiry).

RED: an expired direction still widens the directory read today. ⚠️ *Shown by the reads*: there is no agreement read route (DOC-0143's census), so the lifetime is on the ledger and in the book, not on a new surface.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — the schema had no lifetime column and the three effective-agreement predicates asked only `status = 'accepted'`, so nothing a proposer could declare made a direction end on its own.
- [x] **ADDRESSED** — `migrations/0097_federation_expires_at.sql` (`expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL`); `FederationAgreementRequest.expires_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>`, a past instant `400 invalid_command` before the admission; `propose_direction_in_one_transaction` writes it, and a moved lifetime is a change (the upsert's `WHERE` gains `expires_at IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.expires_at`) that resets the row to `proposed` like any other — ⚖️ it does NOT enter `terms_digest`, because a lifetime is not a term: what is permitted is unchanged by when it ends, and the counterparty's `accepted_against` stays valid across an extension. Every predicate and the acceptance's counterparty read add `AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now())`. Book: `docs/book/src/authority.md` (the direction section's body description).
- 🔎 **FOUND BY THIS LEAF'S CONTROL — a latent `500`, fixed here:** `migrations/0098_cross_domain_receipts_are_events.sql`. B's second acceptance was against A's UNCHANGED terms (a lifetime is not a term), so its receipt named the same `remote_ref` as its first, and `cross_domain_receipts`' `UNIQUE (tenant_id, remote_tenant_id, kind, remote_ref)` (0049) RAISED into `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "cross_domain_receipts_tenant_id_remote_tenant_id_kind_remot_key"` → `500` inside the transaction carrying the admission and the effect record — the forbidden shape. ⛔ Latent since the verbs went on one transaction (`REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0125`) and reachable from the wire the whole time: before 0096 the `remote_ref` was the counterparty's TENANT ID, identical for every acceptance in a direction, so ANY second acceptance after a re-proposal cycle raised it; the record control never saw it because its *accept again* is the `409 AlreadyAccepted` path, which writes nothing. A receipt is a record of one acceptance, two acceptances are two receipts; the card-import side lost nothing (a repeat of the same origin is a replay before any receipt, `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0431`). The constraint is dropped and the control asserts two receipts.
- [x] **VERIFIED** — `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh federation cards migration_upgrade` → federation **6** (5 + `an_expired_direction_widens_nothing_and_cannot_be_accepted_against`), cards 8 (the `_in_tx` predicate), migration_upgrade 8 — **22 passed, 0 failed**. And the first GREEN run failed on the latent receipt key (`left: 500 right: 200` at the second acceptance) before 0098 existed — the finding above, observed rather than reasoned.
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — every direction and card control passes unedited (the field is optional and absent from every existing fixture); the upgrade control's seed was hardened: *the pre-upgrade schema* is whatever the prefix reaches, so once 0096 sits inside the prefix the seed carries the server's digest and the control SAYS it measures survival rather than the backfill (`migration_upgrade: 0096 is inside the prefix …` in its output) instead of silently weakening; strict clippy clean on core and server (`-D warnings`); `cargo fmt`; `make book`; `make gate`.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.3.6 — A revoked recruitment direction does not stop work already queued for an origin-bound identity

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0454`. Opened by DOC-0151.
- 🔴 As found (source reading at `8f383c5`; reproduced RED first by this leaf): after either side revokes the recruitment direction, every NEW act refuses (the respond, the directory, the dispatch `409`, the result fold), but `node_channel::replay` still OFFERS the origin node the importing tenant's already-queued rows — the payload carries the thread's subject and objective — and a row it already holds still DISPATCHES, because its epoch for the importing tenant never moves (`revoke_direction_in_one_transaction` bumps no epoch and touches no inbox row).
- Owns: (1) the replay offers a row of another tenant than the node's own only while the role its work item names still resolves to this node (`role_execution`); (2) the handshake/poll's `revocation_epochs` becomes the COMPLETE set of tenants the node may act for NOW — its own, and each tenant with an identity whose binding resolves to it — and the node adopts it wholesale (`set_revocation_epochs` replaces the table), so a held command of a tenant that left the set has no reference and is refused at the dispatch gate; RED first for each (offered after revocation; dispatched after revocation); book (`profiles.md`, `node-channel.md`).
- ⚠️ This changes `the_handshake_and_poll_carry_every_held_tenants_epoch`'s expectation (REPAIR-0449 sent every tenant IN THE INBOX; the set becomes every tenant the node is ENTITLED to serve) — the control is updated with the reason, not relaxed.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — the binding was resolved at each NEW act's instant (REPAIR-0446…0451) but the two mechanisms that carry work ALREADY queued — the replay's tail and the node's epoch reference — were keyed on the inbox row and the node's journal, neither of which learns that the binding ended: the tail had no binding predicate, and REPAIR-0449's map listed every tenant with a row in the inbox, which the node merged into what it already held.
- [x] **ADDRESSED** — `node_channel::replay`'s tail offers a row of another tenant than the node's own only while `role_execution` resolves the row's work-item `agent_role` to this node. `epochs_and_server_time` returns the node's COMPLETE entitled set — its own tenant and each tenant with an identity whose `role_execution.node_id` is this node — and the node's `Journal::set_revocation_epochs` REPLACES `tenant_epochs` in one transaction (`set_revocation_epoch_for` is a one-entry set). A departed tenant's held command therefore has no reference and is refused `failed_before_dispatch` naming the tenant. Book: `profiles.md` *Where an imported identity runs* (ending the agreement stops work already on its way), `node-channel.md` *Cached decisions* (the entitled set, adopted wholesale; the replay's rule).
- [x] **VERIFIED** — RED: `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh profiles` with the origin control grown on the `DOC-0151` code → `test result: FAILED. 88 passed; 1 failed` — after the revocation the origin node's poll offered the importing tenant's `work_…` row. GREEN: node crate green (+ `a_tenant_left_out_of_the_map_loses_its_reference`: A served then dropped → no reference → A's held command `failed_before_dispatch`); `profiles` **89** (the control now also: while bound the origin handshake names BOTH tenants; after the revocation the poll offers no importing-tenant row though one is queued, and its map no longer names the importing tenant); `node_channel` **47** (`the_handshake_and_poll_carry_the_epochs_of_the_tenants_the_node_serves`: an unbound tenant's inbox row earns it no entry and is not offered; a bump moves the served tenant's entry; the shared tenant restored), `node_inbox` 11, `node_work` 12, `node_result_ordering` 6, `node_replacement` 2, `node_enrollment` 21, `invitations` 7, `quarantine` 1, `command_api` 42, `cli_end_to_end` 5.

Each restored, `shasum -a 256 -c` OK.

- Status: `done` — ✅ closed by `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0453` with its last child `.5.3.5.3`; `.5.3.5.1` (REPAIR-0434/0435/0437) and `.5.3.5.2` (REPAIR-0436) closed before. - ❌ ADR-026 says the cross-tenant recruitment accepts remote participants only under the agreement's scope; the call machinery has no cross-tenant path at all — offers are bound to the call's tenant (`crates/reasonbraid-server/src/recruitment.rs`, `offer_to_subscribers`), a respondent enrolled elsewhere is refused (`respond_to_call_core`), and the match query clamps `network` to the reader's class (`crates/reasonbraid-server/src/api.rs:6676`). - 🔴 **MEASURED by the census, and it changed the question:** `PHASE-8.1.2` deferred the cross-tenant call widening behind *the call machinery's remote-panel surface* — the feature itself. An open call reaches NO role in ANY tenant: offers are rows and nothing delivers them (`grep -rn "recruitment_offers" crates/reasonbraid-server/src/node_channel.rs crates/reasonbraid-node/src --include=*.rs` → 0; `grep -rn "Advertisement\|\"advertisement\"" crates/reasonbraid-server/src crates/reasonbraid-core/src crates/reasonbraid-node/src --include=*.rs` → 0), so the remote form's first half has no intra-tenant half to extend. An imported role has no node (`respondent_candidate` reads `node_presence`), so even after the import its turns run nowhere. 💡 **WAITING ON THE DIRECTOR:** whose machine runs an imported identity's turns — the origin tenant's node, executing what the importing tenant authorized, or a node the importing tenant enrols (the identity crosses, the machine does not). ROADMAP:549 and :596 leave it open inside one deployment.
- Owns: the three children, in order — `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.3.5.1` the advertisement delivery (intra-tenant first, then federated under the DIRECTORY agreement, classified per candidate tenant), `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.3.5.2` the foreign join request resolved by the import, `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.3.5.3` the imported identity's execution (waits on the director and on DOC-0139's binding lane). ⛔ Federation between independent deployments stays post-v1 (ROADMAP:596).
- Verification: in the children.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-DOC-0144` (the census); the children's own.

- Status: `done` — the DURABLE half by `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0434` (the read), the prompt half by `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0437` (`SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.3.5.1.1`), the federated half by `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0435` (`SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.3.5.1.2`). Opened by DOC-0144.

- Owns: the intra-tenant half first — a read by which a role lists the calls offered to it (THIS commit), and an online node told promptly that an offer waits (`SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.3.5.1.1`); then the federated half (`SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.3.5.1.2`) — a `network`-scope call's offers reach subscribers in tenants holding the EFFECTIVE directory agreement, carrying no more than the network view discloses (the call id, the expression, the window; the thread hidden), classified per candidate tenant the way `directory_presence` does and the match surface does not (`SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.1`); book (`recruitment.md`, `node-channel.md`). ⚖️ *An offer as durable inbox work* was the first design and is NOT what shipped: `node_inbox` is a ledger of ADMITTED work commands (`authz_ref`, `policy_digest`, `revocation_epoch`, the node's journal dedupe, the offline backlog cap, the in-flight count), and an offer is none of those — it has no admission of its own, no thread work, and a node must not run it. ###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.3.5.1.1 — An online node is not told that an offer waits

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0437`. Opened by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.3.5.1` (REPAIR-0434), which shipped the durable half and measured why the offer is not inbox work.
- 🔴 As found: a role learned of an offer only by asking `GET /v1/calls/offered`; §10.5 and ROADMAP:296 want an online eligible node to receive the advertisement promptly. `node_inbox` is a ledger of admitted work commands and an offer is not one (no admission, no thread work, nothing to run), so the prompt half is a NOTIFICATION.
- ⚖️ **The design census, answered in the leaf rather than a record because each answer is one sentence:** (1) *how a node presents its role* — it does not have to: the handshake already authenticates the node, and under the dev rule the node id IS the role id (DOC-0139), so the server counts the role's offers by the node id it just proved, and a node that is no role's node counts zero; the node never calls the control API as a principal, and this slice keeps it that way (the registry lane retires the collapse later). (2) *what the handshake carries* — one integer, `offers_pending`: open calls inside their join window offered to the role and unanswered by it. (3) *what the node does* — the reference node says so on its log and nothing more; the offers are read as the role, and what a node does with them beyond saying so is the adapter's or the operator's.
- Owns: the smallest slice — the handshake response names the count of open offers and the node logs it. RED: a handshake after an open carries nothing about the offer.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — the handshake carried the node's work (the replay), its reconciliation (directives, known events), its lease and its clocks, and nothing about the calls that wanted the role — because until REPAIR-0434 no offer had a consumer at all, and a count of nothing anyone could read had no reason to exist.
- [x] **ADDRESSED** — `HandshakeResponse.offers_pending: i64` on both sides of the mirrored wire (`crates/reasonbraid-server/src/node_channel.rs`, `crates/reasonbraid-node/src/channel.rs`, the node's `#[serde(default)]` so a newer node reads an older server as zero; the reverse is refused by `deny_unknown_fields`, the contract's stance under one channel version, and the two ship together); `NodeChannelState::offers_pending(node_id)` — `recruitment_offers ⋈ recruitment_calls` for the node id, `status = 'open'`, inside the window, `NOT EXISTS` a response by it — wired into the handshake beside the epoch and the clock; the node's reconcile loop (`crates/reasonbraid-node/src/node.rs`, step 3.7) prints *N open recruitment offer(s) await this node's role — GET /v1/calls/offered lists them* when positive. Book: `docs/book/src/node-channel.md` (the response field list), `docs/book/src/recruitment.md` (the offered section names the prompt half).
- [x] **VERIFIED** — `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh node_channel` → **45 passed, 0 failed** (44 + `an_online_node_is_told_how_many_offers_await_its_role`): a seeded node that is a role, one open in-window offer → the state method counts 1 and the certificate-proofed handshake through the real node client carries `offers_pending: 1`; the role answers, a closed call and a lapsed call are offered too → the next handshake carries 0.
- [x] **FALSIFIED** — MUTATION M1, the count's `NOT EXISTS` (the answered-offer exclusion) replaced by a tautology: `assertion left == right failed: an answered, a closed and a lapsed offer are not pending — left: 1 right: 0` — `FAILED. 44 passed; 1 failed`; reversed, `shasum -a 256 -c` OK, `45 passed`. A RED-first run was not possible for a field the typed client cannot read until it exists — the control does not compile against the old wire — so the falsification is by mutation of the count, which is the whole of the logic.
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — every node-channel control passes unedited, including `handshake_rejects_version_mismatch_and_unknown_fields` (the request contract is untouched; the response gained a field the node crate mirrors); the node's reconcile loop is unchanged but for one print; strict clippy clean on core, server and node (`-D warnings`); `cargo fmt`; `make book`; `make gate`.
- ⚠️ **Honest limits, owned:** the count is computed on the pool beside the lease and the clock, not under a lock — a handshake racing an open may read one fewer, and the next handshake reads it; the node does nothing with the count but say so, and the channel version was not bumped for a response-side addition the two crates ship together.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0437`.

ADR-026: *the remote recruitment is the agreement-scoped opt-in*.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — the offer statement had one arm, the tenant's, and the scope was read only as a matching predicate over a candidate's visible claims — never as an audience. Nothing joined the offers to the federation agreements, so the directory opt-in widened reads and never advertisements.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.3.5.2 — A foreign response is a recorded join request

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0436`; the design is `REASONBRAID-DOC-0145` (`docs/decisions/2026-09-23_a-federated-join-is-a-request-carrying-the-roles-own-card.md`), shipped with it. Opened by DOC-0144. After `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.3.5.1`.
- ❌ As found: a federated subscriber's `join` was refused (`respond_to_call_core`: *only a principal enrolled in the call's tenant responds to it*), correctly under ADR-026 — and nothing recorded that it wanted in.
- Owns: a federated subscriber's response recorded on the call as a join REQUEST naming the origin role and carrying the card it exported, visible to the call's initiator and administrator, resolved by the existing import; no local effect until the import; RED first: the foreign response is `403` and leaves no trace. ⚠️ Two things the opening line promised are NOT here, each with its reason in DOC-0145: *the provenance record names the call it was requested for* waits on `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.3.5.3` (it matters only once the imported role can act); *receipts on both sides* — the import already writes the importing side's receipt (REPAIR-0431's provenance + the 0049 receipt), and the origin side has no local effect to receipt until its role's turns run somewhere.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — the respond had one answer for every principal outside the call's tenant, because until REPAIR-0435 no such principal could have been offered the call; once it could, the refusal was still right (no local grant) but silent — the role's wish to join, and the card the call's tenant would need to act on it, had no place to land.
- [x] **ADDRESSED** — `respond_to_call_core` (`crates/reasonbraid-server/src/api.rs`): a foreign principal's response passes three gates — a `join` (anything else: the old words), an offer on file for this role (else: the old words, so a call's existence is not learned by probing), the EFFECTIVE recruitment agreement between the two tenants (`has_effective_recruitment_agreement_in_tx`; else `403` naming the missing agreement) — then the common status, deadline and eligibility checks, then `recruitment::record_join_request` stores `response_kind = 'join_request'` with `{origin_tenant_id, card, digest}` where the card is minted by `mint_card`, the ONE path the export also uses (`get_profile_card` now calls it); the wire answers `200 {"response": "join_request"}`. The close counts `join` and never seats it; the inspection lists it. Book: `docs/book/src/recruitment.md` (*Answering a call*).
- [x] **VERIFIED** — `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh profiles` → **81 passed, 0 failed** (80 + `a_federated_subscribers_join_is_a_recorded_request`): with the directory agreement only, B's offered role's `join` is `403 … no effective recruitment agreement`; with the recruitment agreement too, `200 join_request`; the initiator's inspection lists it with `origin_tenant_id`, the card naming B's role and a `sha256:` digest; a foreign `decline` and an un-offered foreign role hear the old words; the close seats the local joiner only; the administrator imports the request's card and the provenance names B's role.
- [x] **FALSIFIED** — RED FIRST against the unrepaired respond (`git stash push -- crates/reasonbraid-server/src/api.rs crates/reasonbraid-server/src/recruitment.rs`; the control and the book kept): `FAILED. 80 passed; 1 failed` at the control's first assertion on the refusal's wording (`crates/reasonbraid-server/tests/profiles.rs:3270`) — the old sentence where the missing agreement should be named; popped, `shasum -a 256 -c` OK on both, `81 passed`. 🔎 The GREEN run then failed twice on the FIXTURE, and both were the matching rule working: a role that hides its capability from the network is offered (by interests) and found ineligible (by claims) for a network-scope call — *capability code_review is not visible at the requested scope* — first B's role, then A's own; each now publishes its capability at network scope and is re-attested. The rule is `matching.rs`'s and is asserted by its unit test; it is recorded here because the control measured it rather than assuming it.
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — every call control passes unedited; the export's wire is unchanged (the same card from the same path); a local response's path is untouched (the foreign branch is entered only when the respondent's tenant differs from the call's); strict clippy clean on core and server (`-D warnings`); `cargo fmt`; `make book`; `make gate`.
- ⚠️ **Honest limits, owned:** the request's card is the role's profile in full, stored in the call's tenant — the role's own export, attached by the role's own act, under the operators' recruitment agreement; a second request overwrites the first (every response does). A request does not expire with the call's window on its own; the inspection of a closed call still shows it, which is the record the initiator wants.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.3.5.3 — An imported identity's turns run nowhere

- Status: `done` — ✅ closed by `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0453` (`.3.3`, the last child): the `local` binding proven (REPAIR-0441), the `origin` binding built end to end (`.3.1` REPAIR-0446/0447/0450/0451, `.3.2` REPAIR-0449, `.3.3` REPAIR-0453). Was `active` — decided under the director's delegation of 2026-09-23 (`REASONBRAID-DOC-0148`, `docs/decisions/2026-09-23_an-imported-identity-runs-on-a-bound-machine-local-now-origin-designed.md`, shipped with `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0441`): BOTH bindings. The `local` binding is proven by REPAIR-0441 with no server change; the `origin` binding is the three children below, in order. Opened by DOC-0144.
- ❌ As found: the import landed an identity, a grant, a quota and a profile — and no node: `respondent_candidate` (`crates/reasonbraid-server/src/api.rs`) reads `node_presence` for the respondent, and an imported role had no presence row, no incarnation and no machine in the importing tenant.
- ⚖️ **Why both:** §20.10 names *portable agent cards* (a card is portable because a compatible runtime elsewhere runs under it — `local`) and *remote recruitment* (the agent is invoked where it lives, under the local mandate — `origin`); each keeps ADR-026's kill line, since the local grant bounds the action either way and nothing crosses but a description or a delivery.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — an imported identity had no machine because nothing bound one: the dev rule collapses node and role into one id, so a role with no node of its own name could not be resolved to any machine, and the two ways of giving it one had not been chosen between.
- [x] **ADDRESSED** — the `local` binding needs nothing built: the importing tenant enrols a node for the imported role's id (`enroll_node`, the dev rule), attests the claims it relies on with its own administrator's word, and the identity acts under the local grant. Recorded as the decision, with the `origin` binding designed: `card_imports.executes_on` and every role-to-node resolution through it (`.5.3.5.3.1`), the node's per-tenant revocation epoch (`.5.3.5.3.2`, the reason `origin` is not built here), receipts both ways (`.5.3.5.3.3`).
- [x] **VERIFIED** — `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh profiles` → **84 passed, 0 failed** (83 + `an_imported_identity_acts_once_the_importing_tenant_binds_a_node_to_it`): B's role imported into A under the recruitment agreement; a call in A offers the imported identity (its interests came with the card); its `join` is `403 … no enrolled node` — the negative arm; A enrols a node for it and attests `code_review`; the same `join` is `200` and a JOIN, not a request (its tenant is A); the close seats it; its profile's `imported_from` names B's role throughout.
- [x] **FALSIFIED** — by the control's own negative arm rather than a mutation, because no server logic was added to mutate: the identical request is refused before the node is bound and admitted after, so the binding is the fact that changes the answer. A RED-first run is not applicable to a proof of an existing path, and the leaf says so.
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — no source file changed; strict clippy clean over the new control (`-D warnings`); `cargo fmt`; `make gate`.
- ⚠️ **Honest limits, owned:** the local binding runs the importing tenant's OWN runtime under the imported card — the partner's identity and profile, not the partner's agent; the origin binding is the one that runs the partner's agent, and it waits on the node crate's per-tenant epoch. Whether one identity may hold both bindings at once is left open in the record.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0441` (the decision and the proof); the children's own.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.3.5.3.1 — The origin binding is not a ledger fact

- Status: `done` — ✅ closed by `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0451` (`.1.4`, the last child): `.1.1` the binding and `role_execution` (REPAIR-0446), `.1.2` the directory (REPAIR-0447), `.1.3` the dispatch (REPAIR-0450, after `.5.3.5.3.2`), `.1.4` the result (REPAIR-0451).
