##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.3.5 — Reconcile the R2 pack's advertised formats with what its acquisition leg accepts

- Status: `done`; both children complete — the census and decision are REPAIR-0097 and the implementation is REPAIR-0098. Opened by `.7.3.3.4.1`, which measured the first instance live rather than inferring it.
- Finding as measured: the R2 arm serves a reference whose media-type HINT is one of the five formats the pack advertises, but its acquisition leg is the R0 fetcher, whose response sniff accepts a DECLARED content type only when it is `text/html`, `application/xhtml+xml`, or `text/*`. A feed served under its own `application/atom+xml` type is therefore refused `media_type_refused` before the worker is reached. The live control asserts exactly that, against the same bytes that succeed on the sibling path served as `text/xml`.
- Census (the claim is about a SET, so it carries its enumeration, both directions): `git grep -n "R2_RESOLVER_ID" -- 'crates/**/*.rs'` returns three hits — the constant, the single dispatch arm `crates/reasonbraid-server/src/api.rs:2012`, and the `resolver_id` written into the snapshot. That arm makes exactly one acquisition call, `state.fetcher.fetch`. The declared-type acceptance arms of `sniff_kind` (`crates/reasonbraid-server/src/fetcher.rs:767`) are the three above; migration 0027 advertises `application/pdf`, `application/zip`, `application/x-tar`, `application/atom+xml`, `application/rss+xml`. None of the five is in the accepted set.
- NOT yet measured, and therefore not claimed: what an UNTYPED response of each of the five formats sniffs to from its bytes. The byte path is a separate branch of the same function and the source reads as though PDF, ZIP and tar would fail its UTF-8/control-character test while a feed would pass — but reading is not measuring, and `.7.3.3.5` owns settling it per format before any statement about the pack's real reach is published.
- Owns: the per-format census as a mechanical control; then the decision this is currently missing — either the advertised `media_types` are narrowed to what the leg can actually acquire, or the acquisition leg learns the R2 format set under an explicit, bounded rule. The second is a production content-policy change with its own hostile-content surface (`§12.4` sniffing, decompression, quarantine) and does not happen as a side effect of a test.
- Acceptance: a control that fails on the current code for every format the census proves unacquirable, and a recorded decision naming which of the two repairs was taken and why. Neither the registry row nor the sniff changes before that census exists.
- Why it matters beyond tidiness: the pack's advertised capability is what `resolvers::resolve` ranks on, so a caller is routed to a resolver that cannot acquire its document and receives an acquisition refusal rather than the explicit `resource_unresolvable_now` the `§12.2` contract reserves for "no eligible resolver". That is a wrong answer, not merely a missing feature.
- Decomposition, settled before implementation for the same reason `.7.3.3.4` was: the census and the repair need different things — the census needs no production change and must not presume its own conclusion, and the repair is a content-policy change whose shape the census decides. `.5.1` measures and records the decision; `.5.2` implements it.
- Verification / commit: `.5.1` is REPAIR-0097 (the census and the decision); `.5.2` is REPAIR-0098 (the implementation, with the bound proved by a live negative control).

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.3.5.1 — Census the acquisition leg's accept set against the R2 advertisement, and decide

- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0097. The census is mechanical and the decision is recorded.
- Owns: a mechanical control over `sniff_kind`'s accept set — every one of migration 0027's five advertised types in the declared path, both directions of the accepted set, and the untyped path's actual decision rule — plus a decision record naming which repair is taken and why.
- The census must answer a question the finding's first statement did not: the untyped path's verdict may be a property of the BYTES rather than of the format, in which case "the five formats are unacquirable" is the wrong shape of claim and the repair that follows from it would be wrong too.
- Acceptance: the control passes on unchanged production (it is a census, not a regression), enumerates the advertised list verbatim from the migration rather than from memory, and states both directions; the decision record names the rejected option and why.
- **The census DID change the finding's shape, which is why it came first.** Declared: all five advertised types are refused, and the complete accepted set is `text/html`, `application/xhtml+xml` and any `text/*` — three arms, enumerated both directions. Untyped: the verdict is a property of the BYTES, not of the format — an all-printable body is accepted whatever format it belongs to, and the same body with one non-text byte is refused. ZIP and tar cannot reach that branch at all, structurally: a ZIP local file header is `PK\x03\x04` plus nine little-endian integer fields, and a tar header is a 512-byte block with a NUL-padded 100-byte name.
- Consequence for the repair: "the five formats are unacquirable" is true but the wrong SHAPE. The leg's rule is not about formats, so no subset of the advertisement satisfies it — narrowing the registry row cannot express the truth, and the option was rejected on that measured ground rather than on preference.
- Fix: `crates/reasonbraid-server/src/fetcher.rs` gains two controls in its own test module, where `sniff_kind` lives. No production behaviour changes — the leaf's acceptance forbids it until the census exists, and the census is the deliverable.
- Verification: `cargo test -p reasonbraid-server --lib fetcher::` returns `19 passed; 0 failed`; 97 library tests, strict `-D warnings` all-target server lint, workspace format, `make gate` (15 checks) and `make book` pass. FALSIFIED by adding `application/pdf` to `sniff_kind`'s accepted arms: the advertisement control fails with `left: Some(Text), right: None` naming the type, and the untyped control is unaffected — the two measure different things. Reverted and re-run green.
- Explicit limit: the census measures the PREDICATE. It does not measure real files of each format, and does not claim a given real PDF is unacquirable untyped — that depends on the PDF. The ZIP and tar statements are structural facts of those formats applied to a measured predicate, and are labelled as such.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0097 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.3.5.1): census the acquisition leg's accept set and decide`. Decision `docs/decisions/2026-09-12_r2-acquisition-accept-set.md`; promotion: promoted → that record, three indexed answers.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.3.5.2 — Implement the repair the census chose

- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0098. Opened with `.5.1` so the sequence was visible, and started only once the census had closed.
- Owns, now settled by `.5.1`'s decision (`docs/decisions/2026-09-12_r2-acquisition-accept-set.md`): the acquisition leg admits the RANKED resolver's own advertised `media_types`, read at resolution time. Narrowing the registry row was rejected on the census, because no subset of the advertisement is accepted.
- Bounds the decision fixes, and this leaf may not exceed: no change to the destination policy, the scheme list or any SSRF control; no type admitted that the ranked pack does not advertise; no relaxation of an R0-ranked acquisition; the byte ceiling, ratio brake, redirect policy and time ceiling unchanged.
- Acceptance: the live R2 control acquires a document served under an advertised type without the test having to serve it as `text/*`; the census controls in `fetcher.rs` still pass unchanged for the R0 path; and a negative control proves a type the ranked pack does NOT advertise is still refused.
- Fix, in three pieces: `sniff_kind` takes the ranked pack's advertised types and returns the new `SniffedKind::DeclaredType` for a declared type in that set; `Fetcher::fetch_admitting` passes it, with `fetch`, `fetch_head` and `fetch_authenticated` passing an empty slice so R0's shipped accept set is byte-for-byte unchanged; and `resolvers::advertised_media_types` reads the row's own `media_types` per resolution, so a deployment that narrows a pack's advertisement narrows what it may acquire in the same act. A missing or malformed row yields an EMPTY set — a malformed advertisement must never widen a gate.
- Bounds held, with the census that shows it: `git grep -n "fetch_admitting" -- 'crates/**/*.rs'` returns exactly one call site, `api.rs:2032`, the R2 arm. The R0 arm (`api.rs:1813`), the R5 authenticated arm (`:1879`) and the R3 preflight (`:1960`) are untouched and pass no admitted set. No destination policy, scheme list, SSRF control, byte ceiling, ratio brake, redirect policy or time ceiling changed.
- `SniffedKind` gains `DeclaredType`, an additive variant. Its `as_str` is `application/octet-stream`, and that label cannot be reached through this path: the variant is only produced FROM a declared type, so the snapshot's `content_type.unwrap_or_else(sniffed)` fallback does not fire for it. The live control asserts the snapshot records `application/atom+xml`, not a sniffed stand-in.
- Verification: the profiles suite passes 33/33 live with its cluster stopped and removed, including the unchanged R0 and R1 resolver controls; 99 server library tests (19 fetcher, the two census controls among them), 16 completion controls, seven owned-input controls, strict `-D warnings` all-target server lint and workspace format pass.
- Falsification (three injections, each reverted and re-run green): replacing the registry read so the admitted set is NOT the ranked row's advertisement fails the advertised-type acquisition; passing an empty admitted set at the R2 call site fails it identically, so the repair is load-bearing; and adding ONE unadvertised type (`application/json`) to the admitted set makes the unadvertised document acquire and fails the negative control — which is the bound the decision drew, proved live rather than asserted.
- One measured fact this repair deliberately FLIPS: `.7.3.3.4.1`'s control recorded `application/atom+xml` as `media_type_refused`. That refusal is the defect, so the control now asserts the acquisition and a new `application/json` path carries the negative case. The superseded measurement stays recorded in `.7.3.3.4.1` and in the decision's census, because it is the evidence the repair rests on.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0098 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.3.5.2): admit the ranked pack's advertised media types`. promotion: declined (the durable contract is already `docs/decisions/2026-09-12_r2-acquisition-accept-set.md`, which this child implements without changing it).

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.5 — The R3 pack classifies one URL and then hands the page to a browser

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.9.1.3.3`'s classification of `R-31-32-4` clause 1 — `unowned`, and of tranche 4b's third shape: **`.7.3`'s goal line names "enforce browser redirect/subresource isolation" VERBATIM** and none of `.7.3.1`–`.7.3.4` carries it.
- The finding, source-measured at HEAD: `api.rs:2263` runs `state.fetcher.preflight(&reference.original_locator)` — the destination policy, applied ONCE, to the URL the caller named — and then calls `crate::browse::run_browse(...)`. `crates/reasonbraid-browse/src/main.rs:297` subscribes to `EventRequestWillBeSent` for the sole purpose of `log.lock().await.push(NetworkEntry { url, method })`. ⛔ There is no `Fetch.enable`, no `Network.setBlockedURLs` and no classification anywhere in the crate: the pack RECORDS every request the page makes and refuses none of them.
- ⭐ **The two-site contrast is what makes this sharp rather than suggestive.** R0's `fetcher.rs` re-hardens and re-classifies every redirect hop in its own loop; R1's `git.rs` classifies every hop since `.7.2.2`. R3 — the ONLY pack that executes the page's own JavaScript, and therefore the only one whose destinations the caller does not choose — classifies exactly one URL.
- ⚠️ **State the exposure at its real width, and the leaf must not inflate it.** The network log is a genuine disclosure and it is on the receipt, so a redirect or subresource is VISIBLE after the fact. What is absent is refusal, and the reachable targets are whatever the page names — the canonical one being a link-local metadata address, which the pre-flight would refuse if a caller typed it.
- ⛔ **A second mechanism of the same goal line is a population of ZERO and is deliberately NOT given a leaf**: "credential origin binding" for the browser pack. `grep -rn "credential\|cookie\|Authorization" crates/reasonbraid-browse/src/ crates/reasonbraid-server/src/browse.rs` returns no match — the browser carries no credential at all. Enforcing a rule over an empty population is what `.3.4.1` refused to do, and the refusal is recorded rather than left as an apparent gap. ⚠️ The CREDENTIALED pack is R5, and its defect is real and separately owned at `.7.2.6`.
- Owns: reproducing an actual redirect or subresource reaching a refused destination through the real worker, deciding where the control belongs (a CDP request interception in the worker, versus an allowlist the parent passes with the request line), and making a refused request a NAMED refusal on the receipt rather than a silent absence.
- Acceptance: a control drives a local origin whose page issues a subresource request to an address the destination policy refuses, and observes it REACHING that address before the repair; after the repair the same control observes the request refused and the refusal named on the receipt, with the network log still recording it; a redirect hop is covered by the same control or its sibling; an ALLOWED subresource is still fetched, so the repair is a classification rather than a prohibition; and the existing browser suites pass unchanged.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0210.
- 🔴 **THE CENSUS FOUND A SHARPER FINDING THAN THE LEAF WAS OPENED WITH, AND IT CHANGES WHAT THE REPAIR IS FOR.** This is not "a control is missing". `resolvers.rs::gated_advertises` publishes the R3 pack to every caller with `redirect_policy: "deny"` and `subresource_policy: "deny"` — two lines in the resolver registry a caller reads when CHOOSING a pack — and the worker enforced neither. ⭐ `docs/knowledge/a-claim-of-sameness-is-worth-its-call-graph.md`'s exact shape, in a registry rather than a module header, which is worse: a module header is read by maintainers and an advertisement is read by callers.
- 🔴 **REPRODUCED WITH A REAL BROWSER BEFORE THE REPAIR.** `a_subresource_the_pack_advertises_as_denied_is_not_dialed` fails with the ORIGIN's own counter — `assertion left == right failed: a destination the pack advertises as denied must not be dialed; left: 1, right: 0` — under the pinned Chrome for Testing runtime. The page's `<img>` named `0.0.0.0`, the browser dialed it, and the origin served it.
- ⭐ **THE INSTRUMENT IS `0.0.0.0` AGAIN, and this is its second use in this tree** (`.7.2.2` was the first). It classifies `reserved` and the kernel routes a connection to it at the LOCAL host, so the SAME origin answers the subresource and its counter reports whether the request reached a SOCKET. ⛔ A control that asserted on the network log would have recorded the browser's INTENT — the log is written from `EventRequestWillBeSent`, which fires whether or not anything is dialed.
- **The repair: enforce exactly what is advertised, at the CDP `Fetch` domain.** Every request pauses before it leaves the browser. A `Document` request whose URL is one the caller asked to navigate to CONTINUES; everything else fails with `BlockedByClient`. ⭐ That is the two advertised lines with nothing added: a non-document request IS a subresource, and a document request for a URL nobody asked for IS a redirect. ⛔ Deliberately NOT a destination-class check in the worker — that would need `ssrf` moved into a shared crate and DNS inside the interception, and it would enforce something the pack does not advertise.
- **Each refusal is NAMED on the receipt.** `refused_requests` carries the URL, the policy that refused it and Chrome's own resource type, through the worker's wire, `BrowseWorkerResponse` and `BrowserReceipt`. ⚠️ The network log still records the attempt, so the disclosure and the refusal are two separate facts. ⛔ A denial nobody can see is indistinguishable from a page that never asked.
- 🔴 **THE BEHAVIOURAL CONSEQUENCE IS STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED, and it is the part a reader should weigh.** A page that assembles its visible text from an external stylesheet or script now renders LESS text than it would in a desktop browser. That is what "deny" means, and it is the posture the pack advertises for untrusted content — the rendered evidence is what the document itself carries. ⚠️ The alternative was to change the ADVERTISEMENT to `allow`, which would have published a weaker guarantee for untrusted content than §12.3–12.4's posture; it is rejected here and the reason is recorded rather than left implicit.
- ⛔ **`.7.3`'s OTHER dropped mechanism is still a population of ZERO and still gets no leaf**: "credential origin binding" for the browser. `grep -rn "credential\|cookie\|Authorization" crates/reasonbraid-browse/src/ crates/reasonbraid-server/src/browse.rs` returns no match. The CREDENTIALED pack is R5 and its defect was repaired at `.7.2.6`.
- **The interception task is OWNED like every other**: `BrowserOwner::intercept` joins under the same deadline as `handler` and `network`, contributes to `cleanup_confirmed`, and is aborted in `Drop`. ⚠️ Added deliberately rather than spawned loose — `.7.3.1`/`.7.3.2` own exactly this class of escape, and a new task answering a browser that is already gone would have been a new instance of it.
- **FALSIFIED TWICE, with a real browser both times.** (1) Removing the subresource arm reproduces the RED. (2) The ALMOST-FIX — "deny means deny", refusing EVERY request including the navigation — fails differently and loudly: `navigation_failed`, `net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT`, and the title assertion reports `left: Null`. ⭐ So the control discriminates a policy from a blackout, which is the clause about the repair being a classification rather than a prohibition. Restoring: `cmp -s` byte-identical; positive control 1 passed.
- Verification: `python3 -B scripts/ci_browser.py -- cargo test -p reasonbraid-browse --test browser_roundtrip --locked` returns rc=0 with **18 passed / 0 failed**, every pre-existing browser control unchanged — including `the_browser_renders_the_page_and_logs_the_network`, `a_real_navigation_deadline_stops_the_browser_and_origin` and the three storage controls. `cargo test -p reasonbraid-server --lib --locked` 111 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored; `cargo test -p reasonbraid-browse --bins --locked` 8 passed. `cargo clippy -p reasonbraid-browse -p reasonbraid-server --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` rc=0; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0; `make gate` rc=0; `mdbook build docs/book` and `scripts/check_book_links.sh` rc=0.
- promotion: declined (the transferable halves are recorded and were USED rather than rediscovered: `a-claim-of-sameness-is-worth-its-call-graph` for an advertisement outrunning its call graph, `neutralize-into-the-fix-you-almost-wrote` for the blackout neutralization, and the `0.0.0.0` instrument at `.7.2.2`. What is new is that the false claim was in a REGISTRY rather than a comment, which is recorded here and in the advertisement's own `security_evidence`).
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0210 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.5): the R3 pack enforces the deny-policies it advertises`.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6 — Every advertised policy line is a claim with callers, and only two have been checked

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.5` (REPAIR-0210), which found the R3 pack advertising `redirect_policy: "deny"` and `subresource_policy: "deny"` and enforcing NEITHER, and repaired exactly those two. ⛔ The other lines of the same advertisement were not checked, and the finding generalises by construction: a caller choosing a pack reads every field, not the two somebody happened to audit.
- **The population, by command.** `grep -cE "^\s+(egress_class|sandbox_level|redirect_policy|archive_policy|subresource_policy|javascript_policy):" crates/reasonbraid-server/src/resolvers.rs` returns **18** — six policy fields across the three GATED packs (R5, R3, RX). The four non-gated packs declare theirs in migrations (`0024`–`0027`), where `grep -rhoE` over the literals returns 19 `'deny'`, 5 `'follow-classified'`, 5 `'listed'`, 4 `'none'` and 1 `'process'`. ⚠️ Those two counts are NOT one population and must not be summed: one is a Rust literal a reader can trace to a call graph, the other a database row nothing in the tree traces at all.
- **The three R3 lines `.7.3.5` did not check, named so the next reader starts from them rather than from the advertisement:**
  1. `javascript_policy: "allow-bounded"` — inline script runs; external script subresources are now denied by `.7.3.5`'s repair. ⛔ Nothing states what "bounded" MEANS, and no control asserts any specific bound, so the line is neither true nor false as written. ⚠️ `.7.3.5` made this *more* ambiguous, not less, which is why it is named here rather than left.
  2. `egress_class: "listed"` — "listed" implies an allowlist. The pre-flight CLASSIFIES a destination (public versus the refused classes); it consults no list. Decide whether the word is wrong or the mechanism is missing.
  3. `sandbox_level: "vm_container"` — the worker is an ordinary child process in an owned process group. `security_evidence` says `"container_required": true`, which is a requirement ON THE DEPLOYMENT, not a property the code establishes. ⛔ An advertisement that describes the operator's obligation as though it were the product's behaviour is the same defect class `.7.3.5` repaired.
- ⚠️ **Do NOT assume the answer is "enforce them".** `.7.3.5` enforced because the advertised word was unambiguous and the safer reading; here at least one line (`sandbox_level`) may be honestly corrected rather than implemented, and that is a decision this leaf owns rather than a repair it performs.
- ⭐ **And the non-gated packs are the larger half.** R0, R1 and R2 advertise through migration rows that no leaf has ever reconciled against their code. `.7.2`'s own goal line and `docs/decisions/2026-09-12_r2-acquisition-accept-set.md` show the shape: an advertised `media_types` set that the acquisition leg did not accept was a real defect, found and repaired. The policy columns have had no equivalent pass.
- Owns: reconciling every advertised policy line of every pack against what its code performs — decided per line as *enforce*, *correct the advertisement*, or *define the term* — and recording which, with the command that measured it.
- Acceptance: a census naming every advertised line across both populations with its verdict, reproduced by a command in the leaf; each line that is enforced gains a control observed RED first; each line that is corrected records why the advertisement was wrong rather than the code; each term that is defined is defined in the book where a caller reads it; and no line is left with an unstated meaning.
- Status: `done`; closed by its children — `.7.3.6.1` (REPAIR-0266), `.7.3.6.2` (REPAIR-0267), `.7.3.6.3` (REPAIR-0268), `.7.3.6.4` (REPAIR-0269), `.7.3.6.5` (REPAIR-0270).
- ✅ **THE ACCEPTANCE IS MET, CLAUSE BY CLAUSE.** *A census naming every advertised line across both populations with its verdict, reproduced by a command*: `python3 -B scripts/census_advertised_policies.py`, 36 lines, and a doctrine gate refuses an unadjudicated one. *Each line that is enforced gains a control observed RED first*: six `enforced`, each naming the leaf that saw it refuse. *Each line that is corrected records why the advertisement was wrong rather than the code*: exactly one was corrected, R3's `sandbox_level`, and the reason is in the leaf, the source, the ledger and the book. *Each term that is defined is defined in the book where a caller reads it*: `archive_policy`, `egress_class: "listed"` and `javascript_policy: "allow-bounded"` in `docs/book/src/deployment.md`. *No line is left with an unstated meaning*: `undefined` 0, `misdescribed` 0.
- ⭐ **The final tally across the five children: `enforced` 6 · `unverified` 9 · `vacuous` 21.** ⛔ Three defects were repaired in product code along the way (the registry's partial upsert, the egress ladder's comparison direction, the R3 sandbox claim) and one control moved from push-cadence to commit-cadence; the census itself repairs nothing, by design.
- Verification / commit: each child carries its own; the parent adds none.
- ⭐ **DECOMPOSED by `.7.3.6.1`, which built the census the acceptance asks for and found the population is not the one the leaf was opened with.** The children are named from the measurement, not from the advertisement:
  - `.7.3.6.1` — the census instrument and the verdict ledger (the measurement; no product code).
  - `.7.3.6.2` — the registry's upsert writes 6 of its 18 columns, so a re-registration cannot correct a policy line.
  - `.7.3.6.3` — the advertisement and the enforcement are two constants a comment holds together.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.2 — The registry's upsert writes 6 of its 18 columns, so a re-registration cannot correct a policy line

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.1`, from the census's own question — *what would it take to correct one of these lines?*
- **The finding, derived rather than read.** `resolvers.rs::register` INSERTs **18** columns and its `ON CONFLICT (resolver_id) DO UPDATE SET` writes **6** — `schemes`, `egress_class`, `sandbox_level`, `version`, `security_evidence`, `max_bytes`. The other **11** keep their old value on a re-registration: `locator_patterns`, `media_types`, `abilities`, `authentication_classes`, all four `*_policy` columns, `snapshot_formats`, `derivation_formats`, `latency_range_ms`.
- 🔴 **So a corrected advertisement does not reach an existing row.** `sync_gated_entries` calls `register` on every startup while the gate is open, and only DELETEs when it closes — ship new code changing a deny-policy, restart with the gate still open, and the registry keeps publishing the old word.
- 🔴 **And it breaks a documented promise, which is what makes this more than an omission.** `api.rs::register_resolver`'s own doc comment says the operator *registers (**or replaces**)* an advertise, and `advertised_media_types`' own doc comment — `crates/reasonbraid-server/src/resolvers.rs:211`, citing `docs/decisions/2026-09-12_r2-acquisition-accept-set.md` — states that *a deployment that narrows a pack's advertisement narrows what that pack may acquire, in the same act*. ⚠️ **Attribution corrected by `.7.3.6.2`:** REPAIR-0266 put that sentence in the decision RECORD, which does not contain it — the record says the admitted set is *the ranked row's own `media_types`, read at resolution time*, and the *same act* promise is the code's. The finding is unchanged; the citation was wrong and a NAMED INSTANCE is graded exact. `media_types` is the field that decision is about, and it is one of the 11 the upsert drops — so the narrowing silently does not happen, while `advertised_media_types` keeps reading the wider set per resolution.
- Owns: deciding whether the upsert writes every column or refuses a partial replace, and reproducing the stale-row case before repairing it.
- Acceptance: a control registers a pack, re-registers it with a narrowed `media_types` and a changed policy line, and observes the OLD values still served — RED before the repair; after it, the re-registration is either complete or refused by name, with the decision recorded; the `2026-09-12` accept-set decision is re-read and either upheld or superseded; and the existing resolver suites pass unchanged.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0267.
- ⚠️ **The re-read changed the repair, and this is the load-bearing part of the leaf.** Re-reading the 2026-09-12 decision as the acceptance requires turned up a finding this leaf did not make and would have contradicted: `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.9.1.1.1` measured that `resolver_capabilities` has **no tenant column** and a single-column `resolver_id` key, while `register_resolver` admits on the caller's OWN `tenant_admin` grant — so any tenant's administrator can address any row, **the built-in `r0-https-fetcher`'s included**. That is an authority defect owned by `.7.1`, and it says the upsert's reach is too LARGE.
- ⛔ **So "make the upsert write all 18 columns" was REJECTED as the whole answer.** It would have handed an unbound principal eleven more columns on a site-global row — `media_types`, which decides what the acquisition leg admits, and all four advertised policies among them. A repair that satisfies a doc comment by enlarging the surface another leaf has to bind is not a repair. ⭐ `docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` leg 2: the cheapest oracle is the project's own history, and here it had already ruled the other way about the same mechanism.
- **The decision, split by CALLER because the two callers have two different trusts:**

| caller | may replace? | why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sync_gated_entries`, at boot | **yes, completely** — all 17 non-key columns | the advertisement compiled into the binary is the truth; a drifted row loses to it |
| `POST /v1/resolvers` | **no** — `invalid_transition` (409), naming the row | the table has no tenant column, so any tenant admin addresses any row |

- 🔴 **REPRODUCED AT RUNTIME BEFORE THE REPAIR, both halves, each as its own control so neither RED hides behind the other's panic.** (1) `a_replace_is_complete_and_the_http_verb_does_not_perform_one` fails at `the startup sync restores the advertised subresource policy`, `left: "allow"`, `right: "deny"` — drift written into the row survived the boot sync. (2) `the_resolver_verb_refuses_to_replace_an_existing_advertise` fails with `left: 200`, `right: 409` and the product's own body as the evidence: **`{"registered":true,"resolver_id":"rsv-replace-probe"}`** for a re-registration that narrowed `media_types`, changed `subresource_policy`, and changed nothing at all. `test result: FAILED. 56 passed; 2 failed`.
- ⭐ **The first control drives the repair through a path a test can actually reach.** `register` is not exported from the crate root, and `gated_advertises()` is a private literal, so neither can be called directly. Instead: open the gate (the R3 row appears), write drift into the four columns the old upsert did not touch, re-run `sync_gated_entries`. That asserts a real product property — the boot sync is authoritative over the registry row — rather than a function's signature.
- ⛔ **`registered_at` is deliberately NOT in the update list.** It is when the resolver first appeared, and a re-registration does not make it new.
- ✅ **The refusal is a bound, not a blackout**, and the control says so: a DIFFERENT resolver still registers `200` in the same test, and the refused row is read back and asserted byte-for-byte unchanged — a refusal that half-applied would be worse than the no-op it replaces.
- ⚠️ **What is lost, stated rather than discovered.** An operator can no longer change a registered advertise through the API. That capability was never usable for its documented purpose — it could not narrow `media_types` and could not correct a policy line — while the part that did work was the part that should not have. Removing it removes a hazard and no working use case.
- ⭐ **It NARROWS `.7.1`'s surface and does not discharge it.** The replace half of `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.9.1.1.1`'s finding closes; creating a new site-global resolver on a tenant-admin grant is untouched, and that is the larger half. `docs/book/src/qualification-review.md`'s row is narrowed, not removed.
- 🔎 **An environment fact found on the way, and it is a consequence DOC-0060 did not name.** The first RED run reported **3** failures, not 2: `the_r2_acquisition_persists_the_served_document_s_own_evidence` and `the_r2_mismatch_refusal_persists_neither_snapshot_nor_derivation` panicked with *the extraction worker is absent at `target/debug/reasonbraid-extract`: this control cannot be reported either way without it*. ⭐ The controls are right to refuse rather than pass vacuously — but the debug-tree retirement left them unreportable, and the retirement's record says only that the next build is cold. **Run `cargo build --workspace --bins --locked` before the pg suites after a debug retirement.** Both pass once it has run.
- Verification: `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh profiles` → **`test result: ok. 58 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored`** in 13.09 s, rc=0 — the two new controls green and every one of the 56 pre-existing tests unchanged, `the_resolver_registry_resolves_and_fails_explicitly` among them. RED before the repair: `56 passed; 2 failed`, rc=101, with the source files at HEAD and only the test file modified (`git status --short crates/`).
- promotion: declined for a new knowledge note — the transferable sentence is in the decision record (*do not widen a site-global write to satisfy a doc comment; check whether the row has a tenant column first*), and the mechanism is `[[a-claim-of-sameness-is-worth-its-call-graph]]` seen from the writer's side.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2026-09-19_a-replace-is-complete-and-the-verb-does-not-perform-one.md`.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.3 — The advertisement and the enforcement are two constants a comment holds together

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.1`, whose reader census returned **0 reads** across the four `*_policy` fields in 34 field mentions on 32 lines.
- **The finding.** `.7.3.5` made the R3 worker deny what the registry advertises, and hard-wrote the behaviour into the worker: a `Document` request for a requested URL continues, everything else fails. Nothing derives that behaviour from the advertised words, and nothing compares them: `python3 -B scripts/census_advertised_policies.py --readers` classifies every occurrence of each field in tracked Rust and returns **0 reads** across all four `*_policy` fields, with `read` as the default for anything no rule explains, so the claim can only be under-stated. The underlying population, so a reader can check the instrument is hiding nothing: `git grep -c -E 'redirect_policy|archive_policy|subresource_policy|javascript_policy' -- crates | awk -F: '{n+=$2} END {print n}'` → **32 LINES**. ⚠️ The census reports **34** because its unit is a *field mention*, not a line, and one line names three of the four (`crates/reasonbraid-server/src/resolvers.rs:28`, the INSERT's column list): 32 + 2 = 34. Both numbers are right and they answer different questions; the field-mention count is the one the claim is about. The two are joined by a comment (`crates/reasonbraid-browse/src/main.rs:331`) naming `gated_advertises`.
- ⚠️ **Do NOT assume the answer is "read the row".** Letting a database row decide a security posture widens the surface rather than narrowing it — an operator with the register verb would then be able to turn the browser's isolation off by writing a word. `docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` §5B's derived-constant rule offers the cheaper shape: GATE the pair, so an advertisement that moves away from what the code enforces fails a control.
- Owns: choosing between deriving the behaviour from one source and gating the pair, and applying it to the two lines `.7.3.5` enforced.
- Acceptance: flipping the advertised word in the producer, with the worker unchanged, makes a control go RED — observed, not asserted; the chosen mechanism is recorded with the rejected alternative and its reason; and the browser suites pass unchanged.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0268.
- ⭐ **THE PAIR WAS ALREADY GATED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and saying so is most of this leaf.** The leaf was opened expecting to build a mechanism; measuring first found two, built by two earlier leaves that did not know about each other. What was missing was that nothing SAID they were a pair, and that they are guarded at wildly different strengths.
- **Direction 1 — the advertisement moves, the worker does not.** Gated by `scripts/census_advertised_policies.py` (`.7.3.6.1`), whose ledger pins each verdict to the VALUE it was earned for. Observed RED again here, in situ: flipping R3's `subresource_policy` from `deny` to `allow` in `gated_advertises` with the worker untouched prints `the verdict 'enforced' was earned for 'deny', the producer now advertises 'allow'` at `resolvers.rs:320`, rc=1. Restored byte-identical; re-check `36 advertised lines, every one carries a verdict`.
- **Direction 2 — the worker moves, the advertisement does not.** Gated by `a_subresource_the_pack_advertises_as_denied_is_not_dialed` (`.7.3.5`), which drives a real Chrome and reads an origin's own counter.
- 🔴 **AND THAT IS THE ASYMMETRY THIS LEAF REPAIRS.** Direction 1 is a doctrine gate in the pre-commit hook: it runs on **every commit**. Direction 2 needs a browser, so it runs in CI — `.github/workflows/rust.yml` wraps `cargo test --all` in `scripts/ci_browser.py` — and CI runs **at push**. The cadence is ~300 commits (`COMMIT.md`), and the tree is **237 commits ahead of `origin/main`** as this closes. ⛔ So one half of one claim was guarded hundreds of commits more loosely than the other, and nothing said so.
- **The repair: the decision becomes a pure function.** `refusing_policy(is_document, url, requested) -> Option<&'static str>` in `crates/reasonbraid-browse/src/main.rs` is the whole of the R3 request policy, lifted out of the async interception closure it was inline in. It touches no network, no browser and no filesystem, so `cargo test -p reasonbraid-browse --bins` covers it — **8 → 12 tests, 0.08 s**, wherever cargo runs. ⛔ The end-to-end control is NOT replaced: it stays the proof that the decision is actually wired to Chrome's `Fetch` domain, which a pure function cannot show.
- ⚠️ **THE REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, and it is the one the leaf warned about.** Plumbing the advertised word down to the worker — deriving behaviour from one source instead of gating two — would make a value decide whether this pack isolates anything. `resolver_capabilities` has no tenant column (`.11.9.1.1.1`), so that value is writable by any tenant administrator, and `.7.3.6.2` had just refused to widen that same surface. ⛔ A one-source design that puts the source where an attacker can reach it is worse than two sources with a gate between them.
- ⚠️ **A second rejected alternative, cheaper and still wrong:** sharing the label strings (`"subresource"`, `"redirect"`) between the crates via `reasonbraid-adapter`. It would add a dependency edge and bind the wrong thing — the labels are not the claim. `subresource_policy: "deny"` could flip to `"allow"` without either label changing.
- 🔴 **FALSIFIED TWICE, both neutralizations in situ and restored byte-identical.** (1) The **pre-`.7.3.5` defect**, `refusing_policy` returning `None` for everything: `9 passed; 3 failed`. (2) The **almost-fix** `.7.3.5` itself neutralized into — *deny means deny*, refusing every request including the navigation: `8 passed; 4 failed`. ⭐ The discriminating arm is `a_policy_that_refused_everything_would_fail_this`, which fires on (2) and **not** on (1) — so the suite separates a policy from a blackout rather than merely detecting change.
- ⭐ **One arm documents an edge rather than hiding it:** `the_asked_for_comparison_is_exact_and_fails_closed` states that a trailing slash makes a URL a different URL, so a server that normalises the navigation target yields a document request the policy calls a redirect. That is the fail-closed direction, and it is now written down instead of waiting to be discovered.
- Verification: `cargo test -p reasonbraid-browse --bins --locked` → **`test result: ok. 12 passed; 0 failed`** in 0.08 s (was 8). `python3 -B scripts/ci_browser.py --timeout 900 -- cargo test -p reasonbraid-browse --test browser_roundtrip --locked` → see the acceptance block. `python3 -B scripts/census_advertised_policies.py --check` rc=0; `cargo clippy -p reasonbraid-browse --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` rc=0; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0.
- promotion: pending — the transferable half is *two halves of one claim can be gated at cadences hundreds of commits apart, and the weaker one is invisible because both are green*. Recorded in `DEV_NOTES.md` and routed.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0268 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.3): the pair was gated at two cadences, and the looser half is now a pure function`.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.4 — The egress ladder is compared in the direction that admits a wider pack than the caller asked for

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.1`, which had to decide what `egress_class` MEANS before it could grade seven lines and found the comparison answering a different question from the one ADR-018 states.
- **The finding, derived over the whole 4 × 6 matrix.** `resolvers.rs` filters both ADR-018 classes with the same test, `declared >= required`. For `sandbox_level` the ladder runs `none < process < constrained_process < vm_container` — higher is MORE isolated — so the test is a genuine safety floor. For `egress_class` the ladder runs `none < loopback < listed < any` — higher is MORE reach — so the same test is a *capability* floor, and the only combination it refuses out of 24 is a caller asking for the WIDEST class.
- 🔴 **The consequence, stated as a row rather than as a worry.** A caller requiring `egress_class: "listed"` is served `rx-agent-mediated`, which declares `any`. There is no value of `required_egress` that means *do not give me a pack that can dial anywhere* — which is the one thing ADR-018 says the class is for: *the allowed destinations … the claim is the MAXIMUM, never the minimum*.
- ⚠️ **The code is internally consistent and the ADR is what it contradicts, so the repair is a decision and not an obvious inversion.** The shipped default `required_egress: "loopback"` only makes sense under the capability reading — under the bound reading no pack would ever be eligible, since every pack declares `listed` or `any`.
- ⭐ **A second observation from the same matrix, recorded rather than acted on here:** with the shipped defaults (`sandbox_level: "process"`, `egress_class: "loopback"`), R0, R1, R5 and RX are all ineligible, because each declares `sandbox_level: "none"`. Every test in the suite passes `"required_sandbox": "none"` explicitly. Fail-closed and therefore safe, but the documented default of `POST /v1/resources/{id}/resolve` resolves nothing for the flagship pack.
- ⛔ **A third, smaller one:** `required_egress` is not validated against the vocabulary. `crates/reasonbraid-server/tests/profiles.rs:9914` passes `"public"`, which is not an ADR-018 class; `position()` returns `None`, every row is ineligible and the caller gets `unresolvable_now`. Fail-closed, but a typo is indistinguishable from an absence.
- Owns: deciding whether the egress comparison is a bound or a capability, whether ADR-018 is amended or the code is, and what an out-of-vocabulary requirement should answer.
- Acceptance: a control observes a caller requiring `listed` being served a pack declaring `any` — RED before the repair; the decision names which of the two documents moved and why; ADR-018 is superseded or amended in the same commit if it is the one that moved; an out-of-vocabulary required class is answered by name rather than by an empty result; and the resolver suites pass unchanged.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0269.
- 🔴 **REPRODUCED AT RUNTIME, on two resolvers differing in ONE field.** `an_egress_bound_excludes_a_pack_that_declares_a_wider_one` registers `rsv-egress-listed` and `rsv-egress-any` on one scheme, identical but for `egress_class`, and asks for at most `listed`. Before the repair: `{"resolvers":["rsv-egress-listed","rsv-egress-any"],"unresolvable_now":false}` — `left: [rsv-egress-listed, rsv-egress-any]`, `right: [rsv-egress-listed]`. ⭐ One field differs, so nothing else can explain the outcome.
- 🔴 **THE ROOT CAUSE IS ONE TEST WRITTEN FOR TWO LADDERS THAT RUN IN OPPOSITE SAFETY DIRECTIONS.** `declared >= required` is a floor. The sandbox ladder goes up towards more ISOLATION, so a floor is right. The egress ladder goes up towards more REACH, so the same test admitted a pack that reaches further than the caller permitted. ⭐ **The comment above it quoted ADR-018's *the claim is the MAXIMUM* and drew the opposite conclusion in the same sentence** — *"so a resolver claiming LESS than required is ineligible"*, when under a maximum claim a resolver claiming less is claiming to be more constrained.
- **Measured over the whole 4 × 6 matrix before anything changed:** the egress filter refused exactly **one combination of 24**, and it refused the wrong one. Asking for `any` — the widest class — was the only way to narrow the field, and it narrowed it to `rx-agent-mediated`, the single pack declaring no bound.
- ✅ **The decision: the CODE moved, ADR-018 stands unchanged.** `egress` is now `declared <= required`. ⚠️ The code was internally consistent, so this is a decision and not an obvious inversion: the shipped default `required_egress: "loopback"` only makes sense under the capability reading, because under the ceiling reading no pack would ever be eligible. It moved because **a capability floor over a maximum claim is incoherent** — it asks a promise-not-to-exceed to behave like a promise-to-reach, and it cannot express any isolation requirement at all, which is what ADR-018 says the classes are for.
- ✅ **The default becomes `any`, and the BEHAVIOUR is unchanged.** Under the old floor test `loopback` admitted every pack (all declare `listed` or `any`); under the ceiling test `any` admits every pack. Nothing a caller sees changed — the word now says what it does. ⛔ Whether the default SHOULD be permissive is a separate decision this leaf does not take.
- ✅ **An off-ladder required class is refused by name.** `position()` returned `None`, every row became ineligible, and the caller got `unresolvable_now` — fail-closed and silent about which. Now `invalid_command`, and ⛔ validated AFTER the tenant binding deliberately: checking the body first would answer 400 for a resource the caller may not know exists, re-opening the existence oracle `.11.14.3.4` closed.
- ⚠️ **ONE EXISTING TEST CHANGED, and it is recorded rather than quietly edited.** The RX resolution test passed `required_egress: "listed"` and expected `["rx-agent-mediated"]` — which is the defect seen from the suite's own side. It now passes `"any"`, because RX declares `any` and a caller permitting at most `listed` must not be handed it. The reason is written into the test beside the line. 🔎 `.7.3.6.5` may find RX's `any` to be a MISDESCRIPTION (the pack performs no egress at all), in which case that line changes again for a different reason.
- ⭐ **Three arms beyond the bound, so the repair is a filter and not a blackout:** permitting `any` still admits both packs; a bound no pack meets is the explicit `unresolvable_now` with the reference preserved; and the off-ladder class is named.
- ⚠️ **Recorded, not repaired:** `required_sandbox` defaults to `process`, which excludes the four packs declaring `none` — including R0. Every test passes `"none"` explicitly, so the documented default of the resolve verb resolves nothing for the flagship pack. Fail-closed and therefore safe; it is a default-policy question, not a comparison one, and this leaf owns the comparison.
- Verification: `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh profiles` → **`test result: ok. 59 passed; 0 failed`** in 13.09 s. RED before: `58 passed; 1 failed`. `cargo clippy -p reasonbraid-server --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` rc=0; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0; `mdbook build docs/book` + `check_book_links.sh` rc=0.
- promotion: declined for a new knowledge note — the transferable sentence is the decision record's own title, and the mechanism is a second instance of `[[a-control-that-passes-for-an-unrelated-reason]]`'s family seen in a filter rather than a control: one predicate serving two populations that disagree about which direction is safe.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2026-09-19_the-egress-claim-is-a-ceiling-the-sandbox-claim-is-a-floor.md`.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0269 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.4): the egress claim is a ceiling, the sandbox claim is a floor`.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.5 — The terms with no stated meaning, defined where a caller reads them or corrected

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.1`. The census returned **7 `undefined`** and **7 `misdescribed`** lines; this leaf owns both classes, because the same act settles them — deciding what the word is supposed to mean.
- **`undefined` (7):** `archive_policy` on all six packs, defined nowhere in the repository; and `javascript_policy: "allow-bounded"` on R3, where nothing states what *bounded* means and no control asserts any bound. ⚠️ `.7.3.5` made the R3 line MORE ambiguous, not less: inline script still runs while external script subresources are now denied.
- **`misdescribed` (7):** `egress_class: "listed"` on R0/R1/R2/R3/R5 — no list is consulted anywhere; the mechanism is a destination CLASSIFIER (public-only), and ADR-018's vocabulary has no class for *bounded by classification*. `egress_class: "any"` on RX, a pack that performs no egress at all. And **`sandbox_level: "vm_container"` on R3 — G4's open strand**: the worker is an ordinary child process in an owned process group, and `security_evidence` emits `"container_required": true`, a requirement ON THE DEPLOYMENT published as a property of the product.
- ⚠️ **Do NOT assume the answer is "enforce them".** At least `sandbox_level` may be honestly corrected rather than implemented, and `archive_policy` may be a field that should not exist. That is a decision this leaf owns rather than a repair it performs.
- Owns: defining each term in the book where a caller reads it, or correcting the advertisement and recording why the word was wrong rather than the code — per line, with the census re-run to show the verdict moved.
- Acceptance: no line is left `undefined` or `misdescribed`; each definition lands in `docs/book/` where a caller choosing a pack reads it; each correction records why the advertisement was wrong; `.doctrine/advertised_policy_verdicts.tsv` carries the new verdict with its evidence; and G4's open strand is named as discharged or still open, explicitly.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0270.
- ✅ **ALL 36 LINES NOW CARRY A DEFINED VERDICT: `enforced` 6 · `unverified` 9 · `vacuous` 21 — `undefined` 0, `misdescribed` 0.** Thirteen of the fourteen were settled by DEFINING a term; exactly one advertisement was corrected.
- 🔴 **G4'S OPEN STRAND IS DISCHARGED, by correcting the advertisement rather than building a container — and the reproduction is the sharpest of the four children.** The R3 pack advertised `sandbox_level: "vm_container"`, the TOP of the ADR-018 ladder, while `reasonbraid-browse` spawns an ordinary child process in an owned process group — rung one. A caller requiring `vm_container` was served it: **`{"resolvers":["r3-browser-worker"],"unresolvable_now":false}`**. ⛔ That is the silent downgrade ADR-018's exit clause exists to prevent, performed by the one pack that executes untrusted JavaScript.
- ⭐ **NOTHING HAD EVER REQUIRED `vm_container`, and that is why the claim survived.** `git grep vm_container` over `crates/` returns the ladder constant, one SDK vocabulary test and the advertisement itself — no caller, no control. **A rung nobody stands on holds any weight you like.** ⛔ Correcting it therefore broke no test: every strict-sandbox caller in the suite expects either a test-registered resolver that declares its own level or `unresolvable_now`, and the R3 resolution test asks for `none`.
- ⚠️ **`security_evidence`'s `container_required: true` STAYS, and is now consistent rather than contradictory.** The level says what the CODE provides; that key says what the DEPLOYMENT must add to reach the intended posture. The defect was one field claiming the other's content, not the existence of either.
- ⭐ **`archive_policy` WAS DEFINED, NOT CORRECTED, and the definition dissolves the apparent self-contradiction.** `ROADMAP.md` §16 lists the resolver policies as *"…decompression, **archive-depth**, and total-work"* — depth is the axis. So `deny` = the pack does not expand an archive NESTED inside the container it acquired. R2 therefore expands the zip or tar it was GIVEN — its own advertised media types — and refuses one inside it by name (`nested_archive`, `reasonbraid-extract/src/main.rs:342` and `:415`, asserted `:782`). 🔴 The `.7.3.6.1` census called this line *the sharpest instance* of a contradiction; it was the sharpest instance of an **undefined term**, and the two look identical until the term is pinned.
- ⭐ **`egress_class: "listed"` WAS DEFINED, and migration `0025`'s own comment had already said it**: *"the §12.4 public-only destination CLASSES ARE the list the `.2.1` classifier enforces"*. A list of destination classes, not of hosts. The word was not wrong; it was undocumented, and a definition sitting in a migration comment is not a definition a caller can read.
- ⭐ **`javascript_policy: "allow-bounded"` WAS DEFINED FROM THE PRODUCER, by enumerating what actually bounds execution:** external script subresources refused at the CDP `Fetch` domain (`.7.3.5`); a wall-clock budget and a step budget (`BrowseLimits`); a private per-render browser profile, discarded; and no credential of any kind reaching the browser (0 matches for `credential|cookie|Authorization` across the crate). Four bounds, each with a mechanism.
- ⚠️ **ONE VERDICT OF `.7.3.6.1`'s IS CORRECTED, and it was mine.** RX's `egress_class: "any"` was graded `misdescribed` because the pack performs no egress in-product. That judged the wrong granularity: the class is the MAXIMUM of the **acquisition the pack delivers**, and an enrolled agent's reach is genuinely unbounded, so `any` is the honest ceiling. Re-graded `vacuous` — nothing can violate `any`. ⭐ `.7.3.6.4` is what gives it teeth: a caller must now permit `any` to be served this pack.
- 🔎 **A live-document drift found and repaired on the way, and it is the standing corpus rule's own shape.** `docs/book/src/blockers.md` said C2 is CLOSED with all five gate records re-derived; `docs/book/src/qualification-review.md`, two pages of the same book, still said *"The first is done"* and *"Until the remaining four records are re-derived"*. REPAIR-0265 closed C2 and swept the blockers page but not this one. Both passages corrected here. ⛔ Not opened as a leaf: it is repaired in this commit, which is what `§15` asks for.
- ⛔ **NOT CLAIMED: that G4 is now Met.** What closes is the last un-discharged strand of its re-derivation (`.11.4.7.4`). The record's verdict — *G4 must be re-earned* — is unchanged by this leaf, and re-earning it is not this leaf's work.
- Verification: `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh profiles` → **`test result: ok. 60 passed; 0 failed`** in 13.24 s. RED before: `59 passed; 1 failed`, with the body above. `python3 -B scripts/census_advertised_policies.py --check` rc=0, `--self-test` 26/26. `cargo clippy -p reasonbraid-server --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` rc=0; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0; `make gate` green; `mdbook build docs/book` + `check_book_links.sh` rc=0.
- promotion: pending — **a rung nobody stands on holds any weight you like** is the transferable sentence, and it generalises past ladders: an unexercised value in an ordered vocabulary is unverified by construction. Recorded in `DEV_NOTES.md` and routed.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2026-09-19_an-advertised-line-carries-an-adjudicated-verdict.md` gains the definitions; the sandbox correction is recorded there and in the book.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0270 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.5): the terms are defined, and the R3 pack stops claiming a container it does not have`.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.4 — Bound extraction transport and retained storage

- Status: `pending`; concrete parent-worker source boundary separated before .7.3.3 implementation.
- Sources: crates/reasonbraid-server/src/extraction.rs writes stdin synchronously, waits for child exit before draining stdout, and reads the reply without a byte bound; descendants can keep pipes alive after direct-child exit. Own concurrent bounded pipes, total deadlines, descendant containment, deployment-level storage quotas and safe retention/retirement for failed/unconfirmed invocations. Direct-child completion and exclusive inputs alone do not close this boundary. Qualify pressure, cancellation, escaped writers and malicious worker/input controls before claiming full isolation.

- 🔴 **MEASURED, and it is the retention rule's own founding shape in a third place.** `crates/reasonbraid-browse/src/lifetime.rs` retains its whole workspace whenever the render did not succeed **or** cleanup was unconfirmed — and a tripped time budget is a legitimate, documented outcome, so an R3 deployment accumulates one per refused render with no retirement rule at all:

| population | fixtures | bytes | reproducible payload | evidence kept |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| browser lifetime controls + pg clusters (already ruled) | 37 | 1,896,248,619 | 99.93 % | 1.34 MB |
| **`.project-data/browser/run-*` (this clause)** | **48** | **880,130,713** | **99.99 %** | **95,280 B** |

- ⛔ **`scripts/census_retained_fixtures.py` reduced 195 fixtures and 10,364,871,724 bytes on 2026-09-20 and left all 880 MB of this population untouched.** ⚠️ **THE MECHANISM WAS PUBLISHED WRONG AND IS CORRECTED BY `.13.4.4` (REPAIR-0324).** It is not that the instrument never reaches `.project-data/browser/run-*`: measured against the retirement receipts, **14 workspaces there WERE reduced**, transitively, because a `target/browser-lifetime-controls/case-*` fixture names them in its own receipt. ⭐ The real gap is narrower and sharper — **a workspace with NO owning control fixture is never reached**, which is exactly what a standalone worker run leaves, and therefore what a production R3 acquisition leaves. All 48 of the remaining ones are that kind, and every one still holds its `profile/`. ⚠️ Every one of the 48 carries a `completion.json`, so they are receipt-bearing fixtures the existing rule — *keep the receipt, drop the reproducible payload* — already covers in principle.
- ⚠️ **NOT a claim that the retention is wrong to happen.** The workspace IS the diagnostic evidence for an unconfirmed cleanup, which `.11.25` and `.11.25.1` both depended on. What is missing is the retirement, and the third population's ratio (99.99 %) says what it would cost to keep the receipts.

- Status: `pending`.

- ⭐ **ATTACHED CLAUSES — routed-record findings this leaf's goal line does NOT make visible** (`R-40-42-3` clauses 3, 5 and 6, tranche 4b; `docs/tasks/artifacts/signoff_review/RECONCILIATION.md`). ⚠️ Five of that record's eight clauses ARE visible or already handled; these three are the residue, and each is about a vocabulary or a lifecycle state the goal line never names.
  1. 🔴 **The quarantine gate does not exist anywhere in the product.** `git grep -c "quarantine_status" -- 'crates/*/src'` returns **rc=1, no match**, so `migrations/0028_evidence_snapshots.sql:33`'s column is written by its `DEFAULT 'none'` and read by nothing — no acquisition, no citation, no read surface. The §9.8 code that would report it, `evidence_quarantined`, is constructed nowhere either: its only occurrence in the workspace is the registry's own `as_str` arm, and the book's errors chapter already lists it among the eleven registered codes this build never emits. ⛔ The goal line names freshness horizons, tombstone honesty and expiry clocks; §12.6's "quarantine/quality status" is in none of them.
  2. **An assessment replay silently discards the resubmission's text.** `claims::submit` keys the replay on `(claim_id, snapshot_id, assessment, author)` — in the application and again as `claim_assessments_replay_idx` — and returns the FIRST assessment's id, so a second submission with a different `excerpt`, `selector` or `rationale` stores none of them and reports success. ⛔ "distinguish excerpt existence from claim entailment" is about what an excerpt PROVES; nothing in the goal line reaches what a replay KEEPS.
  3. **The derivation kind is unvalidated, and the contrast is inside one feature family at three sites.** `claims.rs` declares `ASSESSMENT_KINDS` and refuses anything outside it, and `migrations/0030` adds a CHECK constraint on the same five values — while `derivations.rs` names its seven kinds (`chunk`, `text`, `excerpt`, `summary`, `ocr`, `caption`, `analysis`) in a doc comment calling them "the §12.6 named set", `derived_kind` is a plain `String` nothing checks, and `migrations/0029` adds no constraint. The vocabulary is enforced twice on one side of the graph and zero times on the other.
- ⭐ **ATTACHED CONTEXT for the two clauses that ARE visible**, because both are stronger than the goal line implies and a future census should not have to re-measure them. `api.rs::submit_assessment` admits on `reader_tenant(…).is_some()` — ENROLMENT — and passes the request body through unchanged, so `author` and `verifier` are caller strings; and `migrations/0030_claim_assessments.sql` gives the table no tenant column, so the surface is SITE-GLOBAL as well as unbound. The citation validation and `derivations::submit`'s parent probe both omit `deleted_at IS NULL`, so a snapshot tombstoned by `snapshots.rs:330` or by the retention sweep still validates a citation — two sites, one omission.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.8.1.1 — The close outcome names ballot results the system never counts

- Opened: `pending` by `.15`, whose ownership audit found this finding routed to `.11.4.7.2.1.2` — a leaf that owns the decision-rule CREATE FIELDS and not the ballot they would be counted under.
- 🔴 **THE SHARP FORM, which is not *there is no vote table*.** `CloseOutcome` has fourteen variants and four of them are BALLOT RESULTS — `AcceptedUnanimously`, `AcceptedWithRecordedObjections`, `AcceptedByRule`, `NoQuorum`. ⛔ `VerdictInput` carries `rule: String` and `outcome: CloseOutcome`, both **supplied by the caller** under `deny_unknown_fields`. So a closer ASSERTS unanimity, asserts the rule it was reached under, and asserts that quorum failed, and nothing counts anything. `git grep -c abstain -- crates migrations` returns **0**, and no migration creates a table naming a vote.
- ⭐ **THAT IS `.8.2.4`'s SHAPE AT THE DELIBERATION LAYER: a stored row asserting a provenance nothing derived** — and it is the sharpest instance this project has, because the asserted words are the product's whole output. A thread's terminal record is what a governance reader acts on.
- ⛔ **IT IS NOT REPAIRED BY ADDING A TABLE.** `vote` is a workflow STEP (`workflows::TERMINAL_KINDS`) and the eight built-in profiles compose it; the question is what a `vote` step DOES, which the decision rule defines. ⚠️ So this leaf is **sequenced after `.11.4.7.2.1.2`** and must not start before it: building a tally against an undecided rule is the rework the sequence exists to avoid.
- Owns: what a `vote` step records, how the tally reaches `CloseOutcome`, and which of the four ballot variants a closer may still assert versus which the server must derive — with abstention in the vocabulary or explicitly out of it.
- Acceptance: `.11.4.7.2.1.2`'s decision-rule contract is quoted and this leaf builds ONLY against it; the four ballot-result variants are each classified `derived` or `caller-asserted` with the reason, because leaving that implicit is the present defect; a close whose asserted outcome DISAGREES with the counted ballot is refused, observed RED first; abstention is either recorded or declined in writing, never absent by accident; and the existing thread-close walk keeps every assertion it has.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0396 (`.1`) + REPAIR-0397 (`.2`) discharge every acceptance clause — the contract quoted and built against; the four ballot words classified in the record's §5 table and enforced by `decisions::classify_close`; a disagreeing close refused, observed RED first through HTTP; abstention recorded with a per-family meaning; the twelve-terminal walk green and untouched. ⛔ `.3`–`.6` are gaps this leaf FOUND and opened, not clauses of its acceptance, so they stay `pending` as their own leaves. SPLIT before implementing (`SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.15`), on `.8.2.5`'s measured shape: the piece nothing depends on lands first, so the commit that adds it cannot break a caller.
- 🔴 **THE LEAF UNDER-QUOTED ITS OWN CONTRACT.** §13.3 does not stop at the seven families: *Every rule defines electorate creation, quorum, denominator, abstentions, recusals, timeouts, unreachable members, role replacement, changed incarnations, veto scope, amendments after voting starts, tie handling, and terminal outcomes.* That is THIRTEEN obligations per rule, and neither `.11.4.7.2.1.2` nor this leaf named them. Each is answered in `docs/decisions/2026-09-22_a-counted-rule-derives-its-outcome-and-a-rule-it-cannot-count-is-refused.md` — decided, or owned by a child, never silent.
- ⭐ **§13.4's last sentence decides abstention under unanimity**: *An initiator who requests unanimity receives failure/deadlock if any applicable member withholds it.* §13.3 removes a member from the unanimity denominator only by RECUSAL, so an abstainer is still applicable and has withheld — `deadlocked`.
- ⛔ **Two families cannot be counted today and are REFUSED at creation rather than accepted and ignored**: `role_weighted` (its weights have no schema — `.11.4.7.2.1.2.1` decision 4) and `human_committee` (§13.3 names it and gives it no bar). Accepting either would be `.11.4.7.2.1.2`'s decision 2 violated in the one place it was written for.

| this leaf's mechanism | child |
| --- | --- |
| the ballot vocabulary, the count, and the close classification — pure, nothing calls them | `.1` |
| `decision_rule` at create, charter-validated after authorization | `.2` |
| the electorate snapshot, the ballot on the `vote` step, the derived close | `.2` |
| the adjudication verdict's free-text `rule` and its ballot-result words | `.3` |
| `role_weighted` and `human_committee` made countable | `.4` |
| the rule-less thread's four caller-asserted ballot words | `.5` |
| recusal, role replacement, changed incarnations, amendments after voting starts | `.6` |

The harness is release engineering (ROADMAP §19), not a tenant product surface. ⭐ The defect is that the ruled gate was never applied.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.8.2.5.2 — Validation moves ahead of the gate, so an invalid input is never an authorization refusal

- Opened: `pending` by `.8.2.5`'s split, after implementing `.1` showed the gate cannot simply wrap the writes as they stand.
- 🔴 **THE PROBLEM THE PRECEDENT ALREADY SOLVED AND THIS FAMILY HAS NOT.** `authorized()`'s closure returns a refusal as a `&'static str`, and `site_receipt_response` renders that to the caller. ⛔ So wrapping a write whose validation lives INSIDE it turns *the baseline score for `c1` is not a number* into an authorization refusal with a static reason — a **403 about authority for a 400 about input**, and it would silently undo the message quality `.8.2.1`–`.8.2.4` just built.
- ⭐ **`site_authority::workflows` states the rule in its own doc comment, and it is the design rather than an accident**: the composition validation runs in the HTTP layer BEFORE the site call and stays a typed 400, because *a caller that fails validation learns nothing about authority, and one that passes it still meets the gate*. `crate::policy::validate` is called ahead of `site::register_policy` for the same reason, and `policy::register` re-validates regardless so the registry never stores an invalid row whatever called it.
- Owns: extracting each write's PURE validation into a `validate_*` function the handler can call before the gate and the write still calls itself, with no behaviour change.
- Acceptance: every pure check now reachable without a database — the digest shapes, the trial count, the declared seed, the non-empty arms and cases, the cohort kinds, the Brier and threshold ranges, the baseline and score shapes; each write calls its own validator FIRST, so the registry cannot store an invalid row whatever calls it; the refusal a caller sees is byte-identical to today's, proved by the `evaluation` suite passing with **no test edited**; and nothing else changes, because a seam that changes behaviour is not a seam.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0391. **Six validators, no behaviour change, and no test edited — which is the only evidence a seam can offer.**
- ✅ **SIX `validate_*` FUNCTIONS, each the pure head of its write, and each still called by that write first**: `validate_corpus` (the two digest shapes), `validate_run` (the trial count and the declared seed), `validate_trial` (non-empty arms and cases, the cohort kinds), `validate_calibration` (non-empty run ids, the Brier range), `validate_gate` (the threshold range, the baseline's shape, its non-emptiness, and every baseline score's type and range), `validate_gate_scores` (every measured score's type and range).
- ⭐ **THE CONTRACT IS `site_authority::workflows`'s, COPIED DELIBERATELY**: the handler may now validate before the gate, and the write re-validates regardless, so *the registry never stores an invalid row, whatever called it*. Neither half is optional — dropping the first returns a 403 for bad input, dropping the second lets a future caller bypass validation entirely.
- ⚠️ **`record_trial_results` HAS NO PURE VALIDATION AND GAINS NO VALIDATOR.** Its body is a raw `Value` and its only check is that the trial exists, which needs the database. ⛔ Stated rather than left as a gap in the list of seven: it will reach `.3`'s gate with nothing to run ahead of it, and that is correct rather than missing.
- ⚠️ **ONE ORDERING MOVED, and it is named because a seam claiming *no behaviour change* owes it.** `evaluate_gate` now checks the submitted scores' shape and range BEFORE it looks the gate up, so a malformed score against a nonexistent gate now reports the malformed score rather than the ghost gate. ⛔ Both were 400s and no control covers that pair; the reorder is required, because a validation that runs after the gate lookup cannot run before the authorization gate either.
- ⭐ **AND THE EMPTY-SCORES REFUSAL DELIBERATELY DID NOT MOVE.** *Compared no case* is a fact about the baseline's INTERSECTION with the submitted scores, so it is not decidable without the stored row. It stays inside the write, and `validate_gate_scores` says so in its own doc comment rather than leaving a reader to wonder why one check moved and its neighbour did not.
- [x] **REPRODUCE / ISSUE** — implementing `.1` showed the gate cannot wrap these writes as they stand: `authorized()` renders a refusal as a `&'static str` authorization reason, so an input error inside a site act becomes a 403 about authority.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE)** — every pure check lived inside the async write in `crates/reasonbraid-server/src/evaluation.rs`, so nothing could run it ahead of a gate.
- [x] **THE FIX** — six pure functions extracted, each called first by its own write. No signature changed, no handler touched, no SQL moved.
- [x] **ADDRESSED (verified)** — `git grep -c "^pub fn validate_" -- crates/reasonbraid-server/src/evaluation.rs` returns **6**, and each is reachable without a pool.
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh evaluation` → **3 passed**, rc=0 and the three unit controls pass, with `git diff --stat -- crates/reasonbraid-server/tests/` **empty**: no test was edited, which is the only evidence a seam can offer. Clippy **0 warnings**; fmt rc=0; `make gate` green.
- [x] **LOCKSTEP** — `MEMORY.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `DEV_NOTES.md`, `LIVE_STATUS.md` and this tree. ⛔ The book is unchanged: no route behaves differently.
- promotion: declined (*validate before the gate, and re-validate inside it* is `site_authority::workflows`'s own documented contract, cited rather than restated).
- Verification: `evaluation` 3/3 live and 3/3 unit, no test edited; clippy 0 warnings; fmt and the doctrine gate rc=0.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.8.2.5.3 — The gate, the reason, and the read side's stated disposition

- Opened: `pending` by `.8.2.5`'s split; **must not start before `.2`**.
- Owns: converting the seven evaluation WRITE functions from `&PgPool` to `&mut sqlx::PgConnection` so each can run inside the site transaction `authorized()` opens; a `site_authority::evaluation` module wrapping them; the `reason` field each site act requires on the seven request bodies; the HTTP wiring; the controls; the read-side disposition; and the book. ⚠️ The READ functions stay on `&PgPool` because they stay outside the gate.
- ⭐ **THE STORE-FAULT DISTINCTION `.8.2.2` BUILT IS WHAT MAKES THE AUDIT HONEST HERE**, and the two repairs compose rather than merely coexisting: `authorized()`'s closure returns `Result<Result<Effect, &'static str>, Error>`, where the OUTER error is *the database could not answer* and the inner is *the caller was refused*. Before `.8.2.2` every evaluation failure was one undifferentiated `Duplicate`, so a store fault would have been audited as a refusal — a permanent site-audit row asserting a decision nobody made.
- ⚠️ **Two routes take a bare JSON body today** — `record_trial_results` and `evaluate_gate` — so acquiring a `reason` changes their shape, not just their fields. That is a documented wire change and the book carries it.
- Acceptance: each of the seven writes refuses a caller with no grant, observed RED first through HTTP, and a grant holder succeeds in the same run; a refusal carries its audit id, as the four existing site surfaces do; an INVALID input from an authorized caller still returns its typed 400 and never an authorization refusal, which is what `.2` exists to make possible; a store fault is NOT audited as a refusal, observed with an injected fault; the read side is stated explicitly — left on enrolment with DOC-0029 cited, or gated with its reason, never changed silently; `evaluation` and `policy` stay green; and the book documents what gates each route.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0392. **The exposure is closed, and three defects the gate made visible were repaired with it.**
- ✅ **THE GATE IS ON ALL SEVEN WRITES.** A `site_authority::evaluation` module wraps each in `authorized()`, so authorization, the effect and the audit are one ordered transaction. Five go through a macro because they are one shape; `record_trial_results` and `evaluate_gate` are written out, the first because its inner call returns `()` and has no row to serialize, the second because it is the OTHER capability.
- ✅ **FALSIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, ONE MUTANT PER CLAIM, sources restored byte-identical** (`api.rs` `9e7be371…`, the site module `e4764877…`):

| mutant | what the server did | which claim it proves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the gate removed from `register_corpus` — the pre-repair path restored verbatim | returned the old `400 invalid_command` with the pre-repair message | the gate is real, and its absence IS the exposure |
| `Action::GateEvaluate` collapsed into `Action::EvaluationRecord` | refused a `gate_evaluate` holder with `site_authority_required` | the two capabilities are genuinely separate |

- ⚠️ **AND WHERE THE FIRST MUTANT'S RED LANDED IS WORTH STATING** (`.11.24.1.3.1`: read WHERE it failed). It fired on the DUPLICATE control rather than the ungranted-stranger control, because that assertion runs earlier in the same test and equally depends on the gate — it requires a 403 with an audit id, which only a site act produces. The stranger control is positioned after it and detects the same class.
- ✅ **THE CONTROLS THE ACCEPTANCE ASKED FOR, all in one green run**: an enrolled principal with **no** grant is refused and the refusal is audited; a holder of `gate_evaluate` alone **cannot** register a gate; the same holder **can** evaluate one, so the grant is real rather than the refusal universal; an invalid input from an authorized caller still returns its typed **400**; and an injected store fault returns **500** with a **null** `audit_id`, because a fault decides nothing and must not leave a permanent row asserting a denial nobody made.
- 🔴 **THREE DEFECTS THE GATE MADE VISIBLE, each repaired here.** ⭐ None was reachable before, and that is the argument for gating rather than merely auditing:
  1. **A failed INSERT aborted the audit transaction.** In PostgreSQL a failed statement aborts its transaction, so the audit row `authorized` writes next failed with *current transaction is aborted* and the caller saw a **500** instead of an audited refusal. ⛔ The remedy is `policy::register`'s, whose comment records the identical trap: `ON CONFLICT … DO NOTHING`, with `rows_affected() == 0` as the duplicate. Five INSERTs converted.
  2. **`ghost_run`, `ghost_gate` and the absent-trial refusal were modelled as `EvaluationError::Duplicate`** — one enum arm meaning both *this identity is taken* and *this identity does not exist*. In prose that was confusing; under a gate that renders a refusal by CLASS it told a caller *that calibration id already exists* when the defect was a run that does not. A `NotRegistered` variant separates them.
  3. **The first refusal strings were one coarse class for the whole module.** Corrected to a per-act pair — *that corpus version is already registered*, *the named corpus version is not registered*, *a named run … was taken against another corpus version or workflow* — which is the quality `policies.rs` already sets.
- ⚠️ **TWO REFUSALS CHANGED STATUS, 400 → 403, and it is a decision rather than a side effect.** Whether a coordinate is taken, or a named run or gate exists, is a question about the DATABASE, so it is answered inside the gate as an audited domain refusal. ⛔ **Answering it before the gate would hand a caller with no site authority an existence oracle over a registry it may not write** — `.6.1.5.4`'s reasoning for the policy registry, applying unchanged. ✅ Input validation is untouched and still returns its typed 400, which is exactly what `.2` was built to preserve and what the suite now asserts side by side.
- ⚠️ **A DOCUMENTED WIRE CHANGE ON TWO ROUTES.** `record_trial_results` and `evaluate_gate` took a BARE JSON body, so acquiring a reason changes their shape: the payload moves under `results` / `scores` beside `reason`, and `deny_unknown_fields` makes the old shape a typed 400 rather than a silently ignored body. The other five gain a `reason` field.
- ✅ **THE READ SIDE IS STATED, NOT CHANGED BY OMISSION.** Reads stay on enrolment: the tables are site-wide by design and §19.7's gate manifest is meant to be auditable, and nothing in the roadmap makes a corpus version or a gate result confidential. ⛔ Gating them is a separate decision about confidentiality and is explicitly NOT taken here.
- ✅ **AND AN INDEPENDENT INSTRUMENT MEASURED THE REPAIR WITHOUT BEING ASKED.** `SHARED-REGISTRY-WRITES` refused the commit because its baseline pins the SET: all seven evaluation routes moved from `identity only` to `site authority`, printed line by line. ⭐ That is a second, structurally different confirmation — the census reads the ROUTES and their admissions, while the suite reads the server's answers — and it was produced by a gate this leaf never touched.

| site-global writers | 25 | 25 |
| …of them on IDENTITY alone | **16** | **9** |
| tables reached by an enrolment-only write | **17** | **10** |
| residue | 0 | 0 |
