###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.7.2.1.2.1 — The charter cannot hold the decision rules §4.1 says it defines

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.4.7.2.1.2`'s measurement; a PREREQUISITE, not a follow-up.
- 🔴 **The measurement:** §4.1 says the versioned `GovernanceCharter` defines *allowed decision rules and approval thresholds*. `enrollment_boundaries.charter_digest` is a `TEXT` column holding a digest, and no table, column or type holds an allowed-rule set or a threshold — `git grep -n "expected_artifact\|decision_rule" -- crates migrations` returns one unrelated `bool`.
- ⚠️ **Why it is a prerequisite and not a nicety.** Without it, a `decision_rule` create field has nothing to validate against and degrades into a GLOBAL enum — which §4.1 explicitly does not say, because the allowed subset is a per-tenant charter property. Building the field first would bake the wrong scope into the refusal.
- Owns: giving the charter a structured, versioned home for its allowed decision rules and approval thresholds, and the read path an authorization check uses to ask *may this tenant decide under this rule*.
- Acceptance: a tenant's charter records an allowed-rule set and its thresholds; the set is VERSIONED, so changing it does not rewrite what past decisions were taken under; a rule outside the tenant's set is refused with a typed error naming the rule and not the tenant's whole set (no enumeration oracle); the digest already stored on the boundary covers the new content rather than sitting beside it; and a control observes a decision recorded under a rule that was allowed WHEN IT WAS TAKEN staying valid after the set changes. Observed RED first.
- ⚠️ §4.1 also names *waiver authority and maximum duration*: if a rule outside the set can be used under waiver, this leaf decides whether that is in scope or explicitly out, rather than leaving `.8.1.1` to assume.
- Status: `done` — REPAIR-0395. ✅ **Every acceptance clause is discharged and each was falsified**, and the design is recorded in `docs/decisions/2026-09-22_a-charter-is-content-addressed-and-registering-one-is-a-site-act.md`.
- ✅ **THE STORE IS CONTENT-ADDRESSED, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES IT VERSIONED.** `migrations/0084_governance_charters.sql` keys a charter by the digest of its own canonical content, so changing the allowed set writes a DIFFERENT row and the old one stays readable forever. ⭐ **That discharges the acceptance's hardest clause with no bookkeeping to get wrong**: `reasonbraid_core::authority` ALREADY folds `charter_digest` into every authorization decision record, so a decision taken on Monday names Monday's charter by digest and that row is immutable by construction. A `version` column with `valid_from`/`superseded_at` would have made the same guarantee depend on range queries nobody re-derives.
- ✅ **REGISTRATION IS A SITE ACT, DERIVED RATHER THAN PREFERRED.** §4.1 makes the charter the document that CONSTRAINS a tenant and §4.4 makes the boundary naming its digest a root/parent-granted ceiling ⇒ a tenant that could rewrite its own allowed decision rules would hold the ceiling it is bound by. `Action::CharterRegister` takes the shape `docs/decisions/2026-09-09_site-operator-authority.md` defines, the same one `workflows::register_profile` and the `evaluation` family carry.
- ✅ **SEVEN WIRE NAMES, NOT NINE.** §13.3's second family is *simple **or** supermajority* and its fifth is *role-weighted **or** chambered*; splitting either would be this project choosing a vocabulary the roadmap did not state. ⭐ **The threshold is what the roadmap already supplies for the first distinction** — which is why §4.1 names *allowed decision rules **and** approval thresholds* in one breath. `majority_of_electorate` is the ONLY family that takes one and it MUST have one, in `(0.5, 1.0]`; a threshold on `unanimity` is a contradiction (unanimity IS 1.0) and one on `advisory_synthesis` would gate a family §13.3 defines as having *no binding decision*.
- ⛔ **THE READ PATH RESOLVES THROUGH THE BOUNDARY AND FAILS CLOSED.** `GET /v1/decision-rules/{rule}` goes tenant → ACTIVE boundary → the digest that boundary was ISSUED under, never by `tenant_id` directly: §4.4 makes the boundary the ceiling, so the charter a tenant is bound by is the one its ISSUER named. A boundary whose digest resolves to nothing answers *the question cannot be answered* — and that is the LIVE case, not a hypothetical, because every boundary issued before `0084` carries a label (`dev-charter-000`, `fixture-charter`).
- ⛔ **A REFUSAL NAMES THE RULE AND NEVER THE CHARTER'S SET**, with a unit control asserting that no other family's wire name appears in the rendered text — enumerating it would answer a question the caller did not ask.
- ✅ **FALSIFIED THREE WAYS, each RED BY NAME, and the source restored BYTE-IDENTICAL (SHA-256 `88c21da3…88e783` before and after).** **(A)** the fail-closed arm made fail-OPEN → `a_boundary_whose_charter_resolves_to_nothing_fails_closed` RED. **(B)** `NotAllowed` made to enumerate the set → `a_refusal_names_the_rule_and_never_the_charters_set` RED in the unit suite AND `a_rule_the_charter_does_not_allow_is_refused_and_names_only_itself` RED in the live one. **(C)** `for_tenant` made to resolve by `tenant_id` newest-first instead of through the boundary → `a_tenant_with_no_active_boundary_has_no_charter` RED.
- ⭐ **AND MUTATION C TOLD ME SOMETHING I HAD NOT ASSERTED: `changing_the_set_leaves_the_earlier_charter_exactly_as_it_was` PASSED under it.** That control does not rest on the boundary-resolution path at all — it is carried by content-addressing alone, which is the right dependency and is now known rather than assumed. ⚠️ Recorded because a control that survives a mutation aimed elsewhere is evidence about WHAT it tests, and `.11.27`'s lesson is that an untested assumption about a control is still an assumption.
- ✅ **THE SURFACES ARE JUDGED, NOT JUST ADDED.** `SURFACE-JUDGEMENT` refused the commit until `governance-charters` and `decision-rules` carried verdicts with their live witnesses; `docs/book/src/governance-charter.md` is the chapter and `SUMMARY.md` reaches it. ⚠️ The book's site-authority capability table also gained `evaluation_record` and `gate_evaluate`, which shipped in `.8.2.5` and were documented only in the evaluation chapter — fixed in passing because this commit edits that exact table, and stated so it is not mistaken for scope creep.
- ⚠️ **§4.1's WAIVER QUESTION, decided rather than left for `.8.1.1` to assume: OUT of scope here.** §4.1 names *waiver authority and maximum duration* as a SEPARATE charter provision from *allowed decision rules*, and this leaf implements one of nine provision families. A waiver path built now would be a second mechanism for the same question before the first has a consumer. ⛔ `.8.1.1` must not read this silence as *waivers are impossible*.
- ⚠️ **`role_weighted`'s weighting has NO schema and the book says so.** §13.3 assigns it to the charter; inventing one here would be a vocabulary decision with no roadmap sentence behind it. The family can be allowed and its weights have no home.
- ⚠️ **Behaviour for existing deployments, stated because it is a behaviour and not an absence**: a tenant reads *not answerable* until a charter is registered and a boundary reissued naming it. Nothing breaks, because nothing consumed decision rules before this commit.
- [x] **REPRODUCE / ISSUE** — `git grep -n "expected_artifact\|decision_rule" -- crates migrations` returned **one** hit and it was `reasonbraid-a2a`'s `SemanticLosses.decision_rule`, a `bool`. `enrollment_boundaries.charter_digest` was `TEXT` holding `dev-charter-digest`, `dev-charter-000`, `fixture-charter` — a NAME with no content. So §4.1's *allowed decision rules and approval thresholds* had no home and §13.3's seven families were prose.
- [x] **CAUSE** — ⛔ Not an omission at one site: the charter was modelled as a DIGEST FIELD rather than as a document. `charter_digest` was introduced by `migrations/0004_authority.sql` as a provenance token for the decision record — and `reasonbraid_core::authority` does fold it into every authorization digest, which is real and useful — so it read as *the charter is represented*. Nothing ever resolved it, because there was nothing to resolve it to. ⭐ **A reference with no referent looks identical to a reference**, which is why four fixture values could sit in it for the project's whole life without a gate noticing.
- [x] **ADDRESSED** — `migrations/0084_governance_charters.sql` + `crates/reasonbraid-server/src/charters.rs` give the digest a referent, CONTENT-ADDRESSED so the existing decision-record provenance becomes load-bearing rather than decorative. `site_authority::charters::register_charter` gates registration on the new `Action::CharterRegister`; three routes carry it; `docs/book/src/governance-charter.md` documents it and `blockers.md`'s new `C3` row states what is still missing.
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — ✅ `charters` unit **13/13**, live **8/8**; `cargo clippy -p reasonbraid-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt --all` applied; `make book` renders. ⛔ **Nothing existing changed behaviour**: the three routes are NEW, `charter_digest` is still written and read exactly as before, and no existing caller consumed decision rules — which is why the fail-closed answer for a label-bearing boundary breaks nothing. 🔴 **Two gates refused this leaf and both were right**: `SURFACE-JUDGEMENT`, because two new route families were unjudged, and `SHARED-REGISTRY-WRITES`, whose baseline pins the SET rather than the count — `POST /v1/governance-charters` appeared as a `site authority` row and was adjudicated in, the second time that gate has caught a new site route (after `.8.2.5`). 🔎 **And SURFACE-JUDGEMENT caught a subtler thing than an unjudged surface: I first recorded a witness derived from an UNSTAGED book.** Its corpus is `git ls-files -- docs/book/src/*.md` — the INDEX — so the chapter I had written but not yet added was invisible, the routes read as undescribed, and the ledger entry I wrote from that reading went green against the wrong fact. Staging the chapter flipped the witness to `-` and the gate refused the stale entry. ⭐ The census's own comment warns about the INVERSE (an untracked draft counting as documentation, seven rows green at `.11.4.6.3`); this is the same trap from the other side, and the same line of code catches both. ⚠️ No published census figure moved: the route is site-gated, so the *identity only* and *site-global* counts the live documents restate are unchanged.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.7.2.1.2.3 — A policy approval's quorum is whatever the approver says it was

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.4.7.2.1.2`'s measurement, which found the declared-not-computed defect at a SECOND surface.
- 🔴 **The measurement:** `lifecycle::ApprovalInput.quorum` is a `serde_json::Value`, and its only validation is that `quorum.participants` is a non-empty array (`crates/reasonbraid-server/src/lifecycle.rs:503`–`510`). The approver supplies the quorum snapshot that justifies their own approval; nothing checks that the named participants exist, are eligible, are non-recused, or that a threshold was met.
- ✅ **THE CENSUS THE CLAIM RESTS ON, run at this commit** — because *nothing checks it* quantifies over the whole tree and is false the moment one reader exists:
  ```
  git grep -n "quorum" -- crates/reasonbraid-server/src | wc -l          # -> 16
  git grep -n "quorum" -- crates/reasonbraid-server/src | grep -E "if |match |==|!=|\.get\("
  #   -> crates/reasonbraid-server/src/lifecycle.rs:509:    if quorum_participants == 0 {
  ```
  **16 sites, and exactly ONE predicate reads the value.** The other 15 are the two struct fields, the `.get("participants")` extraction feeding that same predicate, the `INSERT` bind, the `SELECT`, the echo into `StoredApproval`, and two unrelated `no_quorum` terminal strings in `threads.rs`. ⛔ So the column is written, read back and returned, and the only thing ever ASKED of it is whether an array is non-empty.
- ⛔ **NOT the same leaf as `.8.1.1`**, and the difference is named rather than assumed: that one owns the deliberation ballot and `CloseOutcome`; this is §15's policy-approval path, a different surface with a different record. Both are instances of §13.2 step 11 being unimplemented, which is why they are siblings rather than one leaf.
- ⚠️ **The authority half of this site is SOUND and is not at issue** — `.9.3.1` bound the grant check here (the grant must be live, held by the approver, and the approver must BE the authenticated caller). The defect is that a sound authority check sits beside an unchecked quorum.
- Owns: deriving the quorum from the electorate the system knows, or refusing an approval whose declared quorum it cannot corroborate.
- Acceptance: an approval whose declared participants are not the recorded electorate is REFUSED; the threshold is read from the charter set `.2.1` establishes, never from the request; a recused participant does not count toward quorum; the stored approval records the DERIVED quorum rather than the submitted one; and a control observes an approver who inflates their own quorum being refused. Observed RED first.
- ⛔ Sequenced AFTER `.2.1` — the threshold has no home until then.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0398 (`.1`) + REPAIR-0399 (`.2`). Every acceptance clause is discharged: an inflated quorum is refused (RED first); the threshold travels only charter → thread → decision → approval; the stored approval records the DERIVED quorum; a recused participant does not count — ⚠️ VACUOUSLY, recorded as such. 🔴 **THE MEASUREMENT MOVED THE SCOPE, and the leaf was split rather than built as written.** Its *recorded electorate* is `policy_decisions.electorate`, which `record_decision` stores exactly as the caller sends it; the decision's `rule` is free text too, and the decision never reads its thread's result — it only checks that a `verdict` contribution exists. ##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.7.2.1.3 — Deferral #3's other half: §13.5's moderator exists only in the benchmark

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.4.7.2.1`, whose adjudication split this row — the synthesizer landed, the moderator did not.
- 🔴 **THE MEASUREMENT, in both directions.** `git grep -c "moderator" -- crates/reasonbraid-server/src crates/reasonbraid-core/src` returns **0**; `git grep -l "moderator" -- crates` returns only `reasonbraid-adapter`'s benchmark (`bench/v1/corpus.json`, `bench/v1/prompts.json`, `src/bench/*`, `src/bin/rb-bench.rs`), its harness test and the CLI's bench verb. That is §19's *moderator/synthesis flow* measurement arm, not §13.5's role.
- ⛔ **SO §13.5 IS VACUOUS, NOT ENFORCED, and the distinction is the whole point** (`.7.3.6.1`'s verdict vocabulary). §13.5 lets a moderator classify messages, request clarification, propose round closure, enforce format or length, identify unanswered claims and draft summaries, and forbids it altering votes, authority or evidence records. With no moderator, the prohibitions are true today, guarded by nothing, and false the day one exists.
- Owns: deciding whether §13.5's moderator is in scope for the shipped thread engine at all — and if it is, which of the six permitted acts map onto existing verbs and which need a new one — or recording that the benchmark arm is the only intended home and superseding this half of the deferral.
- Acceptance: each of §13.5's six permitted acts is mapped to an existing thread verb or named as absent, with the command that decides it; the three prohibitions are stated as what would enforce them rather than as prose, since a prohibition over a role that does not exist cannot be tested; the decision names the leaf that owns any implementation; and if superseded, the reason distinguishes the benchmark arm from the product role explicitly, because conflating them is what made this half invisible for the life of the deferral.
- Status: `done` — DOC-0126. ✅ **Every acceptance clause is discharged, and the leaf DID delete part of itself as `.15` predicted the cheapest item might.** Recorded in `docs/decisions/2026-09-22_the-moderator-is-a-role-boundary-not-a-feature-and-five-of-its-six-acts-already-ship.md`.
- 🔴 **A CORRECTION TO THIS LEAF'S OWN ACCEPTANCE, made before using it.** It asks for *the three prohibitions*. §13.5 lists **SIX**: add a vote or approval; suppress a visible dissent except through an appealable moderation action; fabricate evidence or silently change citations; change electorate, quorum, or proposal digest; authorize more spend or tools; publish or deploy policy. All six are adjudicated, not three.
- ✅ **THE MEASUREMENT RE-DERIVES EXACTLY**: `git grep -c "moderator" -- crates/reasonbraid-server/src crates/reasonbraid-core/src` returns **zero**, and every `moderator` in the workspace is `reasonbraid-adapter`'s benchmark or the CLI verb driving it.
- ⭐ **THE SIX PERMITTED ACTS, MAPPED — and FIVE OF SIX ALREADY EXIST AS VERBS.** *Classify messages* → `ContributionKind` (`Position`, `Claim`, `Assumption`, `EvidenceReference`, `EvidenceRequest`, `Question`, `Summary`, `Verdict`, `Assessment`), declared by the AUTHOR on their own contribution and never by anyone over another's. *Request clarification* → `ContributionKind::Question` and `EvidenceRequest`, which targets ONE claim digest of this thread. *Propose round closure* → `thread.advance_round`, gated only by `ensure_participant`, so ANY participant may advance and nothing merely *proposes*. *Identify unanswered claims* → `CoverageItem { item, included, reason }`, as the synthesizer's act. *Draft summaries* → `ContributionKind::Summary` carrying `SynthesisInput`. 🔴 **Only *enforce format/length* has no verb at all.**
- ⭐ **SO §13.5 IS A ROLE BOUNDARY, NOT A FEATURE LIST — and that is the finding.** What is missing is not the ability to classify, ask, propose, summarize or report coverage; it is a principal RESTRICTED to those acts. Reading the deferral as *build a moderator feature* is what made it look large.
- ⭐ **THE SIX PROHIBITIONS, STATED AS WHAT WOULD ENFORCE THEM rather than as prose — and FOUR ARE ALREADY CARRIED by mechanisms nobody wrote for §13.5.** ✅ *Suppress a visible dissent* is **structurally impossible**: `git grep -niE "DELETE FROM thread_contributions\|UPDATE thread_contributions" -- crates/reasonbraid-server/src` returns **no match**, so contributions are append-only and there is no suppression verb to restrict. ✅ *Fabricate evidence / silently change citations* — `snapshots::submit` refuses a `raw_digest` that is not the digest of the bytes handed to it. ✅ *Authorize more spend or tools* — the grant's spend bound covers the declared budget and an excess is refused (`crates/reasonbraid-server/src/api.rs:4965`, `:4978`). ✅ *Publish or deploy policy* — grant-gated via `owning_authority` (`.9.2.1.2`). ⚠️ *Add a vote or approval* **SPLITS**: the approval half is enforced (`.9.3.1` bound the grant check), the vote half has nothing to enforce because the ballot does not exist. ⚠️ *Change electorate, quorum, or proposal digest* **SPLITS THREE WAYS**: the proposal digest is SERVER-COMPUTED so a forged one fails the membership check, the electorate does not exist, and the quorum is whatever the approver declares.
- 🔴 **AND THE TWO UNENFORCED PROHIBITIONS ARE THE SAME TWO DEFECTS THE SIBLING LEAF FOUND, REACHED FROM A DIFFERENT DIRECTION.** `.11.4.7.2.1.2` found the declared-not-computed quorum by reading the approval path; this leaf found it by asking what would stop a moderator changing one. ⭐ **A defect reached twice by independent routes is the strongest evidence this pass produces** — the same signal that made `.9.3.5` a lane.
- ✅ **THE DECISION.** The moderator is IN SCOPE and is an **AUTHORITY SCOPE, not a deliberation feature** — the work is in the role and grant vocabulary, not in the thread engine. ⛔ It is **BLOCKED on `.8.1.1` (the ballot) and `.11.4.7.2.1.2.1`/`.2.3`** (the charter's thresholds and the derived quorum), because a moderator built today would be forbidden from touching a ballot there is none of and from changing a quorum any approver can already declare freely — **enforcing a prohibition against nothing is not enforcement**, and the tests would pass vacuously. ✅ *Enforce format/length* is **DECLINED on its own merits**: it is the only CONTENT control among six procedural ones, and §13.6 constrains form as a WORKFLOW-PROFILE property (*blind initial positions*, *randomized order*, *no display of vote totals before a configured commitment point*) rather than as a principal's discretion. If it returns, it returns as a profile property.
- ⛔ **THE BENCHMARK ARM IS NOT THE PRODUCT ROLE, stated explicitly because conflating them is what made this half invisible.** §19.5's benchmark measures a *moderator/synthesis flow* as one ROUTING SHAPE among four, to compare deliberation topologies. §13.5's moderator is a GOVERNED PARTICIPANT in a real thread. One is a measurement arm, the other an authority scope; they share a word. This record does not supersede the benchmark and no later leaf may read its existence as coverage.
- Verification / commit: `REASONBRAID-DOC-0126`. Docs-only; no Rust changed. All six acts and all six prohibitions were measured at this commit.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.7.2.1.5.3.2.2.1 — A policy-held role's presence reads `available`

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0439`; the decision is `REASONBRAID-DOC-0146` (`docs/decisions/2026-09-23_a-policy-held-role-reads-held-and-presence-has-seven-states.md`), taken under the director's delegation of 2026-09-23 and shipped with the repair. Opened by `.2.2` (REPAIR-0419).
- 🔴 As found: ROADMAP §10.2 fixed SIX presence states — `available`, `busy`, `draining`, `offline`, `suspended`, `unknown` — and none of them named a role that is enrolled, leased and deliberately not being woken (`manual_only`, or outside its operating hours). Such a role read `available` while `replay` handed it nothing, which is the honest-state defect `.11.24.1.2` repaired for `busy`, in a new place.
- ⚖️ Of the three options — (a) a seventh state `held`; (b) read `draining`; (c) keep `available` and add a `hold` field — **(a) with (c)'s reason field beside it**: the state is the one field every client reads and must not lie; `draining` means winding down; every presence model that faced this question answers it with a distinct do-not-disturb state. The roadmap is amended in the same commit.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.7.2.1.5.3.2.2.2 — A positive `concurrency` is not a delivery limit

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0420`.
- Opened by `.2.2` (REPAIR-0419), from DOC-0135's *a non-zero cap gates nothing* — the third of `.2.2`'s three items, split out because it is a different mechanism: `replay` hands the node its whole tail, so a cap needs `in_flight` (`node_presence`, migration 0079's derivation) and a `LIMIT` of `concurrency − in_flight` on the tail, where the two text fields needed only a pre-check.
- The book stated the gap twice (`node-channel.md`: *it is still not a concurrency limiter*), and `.11.24.1.2` made the number decide presence (`busy`) without making it decide delivery.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — `node_channel::replay`'s tail CTE had no bound: every row after the cursor that passed the per-row and per-node predicates was returned and marked `offered`, whatever the profile declared. The declared number reached exactly one reader, the presence derivation (`presence_state`, `busy` at `in_flight >= declared`), so presence and delivery were two opinions about one number.
- [x] **ADDRESSED** — `wake::delivery_budget(concurrency, in_flight) -> Option<i64>`: `None` for no declaration (or a legacy negative), otherwise `max(declared − in_flight, 0)`; zero capacity answers `Some(0)` so it can never disagree with `hold`'s drain switch. `replay`'s pre-check now also reads `node_presence.in_flight` (the ladder's `transport_received` count, migration 0079 — the SAME number presence reads, so `busy` and *handed nothing* are one fact) and binds the budget as `LIMIT $3` on the tail CTE, ordered by cursor: `LIMIT NULL` is PostgreSQL's no-limit, `Some(0)` returns before the statement, and only the rows actually handed over are marked `offered`. Book: `node-channel.md` (the warning replaced by the rule and a five-row table), `profiles.md` (the row).
- [x] **VERIFIED** — unit `wake::tests` 5/5 (the budget: no declaration → none, legacy negative → none, 0 → 0, 2−0, 2−1, 2−2 → 0, never negative). `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh node_channel` → **43 passed** (42 + `a_declared_capacity_bounds_what_the_replay_hands_the_node`): an undeclared capacity hands all 3 queued rows; capacity 2 holding 0 hands exactly `cmd_cap_1`, `cmd_cap_2` in cursor order; acknowledged → `in_flight` 2 → the next replay hands NOTHING; one `work_result` lands → `in_flight` 1 → exactly `cmd_cap_3`; every row carries its `offered` mark once handed over.
- [x] **FALSIFIED** — `delivery_budget` mutated to answer `None` always, observed RED on the whole `node_channel` suite and restored byte-identically (`shasum -a 256 -c` OK, prefix `c4747aefee167181`): `capacity 2 minus 0 held: two rows — left: 3 right: 2` at `crates/reasonbraid-server/tests/node_channel.rs:2075`, `42 passed; 1 failed`. The unbounded control (3 of 3 with no declaration) stays green under the mutation, as it must: it is the arm that would be vacuous if the limit were on by accident.
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh node_work node_result_ordering node_enrollment node_replacement node_inbox profiles cli_end_to_end` → node_work 12, node_result_ordering 6, node_enrollment 21, node_replacement 2, node_inbox 11, profiles 70, cli_end_to_end 5 — **127 passed, 0 failed**; the `.4.2.10` five-shape drain control and the `.2.2` five wake arms pass unchanged; strict clippy clean (`-D warnings`) — it first refused the change because the replay rewrite had stopped constructing the unreadable-block hold, which was a real loss of the fail-closed arm and was restored rather than the variant deleted; `cargo fmt`; `make gate`; `make book`.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.7.2.1.5.3.2.2.3 — The replay holds every role whose profile declares no availability

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0452`. Opened by it: found while building `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.5.3.5.3.3`, whose control's work item was never offered to the origin node (`offered_at` NULL after the handshake — measured by instrumenting the control, not inferred). `.5.3.5.3.3`'s work was parked in a named `git stash` to land this first.
- 🔴 As found: `node_channel::replay` read `profile->'availability'` and parsed any non-SQL-NULL value as an `Availability` block. A profile written without the block is stored with `"availability": null` (the typed profile serializes `None` as `null`; a full read returns it), JSON `null` is not SQL NULL, the parse failed, and the replay held the node as `Hold::Unreadable` — **no work for any role that wrote a profile and declared no availability**. Presence did not agree: `presence::hold_from_stored` (REPAIR-0439) tests `is_null()` and read the same role `available`. Introduced by REPAIR-0419 (`e458683`), which added the inline parse; REPAIR-0439 wrote the null-safe reader for presence and left the replay's copy. ⚠️ The suite never saw it because `a_declared_capacity_bounds_what_the_replay_hands_the_node` seeds an undeclared block as `{}`, a shape no write produces, and no other delivery control gives the node's role a profile.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — two copies of one rule (*what does a stored availability block mean*), written a leaf apart; the second got the `null` case, the first did not, and each copy's tests fed it the shape that copy expected.
- [x] **ADDRESSED** — `wake::stored(block) -> Result<Option<Availability>, FormatError>` is the ONE reading: no block or JSON `null` → `Ok(None)`; the typed struct → `Ok(Some)`; anything else → `Err(Block)`, held fail-closed. `presence::hold_from_stored` and `node_channel::replay` both call it (the replay's budget from the same parse). Book: `node-channel.md` *The wake gate* (the stored `null`, the as-found outage, the one reader).
- [x] **VERIFIED** — RED: `a_profile_without_availability_holds_nothing_back` (`crates/reasonbraid-server/tests/node_channel.rs`: a role whose stored profile carries `"availability": null`, two queued rows) → `FAILED. 46 passed; 1 failed`, the replay handed `[]`. GREEN: unit `wake`+`presence` 16 (+ `a_stored_null_block_declares_nothing`: none, `null`, a typed block, an unreadable one); `node_channel` **47**, `node_work` 12, `node_inbox` 11, `invitations` 7, `profiles` 89.
- [x] **FALSIFIED** — M0 (`stored` reads `null` as a block, the pre-repair shape) → the unit control and `a_profile_without_availability_holds_nothing_back` both FAILED (`left: []`). Restored, `shasum -a 256 -c` OK.
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — every other control in the suites above unedited (the capacity, drain and five wake-arm controls included); strict clippy on `reasonbraid-server` — which also caught a dead initial value in the first rewrite; `cargo fmt --check`; `make book`; the doctrine gate at commit.
- ⚠️ **Honest limits:** the presence reader's `null` case has no separate control under the mutant (presence was already right; it now shares the parser the unit control pins). The capacity control's `{}` seed is left as it is: it tests the capacity arithmetic, and `{}` is a legitimate typed block (every field absent).
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0452`.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.7.2.1.5.3.3 — An offline node's inbox grows without bound

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0424`. §10.7 *maximum offline backlog*; trigger (the `.5` subscriptions) fired with `PHASE-3.5.2`.
- Owns: a per-node cap on undelivered inbox rows with a typed, recorded refusal or coalescing, and the operator's view of a node at its cap.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — `dispatch_work_in_tx` (the `.6.2` hook, the only producer of work rows in product code: `grep -rn "\.enqueue(" crates/reasonbraid-server/src` → 0 callers; `enqueue_in_tx` is called from the hook alone) counted nothing before enqueuing, so a node that never reconnected accumulated rows without bound; §10.2's *not an unlimited historical flood* had no bound at the source.
- [x] **ADDRESSED** — `node_channel::MAX_OFFLINE_BACKLOG = 64` (the dev shape of the fan-out caps; ⛔ not a measured figure) and `undelivered_in_tx` (`node_inbox_state` rows at `queued` or `offered` — the ladder's precedence is the exclusion list). ⚖️ **Refuse, not coalesce**, with the reason: the `.6.2` invariant *an invitation exists iff its work does* forbids landing the command and dropping its work, so the dispatch refuses FIRST (before any reservation), `dispatch_work_in_tx` returns a typed `DispatchRefusal::OfflineBacklog`, and `run_thread_command` rolls the transaction back through its own API — no event, no invitation, no work — then records the refusal on the pool's connection through `refuse_storm` (`offline_backlog`, the cap, the initiator, the thread) so the record survives the rollback; a retry re-validates like every domain refusal. The operator sees the pressure first: every `GET /v1/admin/nodes/presence` row carries `backlog: {undelivered, cap}`. Book: `node-channel.md` (*The offline backlog is capped*), `authority.md`, `recruitment.md`, `errors.md`.
- [x] **VERIFIED** — `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh invitations command_api profiles node_work node_result_ordering node_channel mcp_write` → invitations **7** (6 + `an_offline_nodes_backlog_is_capped_and_the_refusal_is_recorded`), command_api 42, profiles 72, node_work 12, node_result_ordering 6, node_channel 43, mcp_write 7 — **189 passed, 0 failed**. The control: a node seeded with 64 `queued` rows; the presence view shows `{"undelivered": 64, "cap": 64}`; the invited role's accept → `429 storm_control` naming *offline backlog*; the thread still shows the role `invited` and the inbox still holds exactly 64 rows (the rollback); `GET /v1/admin/storm-refusals` lists one `offline_backlog` row with `limit_value` 64, the role as initiator, the thread as target and the caller's words; one seeded row removed → the same accept lands and its work row is the 64th.
- [x] **FALSIFIED** — the cap check mutated to never refuse, observed RED on the `invitations` suite and restored byte-identically (`shasum -a 256 -c` OK): the accept LANDS — `left: 200 right: 429` at `crates/reasonbraid-server/tests/invitations.rs:387`, `6 passed; 1 failed`; green again on the restore, `7 passed`.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.7.2.1.5.3.4 — A storm-control refusal is answered and recorded nowhere, so the breaker's trigger cannot fire

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0423`. Taken BEFORE `.5.3.3` on purpose: a backlog refusal built first would have been one more `storm_control` answered and recorded nowhere, for one commit — this leaf's own defect.
- `POST /v1/calls` answers `429 storm_control` and stores nothing, so *the first multi-tenant storm observed* — the circuit breakers' trigger — can never be seen. Owns: recording each storm-control refusal (tenant, initiator, limit, instant) and a read over them, which turns the breakers' deferral into a condition anyone can evaluate. The breakers themselves stay deferred on it.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — four producers built the `429` by hand and stored nothing: the two fan-out caps in `open_recruitment_call` and, since REPAIR-0415, the cycle and depth refusals in `create_thread_auto`. CENSUS at `0d387f3`: `git grep -n '"storm_control"' 0d387f3 -- crates/reasonbraid-server/src` → **3** sites, all in `api.rs`, none followed by an insert. A trigger nothing evaluates (`.11.4.7.2.1`'s shape).
- [x] **ADDRESSED** — `migrations/0091_storm_refusals.sql` (`refusal_id`, `tenant_id` → `tenants`, `initiator`, `control`, `limit_value`, `target`, `message`, `refused_at`; `control` deliberately unconstrained, the `0088` reasoning). ONE helper, `api.rs::refuse_storm`, records the row and returns the `429`; it is the only place the wire code is spelled as a value — census `grep -c '"storm_control"' crates/reasonbraid-server/src/api.rs` → **1** — so a producer cannot refuse without recording, and a storage failure is an internal error rather than a silent refusal. The four producers go through it (`open_calls_per_tenant` 8, `open_calls_per_initiator` 4, `autonomous_cycle`, `autonomous_depth` with the ceiling in force), each naming the principal and the thread the request named. `GET /v1/admin/storm-refusals?tenant_id=` (`TenantAdminInspection::StormRefusals`, the own-tenant inspection gate) lists them newest first; absent facts omitted. The breaker trigger is now a query: `SELECT count(DISTINCT tenant_id) FROM storm_refusals WHERE refused_at > now() - interval '1 hour'` ≥ 2. Surface judged: `.doctrine/book_surface_verdicts.tsv` admin family `21:-` → `22:-` with the new route named; 26 checked purge plans gained the table. Book: `recruitment.md` (the section, with a real response shape), `authority.md` (the admin table), `errors.md` (the `storm_control` row).
- [x] **VERIFIED** — `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh profiles authority migration_upgrade operator_surfaces health administrative_effects` → profiles **72**, authority 22, migration_upgrade 8, operator_surfaces 1, health 3, administrative_effects 25 — **131 passed, 0 failed**. The storm fixture asserts that after its fifth open the list holds exactly one row — `open_calls_per_initiator`, `limit_value` 4, the human as initiator, the seeded thread as target, and `message` equal to the words the caller was given; the chain fixture asserts two rows newest first — `autonomous_depth` with `limit_value` 3 naming the fourth role and `t3`, then `autonomous_cycle` with NO `limit_value` naming the first role and `t1`. Core: the kind round-trips in `authorization_evaluation` (68 + 10).
- [x] **FALSIFIED** — `refuse_storm` mutated to answer the `429` BEFORE recording, observed RED on the whole `profiles` suite and restored byte-identically (`shasum -a 256 -c` OK): the chain fixture lists `{"refusals": []}` — `left: 0 right: 2` at `crates/reasonbraid-server/tests/profiles.rs:2057` — and the storm fixture the same — `left: 0 right: 1` at `crates/reasonbraid-server/tests/profiles.rs:1695`; `70 passed; 2 failed`. (A first mutation that removed the statement did not compile and so proved nothing; it is recorded here rather than counted.)
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — every other `profiles` control passes; `authority`, `migration_upgrade` (applies `0091` over the fixture history), `operator_surfaces` (the §18.5 mapping is unchanged — §18.5 names no storm surface, so the tsv is not widened), `health`, `administrative_effects` green; strict clippy clean on core and server (`-D warnings`); `cargo fmt`; `make gate`; `make book`.
- ⚠️ **Honest limit, owned:** the first run recorded the fan-out caps' initiator as the `agt_` actor HANDLE (the counter's key) where the auto route recorded the principal; caught by the control's own assertion and corrected to the principal id before commit — the record now names what an operator can resolve.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0423`.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.7.2.1.5.4.3 — A grant's conditions have no vocabulary

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0440`; the decision is `REASONBRAID-DOC-0147` (`docs/decisions/2026-09-23_a-grants-conditions-are-a-closed-typed-evaluable-vocabulary.md`), taken under the director's delegation of 2026-09-23 and shipped with the repair.
- 🔴 As found: §4.2 named `conditions[]` and nothing defined a condition. Candidates — a purpose (as `DelegationConstraints.purpose` already carries), a time window, a requesting network — were product decisions. ⛔ Not built until the vocabulary was decided, so the field was never declared-and-unread.
- ⚖️ **Decided: a closed, typed, evaluable vocabulary** — a member is a typed variant, an issuance rule, an evaluator over facts the admission already holds, a control and a book paragraph, nothing less; the first member is `within_hours` (the profile's operating-hours format, the same parser). Purpose (no command declares one), a requesting network (the admission holds no address), `human_present` (the evaluator is pure; the target's participants are the next facts to carry) and separation of duties (the policy chain's) are each rejected or deferred with the reason in the record.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.7.2.2 — The dependency gate is red: RUSTSEC-2026-0285

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.4.7.2`, which ran `cargo deny check` as the re-derivation of a G1 line and got rc=**1**.
- The finding: `advisories FAILED, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok`. **RUSTSEC-2026-0285** — rustls accepted TLS 1.3 handshake messages sent at the wrong encryption level when they followed a key-changing message in the same record. `rustls 0.23.43`; the advisory names ≥0.23.45.
- ⭐ **The exposure is narrower than "a TLS vulnerability", and the leaf must say which.** The handshake transcript stays authenticated, so a network-position attacker cannot alter or complete a handshake. The practical effect is that a peer may send in PLAINTEXT what should have been encrypted without rustls rejecting the connection. ⛔ Do not restate it as handshake forgery.
- ⚠️ **This is DEPENDENCY drift, not advisory-database drift against a fixed graph.** `git show ecceb8d:Cargo.lock | grep -c '^name = "rustls"$'` returns **0** — rustls entered the graph after Phase 1 (positive control: the same command for `tokio` returns **1**).
- Owns: taking the upgrade, re-running the gate, and deciding whether `cargo update -p rustls` alone is right or the lockfile wants a wider refresh. ⚠️ A lockfile change is a supply-chain change: state what moved and what did not.
- Acceptance: `cargo deny check` rc=0 with all four sections ok; the diff to `Cargo.lock` is enumerated rather than summarised; the workspace builds and its suites pass afterwards; and the leaf records whether any OTHER advisory was masked by the run stopping at the first.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0199. `cargo update -p rustls` — `rustls 0.23.43 → 0.23.45`. `cargo deny check` now returns **`advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok`**, rc=0.
- ⭐ **The lock diff is FOUR LINES, enumerated rather than summarised**, which is the whole reason the acceptance asked for it: a lockfile bump is a supply-chain change, and "just a patch update" is a claim about a file nobody read.
  ```
  3824c3824  < version = "0.23.43"      > version = "0.23.45"
  3826c3826  < checksum = "0283386c…"  > checksum = "0d41d731…"
  ```
  ⛔ Nothing transitive moved. `cargo update` reported `Locking 1 package to latest compatible version` and named 37 unchanged dependencies behind latest, which are deliberately left alone: this leaf owns ONE advisory, not a lockfile refresh.
- **No other advisory was masked.** `cargo deny` does not stop at the first finding — it reports all four sections every run, and the failing run's advisories block contained exactly one `error[vulnerability]` (`grep -c '^error\[vulnerability\]'` = 1, `grep -c '^warning\['` = 0).
- ⭐ **The exposure, stated at its real width rather than as "a TLS vulnerability".** RUSTSEC-2026-0285: rustls accepted TLS 1.3 handshake messages sent at the wrong encryption level when they followed a key-changing message in the same record (RFC 8446 §5.1 requires terminating with `unexpected_message`). ⛔ The handshake transcript stays AUTHENTICATED, so a network-position attacker cannot alter or complete a handshake; the practical effect is that a peer may send in plaintext what should have been encrypted without rustls rejecting the connection. Functionally the same bug as Go's CVE-2025-61730.
- **NO REGRESSION, and it is the strongest evidence this tree has had all session:** `cargo test --all --locked --no-fail-fast` reaches **94 test binaries**, **102 suites ok / 1 failed**, **815 tests passed / 1 failed**. The single failure in the entire workspace is `.11.4.7.2.4`'s known browser control, which predates this change and reproduces without it.
- ⭐ **That run also ANSWERS `.11.4.7.2.4`'s `--no-fail-fast` question with a measurement rather than a preference.** Default fail-fast reached **11** binaries and left four crates unknown; `--no-fail-fast` reached **94** and turned "unknown" into "one known failure". Cost: **319.3 s** of test execution, dominated by one 135.23 s suite. ⚠️ The verdict belongs to `.11.4.7.2.4`, which owns it — recorded here because this leaf is what produced the number.
- ⛔ No product code, schema, migration, test or script changed. `Cargo.lock` is the entire diff.
- promotion: declined. The method exercised — enumerate a dependency diff instead of summarising it — is an instance of `docs/knowledge/a-census-is-an-instrument-not-a-table`, not a new statement.
- Verification: `cargo deny check` rc=0; `cargo test --all --locked --no-fail-fast` 815 passed / 1 pre-existing failure; `make gate` 18 checks rc=0.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0199 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.7.2.2): take the rustls advisory, and enumerate the four lines it moved`.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.7.2.3 — The secret scan is red on a test fixture

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.4.7.2`, which ran `gitleaks detect --source . --redact` as the re-derivation of a G1 line and got rc=**1**.
- The finding: one hit, rule `generic-api-key`, at `crates/reasonbraid-core/tests/delegation_representation.rs:74` — the literal `idempotency_key: "…"`, entropy 3.875 — introduced 2026-09-13 by REPAIR-0134 (`.3.4.5`).
- ⭐ **It is a FALSE POSITIVE and the gate is red anyway, and both halves matter.** A sixteen-hex-character test fixture is not a credential; a red gate is still a red gate, and a project that lets one sit goes blind to the next true positive.
- ⛔ Two repairs are available and they are NOT equivalent. `.gitleaksignore` takes **exact historical fingerprints only** and says so in its own header (`SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.3.1.2.2`, provenance in `docs/decisions/2026-09-09_history-fixture-fingerprints.md`) — suppressing the PATH or the RULE is explicitly forbidden there. The alternative is to change the fixture so it does not read as a secret. ⚠️ Prefer the fixture change where it costs nothing: an allowlist entry is a permanent claim about a line, and the line is a test constant nobody depends on.
- ⚠️ **CI would fail identically** — `scripts/ci_scanners.py` pins gitleaks 8.30.1 and runs `detect --source . --redact=100`, the same detection with the same rules. This is not a local-tooling artifact.
- Owns: the repair, plus the question `.11.4.7.2` raised and did not own — whether `make deny` and `make secret-scan` should join the commit-time gate rather than living only in a CI workflow that has never run.
- ⚠️ That question needs a MEASUREMENT, not a preference: both are slower than the 18 doctrines, and `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.5`'s constraint is that a gate people route around is a gate that lies. Time them before proposing either.
- Acceptance: `gitleaks detect --source . --redact` rc=0; the leaf states which of the two repairs was taken and why the other was not; if an allowlist entry was used, it is an exact fingerprint with a reason; and the commit-time-gate question carries the timing census that settles it.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0200. `gitleaks detect --source . --redact` now returns **`no leaks found`**, rc=0.
- 🔴 **BOTH repairs were taken, because measuring proved my planned one INSUFFICIENT.** The leaf said to prefer the fixture rename and avoid an allowlist entry. ⛔ **A rename cannot reach a historical finding.** `gitleaks detect` scans all 488 commits, and the finding is attributed to the commit that INTRODUCED the line: after renaming, the scan still returned rc=1 with `fingerprint=b3802b16601fb4a2da67a8721d7659ae1e36aed9:crates/reasonbraid-core/tests/delegation_representation.rs:generic-api-key:74`. ⭐ The exact-fingerprint entry is the ONLY instrument that clears it — which is precisely what `.gitleaksignore`'s header says it is for, and what its two existing entries are.
- **The fingerprint** carries its reason inline: a verified test constant, an envelope field in a byte-size instrument, referenced nowhere else (`git grep -c` returns 1). ⛔ The path and the rule are NOT suppressed — `.gitleaksignore` forbids that in its own header.
- **The rename is kept anyway, as forward hygiene**: `b3f1c2d4e5a60718` → `key-delegation-1`. Every sibling fixture already spells these readably (`k-forged`, `client-key-0001`, `key_ac5_second`); the hex blob was the single outlier, and the next author copies what they see.
- ⚠️ **The rename is EXACTLY 16 characters, and that is load-bearing.** `delegation_representation.rs:172` asserts `baseline == 308` — a byte count over the serialized envelope, which contains this field. A shorter or longer name would have silently moved a measurement instrument's number. The file now says so in a comment, so nobody "tidies" it back.
- ⭐ **THE COMMIT-TIME-GATE QUESTION, SETTLED ON WHAT EACH CHECK IS TRIGGERED BY rather than on cost.** A commit CAN introduce a secret → the secret scan is **change-triggered** and belongs in the commit gate. An advisory appears against code nobody touched → `cargo deny` is **TIME-triggered**, so gating it on commits is both too often and too rarely, and a push is the moment the claim leaves the machine.
  - `SECRET-SCAN` added to `scripts/check_doctrines.project.sh` — the 10th project check. Priced first (`.11.5`): **1.07 / 1.14 / 1.15 s** over three runs, scanning 488 commits and 15.11 MB, against a **6.65 s** enforcer — about +17%.
  - `.githooks/pre-push` created, running `cargo deny check` — **1.15 s** with the advisory database cached under the repository-local `CARGO_HOME` (`.project-data/cargo/advisory-dbs`, so §13 holds).
  - ⚠️ **The enforcer's own published cost was STALE**: `check_self_tests.sh`'s header records "about 3.15 s". Measured today: **6.65 s**. Not corrected here — it is another file's number and correcting it in passing is how a leaf stops being bounded — but recorded so the next reader does not inherit it.
- ⛔ **Both new gates SKIP LOUDLY rather than failing closed when their tool is absent**, and that is a deliberate weakening with a stated reason: failing closed would block every contributor who has not installed `gitleaks` or `cargo-deny`. ⚠️ A skip is a weaker guarantee than a pass and must never READ like one, so each prints a notice naming what was not checked.
- **FALSIFIED, three arms, each self-reversing and each proved restored by `cmp -s`:** removing the fingerprint → `SECRET-SCAN` rc=1 naming the re-run command; `PATH` stripped of `gitleaks` → rc=0 with `SECRET-SCAN: SKIPPED` on stderr, never a silent pass; restoring `rustls 0.23.43` in `Cargo.lock` → `pre-push` rc=1, printing the advisory and `pre-push: REFUSED`. Positive control afterwards: rc=0.
- promotion: declined. The transferable half — that a control's reach is a property of what it SCANS, not of what you changed — is an instance of `docs/knowledge/a-claim-of-sameness-is-worth-its-call-graph`; the rest is this repository's tooling.
- Verification: `gitleaks detect --source . --redact` rc=0; `cargo test -p reasonbraid-core --test delegation_representation --locked` 2 passed, so `baseline == 308` survives the rename; `bash scripts/check_doctrines.project.sh` rc=0; `bash .githooks/pre-push` rc=0; `make gate` 18 checks rc=0.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0200 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.7.2.3): clear the secret scan, and give each supply-chain gate the trigger it actually has`.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.7.2.4 — A control asserts the exact fact its own repair made honest

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.4.7.2`, whose G1 unit-baseline re-derivation ran the workspace suite and got rc=101.
- The failure: `crates/reasonbraid-browse/tests/browser_roundtrip.rs:582`, `a_real_navigation_deadline_stops_the_browser_and_origin`, asserting `response["error"]["cleanup_confirmed"] == true`. Observed `false`, with `cleanup_error: "browser stderr completion unconfirmed"`.
- ⭐ **The assertion ABOVE it passes.** `response["error"]["kind"] == "time_budget_exceeded"` holds — which means **REPAIR-0089's fix is working exactly as designed**. That repair found `Lifetime::finish` replacing the response's `kind` with the conjunction of four cleanup facts, and split them: `kind` keeps the render's own outcome, and `cleanup_confirmed` / `cleanup_error` carry the cleanup fact separately. The product is now telling the truth, and the control fails ON the truth.
- 🔴 **So this is not a flaky test and not a regression. It is a control asserting a property the product deliberately stopped claiming.** `docs/decisions/2026-09-10_browser-checkpoint-timing.md` records the cause: detached `chrome_crashpad_handler` and `GoogleUpdater` processes retain the browser's inherited stderr write endpoint after the group exits, so the stderr task cannot observe completion. REPAIR-0089's own note says the rule is "never to CLAIM an unobserved termination".
- ⛔ **NOT a load artifact, measured in both directions.** First observed inside `cargo test --all` while another project was compiling on the same machine (`elapsed_ms` 41170). Re-run ISOLATED on a quiet machine, single-threaded: identical failure, same line, `elapsed_ms` 40022, 81.30 s. Two runs, two load states, one result.
- ⚠️ **The blast radius is larger than one test, and that is why this is a leaf rather than a note.** `cargo test` stops at the first failing test binary, so this failure ABORTS the workspace run at the 11th of many: `reasonbraid-cli`, `-core`, `-node` and `-server` never execute. Every claim of the form "the suites are green" is therefore unverifiable on this machine until it is resolved — including the one `.11.4.7.2` was re-deriving.
- Owns: deciding which of the two is wrong. Either (a) the control over-asserts for a desktop runtime whose documented behaviour it cannot control, and should assert `kind` plus an explicit disposition of `cleanup_confirmed` rather than demanding `true`; or (b) the product genuinely should be able to confirm stderr completion despite the detached handlers, and does not.
- ⛔ **Do NOT resolve this by loosening the assertion to accept either value.** REPAIR-0089 explicitly refused that, for a stated reason: the control would stop proving that the deadline cancels a real in-flight navigation. Whatever is chosen must keep that proof.
- ⚠️ And do not resolve it by widening the 30-second budget: `NAVIGATION_WINDOW` is the thing under test, the render reaches ~40 s against it, and the budget was already refused as a fix once.
- ⭐ Worth asking while here: whether the workspace run should use `--no-fail-fast`, so one environment-sensitive control cannot hide the state of four crates. ⚠️ That is a measurement about run time, not a preference — price it.
- ⭐ **PRICED, at `.11.4.7.2.2` (REPAIR-0199), and the number settles it.** Default fail-fast reaches **11** test binaries and leaves `cli`, `core`, `node` and `server` UNKNOWN. `--no-fail-fast` reaches **94**: **102 suites ok / 1 failed, 815 tests passed / 1 failed**, in **319.3 s** of test execution (one suite is 135.23 s of that). ⛔ So the cost of knowing is not extra failures — there is exactly ONE failure in the whole workspace, this one — it is run time on a run that already takes minutes. ⚠️ This leaf still owns the DECISION and where it belongs (`make test`? a pre-push path?); what it no longer owns is the measurement.
- Acceptance: the failure is reproduced and attributed to (a) or (b) with runtime evidence, never to "flaky"; the repair keeps REPAIR-0089's proof that the deadline cancels a real navigation; `cargo test --all --locked` reaches every crate afterwards and its result is recorded whatever it is; and if `--no-fail-fast` is adopted, the timing census that justified it is in the leaf.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0202.
- 🔴 **THE LEAF'S OWN (a)/(b) CHOICE IS REFUTED, AND THE ANSWER IS A THIRD THING IT DID NOT OFFER: THE RUN HAD PICKED ITS OWN BROWSER.** `crates/reasonbraid-browse/tests/support/mod.rs::browser_binary()` carried a discovery list, so any run that did not go through `scripts/ci_browser.py` — a bare `cargo test --all`, which is exactly what `.11.4.7.2` and `.11.4.7.2.2` used — silently selected `/Applications/Google Chrome.app/…`. The control is qualified against the runtime `.11.4.3.1.2.5` pinned; it was being evaluated against the desktop browser that pin exists to avoid. ⭐ **A pin a second path can bypass is not a pin.**
- **The two-site contrast, one variable.** Same test binary, same machine, same competing load — another repository's release build held a core at 98.8% across both arms, so load is a CONSTANT here rather than a confound — and `R3_BROWSER_BIN` is the only thing that changes:

  | runtime | verdict | worker elapsed | escaped handler last seen | survival past the worker's own exit |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | desktop Google Chrome 152.0.7977.83 | cleanup unconfirmed, FAILED 4 of 4 | 41.07 s | +47.18 s | +6.24 s |
  | pinned Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.36 | cleanup confirmed, PASSED 2 of 2 | 31.13 s | +30.97 s | 0, inside one 150 ms sample |

  ⭐ The ten-second gap between the elapsed times is not noise: it is `CLEANUP_BUDGET` being spent in full on an end-of-file that cannot arrive.
- **PINPOINTED at the file descriptor, never inferred.** `lsof -p` on both processes during a failing run, sampled every 500 ms: the worker's fd 11 is `PIPE 0xbb56abe118065101 ->0x2e37041051b342b4` and `chrome_crashpad_handler`'s fd 2 is `PIPE 0x2e37041051b342b4 ->0xbb56abe118065101` — the two ends of ONE pipe, printed by the kernel rather than deduced. That handler reports `PPID 1` and process group `45254` while the owned browser group was `45239`: it left the group the worker owns and kept the inherited stderr write end. `Lifetime::finish` reaps the owned group — and `verify_browser_groups()` independently confirms its absence — then waits for `read_stderr` to reach EOF, which needs the ESCAPED holder to close too.
- 🔴 **AND THE PINNED RUNTIME ESCAPES IDENTICALLY — the tidy story is wrong.** Under Chrome for Testing the same instrument shows TWO handlers at `PPID 1`, process groups `50752` and `50754` against an owned group of `50742`, both holding `0xe8181443c00b5a90`, whose peer is the worker's fd 11. The structure is the same; only the EXIT LATENCY differs. ⛔ So this control's green is a property of how fast a third-party process exits, **not** a containment guarantee, and saying so is the difference between closing a question and hiding one. Annotated at `.7.3.2`, which owns detached-descendant containment, rather than left as a passing test's implied claim.
- **The repair, in the test harness and nowhere else.** `browser_binary()` is now `std::env::var_os("R3_BROWSER_BIN").map(PathBuf::from)` and nothing more. `ci_browser.py` sets that variable to the build it has just downloaded, SHA-256-verified and version-checked; `make test` and `.github/workflows/rust.yml` both run the workspace suite through it, so the qualified path loses nothing.
- ⛔ **NO PRODUCT CODE CHANGED, and that is a finding rather than an omission.** The worker was right on every run: an escaped descendant holding the pipe IS an unaccounted-for browser process, and `a_render_refusal_survives_an_unconfirmed_cleanup` pins that reading deliberately with an injected `setsid` writer. "Repairing" this in `lifetime.rs` would have meant claiming a termination nobody observed — the exact thing REPAIR-0089 refused by name.
- ⚠️ **A SKIP MUST NEVER READ LIKE A PASS, and this one nearly did.** Removing the fallback turns six failures into six skips, and `libtest` captures `println!`/`eprintln!` and replays them only for a FAILING test — invisible in precisely the run that needs them. MEASURED rather than assumed, with a one-test `rustc --test` probe: a write through the `std::io::stderr()` HANDLE escapes the capture and the macros do not (`PROBE-direct-stderr-handle` printed, `test result: ok. 1 passed`, the two macro lines absent). `support::skip_without_browser` uses the handle, so an ordinary `cargo test -p reasonbraid-browse` prints six lines naming what went unqualified and the command that qualifies it.
- ⭐ **THE `--no-fail-fast` DECISION, TAKEN — on `.11.4.7.2.2`'s priced census rather than on preference.** Default fail-fast reaches **11** of 94 test binaries and leaves `cli`, `core`, `node` and `server` UNKNOWN; `--no-fail-fast` reaches **94** — 102 suites ok / 1 failed, 815 passed / 1 failed — for **319.3 s** of test execution, one suite being 135.23 s of it. ⛔ The cost of knowing is not extra failures; it is that a RED run now pays full price instead of stopping early. A command whose job is to answer *is the workspace green* cannot answer it from 11 binaries, so `--no-fail-fast` is adopted in `make test` and in the `rust.yml` workspace command — the two places that run the whole workspace — and nowhere else. ⚠️ The number is one leaf old and its producing command is recorded, so it is REUSED rather than re-derived; this line says so instead of implying a fresh measurement.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.8 — The only qualified browser path does not fit its own deadline on this machine

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.4.7.2.4`, which made `make test` the ONLY way to qualify a browser control and then watched what that costs.
- 🔴 **AND THE FIRST RUN AFTER THAT CHANGE WAS CUT OFF, which is how this leaf stopped being about bandwidth alone.** `make test` reached **78 of ~94 test binaries with ZERO failures** and then died at `ci_browser.py`'s own `COMMAND_SECONDS = 3600` cap: `ci-browser: refused: Command [...] timed out after 3600 seconds`, `make: *** [test] Error 2`. ⛔ **A gate that cannot finish reports nothing**, and this is the ONLY path that can now qualify a browser control.
- **Censused rather than asserted: this is the FIRST timeout in the harness's history here.** Of 16 `target/ci-browser/*/browser.json` receipts, 12 read `completed exit=0`, 3 read `completed exit=101` (real test failures) and exactly 1 reads `failed … TimeoutExpired` — this run.
- ⛔ **NOT attributable to `--no-fail-fast`, and the argument is stated rather than assumed.** Fail-fast stops at a FAILURE; with zero failures in the 78 binaries that ran, both settings do identical work. ⚠️ That is reasoning, not a measurement, and this leaf owns measuring it — the honest reading is that the flag is not exonerated until a completed run exists with and without it.
- **What IS measured about the cost, from this project's own records:** macOS validates each freshly written executable on its FIRST run at about **21.9 s** apiece on this volume against 0.15 s on the boot volume (`.11.4.3.1.2.15`), and this run compiled every test binary from cold — roughly 34 minutes of validation before a single assertion. On top of that, a competing release build from another repository held a core at 98.8% for the entire run.
- **The finding, read from the source rather than timed once.** `scripts/ci_browser.py::execute` downloads `archive.zip` on EVERY invocation — `PINNED_ARCHIVES["mac-arm64"]` is **191,016,009 bytes** — extracts it member by member with size and link validation, verifies the executable's version, and on success `shutil.rmtree(runtime)` plus `archive.unlink()` retire the payload. So a second run repeats the whole acquisition. ⭐ The retirement is DELIBERATE and correct as a containment property (`.11.4.3.1.2.5`: each call owns its download; a failure retains it for inspection); what has never been priced is its recurring cost now that it sits on the only qualified path.
- ⚠️ **Measured incidentally, not as a census**: one invocation this session had reached 154 MB of 191 MB after roughly two minutes. `du -sh target/ci-browser/` returns **2.2 G** across **16** workspaces — twelve retired theirs and occupy 8.0 K each, while **three retained failures keep 542 M apiece** (the archive AND the extracted runtime, not the archive alone, which is why a first estimate of ~573 M was low by a factor of three).
- ⛔ **The tension is real and must not be resolved by removing the verification.** The pin's value is that the bytes are hash-checked on the path that uses them; a cached runtime that nothing re-verifies is a different guarantee wearing the same name. ⚠️ `.11.5`'s constraint applies directly: a gate people route around is a gate that lies, and a two-minute download in front of every browser control is exactly the shape people route around — which is how the fallback this leaf's parent deleted came to matter in the first place.
- Owns: a COMPLETED qualified workspace run and the deadline that admits it — whether `COMMAND_SECONDS` rises, whether `make test` passes its own `--timeout`, or whether the workspace run is tiered so the browser harness wraps only the suites that need a browser; pricing the acquisition (download, extraction, version check) as three separate numbers rather than one; deciding whether a repository-local verified cache keyed by the recorded SHA-256 preserves the property the per-call download provides, including what re-verification a cache hit must still perform; and the disposition of the three retained failure payloads, against `scripts/census_pg_test_clusters.py`'s precedent of measuring before retiring.
- Acceptance: one COMPLETED `cargo test --all --locked --no-fail-fast` under the pinned runtime, with its binary count, pass/fail totals and wall-clock recorded, and the deadline change that admitted it named; the three phase timings recorded from at least two runs; an explicit statement of which property the per-call download provides and whether a verified cache provides the same one or a weaker one, named either way; a decision taken with its reason; and, if a cache is adopted, a falsification showing a corrupted or substituted cached payload is refused.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0203.
- ✅ **THE COMPLETED RUN EXISTS, AND IT IS GREEN.** `python3 -B scripts/project_env.py python3 -B scripts/ci_browser.py --timeout 7200 -- cargo test --all --locked --no-fail-fast` returns rc=**0** with `ci-browser: completed; evidence target/ci-browser/mac-arm64-_kx2kgdt`: **94 test binaries plus 9 doc-test targets — 103 suites, 816 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored**, in `real 30m15.757s`.
- ⭐ **The arithmetic against `.11.4.7.2.2` is exact, which is what makes it checkable.** That run measured **815 passed / 1 failed** over the same 94 binaries; this one measures **816 passed / 0 failed**. One test moved from failed to passed and nothing else moved — precisely `.11.4.7.2.4`'s control. ⛔ And **zero** `SKIP (R3_BROWSER_BIN unset)` lines appear, so the qualified path skips nothing: the 816 is full coverage, not coverage minus six.
- **THE THREE ACQUISITION PHASES, measured separately as the acceptance asked**, by watching `ci_browser.py`'s own fsynced receipt rather than by instrumenting the script under measurement:

  | phase | elapsed | what it moved |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | download | 51.54 s | 191,016,009 bytes at about 3.7 MB/s |
  | extract + binary SHA-256 | 0.63 s | 675 entries, 5 links, 375,683,518 expanded bytes |
  | version check | 1.86 s | one execution of the binary, output compared to the pinned version string |
  | **acquisition total** | **55.27 s** | from process start to the first test |

  ⚠️ The extraction figure is fast enough to deserve its limit stated: the writes land in the page cache rather than on the platter, so 0.63 s is the cost the RUN pays, not a durable-write measurement.
- ⛔ **SO THE CACHE IS REFUSED, and the number is the whole argument.** Acquisition is **55.27 s of a 1,872 s run — 3.0%** — and 93% of that is the download. **The property the per-call download provides**: these exact bytes, fetched from the pinned origin and hash-checked by THIS process on THIS invocation. **What a cache would provide**: bytes verified on some earlier invocation, re-hashed on the hit — nearly the same guarantee, but trusting the local filesystem between runs instead of re-fetching. ⚠️ Nearly is not the same, and the price of the difference is **52 seconds**. A containment property is not worth trading for 3%.
- ⭐ **THE DEADLINE IS THE REAL DEFECT, and it is fixed in two places rather than by raising a number.** (1) `make test` and `.github/workflows/rust.yml` now run `cargo test --all --locked --no-run` BEFORE entering the browser harness, so its deadline bounds test EXECUTION rather than a compile. (2) Both pass `--timeout 5400` for the workspace run, leaving `COMMAND_SECONDS = 3600` as the script's default for the crate-scoped invocations the book documents, which finish in 31 s.
- ⚠️ **The cold path is NOT re-measured, and the leaf says so rather than implying otherwise.** 5400 rests on TWO observations — a warm run executing in 1,816.78 s, and a cold run cut off at 78 of 94 binaries by the 3600 s cap — not on a third run from a wiped `target/`. ⛔ The remaining cost inside the harness on a cold tree is macOS validating each freshly written executable on its FIRST run, about 21.9 s apiece here (`.11.4.3.1.2.15`), which `--no-run` does NOT move because validation happens at execution. ⭐ **The instrument that will actually settle it is the remote runner** — a cold Linux checkout with no such validation cost — which is blocker **C1**.
- **The retained payloads, censused before retiring, on `scripts/census_pg_test_clusters.py`'s precedent.** `du -sh target/ci-browser/` measured **2.2 G** across 16 workspaces: 12 had retired their own payload (8.0 K each) and **4 retained 542 M apiece**. ⛔ `mac-arm64-0281kcb0` is KEPT because `docs/tasks/artifacts/signoff_review/extraction-fixture-ownership.md:18` says in tracked text that it "remains preserved" — deleting it would make a committed sentence false. The other three were retired to **8.0 K** each, keeping `browser.json` and `version.log`: each receipt carries `archive_sha256` and `binary_sha256`, so the payload is byte-reproducible from the pin, and the receipt was the evidence all along. `target/ci-browser/` now measures **542 M**.
- promotion: declined. The transferable half — that a deadline should bound the phase it is about, and that a cost is priced as a RATIO against the run it sits in — is already carried by `docs/knowledge/a-census-is-an-instrument-not-a-table` and by `TOOLBOX.md`'s slow-gate section, which this leaf applied rather than extended.
- Verification: the completed run above, rc=0, 816 passed / 0 failed. `make gate` 18 checks rc=0; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0; `make -n test` expands to the three steps in order. ⛔ No Rust source changed in this leaf — the diff is two build-command files and a task tree.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0203 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.8): the qualified run finishes, and the deadline now bounds what it is about`.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.6 — Which shipped surfaces the book does not cover, measured before it is called a gap

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.6.1.1`, which repaired an agent-facing surface and found the book says nothing about it.
- Finding, concretely: the six MCP tools are a shipped, user-visible surface — three reads and three writes, with authorization semantics a caller must understand — and `docs/book/src/SUMMARY.md` has no chapter for them. ⛔ **CORRECTED 2026-09-21 (`.11.4.6.1`): IT HAS ONE, AND A SIBLING LEAF PUT IT THERE.** `docs/book/src/mcp.md` has existed since `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0294` (`SIGNOFF-REPAIR.6.5`) — 7,539 bytes, all six tools in two tables with the admission each performs and its HTTP twin, the enrolment binding, the per-principal quota and a *what a client sees when it is refused* section — with `mcp-listen.md` beside it. So this leaf's second acceptance clause was **already met** when it was read back. The superseded sentence stands per `TOOLBOX.md` as the record of a finding a sibling closed while this leaf went on stating it — the `.11.2.1.1` shape exactly. `.6.1.1`'s repair changed that surface's behaviour (a tool parameter removed, refusals added where a caller previously got data) and the only place it could be written down was `qualification-review.md`, which is a findings page, not a surface page.
- ⛔ **The population, NOT a defect count.** `grep -o '"/v1/[a-z-]*' crates/reasonbraid-server/src/api.rs | sed 's|"/v1/||' | sort -u` -> **29 route families**; `docs/book/src/SUMMARY.md` lists **15 content chapters** *(⚠️ **CORRECTED by `.11.4.6.1`: both were published UNPINNED and both moved — 30 families and 22 `SUMMARY.md` entries at `05f3fe7`, 18 of them content once the four meta pages are set aside.** And the command is narrower than its subject: five files under the server's `src/` register routes, three of them declare a `/v1/` family, and deriving over all five returns the same 30 — so it was right by luck. Re-derive rather than read: `python3 -B scripts/census_book_coverage.py`)*, and the two are not 1:1 — one chapter can cover a family (`profiles.md` covers `/v1/profiles`), several families can belong to one subject (the eleven `policy-*` families), and several chapters cover no route family at all (the CLI, the node journal, the demonstration). ⛔ Publishing "14 surfaces are undocumented" from that subtraction would be the exact anti-pattern `docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` names: a search count shipped as a defect count. Classification is the first half of this leaf, not a step before it.
- ⭐ Precedent, and it CLOSED: `.11.4` records the same shape for `/v1/profiles` — "no book chapter at all", routed here to be written once the wire behaviour settled. `docs/book/src/profiles.md` now exists and covers it. The route works; the backlog it implies has never been enumerated.
- Owns: the classification — for each route family and each non-HTTP surface, whether it is (a) covered by a chapter, (b) deliberately internal, or (c) a genuine gap — and then the gaps, written or explicitly declined with a reason. The MCP tools are the first known (c). ⛔ **CORRECTED: they are not — see the finding above.** The population is `.11.4.6.1` (`done`); the per-member judgement is `.11.4.6.2`.
- ⭐ **AND THE POPULATION, ONCE MEASURED, SAYS WHERE TO LOOK.** Of the 30 route families, **9 are mentioned by no chapter at all**, and **seven of the nine are `policy-*`** ⚠️ **CORRECTED: it is SIX of the nine, not seven** — `policy-decisions`, `policy-drift`, `policy-outcomes`, `policy-projections`, `policy-proposals`, `policy-reviews`; the other three are `audit`, `deployments` and `evaluations`. The nine themselves re-derive exactly. : `policy-decisions`, `policy-drift`, `policy-outcomes`, `policy-projections`, `policy-proposals`, `policy-reviews`, plus `audit`, `deployments` and `evaluations`. The gap is CONCENTRATED in the policy lifecycle rather than spread across the surface, which is a different backlog from the one this leaf opened expecting.
- Acceptance: a classified census, by command, in this leaf, with every family in exactly one of the three states and the (b) entries carrying their reason; an MCP tools chapter in `SUMMARY.md` describing the six tools, their authorization and their refusals, with `.6.1.1`'s repaired semantics in it; and `BOOK-LINKS` plus `mdbook build` green.
- ⚠️ Ranked below the live defects: this is a coverage gap, not a wrong statement. ⛔ It is NOT a `LIVE-DOC-CURRENCY` or `BOOK-FRONTIER` breach — both of those police what the book SAYS; nothing gates what it omits, which is why this went unmeasured.
- ✅ **CLOSED, and something now DOES gate what the book omits.** The sentence above — *nothing gates what it omits* — was true when written and is no longer: `SURFACE-JUDGEMENT` refuses a commit that adds a shipped surface nobody has judged. That is the leaf's most durable output, because the coverage this leaf restored would otherwise decay exactly as it accumulated.
- ✅ **THE THREE ACCEPTANCE CLAUSES, each met and each verified**: (1) *a classified census with every family in exactly one of three states and the (b) entries carrying their reason* — `.doctrine/book_surface_verdicts.tsv`, **43 members, 40 covered · 3 internal · 0 gap**, every `internal` naming its reason and the guard refusing an unjudged one; (2) *an MCP tools chapter* — already met before this leaf ran, which `.11.4.6.1` found and corrected in place; (3) *`BOOK-LINKS` plus `mdbook build` green* — both rc=0.
- ⭐ **AND THE BACKLOG IT OPENED EXPECTING IS NOT THE ONE IT CLOSED.** It opened on *fourteen undocumented surfaces* derived by subtraction. The measured population was **17 gaps over 43 members**, and the largest single cause was not absence at all: **fourteen routes were already explained and simply never addressed**, repaired by seven contract blocks rather than fourteen sections (`.11.4.6.6`, promoted as `a-coverage-gap-names-what-is-missing-not-what-is-absent`).
- ⭐ **Every `/v1/` product route is now documented.** `census_route_documentation.py` moves **62 described / 2 mentioned / 40 absent** at the leaf's start to **101 / 1 / 2**, and the remaining three are the console's own page and its two assets.
- Status: `done`; children `.1`–`.8` all `done`.
- Verification / commit: per child; the closing child is `.11.4.6.8` (DOC-0117), whose acceptance section also records this parent's closure.

The `.11.33.1` class again: a number true when taken, carrying no revision.

- Owns: the population instrument and the parent's stale finding. ⛔ NOT the classification itself — deciding that a family is *deliberately internal* is a judgement per member, and `docs/knowledge/a-sample-is-not-a-traversal.md` is explicit that prose cannot hold it: it belongs in a table keyed to each member, guarded so it refuses when a member exists that nothing judged. That is `.11.4.6.2`.

- ⭐ **AND THE MEASUREMENT REFRAMES THE BACKLOG.** **9 of the 30 route families are mentioned by no chapter**, and **seven of the nine are `policy-*`** ⚠️ **CORRECTED: it is SIX of the nine, not seven** — `policy-decisions`, `policy-drift`, `policy-outcomes`, `policy-projections`, `policy-proposals`, `policy-reviews`; the other three are `audit`, `deployments` and `evaluations`. The nine themselves re-derive exactly.  — `policy-decisions`, `policy-drift`, `policy-outcomes`, `policy-projections`, `policy-proposals`, `policy-reviews` — with `audit`, `deployments` and `evaluations` the other three. The gap is CONCENTRATED in the policy lifecycle, not spread across the surface, so the backlog `.11.4.6` implies is one subject rather than fourteen.
