##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.6.2 — The judgement, keyed to each member so it cannot be a sentence

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.4.6.1`, which measured the population and deliberately stopped short of judging it.
- **The question, per member**: each of the 30 route families and 10 binaries is (a) covered by a chapter, (b) deliberately internal, or (c) a genuine gap. ⛔ Only (a) is decidable by machine, and even then only as *some chapter mentions it*; (b) and (c) are judgements.
- ⭐ **THE SHAPE IS ALREADY DECIDED BY THIS PROJECT'S OWN KNOWLEDGE.** `docs/knowledge/a-sample-is-not-a-traversal.md` is explicit: *if the argument genuinely requires a statement about every member, prose will not hold it. Carry the judgement as a table keyed to each member, and guard it so that it refuses when a member exists that nothing judged; a judgement exists for a member that is gone; a member's inputs have changed since it was judged.* The third is the one usually missing and the one that makes a stale judgement look current.
- **Where to look first, measured rather than guessed**: **9 of 30 families are mentioned by no chapter**, and **seven of the nine are `policy-*`** ⚠️ **CORRECTED: it is SIX of the nine, not seven** — `policy-decisions`, `policy-drift`, `policy-outcomes`, `policy-projections`, `policy-proposals`, `policy-reviews`; the other three are `audit`, `deployments` and `evaluations`. The nine themselves re-derive exactly.  — `policy-decisions`, `policy-drift`, `policy-outcomes`, `policy-projections`, `policy-proposals`, `policy-reviews` — with `audit`, `deployments` and `evaluations` the other three. ⭐ That is one subject, not nine, so the likely answer is a policy-lifecycle chapter rather than nine pages.
- ⚠️ **The binary half is a weak signal and must not be judged from it.** *0 of 10 unmentioned* rests on matching a bare name, and `rb` is two letters; it reads as *no binary is obviously absent*, never as *every binary is documented*.
- Acceptance: every member of both populations carries a judgement in a tracked table, with (b) entries naming their reason; the table is guarded so a member nothing judged refuses, and so a judgement for a member that is gone refuses; the gaps that survive are written or explicitly declined with a reason; and `BOOK-LINKS` plus `mdbook build` stay green.
- 🔴 **THE COARSE SIGNAL OVERSTATES COVERAGE, AND THE JUDGEMENT MUST NOT BE READ OFF IT.** `.11.4.6.1` asks *does any chapter mention this family*, which makes **21 of 30** look covered. Asked per ROUTE — does the book name each of the family's routes beside a method, `.11.8`'s own `described` test — only **14 of 30** have every route documented. **Seven families the coarse signal calls covered carry undocumented routes**: `admin` 7 of 17, `calls` 3 of 4, `nodes` 5 of 14, `federation-agreements` 2 of 3, `routing` 2 of 4, `policies` 1 of 3, `threads` 1 of 7.
- ⭐ **`calls` IS THE SHARPEST, AND A SIBLING HAD ALREADY PROVED IT BY HAND.** The coarse signal credits it to `authority.md`; `.11.8.1` re-derived that the collection `POST /v1/calls` is genuinely undocumented, the chapter's line being a contract for the ITEM route. A family-level mention test cannot see that, which is precisely why the judgement is per member and keyed to evidence rather than to a string hit.
- 🔴 **AND THE PINNED POPULATION DOES NOT COVER THE PRODUCT SURFACE.** 30 families is every family under `/v1/`, and **three product routes belong to no `/v1/` family at all** — `/`, `/app.js`, `/style.css`. A population scoped to `/v1/` misses them exactly as a population scoped to route families would have missed all ten binaries (`.11.4.6.1`'s own finding, one lane over). They are judged here as a third member kind, so every product route is covered by something.
- ⭐ **AND THE `/` ROW IS WHY A TABLE BEATS THE SIGNAL IN THE OTHER DIRECTION TOO.** Mechanically `/` is a bare `mentioned`; in fact `docs/book/src/web-ui.md` is a whole chapter about the console served there. The machine under-reports it and the judgement corrects it — the same table catching the signal wrong in both directions.
- promotion: declined (both lessons are already recorded and this is a further instance of each: a per-member judgement belongs in a guarded table is `docs/knowledge/a-sample-is-not-a-traversal.md`, and keying it to the words it judged is `an-adjudication-is-keyed-to-the-words-it-judged.md`. ⭐ What is NEW here is recorded in `DEV_NOTES.md` rather than as a third file: a coarse signal can be wrong in BOTH directions at once, and the under-reporting half is the one that makes a table worth more than a count — a census that only over-reported could be fixed by tightening it.)
- Instrument: `scripts/census_surface_judgement.py` (`--check`, `--self-test`, `--json`); ledger `.doctrine/book_surface_verdicts.tsv`. ⛔ It does NOT re-implement the route classifier — it imports `census_route_documentation.py`, because a second copy of that logic is the exact drift this table exists to prevent.
- Status: `done`.
- Verification / commit: see the commit acceptance section for this leaf.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.6.3 — The policy lifecycle chapter: seven families, nine routes, one subject

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.4.6.2`, which adjudicated the surface and found this the largest concentration in it.
- The members, from `.doctrine/book_surface_verdicts.tsv` rather than from this sentence: `policy-decisions`, `policy-drift`, `policy-outcomes`, `policy-projections`, `policy-proposals` (one route each), `policy-reviews` (three: list, `schedule`, `{}/done`) and `policies`' `{}/{}/impact` read. ⛔ Re-derive with `python3 -B scripts/census_surface_judgement.py`; do not read the list from here.
- ⭐ Why one chapter and not seven pages: the six `policy-*` families are stages of ONE lifecycle — a proposal is reviewed, decided, published, and its outcomes, projections and drift are read back. `policy-approvals`, `policy-corrections` and `policy-publications` are already `covered`, so the chapter joins documented stages to undocumented ones rather than starting from nothing.
- Acceptance: a chapter in `SUMMARY.md` naming each of the nine routes beside its HTTP method, with the lifecycle's ordering and the authorization each stage takes; the ledger's seven rows re-judged to `covered` with their witnesses recomputed; `BOOK-LINKS` and `mdbook build` green.
- ✅ **DELIVERED**: `docs/book/src/policy-lifecycle.md`, in `SUMMARY.md` after `site-authority.md`. The route census moves **62 described / 2 mentioned / 40 absent → 71 / 2 / 31** — exactly the nine, and nothing else.
- ⭐ **THE AUTHORIZATION WAS DERIVED, NOT ASSUMED, AND IT IS WORTH STATING PLAINLY**: all nine routes admit on **enrolment alone** (`reader_tenant`), with the tenant taken from the enrolment rather than the request, and every read filtered to the caller's own tenant. ⛔ No grant is required anywhere on this page — **the grant requirement begins at publication** (`.9.2.1.2`'s held `owning_authority`), so the trail records what a tenant decided and is not itself the authority to put a policy into force. The chapter says exactly that.
- ⭐ **AND ONE APPARENT DEFECT WAS CHECKED AND IS NOT ONE.** `policy_impact` passes NO tenant to its query, which is the shape `.6.1.5.3` and `.3.3.4.10.3` were both defects. It is correct here: `migrations/0038` gives `policy_versions` no `tenant_id` at all — the policy register is deployment-wide, owned by an `owning_authority` — while `migrations/0073` added `tenant_id` to the nine LIFECYCLE tables, which are the ones the tenant-bound reads cover. Checked before writing rather than documented as found.
- 🔴 **THE GATE THIS TREE JUST BUILT CAUGHT A DEFECT IN ITSELF, ON ITS FIRST REAL USE.** `census_surface_judgement.py` read the book with a filesystem `glob` while the classifier it imports reads `git ls-files`, so the seven rows went **green against a chapter that was not yet in the index** — an UNTRACKED draft counted as documentation, and a fresh clone would not have had it. Repaired to `git ls-files` (which includes the index, the right corpus for a pre-commit gate) in both the route corpus and the quoted-witness reader. ⭐ Found because the two instruments disagreed: the route census still said 40 absent while the judgement said all nine were covered. Two numbers disagreeing is what finds this; two agreeing would have proved nothing.
- Status: `done`.
- Verification: `python3 -B scripts/census_route_documentation.py` → 71 / 2 / 31; `python3 -B scripts/census_surface_judgement.py` → **30 covered · 3 internal · 10 gap**, held by five leaves, `--check` rc=0, `--self-test` rc=0; `bash scripts/check_book_links.sh` rc=0; `mdbook build` rc=0; `make gate` → `=== all doctrines green ===`.
- promotion: declined (the transferable lesson — an instrument must read the SAME corpus as the instrument it imports, or it judges against a world its own evidence cannot see — is `docs/knowledge/a-census-is-as-wide-as-its-key.md` in the corpus dimension, and `.11.8`'s own *check an instrument's first number against one obtained a DIFFERENT way* is exactly how it was found. Recorded in `DEV_NOTES.md` rather than as a third file.)
- Commit: see the commit acceptance section for this leaf.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.6.4 — The evaluation harness: seven routes, none documented

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.4.6.2`. ⛔ The largest single-subject gap in the surface, and the only family where NO route carries a contract line.
- The members: `/v1/evaluations/calibrations`, `/corpora`, `/gates`, `/gates/{}/evaluations`, `/runs`, `/trials`, `/trials/{}/results`.
- ⚠️ Ranked behind `.11.4.6.3` deliberately: `PHASE-5`'s G5 gate was Met **as a subtraction gate with the quality-lift claim withdrawn**, so the chapter must describe what the harness records rather than what it demonstrates. Writing it before that distinction is stated would publish the withdrawn claim.
- Acceptance: a chapter naming all seven routes beside their methods, carrying G5's withdrawal explicitly; the ledger row re-judged; `BOOK-LINKS` and `mdbook build` green.
- ✅ **DELIVERED**: `docs/book/src/evaluation-harness.md`. The route census moves **71 described / 2 mentioned / 31 absent → 78 / 2 / 24** — exactly the seven.
- ⭐ **AND THE CHAPTER'S HARDEST JOB WAS NOT DESCRIBING THE HARNESS BUT REFUSING TO VOUCH FOR IT.** Four findings already owned by `.8.2` are stated in the chapter rather than discovered here, each named with its clause: **(1)** every route admits any enrolled principal and the service receives no principal at all — none of the seven `evaluation_*` tables carries a `tenant_id`, so the harness is deployment-wide and one caller reads and writes every other caller's records; **(2)** the seeded assignment's `draw as usize` truncates to 32 bits where the comment beside it promises cross-platform stability; **(3)** 🔴 **a gate that measured NOTHING reports `pass`** — `evaluate_gate` skips any baseline case the scores do not mention, so `{}` compares nothing, finds no failure and returns `passed: true`, while the WRITE side of the same file refuses an empty baseline; **(4)** six write paths and three read paths turn any database error into *already exists* / *not registered*, so an outage is indistinguishable from a duplicate.
- ⛔ **NO NEW LEAF OPENED, and that is the correct outcome rather than a shortcut**: all four are `.8.2`'s clauses 1–4 verbatim, recorded there on 2026-09-19 with `evaluation_trial_results` named as the seventh table a per-file count misses. Opening a fifth leaf for findings already owned would be a second copy of an owned backlog. The contribution here is that they are now in the surface the director reads, beside the routes they belong to.
- ⚠️ G5's position is stated at the head of the limits section: **Met as a subtraction gate with the quality-lift claim withdrawn** — nothing in the chapter demonstrates that deliberation improves an answer.
- Status: `done`.
- Verification: `python3 -B scripts/census_route_documentation.py` → 78 / 2 / 24; `python3 -B scripts/census_surface_judgement.py` → **31 covered · 3 internal · 9 gap**, held by four leaves; `--check` rc=0; `bash scripts/check_book_links.sh` rc=0; `mdbook build` rc=0; `make gate` green.
- promotion: declined (no new transferable lesson — the finding here is that a chapter's duty is to carry its subject's KNOWN defects, which `docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` already governs, and every defect named was already owned by `.8.2`.)

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.6.5 — The governance receipts: audit and deployments

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.4.6.2`.
- The members: `/v1/audit/receipts`, `/v1/deployments`, `/v1/deployments/{}/{}/receipt` — three routes over two families, neither named by any chapter.
- ⭐ These are the two surfaces that answer *what actually happened*: the authorization receipt trail and the evidence that a publication reached a target. A governance platform whose receipt reads are undocumented cannot be audited by the person it exists for.
- Acceptance: the three routes documented beside their methods — in `authority.md`/`deployment.md` if they belong there, in a new chapter otherwise, decided by where the reader already is; both ledger rows re-judged; `BOOK-LINKS` and `mdbook build` green.
- ✅ **DELIVERED, and the two families went to DIFFERENT chapters, which is the answer the acceptance asked for rather than a new chapter by default.** Census **78 described / 2 mentioned / 24 absent → 81 / 2 / 21**, exactly the three.
- ⭐ **`/v1/audit/receipts` → `authority.md`, because that chapter already writes one.** Its federation section says the acceptance carries *the cross-domain receipt in the same commit* — so the trail was already described from the WRITE side and had no read. The new section gives the read, its response shape and its oldest-first ordering. ⛔ And it corrects an admission a reader would otherwise assume: this route is **`tenant_admin`-gated and takes `tenant_id` explicitly** — the read carve-out's surface — not the enrolment admission the lifecycle routes use.
- ⭐ **`/v1/deployments` → `policy-lifecycle.md`, because the pair it stores is what the next section already needed.** A deployment assigns an effective publication to a target in a canary wave with the DESIRED pair; the receipt attests the OBSERVED digest; and drift — documented one section below — is exactly the comparison of those two. The stage diagram gains the `deployment → receipt` hop it had been missing, so the chapter's own picture now reaches drift by the route the data takes.
- ⚠️ Stated rather than implied: **a receipt is the target's claim, not the deployment's verification.** The server stores the reported digest and re-reads nothing; the record makes a disagreement visible and does not adjudicate it. And an assignment refuses a publication that is not EFFECTIVE, so a target is never pointed at something the deployment has not put into force.
- 🔎 **Observed while placing the receipt section, routed to `.11.4.6.6` rather than fixed here**: `authority.md` DOES describe the two federation verbs `.11.4.6.6` owns — *the three verbs — `POST /v1/federation-agreements`, `…/accept` and `…/revoke`* — but writes them with ELIDED paths. So that family's gap is largely notation, not absence, and the repair is cheaper than the ledger's route count suggests. ⛔ Not fixed here: `.11.4.6.6` owns it, and the pivot rule holds.
- Status: `done`.
- Verification: `python3 -B scripts/census_route_documentation.py` → 81 / 2 / 21; `python3 -B scripts/census_surface_judgement.py` → **33 covered · 3 internal · 7 gap**; `--check` rc=0; `bash scripts/check_book_links.sh` rc=0; `mdbook build` rc=0; `make gate` green.
- promotion: declined (no new transferable lesson: the placement rule — put a surface where the reader already is, not in a new chapter by default — is `README_POLICY.md`'s routing discipline applied to the book, and the elided-path observation is routed to the leaf that owns it rather than generalised from one instance.)
- Commit: see the commit acceptance section for this leaf.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.6.6 — The operator verbs the existing chapters omit

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.4.6.2`. ⛔ This is the group the coarse mention test hid: all four families ARE named by a chapter, and 16 of their routes are not.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.6.8 — The release manifest tool, whose entire book presence is one table cell

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.4.6.2`.
- ⚠️ **THE WEAK SIGNAL HID THIS ONE, exactly as its own instrument warned.** `census_book_coverage.py` reports *0 of 10 binaries unmentioned* and says in its own report that a binary is matched by its bare name and `rb` is two letters, so it reads as *no binary is obviously absent*. `rb-release-manifest`'s whole presence in the book is `| \`rb-release-manifest\` | release manifest tooling |`.
- The surface: a clap CLI with `keygen`, `generate`, `pubkey`, `resign` and `verify` (ADR-027). ⭐ `pubkey` exists precisely so a party who does NOT hold the signing key can verify a release — `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.24.1.4.1` added it because until then *every verification required the PRIVATE key*, and a signature whose verifier must hold the signing key proves nothing to anybody else. That verb is unusable while undocumented, which makes this the one binary gap with an external consumer.
- Acceptance: the verbs documented with a worked generate-and-verify, naming ADR-027's deferrals (protected identities, reproducible builders) rather than implying they are met; the ledger row re-judged; `BOOK-LINKS` and `mdbook build` green.
- ✅ **DELIVERED**: `docs/book/src/deployment.md` § *Release manifests and verifying a build* — `keygen`, `generate`, `pubkey`, `verify` by **both** paths, `re-sign`, and the `certify sign`/`certify verify` pair, each with a worked invocation.
- ⭐ **The section's centre is the third-party path, because that is the verb that had no reader.** `pubkey` exists so somebody who does NOT hold the signing key can verify a release (`.11.24.1.4.1`); before it, `verify` derived the public key from the PKCS8 file, so **the only party who could check a release was the party who signed it** — which caught accidental corruption, never forgery. A verb that exists to serve an outside audience and is documented nowhere they can read is the sharpest form of this whole leaf's subject.
- ⛔ **Three things stated rather than implied, each of which the code is explicit about**: `generate` is **NOT reproducible** — `created_at` is the clock, so two runs over one unchanged binary differ, which is precisely why `re-sign` exists; `re-sign` signs the manifest's bytes **verbatim** and deliberately does not verify the old signature first, because the key that would check is the one presumed compromised; and ADR-027's **protected identities and reproducible builders are named deferrals**, so a verified manifest says *these bytes are the bytes that identity signed*, never *these were built from the source they claim*.
- Status: `done`.
- Verification: `python3 -B scripts/census_surface_judgement.py` → **40 covered · 3 internal · 0 gap**, `the gaps are held by 0 leaf/leaves`; `--check` rc=0; `bash scripts/check_book_links.sh` rc=0; `mdbook build` rc=0; `make gate` green.
- promotion: declined (no new transferable lesson — this is the weak-signal warning `census_book_coverage.py` already prints in its own report, confirmed by one more instance: a binary matched by its bare name can be *mentioned* by a single table cell and still be undocumented.)
- Commit: see the commit acceptance section for this leaf.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.5.1 — The doctrine registry is data, so it must not be executable

- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0094.
- Reproduce: each registry entry is a bash DOUBLE-quoted string, so backticks in a description are command substitution. The description added in REPAIR-0092 contained them, and the enforcer printed `line 36: - : command not found` and `line 36: pending: command not found` while rendering that description with the backticked words silently MISSING — bash had executed them and substituted the empty result.
- Why the instance fix was not enough: REPAIR-0092 removed the backticks and censused the other rows, but left the trap armed. Every other doctrine description in `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md` uses backticks, so copying one into the registry is the natural next move, and the only symptom is stderr noise plus words vanishing from a description nobody re-reads.
- The half that matters more than the output damage: the driver **executes** whatever a description contains, in the pre-commit hook and in CI. Today it ran `- Status:` and `pending` and got "command not found". A description carrying `$(...)` would be run the same way.
- Fix: a self-guard at the top of `scripts/check_doctrines.sh` that reads its own SOURCE TEXT and refuses a backtick, `$(`, `${` or a bare `$` inside the registry block, placed BEFORE the array assignment — the only placement that prevents the execution rather than reporting it afterwards.
- Verification: 15 checks green. FALSIFIED by reintroducing the exact original text — the guard exits 1, names line 12 and the offending entry, and no check runs; restoring the repair returns `=== all doctrines green ===`.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0094 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.5.1): refuse shell expansion in the doctrine registry`.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.5.2 — A LOCKSTEP box may not claim a document the commit does not touch

- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0099. The census was decisive, and the check it specified now enforces it.
- Reproduce: commit `6bf0c40` (REPAIR-0092) carries a ticked LOCKSTEP box naming `MEMORY.md` and `LIVE_STATUS.md`, and staged neither. Cause chain: a scripted multi-edit hit a failed `assert`, the script exited non-zero, the compound command ran `git add -A && git commit` regardless, and `-A` staged whatever partial state existed. The commit succeeded with a checklist box that was false.
- Why `TASK-ACCEPTANCE` cannot catch it: that gate proves the box is TICKED and CITES something re-runnable. It does not and cannot prove the cited edit landed. This is the complementary half.
- census, run before proposing any rule, because the obvious rule is wrong: over the last 25 commits, 10 close a leaf, and of those `CHANGELOG.md` is staged 10/10 but `MEMORY.md` only 6/10, `LIVE_STATUS.md` 7/10 and `DEV_NOTES.md` 7/10. A blanket "closing a leaf must stage MEMORY" would assert a rule the project does not follow, would flag four pre-existing commits, and would not even catch `6bf0c40`, which did stage `CHANGELOG.md`.
- census of the rule that DOES hold: of the 6 commits in that window adding a `**LOCKSTEP**` bullet naming a core live document, exactly **one — `6bf0c40`, this session's own — named a document it did not stage**. Zero false positives across the rest. Keying the gate on the author's own CLAIM rather than on a blanket requirement is what makes it sound: a leaf that does not claim `MEMORY.md` is not required to stage it.
- Owns: `scripts/check_lockstep_claim.sh`, staged-diff-scoped like `TASK-ACCEPTANCE` and `TABLE-ARITY-RATCHET` — for each staged `docs/tasks/*.md`, take the ADDED lines containing `**LOCKSTEP**`, and require every core live document named there to be in the staged set. Register it and mirror it in `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md`.
- Known false-positive shape, to handle honestly rather than guess at: a box naming a document in order to say it is UNCHANGED. Prose negation detection is fragile, so follow the `GAP-CLAIM-CENSUS` precedent and provide an explicit escape in the same section — `lockstep: <doc> unchanged (<why>)` — rather than parsing intent.
- Acceptance: the check must FAIL against `6bf0c40`'s staged shape and PASS against `c6a843f`'s, and its `--self-test` must prove both directions.
- Fix: `scripts/check_lockstep_claim.sh`, registered as `LOCKSTEP-CLAIM` and mirrored in `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md`. Staged-diff-scoped over `docs/tasks/*.md`: for each ADDED line carrying a bold `**LOCKSTEP**` bullet, every core live document named on it must be in the changed set. The claim shape is the BOLD bullet, so narrative that merely reports on a past box — `c6a843f`'s two "its LOCKSTEP box overstated" lines — is not a claim about this commit and is deliberately not matched.
- The document list is COMMIT.md's root live documents (`README.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `LIVE_STATUS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `DEV_NOTES.md`). `docs/decisions/` and `docs/book/` are directories a box names by area rather than by file, and `KNOWLEDGE_MAP.md` is derived with its own gate. The `--self-test` re-checks that every listed name still appears in COMMIT.md, so the list cannot drift silently away from the document it was taken from.
- The escape is the `GAP-CLAIM-CENSUS` precedent rather than prose parsing: `lockstep: <doc> unchanged (<why>)` in the claim's own heading section. The refusal text says explicitly that deleting the document's NAME is not a discharge — the name is the claim, and removing it hides the decision instead of recording it.
- A third mode beyond the gate and the self-test: `--against <sha>` re-runs the predicate over any past commit, which is what makes this leaf's acceptance literally executable rather than argued.
- Verification: `--self-test` passes (2 claim shapes matched, 2 narrative lines ignored, 3 naming cases including a nested path and a longer filename, the escape both ways, 5 documents confirmed in COMMIT.md). The acceptance runs as stated: `--against 6bf0c40` FAILS, naming `docs/tasks/SIGNOFF-REPAIR.md:2284` and both `MEMORY.md` and `LIVE_STATUS.md`; `--against c6a843f` passes. `make gate` prints `=== all doctrines green ===` with 16 checks.
- census re-run with the FINISHED gate, widened from the 25-commit window the rule was designed on: over the last 30 commits, 11 add a bold LOCKSTEP claim and were therefore genuinely exercised — 10 pass and exactly one, `6bf0c40`, breaches. Zero false positives. The remaining 19 pass vacuously because they add no claim, and that distinction is recorded so "30 green" is not mistaken for 30 tests.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0099 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.5.2): gate a LOCKSTEP box against the commit it claims`.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.5.3 — The tree index's frontier is a second copy, and it drifted

- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0100. Found while updating the frontier for `.7.3.3.4.1`, in the same family as `.1` and `.2` — a rule the project states and nothing checks.
- Reproduce, exactly: `docs/TASK_TREE.md`'s Active Task Trees row for `SIGNOFF-REPAIR` read `.7.3.3.2.2 — director-requested handoff`, a leaf closed by REPAIR-0060 on 2026-09-11. The tree's own Current Frontier table had moved through many rows since. `COMMIT.md` says to update the index "only if the frontier changes", so the obligation exists and was simply not met, repeatedly and invisibly.
- Why this is the same defect class as `.1`/`.2`: a fact is duplicated into a second document that nothing derives, so it is stale by construction the first time someone forgets. `docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` leg 3 states the rule directly — prefer one derived source over N synchronized copies — and the project already applied it once, in `check_book_frontier.sh`, which refuses a BOOK page naming a frontier leaf other than row 1. The index was left out of that repair.
- census of what currently reads the index, run before claiming it is ungated: `git grep -n "TASK_TREE" -- scripts/ .githooks/` returns hits in exactly **five** files, and classifying all five leaves **zero** that read its frontier column — `scripts/bootstrap.sh` seeds the table once, `scripts/check_memory_architecture.sh:50` asserts only that the file EXISTS, `scripts/check_readme_stability.sh:100` carries the path inside a README text fragment, `scripts/check_task_acceptance.sh:63` is a comment about `docs/tasks/<TREE-ID>.md` rather than the index, and `scripts/update_scaffold.sh` lists it as a spine file to sync. One check touches the file at all, and it proves existence, not currency. The population was classified rather than counted, per `.11.4.5.2`'s lesson.
- Census owed before any rule is proposed, because the obvious rule may again be wrong: how many of the index's fourteen rows carry a frontier claim, how many are derived from their tree's own table, and how many are prose that would be flagged. `.11.4.5.2`'s lesson stands — measure the population before asserting a requirement over it.
- Owns, provisionally pending that census: either extend `check_book_frontier.sh`'s comparison to `docs/TASK_TREE.md`'s row for an `active` tree, or generate that column from each tree's Current Frontier table so no copy exists to drift. Prefer the generator: it removes the failure mode instead of detecting it.
- Acceptance: the check must FAIL against the index as it stood at `300de41` (naming `.7.3.3.2.2` while the tree's row 1 was `.7.3.3.4.1`) and PASS against the corrected row, with a two-sided `--self-test`; or, if the generator is chosen, the column has no hand-maintained copy left to test.
- The stale row itself is corrected in REPAIR-0095 rather than left as a specimen — the reproduction is recorded here with its commit, so the gate can still be falsified against it.
- **census over all fourteen rows, run before proposing the rule — and it rejected BOTH of this leaf's provisional options.** Measuring each index cell against its tree's Current Frontier row 1: 3 agree, 1 disagrees, 2 claim no leaf, and 8 have no numbered row 1 at all because a completed tree writes a dash row and points its cell at the NEXT tree's first leaf, which is deliberately not a leaf of that tree. The single disagreement is `PHASE-8`, whose row 1 is the cross-tree prerequisite `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.3.3` while its cell says "corrective prerequisite `SIGNOFF-REPAIR`; then `.5.3`" — an accurate summary of rows 1 AND 2, so equality would flag a legitimate row. A blanket "the cell equals row 1" rule is therefore unsound.
- The GENERATOR, which this leaf provisionally preferred, is rejected on the same census: regenerating the column would destroy accurate curated prose in 13 of 14 rows. Recording the reversal rather than quietly switching, because the preference was written down before the measurement existed.
- Fix: `scripts/check_tree_index_frontier.sh`, registered as `INDEX-FRONTIER` and mirrored in `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md`. The sound rule the census leaves standing is narrow — an ACTIVE tree whose Current Frontier row 1 names a leaf OF THAT TREE must be named by its index cell. Today that is exactly one row, which is also the only row that moves; the rule extends itself the moment another tree becomes active.
- Root cause, dated rather than estimated: `--against` over the last 60 commits finds **39 breaching and 21 genuinely agreeing** (none vacuous), and the drift begins at `1ebfebe` — REPAIR-0060, the commit that CLOSED `.7.3.3.2.2`. The row was written from the leaf just completed instead of the next one, and nothing re-read it for 39 commits.
- Verification: `--self-test` passes (numbered row 1 extracted, a completed tree's dash row correctly yields none, four cell shapes normalised including the dot-shorthand and the prerequisite cell). The acceptance runs literally: `--against 300de41` FAILS naming both leaves, the current tree PASSES. `make gate` prints `=== all doctrines green ===` with 17 checks.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0100 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.5.3): gate the tree index against its own trees`.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.5.4 — The derived map is generated from the working tree and committed against the index

- Opened: `pending`. Found by this session's own commit `991bbf8` — the FOURTH defect in the enforcement spine itself, and the same family as `.1`, `.2` and `.3`: a rule the project states, and nothing checks.
- Reproduce, exactly: `.githooks/pre-commit` regenerates `KNOWLEDGE_MAP.md` and `git add`s it, so *"map-drift is structurally impossible"*. But `gen_knowledge_map.sh` enumerates its sources with `ls docs/tasks/*.md`, `ls docs/decisions/*.md` and `ls docs/knowledge/*.md` — the **working tree** — while the map it stages is committed against the **index**. An UNTRACKED file in any of those three directories therefore enters the committed map as a link to a path the commit does not contain.
- Measured, not asserted: at `991bbf8` (the sixteenth changelog rotation), `git show 991bbf8:KNOWLEDGE_MAP.md | grep -c 'a-control-is-calibrated-against-the-renderer.md'` returns **1** and `git ls-tree --name-only 991bbf8 docs/knowledge/ | grep -c 'a-control-is-calibrated'` returns **0**. A reader checking out that commit gets a map whose link does not resolve.
- ⛔ **CENSUS, and widening it changed the answer** — the first pass scanned `docs/knowledge/` alone and found 2; scoping it to all three families the generator actually lists found **3 of the 139 commits that touch the map**. `MEMORY.md`'s standing *"SCOPE A CENSUS WHOLE"* warning names this exact failure and it still caught me, one leaf after the last time:
  - `991bbf8` — `docs/knowledge/a-control-is-calibrated-against-the-renderer.md` (this session).
  - `a79dd2c` — `docs/knowledge/a-schema-object-is-its-latest-migration.md`; the record landed in `f026c28`, **1 commit later**.
  - `0558ed6` — `docs/decisions/2026-09-06_budget-read-surface.md`, a DIFFERENT family, which the narrow census could not have seen.
- ⭐ **The shape is the same in all three and it is worth naming**: a commit sequenced BETWEEN the work that creates a source file and the commit that adds it. Two of the three are changelog rotations — `.11.4.1.2`'s own ruling *requires* a rotation to be its own commit, so the spine's correct sequencing rule is what exposes the generator's wrong source.
- ⚠️ A second instance of the same root cause, reachable by the same reasoning and not yet observed in the corpus: the `answers:` text is read from the working-tree file, so an UNSTAGED edit to a record is published into the committed map the same way. Same fix.
- Owns: making the generator derive from the COMMIT's sources — `git ls-files` for enumeration and `git show :<path>` for content — so the map cannot name what the commit does not carry. ⭐ Preferred over a detector per `.11.4.5.3`'s ruling: remove the failure mode rather than report it.
- Acceptance: the generator lists only index-present sources and reads their content from the index; a `--self-test` proving both directions (an untracked source is absent from the render, a staged one is present); the census instrument re-run over the same 139 commits still finding exactly the 3 historical instances and no new one; and `make gate` green.
- ⛔ Explicit limit: the three historical commits are NOT rewritten. Each is reachable history and each self-corrected within one commit; the repair stops the next one.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0188.
- ⛔ **The repair's FIRST cut would have published 54 broken links, and the verification pass caught it before the gate did.** Switching `ls` to `git ls-files -- 'docs/tasks/*.md'` looked equivalent; it is not. A git pathspec wildcard MATCHES `/` by default, so that pattern returned **69** paths where the shell's `ls` returns **15**, reaching into `docs/tasks/artifacts/` — and because the link is built from `basename`, all 54 extras would have rendered as links to files that do not exist. Found by diffing the fresh render against the committed map, which is the one comparison that could see it. The corrected pathspec carries `:(glob)` (fnmatch with `FNM_PATHNAME`, where a wildcard does not cross a separator). ⭐ `MEMORY.md` warns that `*.rs` does NOT recurse; this is the SAME confusion in the opposite direction, and the two tools disagree on the same glob.
- Acceptance:
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE)** — `.githooks/pre-commit` regenerates the map and `git add`s it, so the map is committed against the INDEX, while `gen_knowledge_map.sh` enumerated its sources with `ls docs/{tasks,decisions,knowledge}/*.md` — the WORKING TREE. Any untracked file in those three directories entered the committed map as a link the commit does not contain. #### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.4 — A leaf's status can be contradicted inside its own section

- Opened: `pending`; found while updating the frontier for `.11.4.3.1.2.27`.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0092. Two defects, both mechanized.
- Finding as opened: `.7.4.1` and `.7.4.2` each began `Status: pending` and carried `Status: done` further down the SAME section, with a real commit. A careful reader takes the later line; a reader who stops at the first — or any tool that takes the first match, which is the obvious way to write it — gets the opposite answer. `.7.4.1` sat at Current Frontier row 2 for seven commits after it closed, for exactly that reason.
- census of the ENFORCERS, the claim one counterexample refutes: `ls scripts/check_*.sh knowledge-map/scripts/check_*.sh | wc -l` -> 21 registered checks, `grep -ln 'Status:' scripts/check_*.sh knowledge-map/scripts/check_*.sh | wc -l` -> 0, widened to `git grep -ln 'Status: *`' -- scripts knowledge-map .githooks | wc -l` -> 0. Nothing read a leaf's status line.
- census of the AFFECTED LEAVES, run here: **5 sections** across every tracked tree, all in `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.md` — `.11.5`, `.11.4.3.1.2.14`, `.7.4.1`, `.7.4.2`, `.11.4.3.1.2.21`. Each opened with one state and closed with another, and never revised the first.
- **A SECOND defect, found BY that census and not suspected when the leaf was opened.** The first census reported one section holding 18 status lines. It holds one, and had swallowed five children: the tree uses `#######` and deeper for its nested leaves, and **an ATX heading stops at level 6 in CommonMark and GFM alike**. Seven hashes is a paragraph that starts with hashes. Measured across the trees: **29 such lines, at levels 7 through 11, every one in `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.md`**. Their content belongs, for any heading-aware reader, to the nearest real heading above them — which is why the tree's deepest leaves, the ones under active work, were invisible as structure to the project's own instruments.
- Fix: the opening line becomes `- Opened:`, which is what it always meant, so one `- Status:` states what is true now and every word of provenance survives; and every over-deep heading is capped at `######`, because the leaf id already carries the depth and carries it further than six levels ever could. 5 statuses renamed, 29 headings demoted, nothing deleted.
- Mechanized both, so neither can recur: `scripts/check_task_status.sh` (TASK-STATUS) and `scripts/check_heading_depth.sh` (HEADING-DEPTH), each with a `--self-test`, both registered in `scripts/check_doctrines.sh` and mirrored in `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md`. Both skip fenced code blocks, so a template or a shell comment inside a fence is not a breach.
- Defect found in this leaf's own work, and fixed here: the registry entries are bash double-quoted strings, so the backticks in the first TASK-STATUS description ran as command substitution — the enforcer printed `line 36: pending: command not found` and the backticked words vanished from its output. The description is now backtick-free, and `awk '/^DOCTRINES=\(/,/^\)/' scripts/check_doctrines.sh | grep -c '`'` returns 0 for the whole registry.
- promotion: declined (the durable statement is the doctrine registry itself — both rules are now enforced rather than remembered, which is the strongest form this project has; `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md` carries their rationale verbatim).
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0092 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.4): gate a leaf's status and Markdown's heading ceiling`.
- Correction, same leaf: its LOCKSTEP box overstated. Two scripted live-doc edits failed their anchor assertions while the commit proceeded, so `MEMORY.md` and `LIVE_STATUS.md` did not carry this leaf at its own commit. Both are corrected in REPAIR-0093, which also records the miss. The lesson is the commit workflow's, not this leaf's: a scripted doc edit that fails must fail the COMMIT, and `git add -A` after a partially-failed script is how a false checklist box gets written.

### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.5 — Assess the verification strategy for a networked agent platform

- Opened: `pending`; captured 2026-09-11 at the director's request. Proposal only — no pivot, and no change to the accepted §19 test strategy.
- Why it was raised: the director asked how this project intends to exercise its corners, given an agent network over a LAN or the Internet, and whether MCP helps. The answer rests on measured evidence rather than opinion: of the six defects repaired in `REPAIR-0060`–`0068`, NONE was a wrong return value. Each was an identity, lifetime, ordering, concurrency or environment property, found by an instrument that asked the operating system or the catalogue a question — `ps`, `pg_namespace.nspacl`, a process-table probe, a distinctness counter, and a stage census.
- Owns: assess the proposal in `docs/tasks/artifacts/signoff_review/verification-strategy-proposal.md` against ROADMAP §19, and decide which parts become tracked work. Its four ranked proposals are a falsification requirement for new controls, a pipeline-stage coverage registry, the unbuilt `reasonbraid-simulator` with invariants over the event log, and an adversarial concurrency lane. Its MCP finding is that MCP widens reachability and supplies an external conformance yardstick, but caught none of the six defects, is itself unqualified on its wire (`.6.1`–`.6.3` open), and must stay in a conformance lane rather than the correctness lane per ROADMAP §25's stop/reframe trigger.
- Binding constraint on any outcome: the full checkpoint already takes roughly two hours with about 2,982 seconds unaccounted (`.11.4.3.1.2.15`). New lanes arrive with a tiering story or they get routed around, and a gate people route around is a gate that lies.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0087. Assessment recorded as `docs/decisions/2026-09-12_verification-strategy-assessment.md`.
- Outcome: all four proposals accepted in principle and SEQUENCED, with one new lane added ahead of three of them. Order: (0) a clean-state lane, new and not in the proposal; (1) a control must have failed on the defect it was written for, as a doctrine gate; (4) the adversarial concurrency lane, whose fixture-ownership prerequisite is now largely done by REPAIR-0082/0085/0086; (2) the pipeline-stage registry, after `.7.3.3.4` so it is built from a real instance; (3) the deterministic simulator, tracked but deliberately not now.
- The evidence got STRONGER, not merely longer. Four further defects were repaired after the proposal was written — REPAIR-0080, 0083, 0085, 0086 — bringing the count to **ten defects, none a wrong return value, none reachable by MCP**. REPAIR-0086 is the clearest demonstration of proposal 1 the project has produced: its invariant control fails against the superseded design while all three conformance scenarios still pass, which is exactly why the race shipped.
- The new lane goes first because it is cheaper than all the others and has already paid: two of the three "remote-only" failures needed only a CLEAN machine, not a remote one, and each was reproduced by one command after costing CI round-trips.
- MCP's assessment is unchanged and better evidenced: it widens reachability, supplies an external yardstick, caught none of the ten defects, and stays in a conformance lane per ROADMAP §25.
- Binding constraint carried forward: no new lane lands before `.11.4.3.1.2.15` explains the checkpoint's ~2,982 unaccounted seconds. The clean-state lane is exempt because it REPLACES CI round-trips rather than adding to them.
- promotion: declined (the durable method statements are already promoted — `TOOLBOX.md` for the clean-state rule and `docs/knowledge/proving-a-race-is-closed.md` for the invariant rule; this leaf records a scope decision, which belongs in `docs/decisions/`).
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0087 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.5): assess and sequence the verification strategy`.

### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.7 — The published reason-code registry and the codes the product emits have drifted

- Opened: `pending`; routed here from `.3.3.4.7.3`, which needed one of these codes and found the registry did not have it.
- Finding, measured rather than suspected: `ROADMAP.md` §9.8 and `reasonbraid_core::KnownReasonCode` publish **20** codes as "the *complete* §9.8 list, not a Phase-0 subset". The product emits **19** distinct `code: "…"` literals across tracked `crates/*/src`, of which **10 are absent from the registry** — `classification_unqualified`, `commit_outcome_unconfirmed`, `idempotency_conflict`, `locator_digest_conflict`, `not_found`, `quota_exceeded`, `quota_unconfigured`, `storm_control`, `unknown`, `unknown_node` — and **11 registry codes are never emitted**. A client written against the published registry cannot name half of what it will actually receive.
- ROUTING EVIDENCE: the finding reproduces entirely OUTSIDE the authority family it was found in. Of the 10 unregistered codes only `commit_outcome_unconfirmed` belongs to `.3.3.4`'s work; the rest come from classification, bootstrap idempotency, resource locators, quotas, storm control, the node channel and the CLI. What was measured is the two-way set difference above, over all tracked `crates/*/src` Rust sources. What would make the routing wrong is if the emitted literals were internal diagnostics rather than wire codes — they are not: each is the `code` field of a JSON error body a client reads.
- Owns: decide, per code, whether the registry gains it, the emitter changes, or the divergence is deliberate and documented; then decide whether the reconciliation is mechanized, since a registry nothing checks drifted by 10 values without anyone noticing. §9.8 says a stable registry must not be re-churned leaf by leaf, so this is one deliberate reconciliation rather than a value added wherever one is next needed.
- Acceptance: every one of the 19 emitted codes has a recorded disposition; the 11 unemitted registry codes are either kept with a stated reason or removed; and the decision names whether a gate now holds the two in step. "Measured and deliberately divergent" is a legitimate outcome and must stay available.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0162.
- ⛔ **CORRECTION to this leaf's own numbers, and it is `.11.4.5.2`'s lesson turned on the leaf: the emitted set is 18, not 19, and the unregistered set is 9, not 10.** `unknown` appears in the raw grep and is **not a wire code**: both sites — `reasonbraid-cli/src/lib.rs:342` and `reasonbraid-node/src/channel.rs:495` — are a CLIENT building a local error when a response body will not parse. It never travels from the server. A search's N hits were published as a defect count without classifying them, in a leaf whose subject is a published set nobody re-derived.
- The other numbers re-derive exactly: registry **20** (= §9.8's list, verbatim), registered-but-unemitted **11**.
- ⛔ **HALF the finding is REFUTED by the code's own documentation, which the leaf did not read.** `crates/reasonbraid-core/src/error.rs` states, above the enum: *"This is the **complete** §9.8 list, not a Phase-0 subset: a stable registry must not be carved up and re-churned leaf by leaf. The demo consumes a subset; codes the demo never emits are still part of the registry so a client and server can name them consistently."* **Disposition: all 11 KEPT**, reason already stated and now measured. Carving a stable registry down to what one build uses is the thing that module exists to prevent.
- ⛔ **The other half is largely refuted too.** The same doc: *"Codes beyond this list (future versions) are handled by `ReasonCode::Unknown`"*, which **preserves the string verbatim rather than dropping it**. The 9 unregistered codes reach a client intact; the forward-compatibility path works as designed. "A client cannot NAME half of what it will receive" is true and far milder than it reads — it cannot type the code, it never loses it.
- 🔴 **What IS a real gap is not what the leaf opened on: nothing published which codes the product actually emits.** There was no error page in the book at all. A client author reads §9.8, sees 20, and learns about `quota_unconfigured` only by receiving one. That is `.11.8`'s class — a published surface and the real surface with nothing comparing them.
- ⛔ **The registry is NOT extended**, on its own contract plus the freeze: adding the 9 would break its stated invariant of mirroring §9.8 exactly, and §9.8 sits in a roadmap frozen at v0.4.1 to "factual errata, security corrections, and discovered Phase 0 blockers" (`docs/decisions/2026-09-05_roadmap-v0.4.1-frozen.md`). ⭐ A post-code measurement of nine emitted codes is exactly the evidence that record says a **v0.5.0** must cite — recorded as such rather than smuggled into a frozen document by a repair leaf. ⛔ Nor are the emitters changed: a WIRE change across 9 codes that would collapse distinctions the product really makes (`idempotency_conflict` is a bootstrap request id bound to a different request; `idempotency_mismatch` is a replayed command's payload).
- **DELIVERED: `docs/book/src/errors.md`** — all 18 with HTTP status, registry status (§9.8 or ext) and meaning, derived from the sources rather than transcribed; the 11 unemitted with the reason they are kept; and four rules for a client (branch on `code` not `message`; preserve an unrecognized code; treat `commit_outcome_unconfirmed` as UNKNOWN not failed; never infer existence from a `404`). Every emitted code therefore has a recorded disposition, in the place a client actually looks.
- ⭐ **A GATE IS REGISTERED — `REASON-CODE-DOC` — and the census is what justifies it, in direct contrast to `.11.9` one commit earlier.** It fires on **ZERO** breaches today and would have fired on all nine: it catches the NEXT drift rather than presenting a backlog people learn to waive. `.11.9`'s citation gate would have fired on 114 of 131 and was rejected on exactly this test. The same question, measured, answered oppositely — the measurement doing its job rather than a house style.
- The instrument is `scripts/census_reason_codes.py` (tracked, 14-control `--self-test`, in `TOOLBOX.md`, mirrored in `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md`, registered inside `PROJECT-SPECIFIC`).
- 🔴 FALSIFIED: an undocumented code introduced at a real emission site -> `REASON-CODE-DOC: a code the server emits is not in the book's table.`, naming `a_brand_new_undocumented_code` and its file, rc=1; restored -> `all 18 emitted codes are documented`, rc=0.
- ⚠️ The `--self-test` asserts the client/server split in BOTH directions against the REAL tree, because that split is the one thing that can silently inflate the published number — and it already did once, in this leaf's own opening line.
- NO REGRESSION: no product code changed. `check_doctrines.sh` -> `=== all doctrines green ===` (18 checks); `mdbook build docs/book` rc=0; `BOOK-LINKS` passes with the new page in `SUMMARY.md`.
- LOCKSTEP: `docs/book/src/errors.md` (new) + `SUMMARY.md`, `TOOLBOX.md`, `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md`, `scripts/check_doctrines.project.sh`, `MEMORY.md`, `LIVE_STATUS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `DEV_NOTES.md`.
- 🔎 ROUTED, not absorbed: whether §9.8 itself gains the nine at v0.5.0 is a ROADMAP decision under an active freeze. Owned by `.11.7.1`.
- promotion: declined. The method statements — classify a population before publishing it, and measure what a proposed gate would fire on — are `.11.4.5.2`'s and `.11.6`'s and are already durable; the new fact (the same rule shape gated in one leaf and rejected in the next, on the measurement) is recorded in `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md` beside the gate.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0162 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.7): publish the codes the product emits, and gate them`.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.7.1 — Whether §9.8 should gain the nine codes at v0.5.0

- Opened by `.11.7`, which measured the evidence and deliberately did not spend it.
- The measurement, reproducible with `python3 -B scripts/census_reason_codes.py`: the product emits **9** wire codes postdating §9.8 — `not_found`, `unknown_node`, `quota_exceeded`, `quota_unconfigured`, `storm_control`, `classification_unqualified`, `idempotency_conflict`, `locator_digest_conflict`, `commit_outcome_unconfirmed` — each documented in `docs/book/src/errors.md` with its status and meaning.
- ⛔ **THE POPULATION MOVED, AND IT WAS THIS TREE THAT MOVED IT — so it is pinned rather than silently refreshed** (`MEMORY.md`: pin a census your own change invalidates). The nine above are the population at `2e72571`, re-derivable there with `git stash`-free certainty because the sha is in the command: `git show 2e72571:docs/book/src/errors.md | grep -c '| ext |'`. `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.9.2.1.1` (REPAIR-0190) then added a TENTH, `publication_repository_unconfigured` (503), so **this leaf's recommendation owes a verdict on ten codes, not nine**, and its heading is one short. ⚠️ The addition is an `ext` code and touches no frozen document: `ROADMAP.md` §9.8 is unchanged, which is exactly the freeze this leaf exists to respect.
- ⛔ **AND IT MOVED A SECOND TIME, in the other direction, and again by this tree's own hand.** `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.14.3.2` (REPAIR-0218) **retired** `locator_digest_conflict`: the refusal disclosed the cross-tenant existence §9.8 forbids, and it let one principal make a locator uncitable by every other tenant. So the population is **nine**, not ten — the tenth arrived by `.9.2.1.1` and one of the original nine has left. ⭐ The heading's number is deliberately NOT chased: it names the population at the leaf's opening, and every move is recorded as a bullet instead, which is what makes the drift legible rather than invisible. Re-derive the current set with `python3 -B scripts/census_reason_codes.py`, never from any of these sentences.
- ⭐ **The retirement is also EVIDENCE for this leaf's own recommendation, not merely an accounting change.** It is the first `ext` code removed rather than added, and the reason it was removed is the reason `not_found`/`unknown_node` are flagged below as wanting reconciliation: a code can be a §9.8 breach rather than a §9.8 omission. A recommendation that only ever appends cannot express that.
- ⛔ Why `.11.7` did not decide it: `ROADMAP.md` is frozen at v0.4.1 to factual errata, security corrections and Phase 0 blockers, and v0.5.0 "must cite measurements, failure observations, or implementation constraints produced by working code". This IS such a measurement, which makes it INPUT to that decision rather than licence for a repair leaf to edit a frozen document.
- ⚠️ "Add all nine" is not obviously right. `not_found` and `unknown_node` overlap `scope_hidden`'s existence-non-leak intent and may want reconciling rather than appending; `quota_exceeded` sits beside `rate_limited` and `budget_unavailable`, and the three-way distinction should be stated deliberately or collapsed.
- Acceptance: a recommendation per code with its reason, presented as evidence for a roadmap version; ⛔ no edit to `ROADMAP.md` §9.8 without the freeze being lifted or the director deciding.
- Status: `done` — REASONBRAID-DOC-0086 (`docs/decisions/2026-09-20_the-nine-unregistered-reason-codes-recommended-per-code.md`).
- **THE POPULATION, DERIVED AT CLOSURE rather than read off this leaf's own sentences** (`MEMORY.md`, and this leaf's own warning): `python3 -B scripts/census_reason_codes.py` -> registry **20**, emitted **18**, emitted-and-unregistered **9**. The nine are `not_found`, `unknown_node`, `quota_exceeded`, `quota_unconfigured`, `storm_control`, `classification_unqualified`, `idempotency_conflict`, `commit_outcome_unconfirmed`, `publication_repository_unconfigured` — the leaf's opening nine with `locator_digest_conflict` gone (`.11.14.3.2` retired it) and `publication_repository_unconfigured` arrived (`.9.2.1.1`), exactly as the bullets above predicted. ⭐ The heading's number was not chased and did not need to be.
- 🔴 **THE MEASUREMENT THAT REFRAMED THE QUESTION, and it is not the one the leaf was opened to take: ELEVEN of the twenty registered codes have NO PRODUCER.** `rate_limited`, `budget_unavailable` and `provider_outcome_unknown` are among them, and each is arguably what one of the nine is a rename of. ⇒ The registry and the emitted set differ in BOTH directions, so *which of the nine to add* is the wrong shape of question on its own, and three of the nine are better read as *the product implemented a registered concept under another name*.
- 🔴 **THE LEAF'S OWN SECURITY FLAG IS REFUTED, and this is the finding I most expected to confirm.** It warned that `not_found` and `unknown_node` *overlap `scope_hidden`'s existence-non-leak intent*. Measured at every site: they do not leak. `api.rs` says so in its own words — *"Missing and foreign are ONE answer, so a caller learns nothing about another tenant's nodes"* (`.3.1`) — and `node_channel.rs` likewise, *"A node in ANOTHER tenant answers `unknown_node`, exactly as a node that does not exist"*. ⇒ A vocabulary DUPLICATION, not a §9.8 breach, and the recommendation is a tidy-up rather than a security correction.
- ⭐ **THE PRODUCT VOTED 23 TO 3.** `git grep -c "ControlApiError::not_found("` returns **23** and `…::scope_hidden()` returns **3**, for two codes that mean the same thing on the wire. That asymmetry is the evidence for WHICH way a reconciliation should go, and it is a fact no amount of reading the two definitions would have produced.
- 🔴 **`unknown_node`'s published justification is refuted by its own code.** `docs/book/src/errors.md` says it is *"Distinct from `not_found` so a channel client can tell 're-enrol' from 'wrong id'"* — and a foreign node and an absent one give the SAME answer, so the client cannot tell those apart. The recommendation keeps the code and replaces the reason.
- **THE RECOMMENDATION, per code**: ADD AS PUBLISHED **4**; RECONCILE FIRST **3**; GENERALISE RATHER THAN ADD **1** (`publication_repository_unconfigured` is the SECOND instance of an open family — a registry that grows one code per surface is a list, not a vocabulary); and `quota_exceeded` answered by the four-way table the leaf specifically asked for.
- ⭐ **THE FOUR-WAY DISTINCTION IS STATED AND ALL FOUR ARE KEPT**, which is the opposite of the collapse the leaf floated: quota (a declared allowance over a window), rate (going too fast now), breaker (a protective circuit, independent of any allowance), budget (spend). ⛔ Collapsing is REFUSED because a caller told only `rate_limited` cannot tell *slow down* from *your allowance is spent for the month*, and only one of those is fixed by waiting.
- ⛔ **NO EDIT TO `ROADMAP.md`, and no code changed.** The freeze holds; this is the evidence a v0.5.0 decision needs and the director's is the decision. ⚠️ Three follow-on questions are named in the record and deliberately NOT answered here, because each changes shipped behaviour rather than a published list: which of the 23/3 sites move, whether the eleven unemitted codes gain producers or are retired, and whether the two `*_unconfigured` codes collapse. None may precede the freeze decision.
- **NO REGRESSION** — documentation only; `git diff --stat` touches `docs/decisions/`, its `INDEX.md`, this tree, `docs/TASK_TREE.md` and the live documents. No Rust source, no migration, no book page (the book's `errors.md` already documents all nine, which the census confirms: *"… not documented in the book: 0"*). `make gate` -> `=== all doctrines green ===`; `make book` rc=0.
- ⚪ Promotion: declined. The methods used are already in the layer and were consulted rather than rediscovered — *re-derive a population your own tree has moved* (`MEMORY.md`, and this leaf's own bullets) and *an absence claim is a census over the corpus*. ⚠️ Worth a note if it recurs: **a registry drifts in BOTH directions, and counting only the additions hides half of it** — the eleven producerless codes were not what the leaf asked about and are the larger half of the answer.
- **LOCKSTEP** — `docs/decisions/2026-09-20_the-nine-unregistered-reason-codes-recommended-per-code.md` + `docs/decisions/INDEX.md`, `docs/tasks/SIGNOFF-REPAIR.md` (this leaf closed, frontier, commit log), `docs/TASK_TREE.md` index cell, `MEMORY.md`, `LIVE_STATUS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`. lockstep: README.md unchanged (it names no reason code). lockstep: `docs/book/` unchanged — the census confirms all nine are already documented there, and this record recommends rather than restates. lockstep: DEV_NOTES.md unchanged — no new technical lesson; the promotion bullet above says why.
