#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.2.4 — Whether the resume pointer's current-state block should be derived

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.4.2.3`, routing §6's preference rather than acting on it.
- The requirement, verbatim from `MEMORY_ARCHITECTURE.md` §6: *"**Prefer derived over hand-written** — a small script can regenerate the current-state block from `git log` + each tree's frontier row, so it cannot drift."* Today every field is hand-written.
- **What is derivable, field by field**, from the §6 template's five: `latest_commit` and the ahead-count from `git log -1` and `git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD`; `active_work_unit` and the frontier leaf with its status from the tree's Current Frontier row 1, which `scripts/check_tree_index_frontier.sh` already parses; `in_flight_uncommitted` from `git status --porcelain`. **Four of five.** `next_action` is a judgement sentence and must be preserved, never generated.
- ⛔ **`.11.4.5.3` REJECTED its generator and the precedent does NOT transfer — say why rather than citing it.** There the census found regenerating the tree index's column *"would destroy accurate curated prose in 13 of 14 rows"*. Here the ratio is inverted: four of five fields are mechanical and the one curated field is a single line a generator can leave untouched. ⚠️ That is an argument for measuring, not a licence to skip it.
- census owed before anything is proposed (`.11.6`, and `.11.4.5.3`'s own reversal): how often each derivable field has been WRONG in `MEMORY.md`'s history — `git log -p -- MEMORY.md` against the commit each version was written at. ⭐ A generator is worth building if the fields drift and worth declining if they do not, and this session already carried a stale `133 commits ahead` for ten commits and incremented it twice without re-deriving, so the expected answer is not zero.
- ⚠️ A generator that rewrites this file can destroy `next_action`. Whatever is built preserves that line unless explicitly given a new one, and a control must observe it surviving a regeneration.
- Acceptance: the drift census is run and recorded with its command; the decision to generate or decline is taken ON that measurement and recorded either way; if generated, the instrument is tracked with a `--self-test`, a control proves `next_action` survives, and the currency check is registered or explicitly declined with its reason.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0348.
- **The census: `python3 -B scripts/census_memory_pointer_drift.py`** (tracked, 23-control `--self-test`, registered in `TOOLBOX.md`, inside the SELF-TEST gate's discovered population — 48 instruments carry one). It walks **all 645 commits that have touched `MEMORY.md`**, not a window (`.11.22.1`'s whole-history rule).
- ⛔ **THE DENOMINATOR IS THE ANSWER, AND THE LEAF'S OWN QUESTION HID IT.** The leaf asked *how often each derivable field has been WRONG*. A field that reads `derive on read with git log -1 --oneline` carries no value and cannot be wrong, so the rate has to be taken over the versions that CARRIED one. Measured:

⚠️ **PINNED BY `.11.4.2.4.1`, ONE COMMIT LATER: every figure in this table is AT `1fb5a94`.** It was published unpinned and aged the same day — the very next commit touched `MEMORY.md`, so `645` became `646`, the readable frontier claims `385` became `386` and the agreements `375` became `376`. ⛔ The DEFECT COUNTS (7, 10, 152) did not move, which is why nothing here is withdrawn; but *true when taken and published unpinned* is the class `DOC-0088` named four instances of, and this is the fifth, produced by the leaf that named it. Re-derive, never read: `python3 -B scripts/census_memory_pointer_drift.py`.

| field | carried a value | derive-on-read / no claim | wrong | rate over carried |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `latest_commit` | **162** | 482 derive-on-read, 1 unreadable | **7** | **4.3%** |
| frontier leaf | **385** readable claims (423 named a leaf; 38 sat on a tree with no numbered row 1) | 222 era-1 prose asserting no frontier leaf | **10** | **2.6%** |
| ahead-of-origin | **174** | 140 derive-on-read, 331 absent | **152 of 173** transitions | **88%** |

- 🔴 **`latest_commit` SPENT 482 OF ITS 645 VERSIONS (75%) ALREADY DERIVED-ON-READ, AND ALL SEVEN DEFECTS SIT IN THE 162-VERSION CARRIED MINORITY.** The corpus had already run §6's experiment and the result was in the history before this leaf asked for it.
- **The 7 `latest_commit` defects, every one hand-classified** (a tool's verdict is a population, `.11.4.5.2`): **1** is the donor seed (`BEDROCK-MAINTENANCE-0010` standing in the `Initial commit`'s pointer, correct in the donor repo and meaningless here); **5** are stale by one or two work units (`90fa302`, `78b52e7`, `7f3d715`, `ce30dc7`, `8ef6c69`); and **1 is the sharpest single instance this lane has produced** — at `69b6374` the pointer read ``latest_commit: `ba6e77e` — "REASONBRAID-DOC-0037 …"``, and ⛔ **`ba6e77e` NAMES NO OBJECT IN THIS REPOSITORY** (`git cat-file -t ba6e77e` → `fatal: Not a valid object name`). The quoted subject was right; the hash beside it was mistyped, and `git log --grep` puts DOC-0037 at `c8020be`, which is that very commit's parent. A hand-written field pointed at nothing for the life of the commit and no reader noticed.
- **The 10 frontier disagreements split TWO ways, and the second way is the one worth having measured**: **5** are the pointer naming a leaf the same commit had just CLOSED while row 1 had moved on (`d7b7673`, `b8515bd`, `47af7b1`, `50dfa3e`, `78b52e7`); **5** are the opposite — `a700b21`, `2c38b1a`, `0a38359`, `220c07b`, `5908d3d` all decompose a parent leaf into children, and the POINTER names the first child while **the tree's own row 1 is the copy that did not advance**. ⚠️ So "the pointer drifts from the tree" is not what the data says: the two copies drift from each other, and in half the instances the tree is the stale one. A generator that treats the tree as ground truth would have written the wrong value into the pointer in five of ten cases.
- **The ahead-of-origin count is the catastrophe, and it is falsified by a second route.** The census compares consecutive carrying versions (a stated increase must equal `git rev-list --count A..B`; a decrease is a push, not a defect). An independent run-length pass over the same history — a different question, so a different blind spot — returns: **`310` held unchanged across 83 pointer versions spanning 95 real commits**, `269` across 41 versions / 40 commits, and the leaf's own predicted `133` across **8 versions / 7 commits**. ⚠️ The leaf predicted *"carried a stale 133 for ten commits"*; the measurement says **8 versions and 7 commits**, so the prediction's direction was right and its number was not — recorded rather than quietly matched.
- ⛔ **DECISION: THE GENERATOR IS DECLINED, ON THE MEASUREMENT.** Four reasons, each a number from the table above:
  1. **The one field with catastrophic drift is the one the pointer has ALREADY STOPPED CARRYING.** Today's `MEMORY.md` writes *"DERIVE the push distance, never read it here: `git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD`"* instead of a number. The repair that worked on the 88% field was **not carrying the value** — which costs no instrument, no self-test and no gate.
  2. **75% of `latest_commit`'s history already did the same thing**, and the defects are confined to the minority that did not.
  3. **The residual risk is concentrated exactly where a generator must not go.** `next_action` is a judgement sentence the leaf itself warns a regenerating script can destroy, and 222 of 645 `active_work_unit` bullets are curated prose. That is `.11.4.5.3`'s shape — *"regenerating the column would destroy accurate curated prose in 13 of 14 rows"* — and unlike `.11.4.2.4`'s opening argument, the ratio does **not** invert once the denominator is taken correctly.
  4. **In 5 of the 10 frontier disagreements the tree, not the pointer, was stale**, so a generator sourcing the pointer from row 1 would have propagated the wrong value rather than prevented one.
- ⭐ **WHAT IS OWED INSTEAD IS A CHECK, NOT A WRITER, and this census is its calibration.** A checker reads the two mechanical fields and refuses a commit whose pointer names the wrong commit or a frontier row 1 it disagrees with. It writes nothing, so it cannot touch `next_action` or the prose; it catches every one of the **17** hand-classified instances; and because the disagreement is symmetric it must report *which* copy moved rather than assuming. Owned by `.11.4.2.4.1` — ⛔ not routed and parked: the calibration a new gate needs (`DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md`; `.11.9`'s gate rejected at 114-of-131) is finished here, over the whole 645-version history, with every instance classified by hand.
- 🔴 **THE INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG THREE TIMES BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT, and the sequence is kept because it IS the evidence** (`docs/knowledge/a-census-is-an-instrument-not-a-table.md`):
  - **227 wrong SHAs, where the history has 2.** The first cut let a carried token outrank a derivation instruction, so ``derive with `git log -1 --oneline`; review baseline `9c2d2ba` `` read as a claim that the latest commit was `9c2d2ba` — **217** bullets whose actual claim is *derive it*, with a review baseline beside it as a different fact. ⛔ The fix is ORDER and it was measured before it was written: of those 217, **217 put the hint first and 0 put a token first**, and all 217 SHAs are preceded by the literal words `review baseline`.
  - **34 manufactured frontier disagreements.** `normalise_leaf` concatenated literally, as `check_tree_index_frontier.sh` does — correct for `SIGNOFF-REPAIR` + `.11.4.2`, wrong for a tree whose own name ends in a number: the tree `PHASE-1` and the pointer's three-segment shorthand for `PHASE-1.1.1` concatenate to `PHASE-1.1.1.1`, a leaf that does not exist, against a row 1 of `PHASE-1.1.1`. Both readings are now returned and the second-reading population (**24**) is printed rather than absorbed.
  - **A SHA quoted inside a bullet's prose outranking the work-unit id that opens it** — `0e47b27`, cited in a lesson, scored as a latest-commit claim **601 commits stale**. Measured: of the 15 bullets carrying both kinds of token, **15 put the id first, 0 put the SHA first**. The project-prefix spellings `REPAIR-0219` and `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0219` were also being scored as different work units.
  - ⚠️ **And a fourth correction that moved no number, recorded because a fix with no effect is still a finding.** The truth table was keyed off the pointer-touching commits alone, so a parent that never touched `MEMORY.md` looked as though it had no work-unit id. Corrected to walk the whole `git log`; the verdicts were identical (135 / 12 / 5 before and after) and only a displayed diagnostic changed.
- ⛔ **THE PUBLISHED RATES CARRY THEIR REACH.** The 2.6% frontier figure is over the **385** versions that name a frontier leaf in a shape this instrument reads; the other **222** are era-1 progress prose (`` `SIGNOFF-REPAIR`. Full local checkpoint PASSED at `7233122` … ``) and some of them do assert a frontier in substance — `a710651`'s *"`.3.2.3` active"* is one. This census makes **no claim** about those, and says so instead of letting 375-of-385 read as 375-of-607 (`docs/knowledge/an-instruments-zero-describes-its-reach.md`, the rule this leaf's own three defects are further instances of). Likewise `status column — disagrees: 0` is over the **158** versions carrying a status token, not over 423.
- **Today's pointer is CORRECT on both mechanical fields** — `latest_commit` names its own commit's work unit and `active_work_unit` names row 1 with a matching status — so the drift measured here is historical and `.11.4.2.4.1` is prevention, not a live repair. Stated because a census that does not check the present invites the reader to assume the worst about it.
- promotion: declined (this leaf produced instances of two rules the layer already carries, not a new statement — `.11.6`'s threshold). The three instrument defects are a fourth, fifth and sixth instance of `an-instruments-zero-describes-its-reach` (promoted at `.13.4.6.3`, and these are its first uses since), and the denominator finding is `calibrate-over-the-history-that-contains-the-instance` met from a new side. `.11.6`'s threshold wants a statement the layer does not already carry; this leaf produced instances, not a new rule.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.2.4.1 — A currency check for the pointer's two mechanical fields

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.4.2.4`, which DECLINED the generator and owns the alternative here rather than routing it.
- The calibration is finished and is not owed again: **645 versions, 17 hand-classified instances** — 7 in `latest_commit` (one of them a hash naming no object in the repository) and 10 in the frontier leaf. `python3 -B scripts/census_memory_pointer_drift.py` reproduces every one.
- Owns: a check that `MEMORY.md`'s `latest_commit` names the work unit of the commit being made, and that its `active_work_unit` frontier leaf and status agree with the active tree's Current Frontier row 1.
- ⛔ **IT MUST NAME WHICH COPY MOVED, not assume the pointer is the stale one.** `.11.4.2.4` measured the disagreement as SYMMETRIC: in 5 of 10 instances the tree's row 1 was the copy that had not advanced, because a parent leaf had just been decomposed and the pointer named the first child. A message that says "the pointer is wrong" would be wrong half the time and would teach bypass.
- ⚠️ The dot-shorthand is genuinely ambiguous under a tree whose name ends in a number — the tree `PHASE-1` absorbs the leaf path's first segment — which cost the census 34 false disagreements. Whatever ships must accept both readings, as `normalise_leaf` now does — and ⛔ `scripts/check_tree_index_frontier.sh`'s `cell_leaf` carries the literal-concatenation bug today; it does not fire only because the active tree's name ends in a letter. That is a second finding this leaf owns, not a note.
- ⚠️ The frontier row-1 parser is `scripts/check_frontier_status.py`'s and is IMPORTED, never restated — one definition of row 1.
- Acceptance: the check is registered in `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md` with a `--self-test` proving both directions; it is calibrated against `.11.4.2.4`'s 17 instances rather than re-measured; it fires on none of today's tree (the present pointer is correct) and the leaf says so rather than claiming a present defect; `check_tree_index_frontier.sh`'s shorthand bug is either fixed or explicitly deferred with its reason; and `next_action` is provably untouched — the check writes nothing.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0349.
- **The gate: `scripts/check_pointer_currency.py`** (`POINTER-CURRENCY`, 17-control `--self-test`, registered in `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md`, the doctrine registry and the scaffold's `NEUTRAL` list — 23 checks now). It writes nothing, so the generator's whole risk surface — `next_action` and the 222 curated-prose bullets — is untouched by construction rather than by care.
- **Calibrated over the whole history, at `1fb5a94`: 646 pointer versions, 16 breaches across 15 commits, and 0 on today's tree.** ⛔ That last number is stated rather than left implicit: this gate catches nothing present, and its value is preventing recurrence. The 16 reconcile exactly with `.11.4.2.4`'s 17 hand-classified instances minus the one that is unflaggable in principle — the donor seed `BEDROCK-MAINTENANCE-0010` in the `Initial commit`'s pointer, which names a work unit no commit in THIS history carries.
- ⚠️ **The two instruments are NOT independent and the agreement is worth less than it looks.** The census asks *own or parent* and the gate asks *unused or HEAD* — different rules, and they agree. But both IMPORT the same parsing functions, so a parser defect is invisible to both. That is `docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` §1's row *two independent instruments agree… the classifier was shared* — named here rather than discovered later. What the falsification below adds is the part the shared parser cannot fake: breaks driven through the real files.
- 🔴 **FALSIFIED IN FOUR DIRECTIONS ON THE REAL FILES, each restored byte-identical** (SHA-256 compared before and after): an older work unit → refused by name; a frontier leaf the tree does not carry → refused; `ba6e77e` → *NOT A VALID OBJECT*; and ⭐ **the TREE's row 1 moved instead of the pointer** → refused with the same symmetric message, which is the arm that proves the gate is not simply asserting the pointer is wrong.
- 🔴 **AND THE FIRST FALSIFICATION ATTEMPT RETURNED rc=0 ON ALL THREE BREAKS.** The check reads the INDEX — correct, because the index is what a commit carries — and the breaks were in the working tree. ⛔ A gate reading different bytes from the ones in front of you is indistinguishable from a gate with nothing to say, which is this repository's fourth instrument to fail that way. The preference stays and the DIVERGENCE IS NOW ANNOUNCED, so a hand-run can never be misread as a verdict on what is on screen.
- 🔴 **A SECOND INSTRUMENT DEFECT, caught by the calibration disagreeing with the census: 151 fires where the history has 16.** `work_unit_already_committed` walked from today's `HEAD` while judging a commit from months ago, so the walk could see that very commit and a pointer CORRECTLY naming the commit it was part of looked like one reusing an id. Classified rather than argued: of the 140 flagged, **136 had the commit under test as the owner** and **0** had an owner in its future. The history bound is now a parameter, injected, and the rule was right the whole time. ⭐ The disagreement between two instruments is what surfaced it — neither alone would have.
- ✅ **`check_tree_index_frontier.sh`'s shorthand bug is FIXED, not deferred**, as the acceptance required. `cell_leaf` concatenated literally, so a tree whose name ends in a number produced a leaf that exists nowhere. ⛔ It never fired only because that gate checks the ACTIVE tree and the active tree's name ends in a letter — a latent defect waiting for the next `PHASE-N` tree to go active.
- 🔴 **AND MY FIRST FORMULATION OF THAT FIX WAS REFUSED BY THE GATE'S OWN SELF-TEST.** Offering the second reading whenever the tree name ends in a number turns `PHASE-8` + the shorthand `.5.3` into `PHASE-5.3` — *another tree's leaf* — and a reading that can match anything is a checker that cannot refuse. The existing prerequisite control caught it. ⭐ That is the case for keeping a control that looks redundant, and it is why the second reading is now offered ONLY when the shorthand's first segment IS the tree's trailing number — guarded in BOTH implementations, with a control each.
- ⛔ `next_action` is provably untouched: the gate has no write path at all. Asserted structurally rather than by a control, because a control over a function that does not exist is theatre.
- promotion: declined (a fourth and fifth instance of `an-instruments-zero-describes-its-reach`, promoted two commits ago at `.13.4.6.3` — the number describing the instrument, met once in a calibration harness and once in a falsification that read the wrong bytes. `.11.6`'s threshold wants a statement the layer lacks, and the layer has this one).
- NO REGRESSION: no product code, schema, migration or test touched. `make gate` → `=== all doctrines green ===`, **23 checks** (up from 22).
- Verification: `python3 -B scripts/check_pointer_currency.py --self-test` → `17 controls pass`, rc=0; `bash scripts/check_tree_index_frontier.sh --self-test` → rc=0 with `7 cell shapes normalised`; `python3 -B scripts/census_memory_pointer_drift.py --self-test` → `24 controls pass`.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0349 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.2.4.1): the pointer-currency gate the declined generator left owed, and the shorthand bug that made its own census lie`.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.2.6.3 — The second ledger's first rotation, and the chain it has to start

- Opened: `active` by `.11.4.2.6.2`, which derived the threshold, proved the mechanism and deliberately performed no rotation.
- REPRODUCE: `python3 -B scripts/rotate_changelog.py --ledger dev-notes --apply` → **rc=1**, *"carries no rotation ordinal to continue the chain from"*. The tool continues a chain and cannot start one, which is correct behaviour and is also the thing standing between this ledger and its bound.
- 🔴 **A latent defect found while reading the chain-start path, before any code was written for it**: `ordinal_word(0)` returns **`'twentieth'`** — `ORDINALS[-1]`, a silent negative-index wraparound. `render_footer` computes `prev_word = ordinal_word(ordinal - 1)`, so a first rotation would have rendered *"It carries the twentieth rotation's notice in turn"* into a governed ledger. ⛔ Wrong, and plausible-looking, which is the worst combination a rendered figure can have.
- Owns: refusing `ordinal_word` below 1 rather than wrapping; a `--bootstrap` path that starts a chain exactly once and is refused when a notice already exists, so it can never reset one; a first-rotation footer that does not claim a predecessor notice; the rotation itself; and flipping `enforced` once the ledger is demonstrably under its bound.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.2.6.3.1 — `LESSON-PROMOTION`'s decline scan is a race that the task tree outgrew

- Opened: `active` by `.11.4.2.6.3`, **whose commit it blocked**. ⛔ It shares that commit deliberately and the coupling is stated rather than hidden: this gate refuses a correct commit, so the leaf it refused cannot land until it is repaired. Same disposition as `.11.4.2.4.1`, which fixed `check_tree_index_frontier.sh` in its own commit rather than deferring it.
- 🔴 **THE DEFECT — a green gate reporting the opposite of what the tree says.** `scripts/check_lesson_promotion.sh` refused with *"1 new lesson entry in `DEV_NOTES.md` with NO promotion and NO explicit decline"* while the staged task tree carried **53** lines matching its own decline token, the owning leaf's among them.
- **ROOT CAUSE, measured not guessed.** The scan was `grep -E "$DECLINE_TOKEN \(..*\)" "$f" | grep -vqF "$DECLINE_TOKEN (<reason>)"`. `grep -q` exits on its first match and closes the pipe; the producer takes **SIGPIPE and exits 141**; `set -o pipefail` promotes that to the pipeline's status; and the `if` reads a decline that IS present as absent. ⛔ **It is a RACE, so it only bites once the producer's output outgrows the pipe buffer.** Measured on the real tree, whose matches now total **17,388 bytes**: **34 of 40 runs returned non-zero**, against **0 of 40** on a one-match file. The gate did not change — the task tree grew past it.
- ⭐ **It fails CLOSED, which is the safe direction AND the reason it was invisible.** A gate that wrongly PASSES gets found by the defect it let through; this one wrongly REFUSES and blames the author, who then rereads their own correct work looking for the mistake. `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.5`'s constraint is that a gate people route around is a gate that lies, and an intermittent false refusal is the fastest way to earn that.
- 🔴 **AND THE SELF-TEST COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT: nine green controls test `lesson_promotion_verdict`, which was never the broken part.** The pure verdict was carefully extracted and thoroughly controlled; the shell that computes its INPUTS was neither. A control over the decision says nothing about the extraction that feeds it.
- **Fix:** `declined_in` consumes all of its input — no `-q`, so no early close to race with — and the caller tests its output for emptiness.
- ✅ **FALSIFIED against the real defect**: the old racy form was restored into the file and the new self-test refused it by name — *"the decline scan MISSED on 9 of 12 runs over a large file — the SIGPIPE race is back"*, rc=2 — then the file was restored and `shasum -a 256 -c` returned `OK`. ⛔ The race arm needs **400 long matching lines**, because the old pipeline passed on a small file every single time; a control written against a tidy fixture would have been green on the broken code.
- Acceptance: the decline scan is deterministic over a file large enough to have raced; the self-test carries an arm that fails on the old form; the arm's fixture is large enough to reproduce it; and no gate is weakened — a placeholder `(<reason>)` is still rejected and a file with no decline still reports none.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0352.
- promotion: declined (the statement — a self-test over a pure verdict says nothing about the impure extraction feeding it — is a further instance of `docs/knowledge/a-self-test-cannot-be-tidier-than-the-real-input.md`, whose subject is exactly a fixture too clean to reproduce the defect. ⚠️ This instance sharpens it in a direction worth noting if a third appears: there the fixture was too tidy, here the tested UNIT was too small).
- Verification: `bash scripts/check_lesson_promotion.sh --self-test` → `9 verdict + 4 extraction controls (incl. the SIGPIPE race arm over a 400-line file)`, rc=0. `bash -n` clean. The three pre-existing behaviours re-controlled: no decline → none reported, one real decline → found, placeholder `(<reason>)` → rejected.
- Commit: shares `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0352` with `.11.4.2.6.3`, for the reason stated in its opening line.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.2.6.4 — The bound probe must name its subject, and must refuse over a tree that is already red

- Opened: `active` by `.11.4.2.6.3`, which caught the defect and recorded it rather than repairing it — the repair is this leaf, and it comes BEFORE the probe is used to judge the last ungoverned surface. ⛔ **An instrument that gave a wrong answer once is not evidence until the reason it was wrong is gone**, and `LIVE_STATUS.md`'s migration is the next thing it would be asked to grade.
- REPRODUCE, exactly as it happened: with `DEV_NOTES.md` missing its final newline, `python3 -B scripts/census_live_documents.py --probe-bounds` reported **`LIVE_STATUS.md … REFUSED (bounded)`** — a file with no size bound at all, no change in the commit, and a `FILE-TERMINATION` breach in a different file entirely.
- **ROOT CAUSE.** `probe_bound` appends bytes to ONE file and reads the enforcer's EXIT CODE. The enforcer's exit code is its verdict on the whole tree, so any breach anywhere reads as the probed file's bound. ⛔ The instrument's conclusion is an ABSENCE (*"nothing bounds this file"*), and `.11.25.1.1`'s rule made it carry positive controls — which it does, and they did not help, because the controls fail in the same direction for the same wrong reason.
- Owns: making the probe read the enforcer's REASON rather than its return code — a refusal counts only when a failing line NAMES the probed path; and establishing its own baseline first, refusing to report anything over a tree that is already red.
- ⛔ **Both halves are required and neither is sufficient.** Naming alone still misreports if the tree was red before the probe began; a baseline alone still misattributes a breach the probe itself provokes elsewhere.
- Acceptance: the classification is a pure function with controls in both directions (a line naming the subject, a line naming another file, no failing line at all); the probe refuses with a distinct message when its own baseline is red; the re-run reproduces the true four-of-five with `LIVE_STATUS.md` unbounded; and the leaf states plainly that the earlier five-of-five reading was wrong.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0353.
- ⛔ **STATED FIRST AND PLAINLY: the `5 of 5` this probe printed in the previous commit's session was WRONG.** The true reading was and is **4 of 5**. It was corrected by hand before anything shipped, and the hand correction is not the repair — this is.
- **Fix, in two halves, both required.** `probe_verdict(path, rc, output)` classifies from the enforcer's REASON: `unbounded` when rc is 0, `bounded` when a failing line NAMES the probed path, and `refused-for-another-file` otherwise — a state the instrument previously could not express, which is why it reported the wrong one. And `--probe-bounds` now runs the enforcer on the UNMODIFIED tree first and **exits 2 with a distinct message when that baseline is red**, because every verdict it prints is a difference from that run.
- ⛔ **Neither half is sufficient alone, and the leaf says so rather than shipping one.** Naming alone still misreports when the tree was red before the probe began — the failing line naming the subject might have been there already. A baseline alone still misattributes a breach the probe itself provokes in a different file.
- ⚠️ **THE POSITIVE CONTROLS DID NOT SAVE IT, AND THAT IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.** `.11.25.1.1`'s rule is that a probe whose conclusion is an absence owes a positive control in the same run, and this one carried three — `README.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, all refusing. They were useless here, because a breach anywhere makes every surface refuse: **the controls failed in the same direction, for the same wrong reason, as the thing they were controlling.** ⭐ A control only discriminates if it can come apart from its subject.
- ✅ **FALSIFIED BY RECREATING THE EXACT CONDITION THAT PRODUCED THE WRONG ANSWER** — `DEV_NOTES.md`'s final newline removed, which is precisely the state the tree was in when `5 of 5` was printed. The repaired probe returns **rc=2** and refuses to report at all: *"the enforcer is already red on the unmodified tree, so no verdict below would be a property of the file it names."* The file was then restored and `shasum -a 256 -c` returned `OK`; `git status` clean of it.
- ✅ **The live re-run reproduces the true result mechanically instead of by hand**: baseline green, then `README.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and `DEV_NOTES.md` each *"REFUSED (bounded — the refusal names this file)"*, and ⛔ **`LIVE_STATUS.md` `ACCEPTED (unbounded)`** — the one remaining ungoverned core live document.
- ⚠️ **AN HONEST SPLIT IN THE EVIDENCE, stated rather than blurred**: the BASELINE half is falsified live, against the real condition. The NAMING half is controlled by the self-test only — four arms, including a refusal naming another file and a **green** line naming the subject, which must not count as a refusal because the enforcer prints one `✅` line per check and those lines carry doctrine descriptions that mention these very filenames. Arranging a live case where probing one file provokes a breach naming a different one is not something the tree offers to hand, and claiming otherwise would be the kind of sentence this leaf exists to delete.
- promotion: declined (the statement — a positive control that fails in the same direction as its subject is not a control — is a sharpening of `docs/knowledge/a-control-that-passes-for-an-unrelated-reason.md`, which is the same note this probe's failure instanced one commit ago. ⚠️ **That is now three instances in two commits**, and the note's own text says a third should decide whether it earns its own statement; recorded here so the next session does not re-count from zero).
- Verification: `python3 -B scripts/census_live_documents.py --self-test` → **22 controls pass** (was 17), count derived by the runner. `--probe-bounds` over the real tree: baseline green, 4 bounded / 1 unbounded, all five restored byte-identically. `make gate` → `=== all doctrines green ===`.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0353 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.2.6.4): the bound probe reads the enforcer's reason, and refuses over a tree it has not baselined`.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.2.6.7.2 — The growth measurement costs more than the gate that would run it

- Opened: `active` by `.11.4.2.6.7`, whose falsification target is a GROWTH claim — `LIVE_STATUS.md`'s *overwritten rather than appended* — so the scheme cannot express the defect it exists for unless a growth assertion is affordable at commit time. ⛔ **This leaf makes one shared producer affordable and changes no behaviour, no registry row and no gate.**
- REPRODUCE / ISSUE: `census_live_documents.py`'s `measure_history` walks a path's versions with ONE `git cat-file -s` subprocess per version. Measured on the three ledgers the scheme must assert over — `LIVE_STATUS.md` 643 versions, `DEV_NOTES.md` 439, `CHANGELOG.md` 674 — it costs **23.24 s**, against a **28.74 s** whole-enforcer run. A pre-commit leg that nearly doubles the gate is the shape `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.5` refuses: a gate people route around is a gate that lies.
- Owns: making the existing measurement affordable without producing a second implementation of it. ⛔ **NOT by writing a faster copy beside it** — two producers of one number is the drift this repository keeps repairing — but by replacing the per-version subprocess inside the one shared function.
- Acceptance: the cost is measured before and after against the enforcer it would run inside; the replacement is proved OUTPUT-IDENTICAL by running HEAD's own script against the SAME tree rather than before-and-after on a moving one (`.11.4.2.6.6.2`); every field of every `History` is compared, not just the size; the skip semantics for a revision whose object is absent are preserved and tested; and no caller, threshold, registry row or gate changes.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0356.
- ✅ **ONE `git cat-file --batch-check` PROCESS PER PATH INSTEAD OF ONE PER VERSION, inside the existing `measure_history`** — extracted as `version_sizes` so the walk is addressable and `batch_sizes` so the parse is testable. ⛔ No second implementation: the function every caller already uses got faster, rather than gaining a fast twin that can disagree with it.
- ⭐ **THE COST, MEASURED AGAINST THE THING IT WOULD RUN INSIDE rather than in the abstract.** The three ledgers a growth assertion must cover hold 1,756 versions and cost **23.24 s** on the per-version walk, against a **28.74 s** whole-enforcer run — a leg that nearly doubles the gate. They now cost **0.11 s**. Across the 24 paths compared below, **62.19 s → 0.79 s (79×)** with the same numbers.
- ✅ **OUTPUT-IDENTICAL, PROVED BY THE METHOD `.11.4.2.6.6.2` ESTABLISHED**: HEAD's own script was extracted with `git show` and run against the SAME tree as the new one, so a code change is not conflated with a tree that moved. **24 paths, 4,579 versions, every FIELD of every `History` compared — not just the size — and 0 disagreements.**
- 🔴 **AND THE REAL-TREE COMPARISON DID NOT COVER THE ONE SEMANTIC AT RISK, WHICH I CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** The behaviour being preserved is a SKIP: the old walk tested `returncode == 0`, so a commit that DELETED the path — `git log -- path` reports it, `rev:path` does not resolve there — stayed out of the series. **No routed path has ever been deleted**, so all 20 of them exercise it zero times, and a green comparison over them would have been a control that passes for an unrelated reason.
- ✅ **So the skip was measured on paths that DO exercise it**: `docs/decisions/reference_bedrock_provenance.md`, `docs/tasks/BEDROCK-MAINTENANCE.md` and `MAINTAINING.md` each have **2 revisions and 1 resolvable object**, and old and new agree on all three, each dropping exactly one revision. ⭐ Five self-test controls pin the parse besides, including the two ways it could go wrong in opposite directions: a miss counted as **0** instead of dropped, and an `id blob size` report read as a bare size.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.2.6.8 — The rotation notice calls HEAD's bytes "immediately before the rotation", and a rotation runs on a dirty tree

- Opened: `pending`, found by `.11.4.2.6.7.2` while running the rotation `LEDGER-RUNWAY` prescribed for its own commit. ⛔ Not fixed in that leaf: it is a different instrument, and the pivot rule holds.
- REPRODUCE: `DEV_NOTES.md` held **74,204 bytes** immediately before the rotation, of which 2,948 were that commit's own uncommitted entry. The notice it wrote names `918f446` and says *"The exact predecessor — every byte this file held immediately before the rotation"*; that object is **71,256 bytes**. The sentence is false by exactly the uncommitted delta, and the workflow that produces a rotation always has one, because `COMMIT.md` adds the entry that crosses the threshold in the same commit that rotates.
- 🔴 **AND IT WAS NOT DISCOVERED HERE — IT WAS DECLARED AND LEFT.** `.11.4.2.6.3`'s acceptance already carries *"an honest limit on the notice's wording … strictly it holds every byte held at the named commit"*, written at the first `DEV_NOTES.md` rotation and repeated in the leaf body. Stating a defect in the leaf that ships it, with no owner, is `.11.13`'s finding exactly: a limitation ROUTED rather than owned. This leaf is that ownership, and the framing correction belongs on the record rather than letting this read as a fresh discovery.
- ⭐ **THE GUARANTEE IS INTACT AND THE DEFECT IS THE SENTENCE, which is worth separating rather than escalating.** `rotate_changelog.py` verifies every retired heading against `HEAD:<ledger>` before writing the notice and REFUSES otherwise, so a record living only in the working tree cannot be retired into a predecessor that lacks it. Nothing can be lost; a published claim is simply untrue.
- ⚠️ **It is the same class `.11.4.2.6.6` repaired one lane over**: a renderer describing a procedure in words written for a different one. There the notice made three false claims for a seal; here it makes one about what the predecessor is.
- Owns: making the notice say what the named object actually is. ⛔ **The candidate repair is a SENTENCE, not a mechanism** — the anchor must stay at HEAD, because the whole point is a commit a reader can `git show`, and a working-tree state has no address.
- ⚠️ Census owed before the wording is chosen (`.11.6`): how many of this project's rotation notices were written over a dirty ledger, and is the delta always the rotating commit's own entry or sometimes more? A wording fitted to one instance is fitted to one instance.
- Acceptance: the census is recorded with the command that produced it; the replacement sentence is true for BOTH the clean and the dirty case rather than only the one measured; the losslessness guard is proved unchanged; and no threshold, ledger or retired record moves.
- Status: `done`; DOC-0097.
- ⭐ **THE CENSUS, AND IT IS THE MAJORITY CASE RATHER THAN THE INSTANCE I HAPPENED TO HIT: at least 31 of 48 rotation notices describe a ledger that had moved since the commit they name.** `CHANGELOG.md` 29 of 46, `DEV_NOTES.md` 2 of 2, `LIVE_STATUS.md` 0 of 0 — its transition was a SEAL whose notice `.11.4.2.6.6` wrote by hand, and it already says *at the commit named below*. Shipped as `python3 -B scripts/rotate_changelog.py --audit-notices` rather than recorded as a number, because a published number owes a producer.
- ⚠️ **AND THE CENSUS IS A LOWER BOUND, WHICH IT SAYS IN ITS OWN OUTPUT.** It detects a moved ledger only when the rotating commit added a WHOLE record — the same heading-disappearance predicate this file uses everywhere — so a working tree that edited an existing record is invisible to it and counted clean. The 17 "clean" rotations are *not measured clean*; they are *not measured dirty*.
- ⭐ **The delta is uniformly ONE record, never a pile**: exactly one own record in all 31, between **388 and 5,563 bytes** for `CHANGELOG.md` and **2,947 and 8,019** for `DEV_NOTES.md`. That is the workflow's signature — `COMMIT.md` writes the entry that crosses the threshold in the commit that rotates — and it is why a wording fitted to one instance would still have been fitted to the right shape.
- ✅ **THE REPAIR IS A SENTENCE AND THE ANCHOR DOES NOT MOVE.** *"The exact predecessor — this file as it stood at the commit named below, which is the object every retired record was checked against before this notice was written"*. ⛔ Anchoring to the working tree was never available: a state that was never committed has no address a reader can `git show`, and the retrieval command is the notice's entire purpose. ⭐ The replacement is also STRONGER than accurate — it tells the reader why that object is the right one, which the old sentence only implied.
- ✅ **TRUE IN BOTH CASES BY CONSTRUCTION, not by fitting**: it describes the named object and makes no claim about the tree at rotation time, so the clean rotation and the dirty one are described identically and correctly.
- ✅ **FALSIFIED IN SITU** — the old wording put back inside the current file: `--self-test` **rc=1 with 3 controls red by name** (*the notice still claims the working tree's bytes*, *does not say which object it names*, *does not say why that object is the right one*), and **rc=0** restored. The file was compared with `cmp -s` after restoring and is byte-identical.
- ⛔ **THE LOSSLESSNESS GUARD IS PROVED UNCHANGED, and it is the thing that made this safe all along**: `--apply` still refuses when any retired heading is absent from `HEAD:<ledger>`, so a record living only in the working tree cannot be retired into a predecessor that lacks it. The two self-test arms covering that refusal are untouched and still pass. **Nothing was ever at risk of being lost; a published sentence was untrue.**
- ✅ **THE TWO LIVE NOTICES ARE CORRECTED TOO**, not only the renderer — `CHANGELOG.md` and `DEV_NOTES.md` each carry one current footer, and a reader meets those rather than the code. ⚠️ The dated ENTRIES that quote the old sentence as the defect are history and stay.
- promotion: declined — the transferable statement is *a renderer written for one procedure describes a different one in that procedure's words*, which `.11.4.2.6.6` established with three false claims in one notice and which this is the fourth instance of, in the same renderer. It is recorded there and in the source; a note restating it would be the mirror this lane keeps removing.
- Verification: `python3 -B scripts/rotate_changelog.py --self-test` → **38 controls pass** (was 35), count derived by the runner; `--check` rc=0; `--audit-notices` reproduces 31 of 48. `git grep -c "immediately before the rotation" -- scripts/ CHANGELOG.md DEV_NOTES.md` returns only the one dated entry that quotes it AS the defect. `make gate` → `=== all doctrines green ===`; `make book` and `bash scripts/check_book_links.sh` rc=0.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-DOC-0097 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.2.6.8): the rotation notice now describes the object it names, and 31 of 48 said otherwise`.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.2.6.6.1 — The record boundary cannot be derived from this log, so the migration must not try

- Opened: `active` by `.11.4.2.6.6`, whose first owned step is creating the boundary its file lacks. ⛔ **This leaf creates nothing**: it asks whether a boundary CAN be derived, because the answer decides which migration is safe, and a migration chosen before that question is answered is one that finds out during the transition.
- **The candidate population.** `LIVE_STATUS.md`'s correction log has no headings under `## Qualification correction`; its entries are emoji-led paragraphs at column 0. **320 lines match that shape.** Of those, **265 carry a leaf id or a work-unit id** and **55 carry neither**.
- 🔴 **NO MECHANICAL SIGNAL SEPARATES A HEADLINE FROM A CONTINUATION, and the discriminator I expected to work does not.** Classifying each candidate by what PRECEDES it: of the 55 id-less ones, **46 directly follow another entry headline**, 7 follow other prose and 2 follow a bullet. But the 265 id-carrying ones distribute the same way — **95 of them also directly follow another headline**, 169 follow a bullet, 1 follows a heading. ⛔ The context that would have to distinguish a second paragraph of one entry from the first paragraph of the next is identical in both classes.
- ⭐ **THE DECISION THIS FORCES IS BETTER THAN THE ONE IT BLOCKS.** A boundary could still be created by hand-classifying 320 candidates — this repository does hand-classify populations, and has for seven, seventeen and forty-five of them. But the work would be spent retrofitting structure onto **content that is entirely historical**, and the guide's step 7 does not ask for that. It asks to *freeze the exact source boundary* and *create the new current view*.
- ✅ **So the migration SEALS the existing log wholesale into git history rather than rotating it at boundaries it does not have**, and the boundary is created only for what is written AFTER the split, where it can be enforced from the first entry instead of inferred from 320 old ones. ⛔ That is not a shortcut: sealing preserves every byte exactly and retrievably, which is the property rotation exists to provide, and it removes the one step — classifying 320 paragraphs — where a migration could silently lose or merge a record.
- ⚠️ **Stated so the next leaf does not re-open it**: the shipped `rotate_changelog.py` is therefore NOT the instrument for this file's history. It is the instrument for this file's FUTURE, once the new log carries dated `## ` records like the two ledgers it already serves.
- Acceptance: the candidate population is counted; the discriminator is tested and its failure measured rather than asserted; the migration strategy follows from that measurement rather than from resemblance to the other two ledgers; and nothing is created, sealed or moved here.
- Status: `done`; DOC-0095.
- 🔴 **AND MY OWN FIRST COUNT OF THIS POPULATION WAS WRONG IN THE USUAL DIRECTION.** I reported *"320 correction entries"* and used it as the entry count; it is the count of emoji-led LINES, which conflates headlines with continuation paragraphs. The file's own earlier census said 318 and that number was produced the same way. ⛔ Neither is the number of entries, and this leaf does not publish one — because the whole finding is that no mechanical rule produces it. A third instance this session of `docs/knowledge/an-instruments-first-population-describes-its-parser.md`.
- promotion: declined (a third instance of the parser-population note, already promoted, and the sealing decision is a disposition about this file rather than a transferable method — it is recorded in the leaf and carried into `.11.4.2.6.6`'s acceptance).
- Verification: the discriminator measured in both directions in one run — 55 id-less candidates classified by preceding context (46 headline / 7 other / 2 bullet) against 265 id-carrying ones (95 headline / 169 bullet / 1 heading), which is the positive control: if context discriminated, the two distributions would differ and they do not. `make gate` → `=== all doctrines green ===`.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-DOC-0095 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.2.6.6.1): the record boundary cannot be derived from this log, so the migration seals it instead`.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.2.6.6.2 — The live window is a project constant, not a quantity each ledger re-derives

- Opened: `active` by `.11.4.2.6.6`, whose constraint is that the ceiling may not be chosen in the slice that migrates under it. ⛔ **This leaf derives the ceiling and migrates nothing.**
- 🔴 **THE FINDING, AND IT IS ABOUT THE METHOD RATHER THAN THE NUMBER: the derivation's own anchor drifted.** `DEV_NOTES.md`'s threshold was derived at `7fc8913` as *the live window `CHANGELOG.md` runs*, measured as `96,000 / p90 4,734 = 20.279` p90-entries. Eight commits later `CHANGELOG.md`'s p90 is **4,146**, so the same formula now reads **23.155**. ⛔ Applying it today would give the third ledger a window **14% more generous than the second**, for no reason but the date on which it was computed.
- ⭐ **So the window is promoted to a PROJECT CONSTANT, pinned to the moment it was first derived, and every ledger's threshold is that one window expressed in its own measured entry size.** A rule whose anchor moves is not a derivation; it is a fashion. `LIVE_WINDOW = 20.279 p90-entries`, pinned at `7fc8913`.
- ✅ **`LIVE_STATUS.md`'s threshold: `20.279 × p90 2,726 = 55,280` → 55,000, rounded DOWN**, because rounding up grants headroom the derivation does not support. ✅ `DEV_NOTES.md`'s **76,000 stands** — it was derived at the pinned moment and needs no revision.
- ⚠️ **ONE THRESHOLD PER FILE, and the snapshot gets no separate cap — stated rather than quietly omitted.** The adoption guide asks for pressure axes measured independently, and a `bounded_snapshot` sharing a ledger's ceiling can in principle eat the log's runway. It gets none here because **a cap must be derived from a deliberately reviewed survivor and that survivor does not exist yet** — the file has not been split. Inventing one now would be fitting a ceiling to a file I am imagining. If the split survivor shows the snapshot needs its own bound, it gets one then, from the thing itself.
- ⚠️ `entry_size_p90` needs no record boundary — it measures bytes added per non-rotation commit, not per record — which is why a threshold is derivable for a file whose records `.11.4.2.6.6.1` proved cannot be identified.
- Acceptance: the window's drift is measured rather than asserted; the constant is pinned to a named commit with its inputs; the third ledger's threshold is derived from the pinned constant, not from today's; the second ledger's threshold is checked against the constant and left alone if it agrees; the third ledger is registered `enforced=False` with its debt recorded; and ⛔ nothing is migrated and no threshold is raised.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0354.
- ✅ **`LIVE_WINDOW = 20.279` ships as a named constant with its derivation and its pin in the source**, and both derived thresholds are now expressed against it. `LIVE_STATUS.md` joins as a third `Ledger` at **55,000** (`20.279 × 2,726 = 55,280`, rounded DOWN), `enforced=False` with its debt and both blocking measurements recorded on the row.
- ✅ **`DEV_NOTES.md`'s 76,000 is UNCHANGED and that is the check passing, not an omission** — it was derived at the pinned moment, and re-deriving it today would be the exact mistake this leaf exists to stop.
- ⭐ **Two controls now hold the relation without re-measuring anything**: each threshold must be at most the pinned window times the p90 recorded at its derivation, and within 1,000 bytes of it, so a ceiling can never be quietly raised above what its derivation supports; and the window itself is pinned against `96000 / 4734`, so the constant cannot drift silently either.
- ⛔ **THE GATE IS UNMOVED: `--check` stays rc=0 over the two enforced ledgers**, while `--check-all` now returns rc=1 naming `LIVE_STATUS.md has -564304 bytes of headroom under its 55000-byte threshold`. The debt is measurable on demand and sits off the commit path, exactly as `DEV_NOTES.md`'s did before its migration.
- ⭐ **AND THE NO-BEHAVIOUR-CHANGE CLAIM IS PROVED BY A BETTER METHOD THAN LAST TIME.** `.11.4.2.6.2` captured `--plan` before and after, which conflates a code change with a tree that moved underneath it — and it did move: `CHANGELOG.md`'s p90 fell 4,734 → 4,146 and its plan went from retiring 3 records to 6 in eight commits. Here HEAD's own script was extracted with `git show` and run against the SAME tree as the modified one: **byte-identical for `CHANGELOG.md` and for `DEV_NOTES.md`**. ⛔ That separates the two variables instead of hoping only one moved.
- promotion: declined (the statement — *a derivation whose anchor moves is not a derivation* — is recorded in the source beside the constant and in `docs/decisions/2026-09-21_the-second-ledgers-threshold-is-the-first-ledgers-window.md`'s successor position; it is a disposition about this repository's ledgers rather than a transferable method, and `.11.6`'s threshold wants a statement the layer lacks. ⚠️ If a second derived constant in this repository is found to have drifted since it was set, it becomes a knowledge note; the count is one).
- Verification: `python3 -B scripts/rotate_changelog.py --self-test` → **35 controls pass** (was 32), count derived by the runner. `--check` rc=0; `--check-all` rc=1 naming `LIVE_STATUS.md`. `--plan` byte-identical to HEAD's script on the same tree for both enforced ledgers. `make gate` → `=== all doctrines green ===`, 24 checks.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0354 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.2.6.6.2): the live window is a project constant, because the anchor it was read from drifted 14% in eight commits`.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.3.1.7.1 — The cluster instrument's self-test could only ever pass once

- Opened: `pending`; found on 2026-09-13 by RUNNING `--self-test` before acting on the instrument's census, which is the only reason it was noticed.
- 🔴 The finding: `census_pg_test_clusters.py --self-test` exits 1 with `SELF-TEST FAILED: citation guard: an absent name reported references`. The guard's absent-name arm searches tracked files for the literal `run-selftest-no-such-cluster-name` and asserts zero hits — but **that literal is written in the instrument's own source**, which is a tracked file, so `git grep -c -- "run-selftest-no-such-cluster-name"` returns `scripts/census_pg_test_clusters.py:1`. The control searches for a string it contains.
- **Dated rather than estimated:** `git log --diff-filter=A -- scripts/census_pg_test_clusters.py` and `git log -S "run-selftest-no-such-cluster-name"` both name the SAME commit, `cb2f197` (REPAIR-0107, leaf `.11.4.3.1.7`). So the arm passed exactly once — while the file was still untracked and `git grep` could not see it — and has failed from the instant it was committed.
- census of why that survived, the claim one counterexample would refute: `git grep -n "census_pg_test_clusters" -- scripts .githooks .github Makefile knowledge-map` returns **2** hits and both are inside the instrument's own usage docstring. **Nothing invokes it**, self-test or otherwise. Widened to the enforcer: `grep -n "self-test" scripts/check_doctrines.sh` returns **0** — the registered doctrine checks carry `--self-test` arms too, and the enforcer runs none of them. Author-run only, across the board.
- ⚠️ What this does and does not compromise, stated precisely because the instrument guards a deletion: the guard's OTHER direction (a tracked filename reports non-zero) still passes, so cited clusters were still protected. What was lost is the proof that the guard is not simply returning non-zero for everything — i.e. the guard was half-verified, and a half-verified safety check must not authorise retiring 1.8 GB.
- Owns: making the probe a name that CANNOT appear in a tracked file (generated per run rather than written as a literal), so the control cannot poison itself again; and deciding whether the instrument's self-test gains a runner, since "nothing ran it" is the reason a control could sit broken from its own first commit.
- ⛔ Do not simply exclude the script from the grep: that would make the guard blind to the one file most likely to name a cluster in a comment, and it treats the symptom rather than the self-reference.
- Acceptance: `--self-test` exits 0 with both citation directions firing; the absent-name probe is demonstrably absent by construction, not by luck; the §8 retirement runs only after the instrument's own control passes.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0137.
- Fix: the absent-name probe is `f"run-selftest-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"`, generated per run. A literal written in a tracked file can never be absent from the tracked tree; a fresh uuid always is. The comment beside it names the trap so the next author does not re-introduce a literal, and the failure message now prints the probe it used, so a future failure says WHICH name was found rather than restating a constant.
- ⛔ The `git grep` was deliberately NOT narrowed to exclude this script, per the leaf's own prohibition: that would blind the guard to the one file most likely to name a cluster in a comment, and it treats the symptom rather than the self-reference.
- Verification: `python3 -B scripts/project_env.py python3 -B scripts/census_pg_test_clusters.py --self-test` prints `self-test: 6 refusal arms and the citation guard's two directions all fire`, rc=0. **FALSIFIED** by restoring the literal: rc=1 with `SELF-TEST FAILED: citation guard: the absent name run-selftest-no-such-cluster-name reported references`, and rc=0 again on restore. Two-sided on the exact defect.
- ⭐ **And the repair immediately paid for itself: the §8 review it gates had been blocked behind it.** With the control passing, the retirement ran — the first one since `cb2f197`, because the instrument's own self-test had been failing for every review in between.
- **The §8 artifact review, run here** (`CLAUDE.md` §8; `MEMORY.md` recorded it owed on resumption). Census before: **34 clusters / 1,797,794,711 bytes**. Independent safety checks beyond the instrument's own: no process holds a `postmaster.pid` under `target/pg-tests` (probed per cluster, twice, and `ps aux | grep '[p]ostgres'` returns none), and `target/pg-tests` and the repository root report the same filesystem id `100001c0000001a`, so §13's same-volume requirement holds. Retired **30**, freeing **1,591,802,083 bytes**; residue verified at **4 clusters / 205,992,628 bytes**, and a re-census reports `retirable: 0`.
- ⛔ The four survivors are named with WHY, because "kept" without a reason is how evidence gets deleted next time: `run-2o_84bf0`, `run-41n50qyw` and `run-q8myx344` are each cited by a tracked file and are therefore evidence; `run-ptzio417` is under the one-hour floor — it is THIS session's own falsification cluster from `.3.4.3.1.1`, and the floor is what stops a run still being read from being swept. All four were confirmed present after the retirement.
- promotion: declined for a new record — the durable statement is the instrument itself, whose self-test now cannot poison itself and whose comment says why. ⚠️ But the second half of this leaf's finding is NOT closed by it and must not look closed: **nothing runs any `--self-test` in this repository**, the doctrine checks included (`grep -n "self-test" scripts/check_doctrines.sh` -> 0). That is why a control could sit broken from its own first commit, and it is routed to `.11.4.3.1.7.2` rather than absorbed here.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0137 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.3.1.7.1): the self-test searched for a string it contained`.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.3.1.7.2 — Nothing runs a `--self-test`

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.4.3.1.7.1`, whose repaired control had been failing from its own first commit because no runner existed to notice.
- census, recorded here rather than in the parent because the claim quantifies over the tree: `git grep -n "census_pg_test_clusters" -- scripts .githooks .github Makefile knowledge-map` returns **2** hits, both inside the instrument's own usage docstring — nothing invokes it. Widened to the enforcer that would be the natural runner, `grep -n "self-test" scripts/check_doctrines.sh` returns **0**, so none of the 17 registered doctrine checks has its `--self-test` arm run either. Author-run only, across the board.
- Owns: deciding whether self-tests get a runner, and which. ⛔ Census owed first, per `.11.6`: how many tracked scripts HAVE a `--self-test`, how long each takes, and whether running them in the pre-commit enforcer is affordable against the gate's existing cost — `make gate` is on every commit, and a gate people route around is a gate that lies (`.11.5`'s binding constraint).
- ⚠️ Widened on 2026-09-13 by `.3.5`'s census, which ran every census instrument's `--self-test` before trusting its output (this leaf's own lesson, applied): `census_admission_paths.py` reports 5/5 and `census_pg_test_clusters.py` passes, but **`census_authority_paths.py` has no `--self-test` at all** — it takes the flag as a git revision and dies with a `CalledProcessError` traceback rather than a usage error. So the population is not only "self-tests nothing runs" but also "instruments with no self-test to run", and this leaf owns counting both.
- ⚠️ The obvious rule — "the enforcer runs every self-test" — may be wrong in the way `.11.4.5.3`'s generator was. Some self-tests spawn processes or touch the filesystem, and a pre-commit hook is not the place for all of them. Measure before proposing.
- Acceptance: the census is recorded with its command; the decision names which self-tests run where, with the cost measured rather than assumed; "measured and deliberately not mechanized" stays a legitimate outcome.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0142. Mechanized, and the cost was measured before the rule was proposed rather than after.
- **The census, with its commands.** `git grep -l -- "--self-test" -- scripts knowledge-map .githooks | wc -l` -> **17** scripts carry one; `ls scripts/check_*.sh knowledge-map/scripts/check_*.sh scripts/census_*.py | wc -l` -> **28** check/census scripts in total. So **11 have no `--self-test` at all**, which the widened finding at `.3.5` had already shown for `census_authority_paths.py`.
- **The cost, measured rather than estimated, because `.11.5`'s constraint is binding.** Running all 17 takes **1.01 s** in total (the slowest is `census_pg_test_clusters.py` at 0.23 s; twelve are under 0.05 s), and `make gate` costs **3.15 s**. With the new check registered the gate measures **4.27 s** over 18 checks — a real increase of 1.12 s. One second on a three-second gate is not a gate anyone routes around, which is exactly the test `.11.5` set.
- **The decision: MECHANIZE.** `scripts/check_self_tests.sh`, registered as `SELF-TEST` and mirrored in `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md`. It DISCOVERS the population rather than carrying a list, so a new instrument with a self-test is covered the day it lands — which is the property a hand-maintained list would lose the first time someone forgot.
- ⛔ **The gate catches NOTHING today and the check says so in its own header.** All 17 pass. Its value is preventing the `.11.4.3.1.7.1` class — a control that silently stops working — not finding a present defect. A green run is not evidence of one.
- 🔴 **I fell into this gate's own trap while building it, and the defence is stronger because of it.** The check warns at length about self-reference, and excluding its own path was the obvious guard. It was not enough: REGISTERING the check put the flag's literal text into `check_doctrines.sh`'s description, so discovery found the **ENFORCER**, ran it with the flag, and the enforcer — which ignores unknown arguments — ran every check including this one. Unbounded recursion on the first `make gate` after registration; the command was killed at 400 s. The gate exists because a control searched for a string it contained, and building it I made a discovery match a string it had just written.
- Defended twice now, the first making the failure impossible rather than unlikely: an exported `RB_SELF_TEST_GATE` makes any nested invocation exit immediately, so no discovery mistake can recurse; and the enforcer is excluded by path because it is the RUNNER, not a check. Both are asserted by the self-test, alongside the failing-arm and passing-arm directions.
- ⚠️ Residual, in the script's header rather than hidden: a script that merely MENTIONS the flag without implementing it is run with an argument it ignores — i.e. run normally. Every member of the discovered population is a read-only check or census, so that is harmless today; it would not be for a mutating script, and a future one must be excluded there.
- Verification: `bash scripts/check_self_tests.sh --self-test` prints `a failing arm caught, a passing one ignored, neither this script nor the enforcer discovered, the recursion guard short-circuits, 17 scripts discovered`, rc=0 — four-sided. `bash scripts/check_self_tests.sh` rc=0 in 1.05 s. `make gate` prints `=== all doctrines green ===` across **18 checks** in 4.27 s. `mdbook build` and `bash scripts/check_book_links.sh` rc=0, `git diff --check` rc=0.
- **FALSIFIED end to end against the real defect, not a synthetic one**: restoring `census_pg_test_clusters.py`'s literal probe — the exact `.11.4.3.1.7.1` defect — makes `make gate` print `❌ SELF-TEST`, quote `citation guard: the absent name run-selftest-no-such-cluster-name reported references`, and refuse the commit with `1 doctrine breach(es)`. Restoring the repair returns it to green. The gate would have caught the defect that motivated it, on the commit that introduced it.
- ⛔ NOT claimed: this does not give the 11 script without a self-test one, and does not assert that the 17 self-tests are GOOD — only that they still pass. A weak self-test that passes is invisible to this gate, as it should be: judging a control's strength is a reader's job, and `.11.5`'s accepted item (1) — a control must have failed on the defect it was written for — is the separate rule for that.
- promotion: declined for a new `docs/knowledge/` record — the durable statement is the registered doctrine itself, whose `DOCTRINE_ENFORCEMENT.md` row carries the measurement, the cost, what it does not catch, and the recursion it fell into. That is the strongest form this project has.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0142 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.3.1.7.2): run the self-tests, including the one this gate fell into`.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.3.1.7 — Re-run the periodic artifact review, with a tracked instrument

- Opened: `pending`; the `CLAUDE.md` §8 review is due (`MEMORY.md` recorded it as owed on resumption) and `.11.4.3.1.6`'s compiler-cache retirement left no instrument behind — its selection, probes and manifests were task-owned evidence, so the next review starts from prose.
- census, before any disposition: `python3 -B scripts/project_env.py python3 -B scripts/census_pg_test_clusters.py` reports **13 retained clusters / 676,882,885 bytes** under `target/pg-tests`. Every one carries `state: stopped` (the runner verified shutdown) and `command_exit: 101`; by suite, 8 are `profiles`, 4 are `command_ordering` and 1 is `node_result_ordering`, aged 0.1–5.2 hours. `ps aux | grep '[p]ostgres'` returns **0** live servers, and `git grep -c` over each of the 13 names returns **0** tracked files naming any of them — so none is cited evidence.
- Owns: the instrument, not one cleanup. `scripts/census_pg_test_clusters.py` censuses the retained clusters and, only under `--retire --confirm`, removes those passing every check: the receipt says `stopped`, no `postmaster.pid` process is alive, the path is a real directory on the REPOSITORY's own volume, no tracked file names it, and it is older than an age floor. Each check is re-run immediately before the removal, because a census is a snapshot.
- Scope bound, stated rather than implied: this leaf owns the runner's retained clusters. The compiler cache under `target/debug` is NOT touched here — `.11.4.3.1.6` established that it needs native lock probes against the exact installed compiler and a frozen identity-bound manifest, and repeating that at signoff quality is its own slice. What this leaf adds for it is a measurement, and the measurement corrected the obvious guess.
- Where the bytes actually are, measured with `du -sk target/*` and `du -sk target/debug/*` rather than assumed: `target/debug` is **194,349,388 KiB** and every other child of `target` together is under 3.5 GiB, the next largest being `ci-browser` at 1,663,708 KiB and the retained clusters at 101,192 KiB AFTER this leaf's retirement. Inside it, `target/debug/deps` is **134,478,136 KiB** and `target/debug/incremental` is **58,989,732 KiB**.
- That ordering is the finding, because it is the opposite of the expectation this leaf started with. `.11.4.3.1.6` retired **incremental sessions**, which is the cache Cargo garbage-collects and the one with a documented lock protocol; `deps` is 2.3x larger and Cargo does not collect it — a changed crate writes new `.rlib`/`.rmeta`/binary artifacts under fresh hashes and the superseded ones stay. Concrete owner opened: `.11.4.3.1.8`. No deletion under `target/debug` is attempted here, and none should be until that leaf establishes identity and in-use checks for a directory the linker reads by hash.
- Acceptance: the instrument fires every refusal on purpose, the removal names what it removed, and a residue census proves exactly the expected set remains.
- Verification: `--self-test` passes — six refusal arms (a clean cluster refuses nothing, an unverified shutdown, a missing receipt, an unreadable receipt, a live postmaster using this process's own pid, an age under the floor) plus the citation guard in BOTH directions (a tracked filename reports references, an absent name reports none). `--retire --confirm` removed **11 clusters / 573,416,291 bytes** and the residue census verified the **2** remaining, both kept by the age floor because they are this session's own baselines for `.3.3.4.5` and `.3.3.4.4.1`. `make gate` (17 checks) and the Python control suite pass.
- promotion: declined (the durable statement IS the tracked instrument and its `--self-test`; a method statement about retained clusters would be the thing `.11.4.3.1.6` already proved does not survive).
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0107 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.3.1.7): census and retire the runner's retained clusters with a tracked instrument`.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.4.3.1.9 — The artifact sweep, measured before it is run

- Opened: `pending` by the director's instruction 2026-09-19 — *"Clean up target whenever you see fit"* — and MEASURED before anything was deleted, which changed what should be done.
- ⛔ **THE STANDING PROHIBITION HOLDS AND IS RESTATED HERE SO NO SWEEP FORGETS IT:** `cargo clean` must NOT be used. It would take `target/pg-tests`, `target/ci-browser` and `target/browser-lifetime-controls`, which are CITED evidence (`MEMORY.md`, DOC-0060).
- 🔴 **THE MEASUREMENT THAT MAKES A NAIVE SWEEP DESTRUCTIVE: 101 of the 257 top-level `.log` files are CITED in tracked Markdown.** They are the verification records of roughly a hundred closed leaves — `pg*_guard.log`, `*_offline.log`, `load_harness_run.log`, `release_manifest.log`. ⛔ `rm target/*.log` would delete the evidence those leaves' acceptance checklists point at. Re-derive:

```bash
for f in $(find target -maxdepth 1 -name '*.log' | sed 's|target/||'); do
  git grep -q -- "$f" -- '*.md' && echo "CITED: $f"
done
```

- ⭐ **AND THE SWEEP IS NOT WORTH RUNNING, which is the finding rather than the excuse.** The 156 UNCITED logs total **2,680 KB — 2.6 MB of a 16 GB tree, under 0.02%.** Directive 8 names logs and `.bin` files first, and here they are rounding error. `target/debug` alone is **11.9 GB, 74% of the tree**; `target/release` is 1.4 GB; `target/pg-tests` 1.2 GB and `target/ci-browser` 0.5 GB are both cited evidence.
- **So the only disposition that moves the number is the debug tree's, and that is `.11.4.3.1.8`'s, already decided once:** DOC-0060 retired `target/debug` on the director's instruction and it has grown back to 11.9 GB because every build refills it. ⚠️ Retiring it again buys ~12 GB and costs the next build a cold rebuild — measured at **68m 16s** on this host, under `syspolicyd` contention and exhausted swap. That trade is the director's, not a sweep's.
- Owns: the two candidate classes a sweep may take WITHOUT touching evidence or the build cache — the 156 uncited top-level logs, and the stray ephemeral clusters (`target/pg-ephemeral.*`, `target/pg-iter.*`, ~116 MB across three) — each censused against `scripts/census_pg_test_clusters.py`'s citation guard before removal, with a residue census afterwards.
- Acceptance: every deleted path is proved uncited by the command above at the moment of deletion, not from this leaf's stale list; the ephemeral clusters are proved STOPPED and their process groups absent before removal, per `.3.2.1`'s cleanup discipline; file counts and byte totals are recorded before and after; and a residue census proves the exact deleted set is gone and the cited set is intact.
- ⚠️ **Deliberately NOT run in the session that opened it.** The director asked to `/exit`, and a deletion sweep started at a handoff point is how a half-finished removal outlives its session — the exact class `check_no_background_jobs.sh` exists to prevent.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0383. **Run, and the re-measurement inverted which class was worth sweeping.**
- 🔴 **EVERY FIGURE THIS LEAF PUBLISHED HAD MOVED, AND ONE OF THEM BY SIX TIMES — which is why the acceptance says *not from this leaf's stale list*.** Re-derived at `47999b5`, three days after they were written:

| figure | as published | at `47999b5` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target/debug` | 11.9 GB, 74% of the tree | **69 GB, 91% of the tree** |
| the whole `target` tree | 16 GB | **75,539,992 KiB (72 GiB)** |
| top-level `.log` files | 257 — 101 cited, 156 uncited | **401 — 125 cited, 276 uncited** |
| the uncited logs' size | 2,680 KB, under 0.02% | **4,068,864 bytes — 0.0053%** |

- ⛔ **THE LOG SWEEP IS DECLINED AGAIN, AND ON A NUMBER THAT MOVED THE RIGHT WAY.** The uncited logs grew from 2.6 MB to 4.0 MB while the tree grew from 16 GB to 72 GiB, so their share FELL by almost 4× — the class is further from mattering than when the leaf refused it. ⭐ Deleting them is still safe and still pointless, and *safe* was never the question.

- ✅ **RETIRED THROUGH THE PROJECT'S OWN INSTRUMENT, never a hand-written `rm`**, because its refusal set IS this leaf's acceptance, mechanised: an unreadable receipt, a receipt state that is not `stopped`, a live postmaster pid, a symlink or non-directory, a device that is not the repository's, an age under the one-hour floor, a name any tracked file cites, and a cluster already reduced to a `retired.json`. ⭐ It re-checks every cluster **immediately before removing it** and prints a residue census afterwards, so a census minutes old cannot authorise a stale deletion. Before → after:
