##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.24.1.3.1.1 — The parent the render's receipt names is the derivation itself

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.24.1.3.1`'s scoping read, which went looking for where the rendered bytes were and found there were none.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0311. **The parent now exists, and it is the page's own bytes.**
- 🔴 **THE DEFECT, stated as the identity it produced.** `crates/reasonbraid-browse/src/main.rs` built `parent_digest` as `digest_sha256_hex(concat of the chunk texts)`. The worker derives **exactly one** chunk — `body.inner_text()`, whole — so the concatenation *was* that chunk's text and **`parent_digest` equalled `chunks[0].digest` byte for byte, on every render**. The receipt advertised a parent/derivation pair in which the parent WAS the derivation.
- ⛔ **§12.6 is written to keep exactly those apart:** *Every transformation is a `Derivation` edge. A quote, summary, OCR result, model-generated caption, or repository analysis is not the original source. The UI and synthesis preserve that distinction.* An edge whose parent and child are the same bytes preserves no distinction — it asserts one and encodes none.
- 🔴 **AND THE EMPTY CASE WAS WORSE.** With no text the chunk list is empty, so the concatenation is empty and `parent_digest` digested the empty string: a render of a real page that produced no text claimed a parent that was **nothing at all**.
- ✅ **THE REPAIR: the page's own bytes.** The worker reads `page.content()` — the serialized document — before the response is shaped, publishes it as `document`, and digests **it** for `parent_digest`. The text chunk stays a derivation of it. ⛔ The bytes are CARRIED and not merely digested: §12.6's snapshot is addressable by its *raw-byte digest*, and a digest with no bytes behind it is a claim about an artefact nobody kept.
- ⭐ **THE CONSTRUCTION IS NOW A FUNCTION SO THAT A CONTROL CAN GUARD IT** — `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.6.3`'s move, applied a second time in this same file and for the same reason. Inline in the render, the parent/derivation distinction could only be exercised by driving a real Chrome, and the two lines that collapsed it would have needed a browser to catch. `render_response` is pure, and the controls are offline.
- ⛔ **THE CEILING IS UNCHANGED IN MEANING, and that is derived rather than chosen** (`.11.6`). `max_output_bytes` is 4 MiB, set by the server. It used to bound the text alone; it now bounds **document + text**, because the field's own name is the worker's OUTPUT and a second artefact on the wire is more output. Bounding each separately would have doubled the worst case to 8 MiB silently, which is inventing a number by omission.
- **ADDRESSED (verified)** — `reasonbraid-browse` **14 passed, 0 failed** (12 at `c5d8831` — measured on both sides), the two new controls being `the_parent_is_the_document_and_the_chunk_is_not` and `a_page_that_renders_no_text_still_has_a_parent`. ⭐ The first one's load-bearing arm is the **inequality**: asserting only that the parent digests the document would pass against a worker that also built the chunk out of the document.
- ✅ **AND THE SERVER DECODES IT, driven rather than assumed.** `BrowseWorkerResponse` carries no `deny_unknown_fields`, so the new field is ignored and `parent_digest` becomes honest with no server change — but *ignored* is a property of an absent attribute, and an absent attribute is what a later edit adds without noticing. `a_worker_response_carrying_the_document_decodes_and_keeps_its_parent` fails the moment it is added. ⛔ **The field is NOT added to the server struct here**: nothing consumes it yet, and `.11.24.1.3.1` owns the snapshot that will.
- **NO REGRESSION** — ⭐ **verified against a REAL Chrome, which is what a change calling a new CDP method owes.** `R3_BROWSER_BIN=… cargo test -p reasonbraid-browse --test browser_roundtrip` → **17 passed, 1 failed**, the passes including `the_browser_renders_the_page_and_logs_the_network` and `real_step_error_and_output_refusal_finish_before_returning`, which are the two that exercise `page.content()` end to end (`target/browse_roundtrip_0311.log`). `reasonbraid-server --lib` 128 passed. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0; strict clippy rc=0; `make book` rc=0; doctrine gate green; `handoff: OK`.
- 🔎 **THE ONE FAILURE IS PRE-EXISTING, AND IT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ATTRIBUTED AWAY.** `a_real_navigation_deadline_stops_the_browser_and_origin` fails on `cleanup_confirmed`. I stashed both changed files, re-ran that single test at `c5d8831`, and it fails **identically** — same assertion, same `browser stderr completion unconfirmed`, same ~41 s elapsed (`target/browse_baseline_0311.log`); both files then restored byte-identical by SHA-256. ⛔ It is OWNED rather than noted: `.11.25`.
- **FALSIFIED** twice, the file restored byte-identical by SHA-256 (`target/falsify_parent.py`): making the parent digest the chunk text — the exact superseded shape — turns **both** new controls RED, and making it digest the empty string turns both RED. ⭐ Two mutations, and each is a shape the code actually had.
- promotion: **declined**, and the reason is that the rule is already in this file. `.7.3.6.3` wrote *it is a function so that a commit can guard it* into `crates/reasonbraid-browse/src/main.rs` itself; this is that rule applied, not a new one. ⚠️ Trigger for a note: a third site where a distinction is only exercisable by driving a real browser.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0311 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.24.1.3.1.1): the render's parent was its own derivation, and an empty page's parent was nothing`.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.24.1.3.2 — A git acquisition is evidence the snapshot store has no shape for

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.24.1.3`, which decided the snapshot is owed and found the store cannot hold it.
- 🔴 **THE MEASUREMENT.** R1's product is a `GitAcquisition` — `odb_path`, `odb_bytes`, `resolved_commit`, `object_count`, `file_count`, `paths` — an on-disk object database, not a byte string. `evidence_snapshots.raw_digest` is a foreign key into `snapshot_objects (bytes BYTEA NOT NULL)`, so the only representable snapshot today is one whose bytes are inlined into a Postgres column.
- ⭐ **THE EDGE IS ALREADY SETTLED and is NOT this leaf's** (`.11.24.1.3`): §12.6's *repository analysis is not the original source* makes the repository the parent, so R1 owes a snapshot and no automatic edge. This leaf owes only the snapshot.
- ⚠️ **§12.6 PERMITS THE OTHER ANSWER, in its own words:** snapshots *remain addressable for the charter's audit period **or** retain a verifiable external archival reference*. So inlining an object database is one option and not the presumed one, and `storage_class` — measured by `.11.24.1.3` as written by three callers as `"standard"` and read by no predicate — is the field that would carry the distinction.
- ⚠️ **What is NOT claimed:** that the acquisition is unverifiable today. `GitReceipt` publishes `resolved_commit` (the git identity) and a digest over the acquired odb bytes; a caller who keeps the receipt can check a re-clone. The gap is that nothing DURABLE records it, so the provenance dies with the response.
- Owns: the storage decision for an artefact the server holds on disk rather than in memory, and the snapshot that follows from it.
- ⭐ **A SECOND CONSUMER NOW WAITS ON THIS DECISION, and it is a forcing case rather than another reader** (`2026-09-20`, director-greenlit): `PEER-COLLAB.2` wants one agent to attach a reproduction to a bug report and its peer to retrieve it. That is the same artefact class — something the server holds on disk, not a byte string in memory — arriving from the opposite direction, **written by a peer instead of acquired from a source**. ⚠️ It does not widen this leaf's acceptance and must not: `PEER-COLLAB.1` has not yet graded whether that scenario needs a TREE at all, and a store designed for a caller whose requirements are ungraded is a store designed by guess. Recorded so the branch chosen here is chosen knowing a second caller exists.
- Acceptance: §12.6's addressable-or-external-reference clause is quoted and one branch chosen with its reason; if `storage_class` gains a second value, something must READ it — a class no predicate consults is the arrangement `.11.24.1.3` measured and declined to grade, and shipping a second one would make it a defect; a control drives a real acquisition and asserts the snapshot's identity, its `resolved_commit` as the immutable source version, and that a re-acquisition of the same ref does not duplicate it.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0325. **The branch is chosen by MEASUREMENT: the odb is not an identity, so the reference is.**
- **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE)** — the leaf opened as a storage-shape problem and the shape was the symptom. `evidence_snapshots.raw_digest` was `NOT NULL REFERENCES snapshot_objects (digest)` over `bytes BYTEA NOT NULL`, so the only representable snapshot inlined into a Postgres column, while R1's product is an on-disk object database (`crates/reasonbraid-server/src/git.rs`, `GitAcquisition { odb_path, odb_bytes, resolved_commit, … }`). 🔴 **The deeper reason the inline branch is wrong is not size — it is that the acquired object database is not a property of the evidence.** `git::tests::the_acquired_object_database_is_not_a_stable_identity` acquires ONE immutable commit four ways and measures `git_digest`:

| Leg | What changed between acquisitions | `resolved_commit` | odb digest |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | nothing | same | same |
| B | the source gained an unrelated commit on another ref | same | same |
| C | the source repacked — 4 objects, no deltas to choose between | same | same |
| **D** | the source repacked with `pack.window 0` / `pack.depth 0` — 66 objects, delta-capable | **same** | 🔴 **different** |

- 🔴 **Leg D: 6857 bytes against 10071, two digests, commit `1e35b82e05c6867b3eeef749cf71b50a93d4ead0` unchanged.** `pack.window` is read by `git-upload-pack` on the SOURCE side, so the pack is chosen by a remote nobody here controls. Keyed on those bytes, an upstream forge's routine housekeeping would file a SECOND evidence snapshot for evidence that did not change.
- ⭐ **RE-DERIVED BY A DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT, with no product code in the path** — two plain `git clone --depth 1 --no-local` runs against one source across the same config change: commit `dcb8b30fa90e0c6b5abdb9dc23de1781a498a46d` both times, object-database digests `1deb086c945d34cf…` and `159101ecee68fadb…`. The property is git's, not this acquirer's.
- ⭐ **THE THREE NEGATIVE LEGS ARE LOAD-BEARING, and leg C is the one that proves it.** A repack of the four-object fixture changes nothing, because a four-object pack has no deltas to vary — my first attempt at this measurement was exactly that repack, and it reported STABLE. A control written on leg D alone would look like proof while proving something weaker than it claims; A–C are what stop the finding being read as *any repack changes the bytes*, and they are why the fixture had to be rebuilt delta-capable before anything could be concluded.
- **THE DECISION (verified)** — **§12.9's SECOND alternative**, quoted in the migration, the module and the book: *Snapshots used by binding decisions remain addressable for the charter's audit period **or** retain a verifiable external archival reference*. `resolved_commit` is the identity and §12.6 already had the column for it — *immutable source version where available* — and git's object model makes that id a commitment to the entire tree, so re-acquiring and comparing it IS the verification rather than a pointer with nothing behind it.
- ⛔ **THE ODB DIGEST IS EXCLUDED FROM THE REFERENCE ON PURPOSE**, and labelled where it does live. It rides `provider_receipt.git.digest` beside a `digest_note` saying what it is, because a verifier that reached for it as a re-clone check would get a false mismatch — which is what leg D measures. `git_digest`'s own doc comment was corrected in the same change: it read *deterministic for the same acquisition* in a way that invited exactly that misuse, and now says which way the determinism does not run.
- ⛔ **`storage_class` GAINED FOUR READERS IN THE SAME CHANGE, two of them in the database.** `.11.24.1.3` measured it as written by three callers as the literal `"standard"` and read by NO predicate, recorded that, and declined to grade it; shipping a second value nothing consults would have made it a defect. Now: `migrations/0080`'s CHECK (an external-reference row holds no digest, `byte_length = 0`, a reference, and an immutable source version — any other class is the inverse); its partial unique index on `(reference_id, immutable_source_version)`, which is this class's replay key because `raw_digest` is `NULL` here and `= NULL` never matches, and which is an INDEX rather than only a SELECT so two concurrent acquisitions of one commit cannot both insert; `snapshots::submit` refusing the class by name; and `claims::submit` naming it in the refusal.
- ⛔ **`raw_digest` WAS MADE NULLABLE RATHER THAN FILLED WITH A STAND-IN.** The rejected alternative — store a manifest, or the reference document itself, under the digest and keep the column `NOT NULL` — makes one column mean two things depending on a sibling, with nothing stopping a reader joining `snapshot_objects` and calling the result *the evidence*. A nullable column makes the branch structural: the type is an `Option` and the compiler asks.
- ⛔ **A PINNED REFERENCE IS REFUSED BY NAME.** §12.1's `expected_digest` says *these exact bytes* and this class holds none, so filing the snapshot would let it escape the constraint its own reference declares.
- 🔎 **A CONSUMER DEFECT THE STORAGE CHANGE WOULD HAVE CREATED, FOUND AND CLOSED IN THE SAME CHANGE.** `claims::submit` validated an excerpt through an INNER JOIN onto `snapshot_objects`, so a snapshot holding no bytes was indistinguishable from an absent one and a tenant would have been told its OWN cited evidence does not exist. It is a LEFT JOIN now, carrying `storage_class` back, with a named `SnapshotHoldsNoBytes` refusal. ⚠️ It discloses nothing extra — the citation gate one step earlier has already admitted that caller for that snapshot.
- **NO REGRESSION** — `python3 -B scripts/run_pg_tests.py <suite>` run per suite, rc=0 each: `evidence_git_snapshot` **4 passed**, `profiles` **63 passed**, `migration_upgrade` **8 passed**, `quarantine` **1**, `classification` **1**, `cards` **6**, `site_authority` **11**; every owned cluster stopped and removed. `cargo test -p reasonbraid-server --lib` → **133 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored** rc=0 (`target/lib_tests.log`). `cargo clippy -p reasonbraid-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` rc=0 (`target/clippy.log`); `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0; `make book` rc=0; the doctrine gate printed `=== all doctrines green ===` (22 checks); `bash scripts/check_no_background_jobs.sh` → `handoff: OK`.
- **FALSIFIED**, both mutations reverted and the files restored from byte-copies. (1) `immutable_source_version: receipt.digest` — the snapshot keyed on the transport encoding instead of the commit — turns `the_git_snapshot_is_an_external_reference_keyed_on_its_commit` RED at the immutable-source-version assertion (`left: Some("sha256:aa")`). (2) `AssessmentError::SnapshotMissing` restored in place of the new refusal turns `an_excerpt_against_a_byteless_snapshot_is_told_what_it_hit` RED on the literal message `the cited snapshot does not exist` — the exact text this leaf argues a tenant must never see. ⭐ The two shape controls stayed GREEN under both, which is right: neither mutation touches the row's shape.
- ⚠️ **THE CONTROL IS SPLIT ACROSS TWO LEVELS, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN.** The acceptance asks for one control that drives a real acquisition AND asserts the store's behaviour; no single test process can hold both, because production R1 is https-only by `harden_git_url` and an integration test cannot reach a `file://` fixture without weakening an SSRF-relevant allowlist — which would be a worse change than the one it verifies. So the identity assertion runs against REAL acquisitions in `git.rs`, the store assertions run against real PostgreSQL in `tests/evidence_git_snapshot.rs`, and the only thing between them is `git::external_snapshot_submission`, a pure constructor both sides call. Nothing on either side is simulated. ⛔ No cargo feature was added to expose a fixture acquirer: the workspace has no feature flags at all, and a test hook on the production crate is a larger change than the split it would avoid.
- ⭐ **EVERY NEW CONTROL CARRIES A POSITIVE CONTROL IN THE SAME RUN** (`.11.25.1.1`'s method): the replay assertion is paired with a DIFFERENT commit that must NOT replay, the class refusal with the same submission in the default class that must land, and the pin refusal with the same submission against an unpinned reference that must land.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2026-09-20_a-git-snapshot-is-a-reference-because-its-bytes-are-not-an-identity.md` (+ INDEX). Book: a new `docs/book/src/evidence.md` page (in `SUMMARY.md`) — the storage-class table, the measurement, and what changes for a caller.
- ⚠️ **NOT done here:** no general external blob store, and `PEER-COLLAB.2` did not widen this leaf — its requirements are ungraded until `PEER-COLLAB.1` decides whether that scenario needs a tree, and a store designed for an ungraded caller is a store designed by guess. What it inherits is the seam, not a design.
- promotion: **declined**, with the finding recorded in the decision instead. *A control whose falsifying case needs a delta-capable fixture* is `a-control-that-passes-for-an-unrelated-reason` met in a new costume, and it is that note's rule rather than a new one. ⚠️ Trigger for a note: a third measurement whose first fixture was too small to falsify anything.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0325 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.24.1.3.2): a git snapshot is a reference, because the object database it acquires is not an identity`.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.24.1.4 — The release tool cannot re-sign a manifest it already holds

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.24.1`.
- 🔴 **THE MEASUREMENT.** `PHASE-7.4.2` recorded the signing-key compromise record as riding `.2.3`'s manifest tool — *the re-key + the re-sign over the unchanged digests*. `crates/reasonbraid-release-tool` ships `keygen`, `generate`, `verify` and `certify {sign,verify}`; `git grep -ci "re-key\|rekey\|re_sign\|resign" -- crates` → **0**. `generate` takes `--bin-dir` and **re-derives every digest from the binaries**.
- ⛔ **So the recovery the record describes cannot be performed as described.** Re-keying after a compromise means signing the SAME manifest bytes with a new identity; `generate` instead rebuilds the manifest from binaries that must be byte-identical to the originals — which is exactly the assumption a compromise investigation cannot make.
- ⚠️ **Stated at its real width:** `keygen` + `generate` DO give a re-key path when the binaries are known-good, so this is a gap in a recovery drill, not a missing capability outright. The record's wording is what is unsupported.
- Owns: either a `re-sign` command that signs an existing manifest's exact bytes with a new key, or a correction to the `.7.4.2` record stating what recovery is actually available.
- Acceptance: whichever is chosen, a control drives it end to end — for a new command, sign an existing manifest with a second key and verify it against that key while the first no longer verifies; for a correction, the record quotes the commands that exist.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0327. **`re-sign` ships, and BOTH halves of the acceptance were owed rather than one.**
- **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE)** — `docs/runbooks/signing-key-incident.md` prescribes *`keygen` a new identity, re-sign the SAME manifest content (the digests unchanged), and re-verify*. `crates/reasonbraid-release-tool/src/main.rs` shipped `keygen`, `generate`, `verify` and `certify {sign,verify}`, and `git grep -ci "re-key\|rekey\|re_sign\|resign" -- crates` → **0**. No command re-signs an existing manifest.
- 🔴 **AND THIS LEAF'S OWN MITIGATION WAS FALSE, measured rather than reasoned about.** It opened saying *`keygen` + `generate` DO give a re-key path when the binaries are known-good, so this is a gap in a recovery drill*. `generate` stamps `created_at: chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339()`, so two runs over ONE unchanged binary produce different bytes and different signatures — probed directly: `{"release":"0.1.0","created_at":"2026-09-20T14:02:01.829345+00:00",…}` against `…14:02:03.042701+00:00…`, identical digest, `identical: NO`, `sig identical: NO`. ⛔ **So the workaround publishes a NEW release document rather than the same one under a new identity**, and ADR-027 names *the manifest's own digest* as part of the verification unit, so anything pinning it breaks. The gap is a missing capability, not a drill inconvenience.
- 🔎 **AND THE TOOL'S OWN MODULE HEADER SAID THE OPPOSITE, which is how the runbook came to describe an impossible recovery.** It read *the byte-identical regeneration is the re-derivation contract* — a sentence that invites exactly the conclusion that re-running `generate` reproduces the manifest. What is byte-identical is a PARSED manifest re-serialized to its own bytes; what `verify` re-derives is each BINARY's digest. Corrected at the header and at the struct.
- **THE REPAIR (verified)** — `rb-release-manifest re-sign --key <new> --manifest <path> --sig <out>`: the manifest's bytes are read VERBATIM and signed as they stand. ⛔ Parsed only to refuse a file that is not a manifest — a signature asserts what the bytes ARE, so signing an arbitrary file as a release manifest is the one thing it must not do; never re-serialized, because a second canonicalization is a second chance to produce different bytes. ⛔ **The old signature is NOT checked first, deliberately**: the key it would check is the one presumed lost or compromised, so requiring it would make the command unusable in the only situation it exists for. ⭐ **The OLD key is refused BY NAME** — Ed25519 signing is deterministic, so re-signing with it reproduces the existing signature byte for byte, a recovery that appears to succeed and re-keys nothing; when the previous signature sits where `generate` puts it, that is checkable and it is checked. ⛔ `--sig` is required and never overwritten, so the runbook's *keep the old signature — it is the incident's evidence* becomes a rule the tool holds rather than a sentence someone must remember (the stance `keygen` already takes toward an existing key).
- **FIX / LOCKSTEP** — the runbook's Recovery section now quotes the three commands that exist, states in its own words why `generate` must NOT be used for this, and names the same-key refusal; its Closure tests name the new control. The module header and the `Manifest` doc comment are corrected.
- **NO REGRESSION** — `cargo test -p reasonbraid-release-tool` → **2 passed, 0 failed** rc=0 (1 before; measured on both sides — the pre-existing `the_manifest_signs_and_the_refusals_are_typed` still passes). `cargo clippy -p reasonbraid-release-tool --all-targets -- -D warnings` rc=0; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0; `make book` rc=0; the doctrine gate printed `=== all doctrines green ===`; `handoff: OK`.
- **FALSIFIED THREE WAYS, each caught by the leg written for it**, the source restored from a byte-copy afterwards and the suite re-run green:

| Mutation | Verdict | Caught by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sign `canonical_bytes(&parsed)` instead of the file's bytes | RED | leg 5 — `the signature does not verify` |
| drop the same-key refusal | RED | leg 1 |
| let the signature path be overwritten | RED | leg 4 |

- ⭐ **LEG 5 EXISTS BECAUSE THE CONTROL WITHOUT IT MEASURED NOTHING ABOUT ITS OWN HEADLINE.** Every manifest in the fixture round-trips through serde to its own bytes, so a `re-sign` that signed the re-serialization would have passed every other leg — the word *verbatim* would have been unguarded. A **pretty-printed** manifest parses to the same struct and serializes to DIFFERENT bytes, and `verify` checks the signature against the file's own bytes, so that is the one case separating the two implementations. ⚠️ The control asserts the fixture's bytes actually differ before relying on it, because a leg whose fixture silently stopped differing would go quiet rather than fail.
- ⚠️ **NOT solved here, and OWNED rather than noted (`.11.24.1.4.1`):** `verify` and `certify verify` both take `--key`, the PRIVATE PKCS8 file, and derive the public key from it. So the natural next step of a re-key — publish the new identity so somebody else can verify — is not an operation this tool has. Inside ADR-027's named distribution-channel deferral, and the runbook says so in its own words rather than leaving it to be discovered.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2026-09-20_a-re-key-signs-the-manifest-not-the-binaries.md` (+ INDEX).
- promotion: **declined**, with the finding recorded in the decision instead. *A control whose fixture round-trips cannot test that bytes are preserved verbatim* is `a-control-that-passes-for-an-unrelated-reason` again — the second instance this session, after `.11.24.1.3.2`'s four-object pack. ⚠️ **Trigger now armed rather than open-ended: a THIRD instance promotes it**, and the shape to look for is a fixture in which the property under test cannot vary.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0327 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.24.1.4): a re-key signs the manifest, not the binaries`.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.24.1.4.1 — A release manifest cannot be verified without the private key

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.24.1.4`, which needed the re-key recovery to end somewhere a third party could check.
- 🔴 **THE MEASUREMENT.** `rb-release-manifest verify` and `certify verify` both take `--key`, read it with `load_key`, and derive the public key via `ring::signature::KeyPair::public_key()`. There is no public-key input and no public-key export: `keygen` writes PKCS8 DER and prints a path. So **every verification requires the private signing key**, and the only party who can verify a release is the party who signed it.
- ⛔ **Why it matters, stated without overstating it.** A signature whose verifier must hold the signing key proves nothing to anybody else — the property signatures exist for. ⚠️ This is NOT a claim that the shipped posture is wrong today: ADR-027 places the key with the releaser as the dev stance and names the distribution channel as a deferral, and nothing is distributed in the dev profile, so there is currently no second party to verify for. The defect is that the runbook's re-key recovery has no publishable end state, which `.11.24.1.4` hit head-on.
- ⚠️ **What is NOT assumed:** that the repair is a `--public-key` flag. It may be a `pubkey` export verb, an identity file carrying the public key beside a fingerprint, or a manifest field naming the signing identity — and the choice interacts with ADR-027's rungs 3 and 4, which are about a downloaded artefact rather than a local one.
- Owns: the decision and, if a surface ships, the export/verify pair with a control in which the verifying side never touches the private key.
- Acceptance: ADR-027's identity/distribution deferral is quoted and the boundary between it and this gap is stated; if a public-key path ships, a control verifies a manifest holding ONLY the public material, and a second control shows the private key is not required — a verification that silently still reads it would be the same defect with a new flag.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0329. **The identity is publishable, and the control proves the private key is not read by REMOVING it.**
- **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE)** — `crates/reasonbraid-release-tool/src/main.rs`: both `Cmd::Verify` and `CertifyCmd::Verify` took `--key`, read the PKCS8 file with `load_key`, and derived the public key via `ring::signature::KeyPair::public_key()`. `keygen` wrote the private key and printed a path. 🔴 **So every verification required the signing key, and the only party who could verify a release was the party who signed it** — a signature whose verifier must hold the signing key proves nothing to anybody else, which is the property signatures exist for. What the shipped arrangement caught was accidental corruption of a manifest or a binary; it could not catch forgery, because anyone able to run the check was equally able to re-sign.
- ⚠️ **Stated at its real width rather than inflated.** ADR-027 places the key with the releaser as the explicit dev stance and names the distribution channel as a deferral, and nothing is distributed in the dev profile — so no second party was being misled. The defect is that `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.24.1.4`'s re-key recovery, which exists precisely for the moment an identity must change hands, had nowhere to end.
- **THE REPAIR (verified)** — `rb-release-manifest pubkey --key <private> --out <path>` exports the raw 32-byte Ed25519 key as hex, and `--public-key` is the third-party verification path on both `verify` and `certify verify`. ✅ `make release` now exports the identity beside the manifest and the signature: a release that ships a signature and no way to check it is the state this ends.
- ⛔ **The two inputs are mutually exclusive and BOTH is refused rather than silently resolved** — they can name different identities, and a pass whose meaning depends on an argument order nobody wrote down is not a verification. ⭐ **`--key` lost its clap `default_value` to make that expressible**: the fallback to `release-key.pk8` moved into the resolver and applies when NEITHER is given, so *the caller gave nothing* stays distinguishable from *the caller gave `--key`*. The releaser's own `make release` invocation, which passes no `--key` at all, is unchanged.
- ⛔ **A public key of the wrong length is a NAMED caller error**, not a signature failure: letting an 8-byte file travel into `ring` and come back as *the signature does not verify* would blame the signature for a mistyped path. ⛔ **`pubkey` never overwrites** — the key is public by definition so it tightens no permissions, but a published identity replaced in place is this area's whole failure mode, and a re-key writes a new file under a new name.
- **NO REGRESSION** — `cargo test -p reasonbraid-release-tool` → **3 passed, 0 failed** rc=0 (2 before, measured on both sides; the `.11.24.1.4` re-sign control and the original sign/refusal control both still pass). `cargo clippy -p reasonbraid-release-tool --all-targets -- -D warnings` rc=0; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0; `make book` rc=0; the doctrine gate printed `=== all doctrines green ===`; `handoff: OK`.
- **FALSIFIED THREE WAYS**, the source restored from a byte-copy and the suite re-run green:

| Mutation | Verdict | Caught by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--public-key` accepted and the PRIVATE key derived anyway | RED | the verify-with-no-private-key leg — `read the key release-key.pk8: No such file or directory` |
| the both-inputs refusal removed | RED | the ambiguity leg |
| the 32-byte length check removed | RED | the wrong-shape leg |

- ⭐ **THE LOAD-BEARING LEG IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN INSPECTIONAL, and the first mutation is why it had to be.** The control builds a signing directory and a published one, then **deletes the private key** before verifying. A `--public-key` path that silently still reached for `release-key.pk8` would be the same defect with a new flag, and no amount of reading the code proves it does not — only a world without that file does. ⚠️ A first attempt at that mutation failed to COMPILE rather than failing the test, which is not a falsification; it was rewritten until it ran and the verdict came from the assertion.
- ⚠️ **NOT done here, and it is the CHANNEL rather than the capability:** ADR-027's distribution channel, reproducible builders and protected identities stay deferred. Publishing the `.pub` file is a manual act with no automated audience. What changed is that there is now something to publish.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2026-09-20_a-release-identity-must-be-publishable.md` (+ INDEX). `docs/runbooks/signing-key-incident.md`'s recovery gains step 4 and the verifier's command, and the limit it carried is marked discharged.
- promotion: **declined.** *A capability is not proved absent by reading the code; remove the thing it must not use* is `a-control-that-passes-for-an-unrelated-reason` applied to a negative claim, and `.11.25.1.1`'s method — *a probe whose conclusion is an ABSENCE owes a positive control in the same run* — is the same rule from the other side; both were consulted and applied. ⚠️ Trigger for a note: a third control that has to DELETE a resource to prove it is unused.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0329 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.24.1.4.1): a release identity must be publishable, or the signature is ceremonial`.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.24.1.5 — The adapter SDK has no acquisition trait

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.24.1`.
- 🔴 **THE MEASUREMENT.** `PHASE-8.4.1`'s goal says *the resolver SURFACE extracted from the internal registry (the advertise type as the third-party shape — the acquisition trait rides the `.4.4` load side)*. `git grep -n "pub trait" -- crates/reasonbraid-adapter/src` returns **two**: `AttemptStream` and `Adapter`, both the provider contract. `.4.4` is `done` and delivered the allowlist verification ladder.
- ⛔ **So a third party can declare what it resolves and cannot implement resolving it.** The advertise type ships as the SDK's resolver shape; the execution half of that surface does not exist, and `resolvers::resolve` dispatches internally.
- ⚠️ **The decision may be to NOT have one**, and that is a legitimate outcome to record: an out-of-process resolver is a sandbox-boundary question (ADR-018), and a trait that crosses it in-process would undercut the isolation classes the same ADR defines. What is not legitimate is the SDK advertising a surface with half of it absent and nothing saying so.
- Owns: the decision, ADR-018 and ADR-027 quoted for it, and either the trait or an explicit statement at the SDK's own module header that resolution is not third-party-implementable.
- Acceptance: the decision is recorded in `docs/decisions/`; the SDK's public docs say which half a third party may implement; if the trait ships, a control drives a resolution through it.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0326. **The decision is NO TRAIT, and the SDK's front door never mentioned resolvers at all.**
- **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE)** — `PHASE-8.4.1`'s goal deferred the acquisition trait to `.4.4`; `PHASE-8.4.4` is `done` and delivered the ADR-027 allowlist ladder, the ledger migration and the operator verbs, closing with a deferral of its own to `.2.3`. 🔴 **The promise pointed at a leaf that closed without owning it — this tree's own `.11.24` family — and it was not only in the task tree: it sat in `crates/reasonbraid-adapter/src/resolver.rs`'s module header, readable by any third party, the whole time.** Measured: `git grep -n "pub trait" -- crates/reasonbraid-adapter/src` → **2**, `AttemptStream` and `Adapter`, both in `contract.rs` and both the harness contract.
- 🔎 **AND THE LEAF'S PREMISE WAS THE SMALLER HALF OF THE FINDING.** It opened as *the SDK advertises a surface with half of it absent and nothing saying so*. The header did say something — a stale something. What nothing said anywhere is that the resolver surface EXISTS: `lib.rs` declares `pub mod resolver;` and re-exports its types while the **crate-root documentation lists `contract`, `fake`, `fixtures` and `bench` and stops**, and `docs/book/src/adapter-boundary.md` contained the word *resolver* **zero** times. A third party reading the SDK's front page learned nothing about resolvers at all.
- **THE DECISION (verified)** — **there is no in-process acquisition trait and there will not be one**; a third-party resolver contributes a `ResolverAdvertise` row and an out-of-process worker binary. ⭐ **It follows from ADR-018's vocabulary rather than from scheduling**, and the reading it rests on is already adjudicated in this tree: `sandbox_level` states what the resolver's CODE provides (`.7.3.6.1`, which repaired R3's false `vm_container` and left `security_evidence.container_required` beside it to carry the DEPLOYMENT's obligation). `resolvers::resolve` filters on that field as a floor. **In-process code provides `none`, and no arrangement makes it provide more** — so an in-process trait would let a third-party pack advertise `constrained_process` or `vm_container` while structurally being `none`, and the registry would admit it on the claim. ⛔ **That is worse than an absent surface**: the other four policy fields are already consumed by nothing (`2026-09-19_an-advertised-line-carries-an-adjudicated-verdict.md`), so spending one of the two that ARE consulted would leave the advertise contract decorative.
- ⭐ **THE EXECUTION SURFACE ALREADY EXISTS AND IT IS A CHILD PROCESS — measured, not asserted.** `grep -n "Command::new\|\.spawn(" ` over `extraction.rs`, `browse.rs`, `fetcher.rs`, `git.rs` and `mediated.rs`, excluding `tokio::spawn`, returns spawns in exactly **two** production paths: `browse.rs:161` and `extraction.rs:242`. ⚠️ `git.rs`'s two hits are at lines 1910 and 2664, both after `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at 1350 — test-only, and checked rather than assumed. Those two paths are precisely the two packs declaring `sandbox_level: "process"`; the other four run in the server process and declare `none`. **The declared level tracks the execution shape across all six.** ⛔ ADR-027's five rungs — allowlist, digest, signature, API compatibility, capability manifest — are each a property of a distributed BINARY, and none has a meaning for a trait compiled into the server; the workspace has no dynamic-load mechanism for one to arrive through.
- **FIX / LOCKSTEP** — the boundary is stated in all three places a reader reaches, because a boundary inferred from which traits happen to exist is not a documented boundary: `lib.rs`'s crate root names the resolver surface and the asymmetry; `resolver.rs`'s header carries the argument in place of the `.4.4` deferral; `docs/book/src/adapter-boundary.md` gains *The other boundary in the same SDK* — the harness/resolver comparison table, the reasoning, and the six-pack execution table.
- ⚪ **FIVE BROKEN INTRA-DOC LINKS REPAIRED IN THE SAME CHANGE, TWO OF THEM IN THE CRATE-ROOT PARAGRAPH THIS LEAF REWRITES.** The root linked `` [`contract`] `` and `` [`fake`] ``, which are PRIVATE modules, so rustdoc dropped both links on the SDK's own front page; `` [`ProviderRequestId`] `` named a variant without its enum, and `fixtures.rs` linked two items inside a `#[cfg(test)]` module rustdoc never sees. `cargo doc -p reasonbraid-adapter --no-deps` was **6 warnings** and is now **0**. ⚠️ In scope because this leaf's acceptance is *the SDK's public docs say which half a third party may implement*, and a front page whose own links are dropped is that page failing at it.
- **NO REGRESSION** — `cargo test -p reasonbraid-adapter --lib` → **14 passed, 0 failed** rc=0 (`target/adapter_tests.log`). `cargo clippy -p reasonbraid-adapter -p reasonbraid-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` rc=0; `cargo doc -p reasonbraid-adapter --no-deps` rc=0 with **no warnings**; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0; `make book` rc=0; `python3 -B scripts/census_adapter_public_api.py --self-test` → *4 predicate cases, 102 real items parsed*; the doctrine gate printed `=== all doctrines green ===`; `handoff: OK`.
- ⛔ **NOTHING TO FALSIFY, AND THAT IS THE HONEST STATEMENT RATHER THAN A SKIPPED BOX** (`.11.24.1.3`'s shape). No behaviour changed and no predicate was added: the change is a decision plus the documentation that carries it. The acceptance's third clause — *if the trait ships, a control drives a resolution through it* — is discharged by the trait NOT shipping, which is the outcome the leaf itself named as legitimate. ⚠️ The measurements the decision rests on ARE falsifiable and were checked both ways: the spawn census excludes `tokio::spawn` and distinguishes test-only call sites by line against the `#[cfg(test)]` boundary.
- ⚠️ **NOT decided here, and stated in the book as a limit rather than left implicit:** the worker wire protocol is still **not** a published SDK surface — R2's and R3's request/response shapes live in `reasonbraid-server`. Promoting one means taking on a version token, a deprecation story and a conformance oracle, which is a separate decision. And this leaf does NOT make an advertised level verifiable: the registry still accepts what a row claims; what it now has is a boundary under which the claim can be true.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2026-09-20_resolution-is-not-third-party-implementable-in-process.md` (+ INDEX).
- promotion: **declined.** *A deferral naming a leaf that closed without owning it* is `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.24`'s own premise, already the subject of a whole lane; this is an instance of it, found in a SOURCE COMMENT rather than in a tree. ⚠️ Trigger for a note: a third deferral found living in a doc comment rather than in a task tree, where no tree-side gate can reach it.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-DOC-0082 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.24.1.5): resolution is not third-party-implementable in process, and the SDK's front door never mentioned resolvers at all`.

##### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.24.1.6 — A relative leaf reference is ambiguous across trees, and one has already resolved to the wrong leaf

- Opened: `pending` by `.11.24.1`, which met the ambiguity as a false positive and could not tighten its way out of it.
- 🔴 **THE INSTANCE.** `PHASE-8.4.4` writes *"no download mechanism exists (the `.2.3` distribution-channel deferral)"*. Within `PHASE-8.md` a bare `.2.3` reads as `PHASE-8.2.3` — the A2A facade — and that leaf exists, is `done`, and has nothing to do with distribution. The intended referent is `PHASE-7.2.3`, the release-manifest leaf.
- ⛔ **A resolver cannot notice this, and that is the point.** The wrong target EXISTS, so a same-tree resolution returns a real leaf with a real status. `scripts/census_goal_receipt_gap.py` reported the pair as a stranded deferral and only a human reading the words *distribution-channel* caught it.
- ⚠️ **The population is not known**, and this leaf's first job is to measure it rather than assume one instance is one instance: how many bare `.N` references sit in a tree, and for how many does the same-tree resolution disagree with the surrounding words. ⭐ `POSITIONAL-REF` governs `file:line` references and does not reach leaf ids — the adjacent gate that correctly misses this, the shape `.11.22` already documented for three others.
- Owns: the census, then a convention — most likely *a reference to another tree is written in full* — and a gate only if the population earns one (`.11.6`).
- Acceptance: the population is derived from the trees and classified by hand; any convention is stated in `docs/TASK_TREE_README.md`; any gate is calibrated over the history containing this instance and DECLINED with its number if it prices above the bar `POSITIONAL-REF` set.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0328. **The population is 5,634 and it contains a finding the leaf did not predict: TWO DIALECTS.**
- **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE)** — `docs/tasks/PHASE-8.md:1291` wrote *no download mechanism exists (the `.2.3` distribution-channel deferral)* meaning `PHASE-7.2.3`, while `PHASE-8.2.3` exists, is `done`, and is the A2A facade. ⛔ **A resolver cannot notice it**, because the wrong target EXISTS: same-tree resolution returns a real leaf with a real status, and only a reader of the words *distribution-channel* catches it.
- **THE CENSUS** — `scripts/census_relative_leaf_refs.py`, new, with an 11-arm two-sided `--self-test`. **5,634 relative references across the 12 tree files**, classified by whether a reader can resolve them at all:

| Class | Count | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `home` | 3,089 | resolves in its own tree and in no other — nothing to get wrong |
| `shared` | 2,178 | resolves in its own tree AND names a leaf in another — **the opening instance's class** |

### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.17 — Thread sub-reads disagree about whether a thread exists

- Status: `done` — `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0418`. Opened by `docs/decisions/2026-09-23_this-sessions-findings-re-derived-against-the-running-server.md`.
- 🔴 Measured against the running server for a thread id that does not exist: `GET /v1/threads/{id}` → `404`, `…/budget` → `404`, `…/events` → `200 {"events": [], "next_cursor": null}`, `…/audit` → `200` with the caller's own `thread_inspect` records. No other tenant's data appears, so it is not a disclosure; it is one question answered two ways.
- Owns: deciding the one answer for a thread the caller cannot see (the existence-oracle rule `.11.14.3.4` and `.3.5.5` applied elsewhere: foreign and absent answer the same) and making every thread sub-read give it; RED first; book.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE** — `get_events` and `get_audit` ran their selects with no existence check. A tenant-bound `event_log` select over a foreign or absent thread id returns no rows, which is indistinguishable from an existing thread with no events, so the timeline answered `200 {"events": []}`. And `inspect()` writes the caller's `thread_inspect` authorization record BEFORE the read, so `load_thread_authorization_records` for an absent thread returned that very record: the audit view answered a question about a thread that does not exist with records about the asking. `get_thread` (`thread_inspection`) and `get_thread_budget` (the BUDGET-003 ceiling check) already answered `scope_hidden`.
- [x] **ADDRESSED** — `crates/reasonbraid-server/src/api.rs::thread_exists`: the tenant-BOUND `aggregate_state` predicate `thread_inspection` uses, under the same RLS claim, reduced to `SELECT EXISTS`; `get_events` and `get_audit` ask it first and answer `ControlApiError::scope_hidden()` — the item read's exact payload — when it is false. The decision: the one answer is the item read's `404 scope_hidden`, so no view is an existence oracle the item read is not. Consumers checked before changing the contract: the CLI (`crates/reasonbraid-cli/src/lib.rs:947`) propagates any non-200 and reads the item first; the web UI (`crates/reasonbraid-server/web/app.js:234`) renders a non-200 as an error; neither depended on the empty `200`. Book: `docs/book/src/web-ui.md`.
- [x] **VERIFIED / FALSIFIED** — control `every_thread_read_answers_a_hidden_or_absent_thread_the_same_way` (`crates/reasonbraid-server/tests/command_api.rs`): the caller's own thread answers `200` on all four views; a foreign thread named under the caller's tenant and a fresh `thr_` id answer all four with `(404, {"code": "scope_hidden", "message": "the requested thread is not visible in this scope"})`, asserted as ONE payload. RED first on the unrepaired code: `foreign thread, view /events — left: (200, {"events": [], "next_cursor": null, …}) right: (404, {scope_hidden})`, `41 passed; 1 failed`. After the repair: `42 passed; 0 failed`.
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — `bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh invitations node_work node_result_ordering mcp mcp_write cards site_authority cli_end_to_end` → invitations 6, node_work 12, node_result_ordering 6, mcp (lib 6, stdio_transport 1), mcp_write 7, cards 6, site_authority 11, cli_end_to_end 5 — **60 passed, 0 failed**; strict clippy clean (`-D warnings`, 1 m 18 s); `cargo fmt`; `make gate`; `make book`.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0418`.

### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.16 — A domain refusal is not an authority denial, and one variant meant both

- Opened: `pending` by the director's instruction 2026-09-22 — *the judgement is yours to make but better be SOTA and signoff* — against `.8.2.5.3`'s 400 → 403 change, which I had defended by precedent.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0393. **The judgement: my own change one commit earlier was wrong, and testing my reasoning is what found it.**
- 🔴 **THE FLAW IN MY OWN ARGUMENT, and it is a conflation rather than a missing fact.** I justified 403 with `.6.1.5.4`'s existence-oracle reasoning: *answering before the gate would hand a caller with no site authority an oracle over a registry it may not write.* ⛔ That argument is about **ORDER** — check authority first — and says nothing about **RENDERING**. A caller who has PASSED the gate holds the grant and is entitled to the answer, so a 400 discloses nothing. The oracle is closed by the ordering, which was never in question.
- 🔴 **AND WHAT SHIPPED CONTRADICTED ITSELF ON THE WIRE.** `site_receipt_response` renders every `Refused` with `message: "a current site grant for this action and its actual boundary are required"` — a sentence that is FALSE of a caller holding the grant who named a corpus that does not exist. ⛔ An operator debugging CI reads 403 and checks their grants; the defect was a typo. It also incremented `authorization_denials`, so input errors were counted in a security metric.
- ⭐ **IT IS THE SAME DEFECT CLASS, FOR THE FOURTH TIME IN ONE SESSION, AND I SHIPPED THIS ONE.** `site_authority::Error::Refused` carried both meanings in one variant — as `EvaluationError::Duplicate` meant *taken* and *does not exist* (`.8.2.5.3`), and as an `Err(_)` from an INSERT meant *duplicate* and *store fault* (`.8.2.2`). One name, two meanings, and the boundary renders whichever it was handed.
- ⭐ **THE CORRECT PRINCIPLE WAS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN, AT EXACTLY ONE CALL SITE.** `site_registry_response` hand-matched the single reason `undeclared_region` to render it as a bad request, commenting *a domain refusal, not an authority one: the caller held the grant and asked for something the registry cannot express.* ⛔ That one-off is why the principle reached **one of sixteen** domain refusals. A rule implemented as a remembered special case holds exactly where it was remembered.
- ✅ **THE FIX IS AT THE TYPE, so the compiler reaches every site**: `Error::Denied` (the caller lacks the authority — 403, and the only case counted as an authorization denial) beside `Error::Refused` (the caller held it and the act was refused on its own terms — 400, with its reason as `code` and the `audit_id` beside it). Splitting the variant found every match arm, including one in the operator CLI a grep would have missed.
- ⭐ **THE LINE IS CHECKABLE RATHER THAN A JUDGEMENT CALL: exactly TWO reasons in the whole site layer mean the caller lacks authority** — `site_authority_required` and `operator_required`. Every one of the other fourteen is a domain refusal. Re-derive with `git grep -n 'Error::Denied' -- crates/reasonbraid-server/src`.
- ✅ **THE OPERATOR CLI FOLLOWS THE SAME SPLIT**, because one rule rendered two ways is how the two drift: exit `3` stays the authority exit beside `operator_required`, and a domain refusal exits `2` beside `invalid_input`. ⚠️ Its exit vocabulary is not a published contract — no book page states it — and the JSON `code` named both cases distinctly before and after.
- ⚠️ **THE AUDIT IS UNCHANGED, and that is deliberate.** Both are recorded `denied`, because the act did not take effect either way. What changed is only what the CALLER is told; the `audit_id` still resolves the full reason in both cases.
- ✅ **FALSIFIED: rendering a domain refusal as an authority denial again** — the exact code `.8.2.5.3` shipped — returns `403` where the suite requires `400`, red by name. `api.rs` restored byte-identical, SHA-256 `c331879c…`.
- ⭐ **EVERY TEST CALL SITE NOW STATES WHICH CLASS IT EXPECTS.** `site_authority.rs` had ONE helper destructuring `Refused`, which is how a suite of eleven tests could not tell the two apart; it now has `refused()` and `denied()`, each panicking if handed the other. Ten call sites are authority denials and three are domain refusals.
- ⛔ **THIS IS NOT A LOOSENING OF THE SITE GATE, and the structure is what guarantees it**: `authorized()` returns `Denied` *before* the effect closure runs, so an unauthorized caller still receives 403 having learned nothing about the registry's contents. The existence answer is still reached only after the gate passes.
- [x] **REPRODUCE / ISSUE** — the shipped body: `403 {"code": "that corpus version is already registered", "message": "a current site grant … is required", "audit_id": …}`. The code and the message disagree, and the message is false of the caller who received it.
- [x] **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE)** — `site_authority::Error::Refused` conflated an authority denial with a domain refusal, and `api.rs`'s `site_receipt_response` rendered the single variant as 403 with the grant-requirement message.
- [x] **THE DECISION** — split the type; 403 for authority, 400 with an audit id for a domain refusal; the same split in the operator CLI; the one-off string match deleted as subsumed. Recorded in `docs/decisions/2026-09-22_a-domain-refusal-is-not-an-authority-denial.md`, which supersedes the RENDERING half of `.6.1.5.4` and `.8.2.5.3` and leaves both leaves' ORDERING intact.
- [x] **ADDRESSED (verified)** — `evaluation` **3/3** (the two remaining 403s are precisely the two authority denials — an ungranted principal and a holder of the wrong capability), `policy` **26/26**, `site_authority` **11/11**, `site_operator_cli` **3/3**, `site_registry_http` **8/8** unchanged.
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — `profiles` **63/63**, `mcp_write` **7/7**, `allowlist` **2/2**, `regions` **3/3**, `migration_upgrade` **8/8**; clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` **0 warnings**; fmt rc=0; `make book` builds; `make gate` green.
- [x] **LOCKSTEP** — `MEMORY.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `DEV_NOTES.md`, `LIVE_STATUS.md`, `docs/book/src/evaluation-harness.md`, `docs/book/src/site-authority.md`, `docs/decisions/` plus its index, and this tree, in this commit.
- promotion: declined (the transferable rule — *a name that carries two meanings will be rendered as whichever the boundary assumes* — is this session's fourth instance and is stated in the decision record with all four; a knowledge note would be a fifth copy).
- Verification: the mutant red by name and `api.rs` restored byte-identical; nine suites green; clippy 0 warnings; fmt, book and the doctrine gate rc=0.
- Commit: `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0393 (leaf SIGNOFF-REPAIR.16): a domain refusal is not an authority denial, and the 403 I shipped one commit ago told authorized callers a falsehood`.

### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13 — The blocker register: every blocker owned, tracked and re-surfaced

- Opened: `pending` by the director's instruction of 2026-09-15, given three times in one session and each time stronger: a blocker is handled promptly or at minimum put **front and center** and discussed explicitly; it is **reminded until he actively interacts with it**; and it is **listed in the mdBook and task-tree owned/tracked**.
- 🔴 **Why this activity exists, stated as the defect rather than as a process.** Before it, the project's blockers lived in four places and none of them was a register: §16.12's three external gaps were prose inside a closed phase's gate record, the license and name-clearance gates were a sentence in `MEMORY.md`, the one held director decision was frontier row 8, and the never-run remote CI was a cadence note in `COMMIT.md`. Every one was OWNED in the sense §15 means; none was VISIBLE from the director's seat, which is the reply and the book. ⛔ Ownership and surfacing are two obligations and this tree had been meeting only the first.
- ⭐ **The distinction the register is built around:** a blocker that is owned but unsurfaced is buried on a slower timescale than one that is unowned, and therefore harder to notice. `​.3.5.2.1` had sat correctly held, correctly acceptance-bearing and correctly at frontier row 8 for two days — which is exactly what being buried looks like when every individual rule has been followed.
- Owns: the register itself — the `Ack?`-bearing table at the head of this tree's `## Blockers` section, the book's [blockers chapter](../book/src/blockers.md), and one child leaf per blocker that has no other owner. ⛔ A blocker already owned by a leaf (A1 → `.3.5.2.1`, C2 → `.11.4.7`) gets a REGISTER ROW, not a duplicate leaf; the register points at the owner rather than re-owning it.
- ⛔ **The re-surfacing rule is the load-bearing part and it is not mechanizable.** ⚠️ **Its FIRST form was wrong and is superseded by `.13.5` (2026-09-17)**: it made every stopping-point reply list every row whose `Ack?` was `no`, and a row cleared only when the director engaged with THAT row. The column asked a question about the READER, in the maintainer's own register, and the director's answer when he finally saw it was that he had delegated the disposition and therefore *"it is supposed to be you"* who sets it. The corrected rule and the replacement column are at `.13.5`.
- Acceptance: every blocker in the register has an owner — a leaf, or a named external party with the trigger that would clear it; the book chapter lists them all and stays in lockstep with the table; ⚠️ the third clause read *"the `Ack?` column reflects actual director engagement and is never advanced on inference"* and is **superseded by `.13.5`**, which replaces the column with one the maintainer can set and defend; and no blocker is ever removed from the register for being old.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0194 ships the register. ⛔ The register existing is not the blockers clearing: `.13.1`–`.13.3` stay `pending`, and rows A1 and C2 point at `.3.5.2.1` and `.11.4.7` rather than being re-owned here.

Every row carries who it is blocked on, its owner, what it does NOT block, and an `Ack?` column that starts at `no` for all eight.
- **The public face:** `docs/book/src/blockers.md`, registered in `SUMMARY.md` directly after the qualification chapter, because the director reads the book rather than the frontier. It states the same eight, with a closing section on what C2 means for the Internet gate specifically.
- ⭐ **Three rows had no leaf at all before this**, which is the measurement that justifies the activity rather than the instruction alone: B1–B3 lived as prose inside a CLOSED phase's gate record, B5 was tracked by nothing anywhere, and C1 was a cadence note in `COMMIT.md`. ⛔ Two rows did have owners and are deliberately NOT re-owned — a register that duplicates a leaf becomes a second copy that drifts, which is the `INDEX-FRONTIER` failure in another costume.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.1 — The three external G6 preconditions

- Opened: `pending` by `.13`. Covers register rows **B1**, **B2** and **B3**.
- ⛔ **This project cannot produce any of the three, and the leaf must not pretend otherwise.** §16.12 line (1) is an externally reviewed threat model — §2.6 says AI review does not satisfy an independent-review requirement. Line (9) is a penetration test whose critical/high findings are resolved or the release is CANCELLED (§19.6), not waived. Line (5) is the prompt-injection action-boundary suite, which lands with the exposure profile's first action-bearing surface and has nothing to attach to yet.
- What this leaf CAN own, which is not nothing: the input each engagement needs (a threat model fit to be reviewed, a scope and an environment for a pen test), the trigger that starts it, and the durable record of its outcome. ⚠️ Preparing the input is not the gate and the leaf must never let one read as the other.
- Acceptance: each of the three names the party who clears it, the input this project owes them, and the trigger; none is described as "in progress" while it is unstarted; the register and the book say the same thing.
- ⭐ **B3's deferral is now MEASURED rather than inherited, which is the only part of these three that local work could improve.** The gate record said the prompt-injection suite "lands with the exposure profile's first action-bearing surface", and this tree had been repeating that sentence. Measured 2026-09-15 under the director's instruction to unblock:
  - **The dispatched work payload carries no untrusted content.** `threads::work_payload` builds exactly `kind`, `agent_role`, `subject`, `objective`, `reservation`, `reservation_reason`, `allow_possible_duplicate`, plus an optional `target_event_id`. ⛔ No contribution text, no evidence snapshot, no derivation, no acquired bytes.
  - **The adapters hold no tools.** The Claude adapter runs `--restricted --tools ''` and the Codex adapter `--sandbox read-only`; `prompt_for` passes the payload as USER content and never as instructions.
  - **The acquisition packs terminate in evidence, not in action.** R0/R1/R2 produce snapshots and derivations that are stored and served through read surfaces; no path carries them into a dispatched run.
- ⛔ **So §16.6's action boundary genuinely has nothing to guard yet, and the deferral is CORRECT** — which is a stronger statement than the gate record's, because it rests on three measurements rather than on a plan.
- 🔴 **The trigger is therefore mechanical, and naming it is what stops the deferral being silently outlived.** The suite becomes owed the first time ANY of these is true: `work_payload` gains a field carrying acquired or contributed content; an adapter's `AdapterCapabilities.tool_support` becomes `true`; or a model output reaches a publication, a deployment, a grant or a tool call rather than becoming a contribution. ⚠️ Each is a one-line grep, which is the point — a deferral whose end condition cannot be checked is a deferral that outlives its reason.
- ⚠️ **B1 and B2 are NOT improvable this way and the leaf must not pretend otherwise.** An externally reviewed threat model and a penetration test are engagements; no measurement makes either less required. What this project can still own for them is the INPUT — a threat model fit to be reviewed, a scope and an environment for a test — and that remains this leaf's work.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.1.1 — The adapter-load ladder has no caller, and its only ceiling permits tools

- Opened: `pending` on 2026-09-15. ⚠️ **Provenance, stated because it matters:** this was NOT found by a leaf. The director asked whether a locally spawned open-weight model (Kimi, Qwen, GLM, DeepSeek) or a remote instance could join the network, and whether the network cares which agent type connects. Answering that required reading the admission path, and the reading contradicted the answer I had already given him. ⭐ The question was better than my census.
- 🔴 **`verify_ladder` HAS NO PRODUCTION CALLER.** `git grep -n "verify_ladder" -- crates` returns 8 hits: the definition (`crates/reasonbraid-adapter/src/allowlist.rs:150`), a `pub use` re-export (`crates/reasonbraid-adapter/src/lib.rs:43`), and **six call sites all inside `allowlist.rs`'s own `#[cfg(test)]` module** (lines 266, 286, 301, 315, 331, 351). The five-rung fail-closed adapter-load ladder is a tested library that nothing runs. Same for `capabilities_within`: its only non-test caller is `verify_ladder` itself.
- ⛔ **`dead_code` cannot see this** — `verify_ladder` is `pub` and re-exported from `lib.rs`, so the compiler is satisfied. MEMORY has carried that warning since `.11.4.5.4`; this is a fresh instance of it, at an admission control.
- 🔴 **AND the ceiling would not refuse tools even if it were wired.** `AllowedCapabilities::dev()` (`crates/reasonbraid-adapter/src/allowlist.rs:44`) is the **only constructor in the crate**, and it sets `tool_support: true`. Rung 5 is `!declared.tool_support || allowed.tool_support` (`crates/reasonbraid-adapter/src/allowlist.rs:140`), so under the one profile that ships, an adapter declaring tool support passes.
- ⭐ **This is `.3.4`'s shape at a security control: a goal line naming a mechanism its own split dropped.** `PHASE-8.4.4`'s Goal reads "the five-rung verification **at the adapter-load path**". Its Done list ships the ladder function, migration `0052_adapter_allowlist.sql` and the `tenant_admin`-gated registry verbs — and no load-path call. The leaf is `done`.
- ⛔ **What this does NOT mean, and the leaf must not overstate it** — the correction I already had to make once here. The shipped adapters are **compiled in**, not downloaded, so no unverified adapter is loading today; `allowlist.rs`'s own header says the dev adapters "satisfy the ladder BY CONSTRUCTION". The exposure is that the control is **inert for the case it was built for** — a downloaded or operator-supplied adapter — not that something malicious is loading now.
- ⚠️ **What actually holds the action boundary today is declaration-side and narrower than the ladder suggests:** every `Adapter` implementer declares `tool_support: false` (`claude.rs:121`, `codex.rs:94`, `scripted.rs:152`, `contract.rs:279`), and the two real adapters pass `--restricted --tools ''` (`claude.rs::EXEC_ARGS`) and `--sandbox read-only` (`codex.rs::EXEC_ARGS`). ⛔ Those are the facts `B3`'s deferral rests on — NOT the ladder.
- 🔴 **Consequence for B3, which is why this sits under `.13.1`.** `.13.1` records B3's deferral as measured. The measurement stands, but its stated ground was partly wrong: the ladder is not enforcing anything. ⚠️ A third-party adapter — exactly what an open-weight local runner would be — is the case the ladder exists for, and it is the case with no enforcement.
- Owns: deciding and recording (a) whether to wire `verify_ladder` into the adapter-load path or to state plainly that no load path exists yet and the ladder is ahead of its caller; (b) whether `AllowedCapabilities::dev()`'s `tool_support: true` is intended, given that no adapter declares it and B3's deferral depends on none doing so; (c) correcting `.13.1`'s B3 text and the book's blocker page so neither cites the ladder as the control.
- ⚠️ **Prefer (a)-as-a-statement over (a)-as-a-wiring until a load path exists.** Wiring a verification into a path that never runs buys nothing and creates a second false assurance. ⛔ But a `pub` control with no caller and no note saying so is the thing that produced this finding — whichever is chosen must leave a reader unable to make my mistake.
- Acceptance: a census of every `pub` item in `reasonbraid-adapter` with no non-test caller (not just these two — scoping to the two with known answers is `.3.3.4.10`'s mistake); a decision on (a), (b) and (c) each with its rationale; if the ceiling stays permissive, the leaf says what would refuse a tool-declaring adapter instead; and `.13.1`, the register and `docs/book/src/blockers.md` stop attributing the boundary to the ladder.
- [x] **THE CENSUS, CRATE-WIDE AND IN A TRACKED INSTRUMENT** — `scripts/census_adapter_public_api.py` (leg 3: the producer is tracked, `--self-test` two-sided). **102 `pub` items; 17 with no non-test caller outside their own file.** ⛔ The leaf named TWO items; the census says **THREE** — `AllowedCapabilities` joins `verify_ladder` and `capabilities_within`, which is exactly why the acceptance forbade scoping to the known answers.
- 🔴 **All three have exactly ONE non-test mention outside their own file, and it is the SAME line** — `crates/reasonbraid-adapter/src/lib.rs:43`, `pub use allowlist::{capabilities_within, verify_ladder, AllowedCapabilities, RungRefusal};`. ⭐ **A re-export is not a caller, and it is also the mechanism that blinds `dead_code`**: without it the items would be crate-private, unused, and the compiler would have said so on the first build. ⚠️ A mention-counting census over-counts by exactly one per re-export, and **one is the most dangerous answer** — it reads as "it has a caller", where a zero would have prompted a second look.

It changes the DIRECTION the ladder fails if it is ever wired: closed rather than open, with a tool-using adapter needing a deliberate profile.

It is textual, so a flag passed through a variable rather than the pinned const would not be seen. And it says nothing about the acquisition packs, which are the untrusted-INPUT side, owned by `.7.2`.

Fixed by BRACE MATCHING from the function's opening brace. ⛔ A terminator that depends on how the next declaration happens to be spelled is not a delimiter.

The probe now asserts the EXACT key set and names extra/missing on failure. ⚠️ Second instance this session of `docs/knowledge/a-self-test-cannot-be-tidier-than-the-real-input` — there the fixtures were tidier than the file; here the ASSERTION was weaker than the claim.

- 🔴 **A SECOND DEFECT, AND IT IS MINE FROM THE PREVIOUS COMMIT: `SECRET-SCAN` COULD NOT SEE THE COMMIT IT WAS GATING.** Registering `ACTION-BOUNDARY` ran the full enforcer, and `SECRET-SCAN` — installed one commit earlier by REPAIR-0200 — fired. Not on this leaf's work: on REPAIR-0200's own.
  - ⛔ **The superseded claim, named rather than quietly replaced:** REPAIR-0200 recorded `gitleaks detect --source . --redact` rc=0, `no leaks found`, as its ADDRESSED evidence. That measurement was taken against an **UNCOMMITTED working tree**, and `gitleaks detect`/`git` scans **HISTORY**. So it verified the state BEFORE the change, and the value it introduced — `key-delegation-1` — surfaced as a new `generic-api-key` finding at `b6445d1818e0` the moment it was committed.
  - ⭐ **The irony is exact and worth stating.** That same leaf's headline lesson was "a rename cannot reach a HISTORICAL finding, because `detect` scans every commit". The identical fact cuts the other way and I did not turn it around: **a history scan cannot reach an UNCOMMITTED change either.** One sentence, two consequences, and I took only the one that was in front of me.
  - ⚠️ **And the rename was ineffective on its own terms.** `key-delegation-1` scores entropy **3.578**; `generic-api-key` fires above roughly 3.5. It was chosen for readability and never measured against the rule it existed to satisfy. The value is now `idem-test-000001` — still 16 characters, so `baseline == 308` holds, and entropy **2.899**, which trips nothing. The fixture now says BOTH properties are load-bearing, because a future editor checking only the length would reintroduce this.
  - **Fixes:** `gitleaks git --staged` added as a FIRST arm to `SECRET-SCAN`, so the gate reads what is actually being committed — **0.03 s**, and falsified by staging a high-entropy literal (rc=1, naming the staged arm) then restoring (rc=0, `cmp -s` identical). The history arm stays as the second. ⚠️ `detect --no-git` was measured and REJECTED: it walks `target/` and `.project-data/` and did not finish in **120 s**.
  - ⛔ The `b6445d1` finding needed a fingerprint anyway — it is in history now — and `.gitleaksignore` records that it is **my own defect rather than an inherited one**. ⭐ The staged arm means the NEXT one will not need a fingerprint at all, which is the whole point: a finding caught before it is committed is a value you fix, not a line you permanently annotate.
- ⭐ **Measured before registering, the `REASON-CODE-DOC` shape:** it fires on **zero** breaches today, and would have fired on none historically either — because the boundary has never moved. ⚠️ So unlike the licence gate, this one catches no present or past defect. Its entire value is the NEXT change, which is exactly what deferral #5 needed and did not have.
- ⚠️ **What this does NOT do:** it does not write the prompt-injection suite, and it must not be described as progress on B3. B3 remains an external blocker whose suite lands with the first action-bearing surface. This gate only guarantees that the day that surface lands, the commit that lands it says so.
- promotion: declined. Both lessons exercised already have records — the parser-vs-self-test half is `docs/knowledge/a-self-test-cannot-be-tidier-than-the-real-input` and the trigger half is stated in `.11.4.7.2.1`'s acceptance, which owns the general question.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.2 — The open external decisions: name clearance and licence

- Opened: `pending` by `.13`. Covers register rows **B4** and **B5**.
- **B4 — ADR-001 public-name clearance.** `ReasonBraid` is a WORKING name on a preliminary exact-name screen, which §2.7 is explicit is not legal clearance. Blocks public branding and any assumption that the crate, domain or handle names are obtainable; it does NOT block repairs, and this repository is deliberately public regardless.
- **B5 — the licence decision.** Tracked by no leaf before this one, which is why it is here: `Cargo.toml` carries a workspace `license` field and §19.6's G1 gate names a licence policy, so the decision has consumers even though nothing currently fails without it.
- ⚠️ Both are the director's, and neither has a technical precondition this project can supply — which makes them exactly the kind of blocker that goes quiet. The register is the reason they will not.
- Acceptance: each carries its decision-maker, what it blocks, what it does NOT block, and the trigger; the book states both as open rather than implying either is settled.
- 🔴 **MEASURED 2026-09-15 under the director's instruction to unblock the blockers, and B5's framing is WRONG: the licence is not undecided.** `git grep -rn "^license" crates/*/Cargo.toml Cargo.toml` returns **ten** declarations of `license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"` — the workspace package plus every crate, four of them spelled out literally and the rest inheriting. The Rust ecosystem's conventional dual licence, chosen, written down, and shipped.
- 🔴 **What is missing is the LICENCE ITSELF.** `git ls-files | grep -iE "licen[cs]e|copying"` returns exactly one path, `migrations/0031_snapshot_license_freshness.sql`, which is a snapshot-retention migration and not a licence. **There is no `LICENSE`, `LICENSE-MIT`, `LICENSE-APACHE` or `COPYING` anywhere in the repository.**
- ⛔ **The consequence, stated precisely rather than dramatically.** A manifest's SPDX expression is metadata, not a grant. This repository is PUBLIC and must remain so, and absent an accompanying licence text the default position is ordinary copyright: a reader has no rights the licence expression appears to offer. ⭐ The project also enforces a permissive-only licence policy on its DEPENDENCIES (`deny.toml`'s `allow` list, with one narrow file-level MPL exception for `uluru`) while granting nothing itself — a rule applied outward and not inward.
- **The dependency graph constrains nothing**, so the choice is unforced: every allowed licence is permissive (Apache-2.0, MIT, ISC, Unicode-3.0, BSD-3-Clause, Zlib) and the single MPL-2.0 dependency is file-level copyleft used unmodified. Nothing in the tree compels or forbids any licence for this project.
- ⭐ **So B5 is not a decision the director owes — it is a decision already taken in ten places that was never given effect**, and the reframing is the unblocking. Of the work it implies, exactly ONE item is not mine to supply.
- ⛔ **THE ONE THING NEEDED FROM THE DIRECTOR: the copyright holder's name**, as it should appear in the `Copyright (c) <year> <holder>` line of `LICENSE-MIT` and the Apache-2.0 appendix. A legal identity is a fact about the world, not an engineering choice, and inventing one would be worse than leaving the blocker open. ⚠️ Everything else — which licences, their exact texts, where they live, the `README` pointer — is determined by the ten declarations already in the tree.
- Owns: recording the above as a decision record; adding `LICENSE-MIT` and `LICENSE-APACHE` with the verbatim upstream texts once the holder is known; a `README` licence section; and a check that the manifests and the files cannot drift apart.
- ⚠️ Do NOT change the licence expression to something narrower or broader on the way: **13 tracked manifests** already declare it, `cargo publish` reads it, and a change would be a relicensing act rather than a completion.
- ⚠️ B4 is untouched by this and stays open: the name clearance is a separate external gate, and a licence grants nothing about a trademark.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0197. The director supplied the one missing fact on 2026-09-15 — **the copyright holder is Richard DJE** — and that was the whole of what remained.
- ⭐ **Both licence texts are CORROBORATED ON DISK rather than reproduced from memory, which is the part of this worth keeping.** A licence is a legal document: a paraphrase is not it, and a plausible-looking reconstruction is worse than none because nothing signals the drift. So neither was typed.
  - `LICENSE-APACHE` is byte-identical to the copy shipped by **104 crates** in this workspace's own vendored registry (201 lines, the complete official text including the APPENDIX with its `Copyright [yyyy] [name of copyright owner]` placeholder, left as the canonical document has it — filling it would modify the licence).
  - `LICENSE-MIT`'s body is whitespace-identical to the copy shipped by **127 crates**; only the copyright line differs. Reproduce with `cmp` and a whitespace-normalised `shasum` against `arc-swap-1.9.2`.
  - ⚠️ Three distinct Apache-2.0 variants exist in the registry; they differ only in INDENTATION, confirmed by `diff`. The 201-line form with the appendix is the complete apache.org document and is what shipped.
- **Fix as shipped:** `LICENSE-APACHE` and `LICENSE-MIT` at the repository root, plus a four-line `## License` section in `README.md` pointing at both. ⛔ The licence EXPRESSION is untouched — the manifests already declared `MIT OR Apache-2.0`, and changing it would have been a relicensing act rather than a completion.
- ⚠️ The README section fits inside the existing caps rather than requiring a raise: **57/60 lines, 2,188/2,400 bytes**, `README-STABILITY` rc=0. ⛔ `README_POLICY.md` forbids raising a cap to land content, and this did not need to.
- ⛔ **B4 is untouched and stays open.** A licence grants copyright permissions; it says nothing about a trademark, and ADR-001's name clearance is a separate external gate.

The census says **13**: the workspace root plus 12 crates, of which **5 state `MIT OR Apache-2.0` literally and 8 inherit it** with `license.workspace = true`; one distinct expression tree-wide; zero `license-file` keys. Re-derive with `git ls-files '*Cargo.toml' | xargs grep -h '^license'`. ⚠️ The superseded figure is named here rather than silently replaced, per `docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md`. ⭐ **Nothing about the fix changes** — which is exactly why the error survived: a wrong count that does not alter a conclusion is the kind nobody re-checks. It was caught only because `LICENCE-GRANT` had to enumerate the manifests to gate them.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.3 — "Remote CI has never run" was never true

- Opened: `pending` by `.13`. Covers register row **C1**.
- The finding **as opened**: `COMMIT.md` names the REMOTE run as the authoritative pre-push gate (`docs/decisions/2026-09-12_checkpoint-gate-authority.md`), and it has never run — so every gate result in this tree, including the full checkpoint pass, is a LOCAL qualification.
