- **What that green covers, read from the workflow files rather than assumed:** `doctrines` runs the enforcer; `supply-chain` runs pinned `cargo-deny` and pinned Gitleaks over history; `rust` runs the workspace check, the Python controls with the full owned PostgreSQL collection, and the book build.
- ⭐ **ROOT CAUSE — the row was written from `COMMIT.md`'s cadence note rather than from the remote, and `COMMIT.md` CONTRADICTED IT FOUR LINES BELOW.** That page's push section ends *"Provenance: director instruction 2026-09-11, during the first remote-CI repair sequence."* A remote-CI repair sequence is a sequence of remote CI runs — and the 12 measured failures are largely it: `rust` failed at REPAIR-0076, 0077, 0078, 0079, 0080 and 0083, then went green at 0086, which is exactly the one-repair-per-push pattern `COMMIT.md` describes as its own standing exception. ⛔ `docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` leg 1 in its plainest form: a fact quoted from the project's own documentation instead of re-derived from the source, when the source was one `gh` call away.
- **The corrected statement, which is narrower and still real:** the remote gate is green at `origin/main`, and **167 local commits sit beyond the last remotely-gated commit** — inside the ~300 cadence the project documents, therefore not a schedule failure.
- ⛔ **`.13.3`'s original instruction — do NOT fix this by pushing early — STANDS, and now rests on a true premise.** `COMMIT.md`'s standing exception applies *while a remote gate is RED*; the remote is **green**, so the exception does not apply and the ~300 cadence governs. The earlier reasoning reached the right answer from the wrong fact, which is worth recording because the answer surviving is what makes the wrong fact easy to keep.
- ⚠️ **One downstream conclusion was built on the false premise and is CORRECTED rather than deleted.** `.11.4.7.2.3` wrote that the supply-chain gates "live only in `.github/workflows/supply-chain.yml`, which runs in REMOTE CI — and remote CI has never run … it is why two supply-chain gates have been red with nobody able to see it." The supply-chain workflow **ran and was green** at `c17841c`. The true cause is the unpushed gap plus both findings post-dating the last push — which that leaf had already established in its very next sentence. The conclusion survives; its stated cause does not.

A gate that cannot run is worse than a documented command — so the command is documented and every claim names the commit it was measured at.
- Acceptance (as opened): the first remote run is consumed, not merely triggered; its result is recorded against the local checkpoint it corroborates; and every place this tree calls a gate "passed" is qualified as local until then. ⭐ **Met differently than written**: the runs were already there to consume, and consuming them is what falsified the leaf's own premise.
- Status: `done`; `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0220`. Register row **C1 is rewritten to what is true** rather than cleared — the row stays visible because the 167-commit gap is real, but it no longer claims the instrument has never run.
- Verification / commit: the four `gh` measurements above, each re-derivable; `docs/decisions/2026-09-17_remote-ci-has-run-and-is-green.md`; `make gate`; `make book`. `REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0220`.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.5 — The register asked a question about its reader

- Opened: `pending` by the director, 2026-09-17: *"Regarding the Blockers what does Ack? means? who decide that it should yes? To me, it is supposed to be you since I delegated that to you!"*
- 🔴 **THE DEFECT, named rather than apologised for.** `.13` gave the register an `Ack?` column meaning *"has the director engaged with THIS row"*, and a rule that every stopping-point reply re-surface every row whose value was `no`. ⛔ **That is a field whose value is a fact about the READER, in the maintainer's own register.** The register cannot observe it and the maintainer cannot set it, so the only mechanism available was to keep repeating the row until the reader reacted.
- **Measured, not felt.** `git log -S"Ack? = yes" -- docs/tasks/SIGNOFF-REPAIR.md docs/book/src/blockers.md` returns **nothing**: from 2026-09-15 to 2026-09-17 the column was `no` on every open row and never once anything else. ⭐ A column whose value has never changed in its lifetime carries no information — the same shape as a control never seen RED, which this tree already refuses everywhere else.
- ⛔ **And it inverted a delegation.** The director had delegated blocker disposition; the column made his attention the precondition for a row to stop being repeated at him. The instrument for *surfacing* became an instrument for *nagging*, which is the failure mode that makes a reader skip the section the register exists to be read.
- ⭐ **THE REPLACEMENT, and it is a different question rather than a renamed one.** The register must answer *"is there anything left that THIS REPOSITORY can do about this row?"* — the only question that separates a blocker the maintainer should still be working from one genuinely parked on an outsider. The column becomes **`Owed here?`**, set by the maintainer from the owning leaf, beside the named next action.
- **The re-surfacing rule that follows from it:** a row with `Owed here? = yes` is **work**, belongs in the frontier and is worked like any other leaf; a row with `Owed here? = no` is surfaced **once per session** with its external party and trigger, not in every reply.
- 🔎 **The replacement paid for itself immediately, and this is the finding rather than the process.** Under `Ack?`, B1–B3 were reported to the director as *"OUTSIDE"* with nothing owed. Under `Owed here?` all three are **yes**: they share one in-repo prerequisite — `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.14`'s frozen exposure candidate — which `docs/book/src/blockers.md` had *already named* under "The route out, decided 2026-09-16". ⛔ **The old column was hiding the maintainer's own work from the maintainer**, and the same reply that listed those rows as external also linked the page that said they were not.
- **The corrected values, derived from each owning leaf:** B1 **yes** (the threat model exists; its fitness for review is owed, and `.14` is what a reviewer reviews), B2 **yes** (the scope/environment document, and `.14`'s freeze is this row's own stated trigger), B3 **yes** (it lands with `.14`'s first action-bearing surface), B4 **no** (professional clearance in three jurisdictions — the only row with nothing owed here), C1 **no** and relabelled *not a blocker — a limit on what may be CLAIMED*, C2 **yes** (four gate records remain).
- Owns: the column, the rule that reads it, both copies of the register, and the correction to `.13`'s own acceptance clause.
- Acceptance: the column is one the maintainer can set and defend from a leaf; `.13`'s superseded clause is marked superseded rather than edited away; both the tree's table and the book chapter carry the new column and agree; the measurement that the old column never changed is recorded; and no row is removed.
- ⚠️ **What this does NOT change.** No blocker's substance moves: B1, B2 and B4 still require outside parties, and `.14` remains under its standing prohibition against turning the exposure profile on. What changes is which of them the maintainer treats as work.
- lockstep: README.md unchanged (this leaf changes a register column and the rule that reads it; the README names neither).
- Status: `done`.
- Verification / commit: `REASONBRAID-DOC-0043`.

#### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.4 — A corrected claim was corrected in the register and left standing in the corpus

- Opened: `pending` by `.13.4` itself, during the startup read of this session: the book's qualification chapter still stated *"remote CI has never run … the license decision remain open"*, two days and one day respectively after each had been measured false.
- 🔴 **THE SHAPE, and it is the one this tree has now met three times.** `.13.3` (REPAIR-0220) corrected blocker **C1** in the register, the book's blockers chapter, the decision record and the one downstream conclusion it could name inside this tree. `.13.2` (REPAIR-0195) cleared **B5**, the licence. Neither swept the LIVE-DOCUMENT corpus, so the superseded claims stayed readable in the two documents the director actually reads.
- **The census, over the live documents only** — `README.md`, `LIVE_STATUS.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `docs/book/src/*.md`, which are the documents COMMIT.md holds to CURRENT truth; `CHANGELOG.md`, `DEV_NOTES.md`, `docs/decisions/` and `docs/tasks/artifacts/` are dated ledgers and are correct as history:

```bash
git grep -nI -E "never run|licen[cs]e decision|license decision" -- \
  README.md LIVE_STATUS.md MEMORY.md 'docs/book/src/*.md'
```

  **11 hits, classified: 4 STALE, 7 sound.** The four: `LIVE_STATUS.md:356` (the false CAUSE — "remote CI has never run" given as why two supply-chain gates were invisibly red), `:382` (the register's own description of row C1), `:1541`+`:1543` (the checkpoint paragraph, carrying BOTH stale claims), and `docs/book/src/qualification-review.md:546` (the same sentence, in the book). The seven sound ones are three unrelated uses of "never runs" (a DNS hook, an adapter load path), the two `blockers.md` passages that STATE the correction, and `MEMORY.md:17`, already corrected.
- ⭐ **The classification is the leaf, not the count.** A raw grep returns 11 and publishing that as a defect count would have been wrong in 7 cases — `docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` §3 leg 2's mirror, that a search hit-count is a population.
- **ROOT CAUSE (WHY + WHERE)** — `.13.3`'s acceptance line reads *"every place this tree calls a gate 'passed' is qualified as local until then"*. **This tree.** The correction's scope was the register and the task tree, and it did reach both, plus the one downstream conclusion at `.11.4.7.2.3` it happened to know about. ⛔ Nothing in its acceptance asked what else in the CORPUS restated the claim — which is precisely the defect class `.11.16` owns: a fact restated where nothing derives it. A claim corrected in its owner and left in its copies is the same failure as a number corrected in its source and left in its mirrors.
- **FIX** — the four stale instances are corrected in place and NOT deleted, each naming what it used to say and what measured it false, so a reader who remembers the old sentence finds out what happened to it. The dated artifact `checkpoint-7233122.md` is left **byte-unchanged**: it records what was measured on its date, and the book now says so explicitly.
- **ADDRESSED (verified)** — the census command above, re-run, returns **13** hits (the corrections are themselves text, so the population grows) and **0** of them assert either claim. The narrower probe is the one that closes the leaf: `git grep -nI -E "remote CI has never run|licen[cs]e decision remain open"` over the same four live documents returns **7** lines, and every one is a QUOTED correction — the register's rewritten row, the book's own correction table, `MEMORY.md`'s corrected blocker line and this leaf's own copies — with no bare assertion left. `make gate` 18/18; `make book` rc=0.
- **NO REGRESSION** — documentation only; no Rust source, migration or script changes, so the focused Rust checks are not the instrument for this slice. `make gate` runs the same staged-file doctrines a code commit does, including `DOCPATH`, `TABLE-ARITY-RATCHET`, `LIVE-DOC-CURRENCY` and `INDEX-FRONTIER`.
- ⚠️ **What this does NOT do.** It sweeps two corrected claims, not every claim. Whether a corpus sweep should be MECHANICAL — a gate that fails when a live document restates something a decision record has superseded — is `.11.16`'s question and is deliberately not answered here: the population has to be classified before a rule is proposed, which is `.11.6`'s standing rule and the reason this leaf publishes 4-of-11 rather than 11.
- ROUTING EVIDENCE: the general rule — *a correction is not complete until the corpus that restates it has been censused* — is routed to `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.16`, which already owns numbers restated where nothing derives them. What was measured here is that the shape reproduces OUTSIDE that leaf's original instance: `.11.16` was opened on a doctrine-registry count, and this is a prose CLAIM in two live documents, corrected by two different leaves on two different days. Two instances, two claim kinds, one shape.
- lockstep: README.md unchanged (it names neither claim; `git grep -nI -E "never run|licen[cs]e decision" -- README.md` returns nothing).
- Status: `done`.
- Verification / commit: `REASONBRAID-DOC-0042`.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.4.3.1 — The revocation backfill is shipped and no control drives it

- Opened: `pending` by `.13.4.3`, which re-derived `REPAIR-0303`'s claims and found this one unexercised rather than wrong.
- 🔴 **THE MEASUREMENT.** `migrations/0077_authority_revoked_at.sql` carries two `UPDATE … FROM administrative_effects` statements that date already-revoked grants and boundaries from the act that revoked them. Every pg suite applies the migration, so the SQL parses and the upgrade path runs — but `git grep -n "revoked_at" -- crates/reasonbraid-server/tests` returns hits only for `node_certificates.revoked_at`, an older unrelated column, and for `.11.24.1.1.2.1.1.1`'s own control, which exercises the LIVE write path and not the backfill.
- ⛔ **So nothing asserts the backfill produces the right instant** — or any instant. A join that matched nothing would be indistinguishable from one that matched correctly, and `migration_upgrade` would stay green either way. That is `.7.1.2.2.1`'s shape (*a green gate is not evidence a suite runs*) applied to a data migration rather than a test suite.
- ⚠️ **What is NOT claimed:** that the backfill is wrong. Its predicate was read against the effect record's shape and its three legs argued in the migration header. The claim is that it is unwitnessed, and an unwitnessed migration is a class this tree has been bitten by before.
- Owns: a control that seeds a revoked row with an `applied` effect record and no instant, runs the migration, and asserts the instant equals the effect record's — plus the negative arm, that a revoked row with NO effect record is left NULL rather than defaulted.
- Acceptance: the control drives the MIGRATION, not the live write path (`migration_upgrade`'s existing fixtures are the shape to follow); both arms present; the `no_op`-outcome exclusion is driven too, since a repeated revocation must not re-date a row.
- Status: `done`; REPAIR-0306. **The backfill is witnessed, and it was right — six of its nine predicates can be turned red, and the three that cannot are recorded rather than faked.**
- ✅ **THE CONTROL EXISTS AND IT DRIVES THE MIGRATION.** `authority_revoked_at_upgrade_dates_only_what_an_applied_effect_dates` in `crates/reasonbraid-server/tests/migration_upgrade.rs` follows `policy_lifecycle_tenant_upgrade_…`'s shape exactly: migrate `through(76)`, assert `revoked_at` is **absent** from both tables at that version (so the fixture cannot be seeding into the post-migration schema and measuring nothing), seed the pre-`0077` rows, snapshot them, `through(77)`, then read the column back.
- **ELEVEN ROWS, EACH WITH ITS ANSWER KNOWN BEFORE THE MIGRATION RUNS, and every effect record on a DISTINCT past instant** — so a predicate that lost a leg dates the wrong row with the wrong instant rather than merely dating one row too many, and an implementation reaching for `now()` fails rather than passes.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.4.6.1 — A shipping wire code is invisible to the reason-code census, so the gate reports coverage it does not have

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.4.6`, which re-derived the emitted set by a second route and got **10** where the census reports 9.
- Reproduce, at the source: `scripts/census_reason_codes.py`'s `_CODE_LITERAL` is `code:\s*"([a-z_]+)"` — a Rust STRUCT FIELD. `crates/reasonbraid-server/src/api.rs:8125` emits `json!({"code": "undeclared_region", …})`, a QUOTED JSON key, which that pattern cannot match. `git grep -hoE '"code"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"[a-z_]+"'` over the server and core sources returns exactly one such code.
- 🔴 **The consequence is not a miscount.** `grep -c undeclared_region docs/book/src/errors.md` returns **0**, and the census prints *"… not documented in the book: 0"*. A `400 undeclared_region` is returned from the site-registry pairing route and asserted by `tests/site_authority.rs:261` and `tests/site_registry_http.rs:490` — so a shipped, tested wire code is undocumented and `REASON-CODE-DOC` says the book is complete.
- ⛔ And it reaches a published record: `DOC-0086` recommends per code over a population of **9**. The population is **10**, so that recommendation is one code short and must gain a verdict for `undeclared_region`.
- Owns: widening the matcher to both emission forms with a self-test case per form; documenting `undeclared_region` in `docs/book/src/errors.md`; and adding its verdict to `DOC-0086`.
- ⚠️ Widening a matcher can only ADD codes, so the gate may start failing on further undocumented ones. That is the gate working; census before repairing, and do not narrow the matcher to keep it quiet.
- Acceptance: the census observed RED first — reporting `undeclared_region` as emitted and undocumented — then green once the book documents it; a self-test case for each emission form, and a positive control proving the new arm is what finds it rather than the old one; and `DOC-0086` amended with the tenth code.
- Status: `done` — REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0345.
- **THE FIX** — `_CODE_LITERAL` becomes `(?:\bcode:|"code"\s*:)\s*"([a-z_]+)"`, reading BOTH forms a wire code reaches a client by in this codebase: the Rust struct field and the quoted JSON key. ⛔ Deliberately NOT `"?code"?`, which would also match `code` inside a longer identifier; each form is spelled out.
- **ADDRESSED (verified), and the gate moved in both directions.** Widening it alone: `python3 -B scripts/census_reason_codes.py --check` **EXIT STATUS 1**, naming *`undeclared_region` (emitted by crates/reasonbraid-server/src/api.rs)*, with the census reporting emitted **18 → 19**, unregistered **9 → 10** and **not documented in the book 0 → 1**. After `docs/book/src/errors.md` gains the row: **EXIT STATUS 0**, undocumented back to **0** — and now truthfully.
- ⭐ **THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS THE LOAD-BEARING SELF-TEST CASE** (`MEMORY.md`: a probe whose conclusion is an absence owes a positive control in the same run). Two cases assert the new arm FINDS the JSON form; a third asserts the **OLD** pattern does **NOT** — so the arm is demonstrably what does the work, rather than the case passing for an unrelated reason. Two more assert the widening does not match `reason_code:` or `"status_code":`. `--self-test` **31 controls pass** (26 before).
- ⛔ **`DOC-0086` IS AMENDED, NOT REWRITTEN.** Its title still says *nine*, for the reason `.11.7.1` gives about its own heading: the number names the population at writing, and every move is a recorded correction rather than a silent edit. The record gains a correction banner, a §B2 verdict for the tenth code — **add as published** — and a note that a recommendation is only as complete as the census under it.
- ⚠️ **The verdict itself is the least interesting part, and the record says so.** `undeclared_region` is a domain refusal raised AFTER the authority check; `invalid_command` is the nearest registered code and would collapse *your request is malformed* into *the registry cannot express this pairing yet*. What matters is that this record's population came from an instrument with a blind spot, and *the census printed a zero* is not evidence of coverage.

###### SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.4.6.2 — A blank line silently disables every FRONTIER-STATUS rule

- Opened: `pending` by `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.13.4.6`, which drove it rather than reasoning about it.
- Reproduce: insert one blank line after the frontier table's delimiter row. `python3 -B scripts/check_frontier_status.py` exits **0** — all three rules pass over a table it parsed as zero rows. A blank line ends a GFM table, `frontier_rows` correctly stops, and `breaches` finds nothing to report because there is nothing to read.
- ⛔ **This is not hypothetical and it is not new.** `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.11.19` was opened on exactly this blank line being present in this very table, and `.13.4.6`'s calibration measured its cost: at **10** historical commits the parser saw 0 rows, which is why `.11.14.3.10`'s duplicate shape counts **24** through the gate and **34** through a direct grep.
- ⭐ **The enforcer does catch it today, and by luck.** `census_frontier_duplicates.py --self-test` exits 1 on the same tree, because of a real-file probe asserting the imported parser still finds ≥20 rows — written for a different reason — and `check_self_tests.sh` runs that census. ⛔ A guard that lives in a neighbouring instrument's self-test is one refactor from vanishing, and nothing records that the gate depends on it.
- Owns: the gate asserting its own parse is non-empty for a file that HAS a `## Current Frontier` heading, so an unparseable table is a breach rather than a pass; and deciding whether the census's real-file probe is then redundant or is kept as the second belt, with the reason.
- ⚠️ A tree may legitimately carry the heading with no table yet — `frontier_rows` already returns `[]` for prose-before-any-table, and the self-test asserts that case is silent. Distinguish *no table* from *a table that failed to parse*, or the new rule will fire on a legitimately empty tree.
- Acceptance: the gate observed RED first with a blank line inserted into the live table, and byte-identically restored; a control for a tree whose heading has no table at all, asserted SILENT; and the `.11.19` instance named as the historical population.
- Status: `done` — REASONBRAID-REPAIR-0346.
- 🔴 **THE FIRST FORMULATION WAS WRONG, AND RUNNING IT IS WHAT SAID SO.** I wrote rule 4 as *the heading is present and NO rows parsed* — the obvious reading of the defect — and it refused **5 of the 16** tracked trees on two shapes that are both correct: `PHASE-0` writes a completed tree's `| — | — | — | … |` dash row, which carries no backticked leaf id for `ROW` to match, and `PHASE-1` replaces the table with prose. ⛔ `.11.6` again, in the leaf that cites it: **the rule was proposed ahead of its population and the population refused it**, within one minute, because I ran it before believing it.
- **THE FIX** — rule 4 is narrowed to the defect's actual signature: **a blank line with pipe lines on BOTH sides, inside the frontier section**. That is unambiguous, it cannot fire on either legal shape, and it is exactly what GFM reacts to.
- **ADDRESSED (verified)** — with the `.11.19` shape restored into the live table, `python3 -B scripts/check_frontier_status.py` exits **1** with one rule-4 message naming the line (`line 9939`); restored and confirmed byte-identical with `cmp -s`, the gate exits **0**. On the unmodified corpus it exits **0** across all 16 trees.
- ⛔ **BOTH WRONGLY-REFUSED SHAPES ARE NOW SELF-TEST CASES ASSERTED SILENT**, copied from the real corpus rather than invented. If either fires, rule 4 has reverted to the first formulation, and the test says so by name.
- ⭐ **THE GUARD MOVES FROM LUCK TO DESIGN, and the neighbour's probe is KEPT.** Before this, the only thing that noticed a severed table was `census_frontier_duplicates.py`'s real-file probe — written for another reason, and one refactor from vanishing. - 🔴 **THE ONE THAT FAILED IS MINE, AND IT WENT STALE INSIDE THE SAME SESSION.** `.7.1.2.2.3` (REPAIR-0284) published *"scanning ALL of `docs/decisions/` — over **170** records"*. `git ls-tree` gives **170 at `d29478a`**, the commit that published it, and **171 from `48ffdfb`** — because REPAIR-0286, two commits later, added `2026-09-19_the-write-quota-counts-calls-not-effects.md`. **I published a corpus size and then grew the corpus.**
- ⛔ **AND IT WAS STANDING IN THE RETRIEVABLE LAYER**, which is the finding this leaf exists for rather than the number. `.13.4` defines the live-document corpus as `README.md`, `LIVE_STATUS.md`, `MEMORY.md` and `docs/book/src/*.md`, with the dated ledgers correct as history. `docs/knowledge/` is in NEITHER set — so the stale figure sat in `a-metric-scoped-to-one-record-ages-silently.md`, **a note whose entire subject is figures that go stale**, and no rule said to sweep it. ⚠️ A stale number in a ledger is history and is correct as history; a stale number in a note is wrong every time the note is consulted, which is what a note is for.
- ✅ **THE REPAIR IS MECHANICAL, NOT A CORRECTION.** The note no longer quotes a corpus size at all — the argument rests on the **nine** and the **twelve**, which are properties of the key and do not grow — and it says so, naming its own first draft as the instance. `LIVE_STATUS.md` likewise. ⭐ And `census_shared_registry_writes.py`'s `RESTATING_DOCUMENTS` now includes that note, so the next movement in these figures NAMES it: the note restates the census's lineage, so it is part of the census's corpus by construction rather than by anyone remembering.
- ⚠️ **`CHANGELOG.md` keeps the `170` verbatim** — `.13.4`'s own rule: a dated ledger is history and is correct as history. The task-tree leaf and frontier row are ANNOTATED rather than rewritten, for the same reason.
- 🔎 **A SHARPENING ROUTE D PRODUCED, which is more interesting than the stale number.** `.7.1.2.2.3` wrote *"a metric naming ONE record ages the moment a second is written."* Measured at the two commits themselves: at `4c36840` the residue is **16 against DOC-0029 alone and 0 against DOC-0029 + DOC-0066**, and at `d1ba384` it is **14 and 0** — and **DOC-0066 already existed in the tree at both commits.** ⛔ So `residue 16` and `residue 14` were not *aged*; they were **misleading on the day they were published**. The figures are correct under their stated definition and wrong under the natural meaning of the WORD residue, which is outstanding work. The metric was not overtaken by a later record — it was already behind one.
- ⭐ **That is why the repair had to be the scope and not the number.** Bumping 17→16→14 kept producing arithmetically correct figures about a question nobody was asking any more.
- ⚠️ **Scope, stated: this pass verified PUBLISHED FIGURES, not every sentence.** Sixteen numeric or enumerable claims were re-derived. Prose judgements — *the repair is a direction*, *a clamp not a refusal* — are decisions with reasons recorded at their leaves and are not the kind of claim this instrument answers.

The three verification worktrees were removed and `git worktree list` shows only the main tree.

- promotion: **declined, with the extension recorded instead** — the transferable rule is already `docs/knowledge/a-metric-scoped-to-one-record-ages-silently.md`'s, and what this pass adds is that **the note itself was in the blast radius**. 🔴 **The command this caption used to publish that number was wrong, and it had been under-reporting for as long as the `TASK-STATUS` convention has existed.** It matched `- Status: \`pending\`` only. Since `TASK-STATUS` made a leaf's opening line `- Opened:`, a leaf that has never closed may carry `- Opened: \`pending\`` and **no `- Status:` line at all** — 11 leaves do. The caption said 36 where the tree held 46. A leaf's state is its last `- Status:` line if it has one and its `- Opened:` line otherwise, and the command re-derives it that way:

```bash
awk '/^#{3,6} SIGNOFF-REPAIR/{if(h!="")print s; h=$0; s="none"} \
     /^- Status:/{s=$0} /^- Opened:/{if(s=="none")s=$0} \
     END{if(h!="")print s}' docs/tasks/SIGNOFF-REPAIR.md | grep -c '`pending`'
```

## Commit acceptance — SIGNOFF-REPAIR.6.2.2
- [x] **REPRODUCE / ISSUE** — `assertion left == right failed: the cursor is a HIGH-WATER MARK and does not rewind; resume_plan reads it as the resume point, so a rewind re-offers everything above it`, `left: 5`, `right: 100`, `test result: FAILED. 2 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored`. - [x] **FIX / the decision** — `SET last_cursor = GREATEST(last_cursor, $1)`: a **CLAMP, not a refusal**. ⛔ Refusal was REJECTED with its reason: a late delivery is a real delivery, the dedup check immediately above has already established it is new, and dropping it is a worse outcome than the cursor problem it would fix. The delivery is applied and enters the window; only the mark is protected. ⭐ A second decision rides with it — `last_delivery = CASE WHEN $1 > last_cursor THEN $2 ELSE last_delivery END`, so the pair stays ONE fact, *the delivery that set the mark*, rather than two independent latest-writes that can disagree about which delivery they describe. `listen_state` returns them together as the reconnect's input.
- [x] **ADDRESSED (verified)** — `RB_DEMO=0 bash scripts/run_pg_tests.sh mcp_listen` → `test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out`, rc=0 (2 after `.6.2.1`, 1 before the lane opened). `cargo clippy -p reasonbraid-server --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` rc=0; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` rc=0.
- [x] **FALSIFIED (in situ, self-reversing, restored byte-identical)** — restoring the unconditional `SET last_cursor = $1, last_delivery = $2`, the exact clause this leaf replaced and nothing else, reproduces the identical RED: `left: 5`, `right: 100`, `2 passed; 1 failed`. `cmp -s` reports `mcp_listen.rs` byte-identical against its pre-neutralization copy; the run afterwards is 3/3.
- [x] **THE ARM THAT KEEPS IT A CLAMP RATHER THAN A SILENT DROP** — the control REPLAYS the late delivery and asserts it is refused, which proves its id really entered the dedup window. ⛔ Without it, a repair that simply ignored low-cursor deliveries would pass every other assertion in the test: the cursor would read 100, `last_delivery` would read `d-hi`, and the delivery would be gone. A control that only checks the number it was worried about cannot tell a fix from a different bug.
- [x] **NO REGRESSION** — one SQL statement changed in one product file. Forward progress is asserted unchanged in the same control: a delivery above the mark advances BOTH halves. The two pre-existing controls are untouched and pass. `bash scripts/check_doctrines.sh` green (21/21).
